title: Project Manager, Nurse Practitioner
jd_text: Compensation Range: Annual Salary: $63,720.00 - $86,020.00 Position Summary Under the general supervision of the Senior Director of Community Affairs in Health, the Project Manager Nurse Practitioner (PMNP) is responsible for supporting the day-to-day operations for the Gloria J. McNeal Nurse Managed Clinic (GJMNMC) grant-funded initiatives designed to enhance the quality of care, improving access to behavioral and primary care services. The PMNP oversees clinic operations across multiple site locations in Los Angeles and San Diego, ensuring efficient clinic workflows and continuity of care. This includes management of the Electronic Health Record (HER) System (Practice Fusion), monitoring remote telemetric patient biometric data, and providing administrative and clinical support to advanced practice nurses, Master of Social Work (MSW) students, and community health administrative staff. The PMNP collaborates closely with faculty and staff from the National University (NU) JFK School of Psychology and Social Services, nurse faculty, and preceptors to ensure high-quality training and care delivery in simulated and live settings. In their grant role, the PMNP directs grant activities in collaboration with internal and external partners, assists and monitors outcome reporting systems, and assists with communications with federal grant staff and stakeholders. The PMNP will assist with budget, supporting grant objectives across the institution, and supporting the Principal Investigator with additional project duties. This position also includes scholarly and community engagement responsibilities, including co-authoring publications and reports related to clinic outcomes, collecting data for the federal Uniform Data System (UDS), and building relationships with community leaders, social service agencies, and CBOs to expand clinic services to new community site locations. Essential Functions: Ensure the successful completion of all grant-funded activities in accordance with Health Resources Services Administrations guidelines. Assist with quarterly and final reports in a timely manner to meet grant compliance requirements. Maintain ongoing, meaningful outcomes assessment related to all grant-funded initiatives. Supervise the Nurse Practitioners and Community Health Administration Coordinator directly. Manage vendor contracts, payments, and the implementation of contracted services. Oversee day-to-day needs related to the coordination and execution of grant project activities. Collaborate with the project evaluator to support quarterly data collection and reporting processes for annual reports. Clinic Operations Manage and support all aspects of daily clinic operations, ensuring efficient, effective, and patient-centered service delivery. Respond promptly to clinic needs, including addressing patient concerns, supporting real-time troubleshooting, and maintaining clinic flow. Lead efforts to optimize clinic hours, scheduling, and patient appointment systems. Collaborate with advanced practice nurses to manage clinic schedules and create provider calendars in Practice Fusion. Ensure clinical operations meet standards for cultural competency and quality care delivery. Develop, implement, and enforce clinic policies, procedures, operational systems, and workflow improvements. Support billing and credentialing processes to ensure compliance with insurance and professional standards. Evaluation and Compliance Ensure all clinical evaluation tools are current and that evaluations occur annually, including patient experience surveys and screening tools tied to social determinants of health. Maintain awareness of and adherence to current licensing and scope-of-practice requirements for all clinical staff. Implement systems and processes that align with revenue goals, productivity benchmarks, and clinic efficiency targets. Communication and Outreach Communicate effectively with clinic staff, providers, patients, and external stakeholders. Participate in community outreach initiatives and represent the clinic at health fairs and public events. Stay current with healthcare trends and best practices through professional reading and attendance at relevant conferences (as funding permits). Additional Responsibilities Perform other duties as assigned by the Director, Principal Investigator, or project leadership. Supervisory Responsi bilities : This position will directly supervise advanced practice nurse practitioners, and community health coordinators. Supervisor duties to include: Screens, interviews candidates, and recommends individuals for hiring. Assign work to new and continuing employees. Delegates task and provides effective direction to team members to produce substantial business results. In conjunction with HR, determines corrective action as needed for direct reports. Requirements: Education & Experience: Education Doctoral degree in healthcare or a related field, preferred. Master of Science in Nursing required. Licensure & Certification Current and unencumbered Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN) Certification and Registered Nurse (RN) Licensure required. Active California furnishing number, National Provider Identifier (NPI), and DEA registration number required. Maintain current national and state board certification as a Nurse Practitioner from an approved organization such as: American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) American Academy of Nurse Practitioners (AANP) National Certification Corporation (NCC) for Obstetrics, Gynecologic, and Neonatal Nursing Specialties Experience Minimum of 5 years of experience in healthcare management and leadership required. At least 5 years of experience in higher education student success programming, grants management, or related work with Hispanic adult learners preferred. Experience coordinating or managing federal grant programs preferred. Background working in or with communities of color or other underserved populations preferred. Evidence of prior experience serving in a nurse faculty position preferred. Competencies/Technical/Functional Skills: Teamwork & Leadership Strong ability to work collaboratively as part of a diverse team, contributing to shared goals without always taking the lead. Accepts personal accountability; demonstrates integrity, honesty, and respect in all professional interactions. Proven ability to influence and build effective relationships with peers, partners, and stakeholders to achieve business and organizational objectives. Demonstrate leadership through goal-setting aligned with organizational mission and strategic priorities. Communication & Interpersonal Skills Excellent interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills. Skilled in communicating professionally with a wide range of individuals across diverse communities. Ability to foster a cooperative spirit within large or small, multicultural teams in fast-paced, deadline-driven environments. Problem Solving & Innovation Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail and accuracy. Demonstrated ability to resolve challenges proactively and creatively. Encourages innovative thinking and contributes to the design and implementation of new or cutting-edge programs and processes. Organizational & Office Management Knowledge of office policies, procedures, and systems, including within a higher education or healthcare environment (preferred). Strong organizational and multitasking skills with the ability to manage shifting priorities in dynamic settings. Demonstrates understanding of broader organizational issues and their impact on day-to-day operations. Technical Proficiency Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Publisher, and SharePoint. Skilled in Adobe, Practice Fusion, and PeopleSoft/Student Information Systems (e.g., SOAR). Proficient in data entry and completing online reporting forms for local, state, federal, and private grants. Location: Remote, USA Travel: Willingness and ability to travel up to 75% to ensure clinical practice consistency across all clinic locations. Travel may include participation in annual grant team meetings, commencement ceremonies, conferences, and other related events. Candidate receiving offers will be offered a salary/pay rate commensurate with experience that vary based on a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies. Absent exceptional circumstances, candidates will be offered a salary within this range for this position. The minimum salary will be offered based on the minimum exemption threshold based on state of residency. Base pay is one component of National University’s total rewards package, as we are dedicated to supporting the needs of the “whole you” with our holistic approach to employee benefits by offering comprehensive well-being benefits for you and your family. For full details about our benefit plan offerings, please visit benefits.nu.edu . For Part-time benefits, please click here . National University employs more than 4,500 faculty and staff and serves over 45,000 students. We are united in our mission to meet the global education demands of the 21st Century and are dedicated to creating a supportive academic and work environment that allows students, faculty and staff to develop their interests and talents while experiencing a sense of community. With programs available both online and at our many campus locations, National University is a leader in creating innovative solutions to education and meeting the needs of our student population, including adult learners and working professionals. title: Commercialization Project Manager
jd_text: Who We Are: Nutrabolt is a fast-growing, global active health and wellness company with a portfolio of market leading performance-oriented brands that energize and fuel active lifestyles. The company’s disruptive and innovative products compete in the Functional Beverage and Active Nutrition segments, under three consumer-loved brands: C4 ® (one of the fastest-growing energy drink brands in the United States and the #1 selling global pre-workout brand), XTEND ® (the #1 post-workout recovery brand in the United States), and Cellucor ® (an award-winning sports nutrition brand created in 2002). Since its founding 20 years ago, Nutrabolt has set out to meet the discerning needs of performance athletes and fitness enthusiasts, while appealing beyond this core group to include consumers around the globe who are making healthy, active living a daily priority. As a Certified Great Place to Work, Top Workplaces USA honoree, Fortune Best Workplace in Texas, and more – Nutrabolt cares deeply about our people, planet, and the communities we serve. Here, our teammates are united by our mission, and take ownership in creating a healthy workplace environment that promotes strong bodies, clear minds, and a culture of respect and belonging for all. Who You Are: As a Commercialization Project Manager, you will be the timeline and prioritization subject matter expert responsible for creating project timelines aligned with cross-functional partners for your assigned projects (Brand, Product Development, Sourcing, Creative, Regulatory and Quality, Commercial team, etc.) You will proactively monitor your assigned project plans to make sure that all milestones are achieved and helping to keep internal teams organized and on track What You're Good At: Ensure Project/Product scope is clearly defined, establishing project owner/sponsor and identifying core project team, across key New Product Innovation, Renovation, and Line Extension projects. Ensure project roadmap as defined remains on track. Own commercialization timelines. Review current timelines, understand cross-functional team needs and pain points and improve timeline structure. Actively manage timelines from concept to launch. Ensure that all cross-functional parties understand their role in the timeline to aid in delivering on key milestones. Anticipate, mitigate, and escalate possible delays in deliverables with corrective action plans. Hold effective status meetings and work with the cross-functional team to ensure dashboards and reports are maintained accurately to support the management and tracking of progress of all project activities & schedules. Ensure there is a clear purpose, agenda, and action item review for each meeting. Participate in continuous improvement initiatives and activities, supporting the team in success now, and as the organization continues to scale. Work effectively with Brand Marketing, Commercial, Operations, Product Development, R&D, Quality, Finance, Regulatory and other key stakeholders by building strong and meaningful relationships. Identify and create meaningful, relevant measurements and reporting to facilitate learning and improvement for assigned projects. Perform other duties as necessary What You Contribute: Bachelor’s degree preferred. 5+ years of experience in project management, preferably within commercialization of CPGs You’re self-motivated with effective project, prioritization, and time-management skills, with a desire and ability to balance multiple high priority and high visibility projects simultaneously. You love the challenge of figuring things out and making an impact right away. You are highly organized, with an innate ability to connect the dots and understand the knock-on implications of actions or delays to cross functional teams. You keep project teams on the same page through incredible communication skills and can quickly build relationships, while also keeping people accountable. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite Programs Familiarity with project management tools and principles Familiarity with cost of goods and P&L management Ability to build trust and confidence by sharing information, presenting research and data objectively, and providing feedback confidently. Excellent written and verbal communications skills; able to effectively communicate cross-functionally and through all levels of management. Entrepreneurial spirit and enthusiasm Team player, with the ability to inspire and be inspired by many different types of people and roles. Why Nutrabolt? title: Datacenter MPU Product Manager
jd_text: Datacenter MPU Product Manager Join NXP’s Edge Processing Product Innovation team at the forefront of AI and edge computing innovation, helping drive NXP's participation in the once-in-a-generation transformation of datacenter infrastructure driven by artificial intelligence. We are shaping next-generation applications processors that power billions of smart devices worldwide. Product Ownership: Translate market problems into clear Product Requirements Documents, feature specs, and phased roadmaps; make data-driven trade-offs across silicon area, power, performance, and BOM. Market Leadership: Develop competitive positioning, value propositions, and go-to-market strategies to win in relevant segments. Your Background BS in Computer Science, Electrical, or Computer Engineering (MS/MBA a plus). 10+ years in product management, product marketing, customer management, or systems engineering for MPUs, SoCs, or embedded systems. Demonstrated ability to turn customer requirements into actionable specs for hardware, software, and systems teams. Strong understanding of heterogeneous compute architectures (CPU/GPU/NPU/DSP), memory systems, and interconnects. Solid understanding of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) concepts, algorithms, frameworks, and toolchains. Familiarity with edge AI applications, including computer vision, natural language processing, and sensor fusion in embedded systems. Working knowledge of Arm cores, PCIe, and Ethernet. Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced industry. Exceptional communication, presentation, and people skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all levels of an organization. Strategic thinker with a passion for innovation and operational excellence. Ability to influence cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders. Drive cross-functional execution across architecture, design, verification, validation, software, and SoC integration teams. Proven ability to analyze program execution, schedule performance, resource utilization, risk trends, and release readiness data to drive informed business and engineering decisions. Experience translating complex engineering and project data into concise executive-level insights, recommendations, and action plans. This role sits within Strategy and Architecture, part of the Governance & Strategy organization in the Chief Information & Digital Office, and serves as a capability-aligned architecture role spanning organizational boundaries, solution portfolios, and enabling functions rather than a single project or system. The Enterprise Focused Business Capability Architect is responsible for guiding capability evolution across workforce, supply chain, finance, portfolio and project governance, acquisition, and enterprise-management processes, along with the related data, platforms, controls, and integration patterns required to connect those domains into one coherent capability roadmap rather than disconnected local improvements. The successful candidate will: own the current-state and target-state architecture for the enterprise-focused capability portfolio spanning Human Capital Management, Supply Chain Management, Financial Management, Portfolio and Project Management, Business Acquisition, and Enterprise Management across organizational and solution boundaries; define capability roadmaps spanning platforms, workflows, data exchanges, operating processes, reporting needs, controls, and modernization initiatives that support enterprise-focused outcomes; partner with business, application, data, technology, security, infrastructure, and delivery stakeholders to improve coherence in enterprise-focused decisions; and help translate enterprise architecture direction into practical capability priorities, sequencing, and transformation guidance for integrated enterprise-focused business outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Serve as the Business Capability Architect for the combined enterprise-focused capability portfolio spanning Human Capital Management, Supply Chain Management, Financial Management, Portfolio and Project Management, Business Acquisition, and Enterprise Management. Define and maintain the current-state and target-state architecture for the supported enterprise-focused capabilities across the enterprise. Develop capability roadmaps that span multiple systems, services, products, and initiatives supporting workforce, supply chain, finance, portfolio governance, acquisition, and enterprise-management functions. Translate enterprise standards, architecture methods, and target-state direction into capability-specific architecture guidance for the supported enterprise-focused portfolio. Identify dependencies, sequencing needs, reuse opportunities, and trade-offs across ERP-adjacent, planning, reporting, governance, control, and shared-enterprise management landscapes. Guide solution and delivery teams so initiatives supporting Human Capital Management, Supply Chain Management, Financial Management, Portfolio and Project Management, Business Acquisition, and Enterprise Management advance one coherent target state rather than optimize locally. Partner with stakeholders across Governance & Strategy, Enterprise Applications, IT Infrastructure & Operations, CISO & Global Cybersecurity, Insights & Intelligence, finance, supply chain, HR, acquisition, and PMO-related functions where capability alignment is required. Support enterprise decision-making by clarifying capability outcomes, process implications, data dependencies, control requirements, reporting needs, and operating-model impacts tied to enterprise-focused modernization. Escalate enterprise-level standards conflicts, investment trade-offs, or cross-capability issues to the Business Architecture Lead and Chief Enterprise Architect as appropriate. Contribute patterns, lessons learned, and roadmap updates back into the broader architecture practice. Candidates must have the ability to obtain, and maintain, a U.S. Government Secret level security clearance as a condition of continued employment. Strong experience in architecture for business capabilities, enterprise business systems, ERP-centered or shared-services environments, planning and control processes, or complex cross-functional portfolios. Demonstrated ability to work across organizational boundaries and connect target-state design to delivery planning and operational outcomes. Experience creating roadmaps, patterns, and architecture guidance across multiple solutions, systems, or services. Strong stakeholder-management and influence skills across business and technology organizations. Ability to operate as both strategist and practical architectural guide for a capability area spanning multiple related business capabilities. Experience in regulated, security-conscious, or compliance-driven environments. Knowledge of TOGAF ADM or other Architecture Frameworks Strong knowledge of the Aerospace and Defense business domain. Preferred Qualifications: Prior experience in enterprise, business, domain, or capability architecture roles. Experience supporting human capital, supply chain, finance, ERP-enabled governance, portfolio and project management, acquisition, or enterprise-management processes. Experience in defense, aerospace, federal, or similarly regulated environments. Experience mentoring delivery architects while maintaining common architecture standards. Ability to connect business capability planning with operational execution, modernization investments, and enterprise performance outcomes. Experience working with matrixed stakeholders across strategy, finance, HR, supply chain, acquisition, PMO, cybersecurity, applications, infrastructure, and analytics functions. We offer flexible work arrangements, phenomenal learning opportunities, exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers, and a very friendly team environment. At Northrop Grumman, we are on the cutting edge of innovation. Our diverse portfolio of programs means there are endless paths to cultivating your career. We also offer exceptional benefits/healthcare, a 9/80 work schedule option, and a great 401k matching program. Come join us! Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Who You Are: Reporting to the Manager, Quality Innovation and Technical Services, the Technical Analyst - Quality is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing quality programs and performance metrics that drive continuous improvement initiatives across the organization. The Quality Technical Analyst assists in the quality investigations involving out-of-specification (OOS) results, conducts root cause analyses, and manages corrective and preventive action (CAPA) programs to ensure timely and effective resolution of quality issues. The Technical Analyst - Quality develops and deploys quality strategies, policies, and procedures to ensure products consistently meet or exceed company, customer, and regulatory requirements. Leveraging expertise in chemistry, microbiology, manufacturing processes, analytical testing methodologies, and laboratory equipment, this position supports product quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence. Key responsibilities include overseeing the development, review, and maintenance of raw material and finished product specifications; ensuring appropriate chemical, analytical, and microbiological testing requirements are established; and verifying that testing methods, equipment, and frequencies align with industry standards and regulatory expectations. The role also ensures compliance with FDA regulations, including 21 CFR Parts 111 and 117, and collaborates cross-functionally with internal teams, suppliers, and external partners to resolve quality issues and support continuous improvement efforts. What You're Good At: Support the Manager in the execution and tracking of internal and external CAPA programs related to product formulations, deviations, nonconformances, customer complaints, and out-of-specification (OOS) results ensuring timely implementation, tracking, and verification of corrective and preventive actions. Conduct quality investigations, perform root cause analyses, evaluate quality events, and support timely resolution of issues to facilitate product release and regulatory compliance. Collect, review, and organize supporting data required for investigations and product release decisions. Analyze, trend, and interpret analytical, microbiological, and quality testing data to identify risks, investigate adverse trends, and recommend corrective actions and process improvements. Monitor CAPA effectiveness and maintain records to ensure timely closure and compliance requirements. Prepare investigation summaries, technical reports, and documentation packages for management review Develop, implement, and lead continuous improvement initiatives that enhance Quality processes, systems, compliance, and operational performance. Support the development, review, approval, and maintenance of raw material, component, packaging, and finished product specifications using risk-based quality principles. Monitor, trend, analyze, and interpret analytical testing data for raw materials and finished products to identify quality risks, opportunities for improvement, and emerging trends. Coordinate and support product stability programs, including protocol development, sample management, data review, reporting, and evaluation of product performance and shelf-life trends. Identify quality, compliance, and operational risks; establish priorities and action plans; and manage timelines to ensure effective resolution. Develop, track, and report quality performance metrics, dashboards, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to monitor program effectiveness and support management decision-making. Prepare quality summaries, trend analyses, technical reports, presentations, and management review materials to communicate quality performance and improvement opportunities. Serve as a quality representative on cross-functional projects, ensuring effective communication of project status, milestones, risks, and timelines to management and stakeholders. What You Contribute: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Microbiology, Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline. Minimum 5 years of experience in a Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Laboratory, Technical Services, Product Quality, or Compliance role within a cGMP-regulated environment. Robust working knowledge of Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations including 21 CFR Parts 111 and 117 and FMSA ASQ (i.e. CQA, CHA, CQI, CQE, CQM), PCQI, or HARPC certification preferred Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical writing, and data analysis skills. Basic statistics Average, Standard Deviation, Relative Standard Deviation and ANOVA Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and quality data analysis/reporting tools. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across departments and external partners. Independent, and able to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a fast-paced environment. Familiar with lab environment and using pH meters, scales, and other lab equipment. In this position, your goals and KPI's will be focused on: Earning Trust Sound Judgement Customers First Taking Ownership Relentlessly Pursuing Improvement Why Nutrabolt? Wellness Benefits Nutrabolt cares about our teammates’ physical, mental, and financial wellness by providing benefits like: competitive health insurance, life insurance, mental wellness programs, 401K matching, and a Lifestyle Spending Account. Lifestyle Perks We offer unlimited vacation paid time off and volunteer time off. You’ll get discounts on C4 Energy, Cellucor, and XTEND products, too! Family Support We want you to reach your full potential at work by taking care of all loved ones at home. We provide paid parental leave, in addition to reimbursement for expenses related to childcare, fertility treatments, legal fees, and more through our Lifestyle Spending Account. title: Manufacturing & Tech Ops - Senior Manager
jd_text: When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services. Job Title Manufacturing & Tech Ops - Senior Manager Location(s) US Remote - NJ Job Description This is a full-time salaried position with Project Farma, a PerkinElmer company. The successful candidate will reside in one of Project Farma's primary markets and be willing to travel domestically to meet client project requests. Project Farma’s purpose is to improve patient lives by accelerating the delivery of life-changing therapies. We accomplish this through the successful execution of high-quality life sciences projects across the full project lifecycle. Project Farma (PF) team members collaborate with cross-functional teams to build trusted client relationships, deliver an exceptional customer experience, and contribute to business growth by identifying opportunities and applying data-driven insights to support project planning, cost, schedule, and performance management. This role contributes to organizational success by supporting financial performance, operational efficiency, and continuous improvement, while also investing in people through mentorship, knowledge sharing, and professional development. All team members are expected to embody Project Farma’s values by being curious, personable, and unselfish, while maintaining a strong commitment to a Patient Focused and People First mindset. The Manufacturing & Tech Ops - Manager/Senior Manager is responsible for leading teams and overseeing the execution of work aligned to project, client, and business objectives. This role balances people leadership with operational accountability, including coaching, performance management, resource planning, and ensuring high-quality delivery within defined scope, timelines, and budget. At more senior levels, this role provides experienced leadership and operational oversight across multiple projects or functional areas, with accountability for team performance, talent development, and consistent execution of business priorities, while partnering with senior leaders to drive continuous improvement, scalability, and organizational effectiveness. Key Responsibilities Lead or Support end-to-end program management for complex technical operations initiatives including new product introductions, technology transfers, process validations, and facility fit assessments. Develop integrated program plans, critical path analyses, risk registers, and resource plans; proactively identify and escalate risks and issues. Own stage-gate processes and governance deliverables, ensuring milestones are met on time, within scope, and aligned to regulatory commitments. Coordinate or work with cross-functional workstreams across Manufacturing, Process Development, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and Engineering. Partner with technical subject matter experts to translate scientific and process requirements into executable operational plans, development of staff awareness of critical process parameters (CPP) and critical quality attributes (CQA). Support technology transfer activities from development into GMP manufacturing, including documentation, gap assessments, and readiness reviews. Facilitate resolution of technical, operational, and quality issues that arise during operations, startup or shutdown of manufacturing equipment. Development of manufacturing batch records, SOPs or validation protocols as required. Perform operational readiness assessments that fully evaluate equipment suitability and reliability, facility fit and finish, material workflow, supply chain planning, training materials and programs, quality and compliance, sampling plans, area risk assessments and personnel PPE/gowning requirements, cleaning procedures and frequency, tier communication plans, warehouse operations and operational planning that incorporates planned downtime for necessary asset maintenance and repair. Support the primary point of contact and program communicator in their efforts to align with senior leadership, cross-functional partners, and external collaborators or CDMOs. Drive alignment across stakeholders with competing priorities; facilitate trade-off discussions and decision-making. Prepare and deliver high-quality program status reports, executive briefings, and governance committee presentations. Support the development and deployment of program management frameworks, tools, and best practices across the organization. Lead, Coach and develop a team of technical professionals to deliver high‑quality work aligned with project, client, and business objectives. Provide day‑to‑day people leadership, including onboarding, training, mentorship, and ongoing skills development, to build a strong and capable technical team. Set clear performance expectations and provide regular feedback, coaching, and guidance to support individual growth and accountability. Other duties as assigned Experience Required Bachelor’s Degree in Life Science, Engineering, or related discipline (OR a combination of equivalent work experience in capital project engineering, pharma cGMP facility start-up, CapEx/OpEx project management and/or comparable military experience). 7-13+ years of experience in engineering or operations within pharmaceutical, biotech, or regulated manufacturing environments. Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional programs or clinical and/or commercial technology transfer projects in a GMP environment. Strong understanding of pharmaceutical development and manufacturing processes (biologics, small molecules, or both). Ability to interpret technical documentation and engineering drawings. Working knowledge of cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Parts 210/211, ICH guidelines, EMA requirements). Experience applying continuous improvement tools and methods. Exceptional organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills. Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and drive results in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Experience leading teams Travel: Willingness to travel as required for client project assignments. Other Preferred Certification in First Aid or CPR, Familiarity with ISO standards and FDA audit processes. Experience supporting equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ). Experience with aseptic processing is a plus Familiarity with regulatory submission processes (IND, BLA, NDA, MAA). Proficiency with program management tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Veeva Vault). Six Sigma, Lean, or other continuous improvement certification. Project Farma is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, or veteran status or any other characteristics protected by applicable law. PerkinElmer is committed to a culturally diverse workforce. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. We will not sponsor applicants for current or future work visas for this position. This position may require significant travel to support project and business needs. We cannot employ anyone with an invalid driver's license. The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $(147,000) to $(160,000). The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. PerkinElmer is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, or veteran status or any other characteristics protected by applicable law. PerkinElmer is committed to a culturally diverse workforce.

title: Architecture Operations and Enablement Lead
jd_text: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. At the heart of Defining Possible is our commitment to missions. In rapidly changing global security environments, Northrop Grumman brings informed insights and secure technological solutions to enable strategic objectives. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. By joining in our shared mission, we will support yours by expanding your personal network and developing skills, whether you are new to the field or an industry thought leader. At Northrop Grumman, you will have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career. Northrop Grumman’s Corporate Sector Chief Information & Digital Office (CIDO) is seeking a Staff Computer Systems Architect to serve as the Architecture Operations and Enablement Lead , establishing and running the operating model for the enterprise architecture function within the Strategy & Architecture team of the Governance & Strategy organization. This role will serve as the practice operations lead for architecture governance, review coordination, methods, standards lifecycle, metrics, communications, intake, onboarding, and knowledge enablement across the architecture organization. This role is aligned to the target architecture operating model in which the Head of Strategy and Architecture, reporting through Governance & Strategy, leads the broader architecture function through the Chief Enterprise Architect and a strong-core architecture team that includes business, data, application, technology, security, and architecture operations & enablement lanes. The Architecture Operations and Enablement Lead is responsible for helping that team operate as one coherent practice by creating repeatable ways of working, improving visibility into architecture work, and enabling effective execution of governance, decision-support, accountability, and practice-health processes. The successful candidate will: define and operate architecture governance workflows, review cadences, and intake processes; coordinate architecture standards, methods, templates, and practice artifacts across the enterprise architecture team; establish and track architecture practice metrics, health scorecards, and reporting to improve visibility, accountability, and continuous improvement; support onboarding, communications, training, and knowledge-sharing across the architecture population; and Support the Head of Strategy & Architecture and domain leads maintain an effective, disciplined, and scalable architecture operating model within Governance & Strategy. This position will be available as a virtual telecommuter, however, the incumbent most be within 90 miles of a major Northrop Grumman location for ad hoc onsite meetings. Key Responsibilities: Serve as the Architecture Operations and Enablement Lead for the enterprise architecture function. Define and maintain architecture governance processes, review workflows, decision tracking, and operating cadences. Coordinate architecture intake, review scheduling, action tracking, communications, and follow-through across architecture forums and working sessions. Develop and maintain architecture methods, templates, standards governance processes, and repository discipline for architecture artifacts. Define, implement, and track architecture practice metrics and dashboards, including measures of review throughput, standards adoption, decision closure, artifact quality, and practice health. Partner with the architecture leads to improve consistency in how architecture work is initiated, reviewed, governed, and communicated. Support architecture onboarding, training, community-of-practice activities, and knowledge transfer across enterprise, business capability, solution, and system architects. Help surface process friction, governance bottlenecks, and operating-model gaps and recommend improvements that increase clarity, speed, and effectiveness. Lead or participate in architecture governance boards, methods reviews, standards lifecycle activities, and cross-functional planning sessions. Provide coordination and operational support for executive-facing architecture reporting, status visibility, and presentation readiness. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business Analytics, or related technical discipline and 12+ years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree with 10+ years, or PhD with 8+ year. Candidates must have the ability to obtain, and maintain, a U.S. Government Secret level security clearance as a condition of continued employment. Demonstrated experience in enterprise architecture governance, architecture operations, technical program coordination, practice enablement, or a closely related discipline. Experience defining or operating repeatable processes, workflows, standards discipline, review boards, or operating cadences in a technical organization. Experience working across multiple stakeholders, teams, or technical domains to improve coordination and execution. Strong communication, facilitation, organization, and follow-through skills. Ability to translate architectural intent into practical methods, routines, templates, measures, and governance mechanisms. Experience using metrics, reporting, or operational dashboards to improve technical or organizational performance. Knowledge of Architecture Frameworks such as TOGAF ADM, DoDAF/UAF, Zachman, or equivalent. Awareness and understanding of DevSecOps. Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting or maturing an Architecture practice, chief engineer organization, engineering governance function, or comparable technical center of excellence. Experience in defense, aerospace, federal, or other regulated environments. Experience supporting design reviews, technical review boards, standards lifecycle processes, or architecture repositories. Familiarity with enterprise architecture methods, systems engineering governance, or software delivery governance practices. Experience creating training, onboarding, communications, or knowledge-management approaches for technical communities. Ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leaders. We offer flexible work arrangements, phenomenal learning opportunities, exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers, and a very friendly team environment. At Northrop Grumman, we are on the cutting edge of innovation. Our diverse portfolio of programs means there are endless paths to cultivating your career. We also offer exceptional benefits/healthcare, a 9/80 work schedule option, and a great 401k matching program. Come join us! Primary Level Salary Range: $161,000.00 - $241,400.00 The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

title: Experienced Yield Enhancement Technician / Tool Owner
jd_text: The Yield Enhancement Technician / Tool Owner is responsible for improving manufacturing yield, optimizing process tool performance, and ensuring equipment reliability within a semiconductor fabrication environment. This role combines hands-on technical support with ownership of specific process tools, driving continuous improvement through data analysis, troubleshooting, and collaboration with engineering teams. Primary Responsibilities: Monitor wafer yield metrics and identify trends, excursions, and systematic defects. Perform root cause analysis on yield loss using defect inspection, SPC charts, and process data. Implement corrective and preventive actions to improve yield and reduce variation. Analyze inline and end-of-line data to detect early warning signals for yield degradation. Work closely with process engineers, integration engineers, maintenance technicians, and operations teams. Serve as the primary technical owner for assigned inspection tools (e.g., KLA2367, SP1/2, Puma, Altair). Ensure tool uptime, availability, and performance meet fab targets. Track and drive key tool metrics such as OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) and uptime. Qualify tools after maintenance, upgrades, or process changes to ensure production readiness. Provide training and technical guidance to operators and junior technicians. Required Qualifications Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or related field. 3+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, equipment engineering, or yield improvement. Strong problem-solving and analytical skills. Familiarity with SPC, FDC, and yield management systems. Knowledge of specific semiconductor process areas (e.g., lithography, etch, deposition). Familiarity with semiconductor defect inspection and metrology tools. Analytical thinking and root cause problem-solving. Attention to detail and data-driven decision making. Strong communication and teamwork skills. Semiconductor fabrication facility (cleanroom environment). Requires use of cleanroom attire (bunny suit). Must be able to lift and carry objects up to 25 pounds. May include shift work, on-call support, or extended hours during critical issues More information about NXP in the United States... title: Manager, Control Tower Operations (Hybrid/Remote)
jd_text: We’re hiring at Pitney Bowes, where top talent builds meaningful careers and lasting impact. We Move fast, Deliver excellence, and Win together…that’s The Pitney Bowes way. Here, how we work matters just as much as what we achieve. We’re looking for people who: Act with urgency, accountability, and purpose Deliver high quality work with consistency and pride Collaborate effectively and elevate those around them Focus on outcomes that drive impact and growth Job Description: Pitney Bowes is now hiring for a Manager, Control Tower Operations at our Omaha, NE presort facility! ***This position is hybrid, with a strong preference for candidates located in Omaha, NE. However, strong candidates outside of the Omaha, NE area will be considered with ability to travel to Omaha, NE. *** The base salary range is $80,000-95,000 / annually + a 10% field bonus. As part of our commitment to a flexible work schedule, this role does not have a set amount of vacation per year. You are: An operations-focused people leader who drives performance, consistency, and strategic execution across the Pitney Bowes Control Tower. You lead a team of Control Tower Specialists and Transportation Coordinators, setting direction for daily operations while building a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and service excellence. You are equally comfortable guiding your team through complex exceptions and competing priorities as you are representing the Control Tower in carrier performance conversations and corporate transportation initiatives. This position ensures the safe, reliable, and compliant operation of automated control systems, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), remote terminal units (RTUs), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) interfaces, field instrumentation, communication networks, and related equipment. Working with limited supervision, the Automation Technician Senior independently performs complex technical assignments, diagnoses non-routine system issues, supports operational reliability initiatives, and serves as a technical resource for automation and control system matters. The role applies advanced technical knowledge to improve system reliability, data accuracy, process control performance, regulatory readiness, and operational efficiency. Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance activities on automation, instrumentation, electrical, and control system equipment. Diagnose and resolve complex automation system issues involving field devices, control logic, communication networks, input/output signals, and process interfaces. Support startup, shutdown, commissioning, and operational readiness activities for automation and control system installations or modifications. Verify system functionality through testing, calibration, loop checks, functional checks, and system validation activities. Monitor automation system performance and identify trends, failures, or reliability concerns requiring corrective action. Perform electrical and instrumentation troubleshooting to support safe and reliable facility operations. title: Staff Business Systems Analyst – Workday Security & ITGC Lead
jd_text: We're looking for a Staff Business Systems Analyst – Workday Security & ITGC Lead to join Procore's Enterprise Technology and Business Platforms team. In this hands-on technical role, you will be the system administrator and technical owner responsible for Workday security architecture, tenant configurations, business process engineering, and key reporting infrastructure. You aren't just managing compliance on paper—you know Workday inside and out, build and maintain complex configurations, manage service account governance, and ensure system-level changes and business processes adhere to strict security and SOX standards. Reporting to the Sr. Director, Enterprise G&A Technology, this is a deeply technical, hands-on role embedded directly within Enterprise Technology. This role is based in Remote US and we are looking for someone to join us immediately. What You'll Do: Hands-on Workday Configuration & Security: Architect, configure, and maintain Workday security models (domain policies, business process security, constraint groups, segmented security), ensuring system configurations and business process workflows align directly with security and compliance controls. Service Account Governance: Manage and audit all Workday integration system users (ISUs), API service accounts, and elevated access permissions; determine and maintain in-scope service accounts for SOX ITGC and logical access reviews. Key Reporting & Data Integrity: Design, build, and maintain the inventory of Workday Key Reports (IPEs) used in financial and operational controls, utilizing advanced custom reports, calculated fields, and robust change-tracking procedures to guarantee data completeness and accuracy. Technical Change Management: Act as the technical gatekeeper for Workday tenant configuration changes, semi-annual feature updates, and new integrations, ensuring change management standards, SDLC protocols, and testing evidence are strictly executed prior to production deployment. Automated Controls & Job Monitoring: Design, operationalize, and maintain IT Automated Controls (ITACs) and system-enforced validation rules in Workday; monitor critical batch jobs, scheduled processes, integration failures, and ensure documented, timely resolution. Audit Leadership & Evidence Technical Lead: Serve as the primary technical liaison for internal and external audits—independently leading walkthroughs, extracting system logs and security reports directly from Workday, and demonstrating how technical configurations prevent risk. Deficiency Remediation & Systems Rationalization: Perform technical root-cause analysis for any control failures, design technical fix/remediation plans in Workday, validate compensating controls, and drive automated solutions that eliminate manual compliance overhead. AI & Operational Innovation: Apply AI/LLM tooling to streamline systems evidence collection, request triage, and audit documentation while maintaining strict data governance and auditability standards. Cross-Functional & Team Mentorship: Partner closely with Enterprise Integrations, HR Technology, Controllership, and Internal Audit, while mentoring Senior and Associate BSAs on Workday configuration standards and compliance execution. What We're Looking For: 7+ years in business systems analysis, IT systems administration, or IT compliance, with 4+ years of direct, hands-on experience configuring and administering Workday. Deep Workday Technical Expertise: Proven proficiency in configuring Workday Security (domain/BP security policies, ISUs, SoD matrix, security groups) and developing advanced Custom Reports and Calculated Fields for key audit reporting (IPEs). Technical ITGC & Change Management Mastery: Practical experience managing ITGC domains in production environments—logical access provisioning, privileged access reviews, service account management, SDLC/change control, and job scheduling. Demonstrated experience independently leading ITGC and ITAC technical walkthroughs with external audit teams for public companies or SEC registrants. Strong understanding of how business process configurations and tenant settings map to system controls, automated business process validations, and risk mitigation. Proven track record of performing exposure analysis, lookback assessments, and technical remediation for system or process deficiencies. Experience or practical interest in utilizing AI/LLM automation tools for systems operations, data processing, or compliance workflows. Relevant certifications strongly preferred (e.g., Workday Pro Security, Workday Pro Reporting, CISA, CISSP). Additional Information Base Pay Range: 114,912.00 - 158,004.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Security Engineering
jd_text: We're looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager, Security Engineering to join Procore's Security Engineering organization. In this role, you'll lead the design and execution of large-scale, transformational programs to build and scale an agentic security fleet — an AI-driven, autonomous system that continuously identifies, prioritizes, and remediates threats across Procore's SaaS platform. Your primary goal is to drive the end-to-end delivery of this next-generation security capability, turning complex, ambiguous initiatives into coordinated programs that ship. As a Staff TPM, you'll partner with Security, Product & Technology, IT, and GRC teams to drive alignment, unblock dependencies, and keep the most consequential security programs on track. Use your program leadership, systems thinking, and ability to influence without authority to deliver a security fleet that operates at machine speed and scales with Procore's growth. This is a rare opportunity to shape the security posture of a category-defining construction tech platform from the ground up — apply today. This position reports to the Senior Director, Security Engineering and will be based in our Austin, TX office. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead the program strategy, roadmap, and execution for Procore's agentic security fleet, coordinating work across multiple product, security, and IT teams from inception through production deployment. Define and manage program structure for complex, multi-quarter initiatives — including milestones, dependencies, risks, and escalation paths — ensuring stakeholders have clear visibility at all times. Partner with Security Engineering leadership to translate organizational security priorities into actionable programs with measurable outcomes and delivery timelines. Drive cross-functional alignment across Engineering, Legal, Privacy, and Compliance to ensure the agentic fleet meets regulatory, audit, and enterprise trust requirements. Identify and proactively resolve technical, organizational, and process blockers that impede program delivery, escalating to senior leadership when warranted. Establish and continuously improve program delivery practices, tooling, and rituals for an AI-native security team operating in a fast-moving environment. Communicate program status, risks, and decisions to executive audiences with clarity and confidence, framing technical complexity in terms of business impact. Evaluate and influence architectural and product decisions where program scope, timeline, or quality are at stake. What we're looking for: 8+ years of technical program management experience, with at least 3 years leading large-scale, cross-functional programs in a security, infrastructure, or platform engineering context. Demonstrated experience delivering transformational or greenfield programs — particularly those involving AI/ML systems, autonomous agents, or security automation — from 0 to production. Deep understanding of security engineering concepts (e.g., vulnerability management, detection and response, threat modeling, compliance frameworks) sufficient to engage credibly with senior security engineers and architects. Proven ability to lead through ambiguity, build program structure where none exists, and maintain momentum across distributed teams with competing priorities. Strong executive communication skills — written and verbal — with a track record of synthesizing complex technical programs into crisp, decision-ready updates for leadership. Experience working in or alongside engineering teams, with familiarity with model deployment pipelines, agent frameworks, or autonomous system lifecycle management. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience; PMP, CISSP, or equivalent certifications are a plus. A bias for action, high ownership, and the ability to build trust quickly across engineering, product, and security stakeholders in a fast-scaling SaaS environment. title: Global Partner Program Manager
jd_text: We’re looking for a Global Partner Program Manager to join Procore’s Partner Strategy & Ops Organization. In this role, you’ll design, optimize, and govern our global partner ecosystem architecture, spanning segmentation, economic modeling, and incentive strategy. Your primary goal will be to build a scalable, profitable, and competitive partner framework that drives measurable business value for both Procore and our partners. As a Global Partner Program Manager, you’ll partner with Sales, Finance, Legal, RevOps, Enablement, and Marketing to establish partner tiering, structure discount models, and align cross-functional governance. Use your financial acumen, analytical expertise, and strategic vision to optimize partner profitability, drive ecosystem growth, and deliver high-impact program refreshes. Join a dynamic team building the foundation of Procore’s global channel engine—apply today! This position reports into the VP of Channel Partners and can be based remotely in the US, with Austin, TX preferred. We’re looking for someone to join us immediately. What you’ll do: Define partner segmentation and build comprehensive tiering frameworks, establishing clear requirements, criteria, and benefits across all partner types. Structure partner discount models by type and tier, conducting continuous profitability modeling and cost-to-serve analysis. Design and implement partner-facing incentives alongside internal sales representative compensation models to maximize ecosystem ROI. Manage MDF and incentive budgets, accurately forecasting program costs and analyzing acquisition economics across partner channels. Establish and govern global program terms, policies, and operational guidelines to maintain consistency and compliance. Lead comprehensive annual program refreshes and drive cross-functional change management initiatives across the global organization. Conduct competitive program benchmarking to ensure Procore maintains a highly attractive, market-leading partner proposition. Collaborate with Revenue Operations and Finance to maintain program metrics, reporting, and dashboard tracking via Salesforce and PRM platforms. What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical work experience. 6+ years of experience in partner program design, channel strategy, or partner operations within a B2B SaaS environment. Deep financial acumen with hands-on experience in partner profitability modeling, CAC analysis, and MDF budget sizing. Strong technical and analytical proficiency with SQL, Python, Tableau, Salesforce, and PRM platforms. Proven track record of designing partner tiering architectures, discount structures, and internal/external incentive models. Demonstrated ability to lead corporate governance, program policy enforcement, and cross-functional change management. Excellent cross-functional leadership skills with a proven track record of influencing partners across Sales, Finance, Legal, RevOps, and Marketing. Builder mentality with a data-driven approach, strong commercial acumen, and a growth mindset. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 129,600.00 - 178,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: Principal Product Manager, Developer Platform
jd_text: We're looking for a Principal Product Manager who thinks like an engineer, advocates for developers, and builds like a founder — to reshape Procore's development platform for the AI era.. In this role you'll shape the future of Procore's development platform by treating our 1,000+ internal developers as your customers, and the developer platform as your product. You'll own the developer platform roadmap. You'll know our developers better than anyone — what they're building, where they stall, what they've stopped bothering to ask for — and you'll turn that into a point of view sharp enough to change what gets built across Procore. And you'll build it for a second customer almost nobody has designed for yet: the thousands of agents those developers are running. Human in the loop, not human in the driver's seat. That's what makes this rare. Most platform PMs are optimizing a portal. You'll be designing the interface between an engineering organization and its agents — at the exact moment that interface is being invented. Get it right and 1,000 engineers feel it every single day. This position reports a Group Product Manager and will be based in our Austin, TX office. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll own The golden paths. You define them, and you make them so good that going around them stops being tempting. Build, test, and deploy that feels the same whether it's Ruby or Go. Preview environments that just work. Pipelines nobody wants to escape. Infrastructure that answers in minutes. Developers declare what they need; the platform resolves it inside a policy envelope — the right shape, the right region, costed and approved before it exists. You'll turn provisioning into a capability engineers call instead of a request they file. Security and compliance as guardrails, not gates. Experience making security, compliance, or cost a property of the platform rather than a tax on teams — policy as code, automated remediation, spend attributed to the team that spent it. Observability and cost, built in by default. Every service born instrumented and attributed — dashboards and alerts live from day one, spend visible to the team that owns it, and telemetry an agent can reason over whether the question is a 2 a.m. incident or an unexplained jump in spend. The agent-native platform. Typed, discoverable capabilities that people and agents call the same way, through the same gates and the same audit trail. Agents do the toil and bring the proof; humans keep the judgment. Very few product managers get to design this layer right now — you'd be one of them. The opinion. You set the point of view. This is an organization ready for someone to say "this is how we build here" and then back it up with something engineers genuinely want to use. What we're looking for 8+ years building infrastructure, platform, or developer tools at SaaS scale — with at least one platform you can point at and say "I built that, here's who used it and why." You've been an engineer, architect, SRE, or in DevRel. Close enough to the work that you could do it yourself. Hands-on depth across the modern stack — Kubernetes, IaC, CI/CD, GitOps, secrets — and opinions about which layers deserve abstraction and which deserve exposure. Real observability chops as part of that breadth: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, metrics and logging pipelines, and the aggregators around them. A track record of being opinionated in public — and the receipts. A path you chose, the people who pushed back, and what adoption looked like a year later. Plugged in outside your own walls — CNCF, platform-engineering communities, the rooms where this is actually being figured out. A working view of how agentic development changes what a platform has to guarantee. Not "we should add AI." The temperament to sit with a skeptical senior engineer, understand their architecture, and co-create the fix. Repeatedly. title: Principal Product Manager, Enterprise AI
jd_text: AI is a company-wide priority at Procore. Our leaders are actively engaged, and teams across the business are eager to experiment. Procore exists to improve the lives of everyone in construction, and that starts with our own people: we want Procore to be a place where people do the best work of their careers. AI is a big part of how we'll get there, by putting better tools in everyone's hands, taking routine work off their plates, and freeing up time for more creative and strategic work. To lead that change, we're building a new Enterprise AI Center of Excellence within Procore's Enterprise Technology & Business Platforms team. The team will set the direction for how Procore uses AI across the business, run the programs that bring it to life, and help every team get real value from it. It's a rare chance to build something from the ground up at a company that's serious about AI. We're looking for a Principal Product Manager, Enterprise AI to join the Enterprise AI Center of Excellence. You'll own the strategy and portfolio for AI for operators and builders across the business, meaning how business teams at Procore use and build with AI: which tools and platforms we invest in, which use cases we prioritize, and how we decide. Your goal is to turn AI from a fragmented, team-by-team effort into a coordinated portfolio with clear standards, priorities, and measurable value. jd_text: Procore runs thousands of services across multiple production regions, and too many of them still authenticate with static, long-lived credentials. You won't be the primary implementer — your staff engineers own the designs and write the code — but rather than managing purely from a distance, you’ll be actively engaged in architectural decisions, making defensible build-vs-buy calls, and building deep system context to help the team navigate tradeoffs and tackle complex, specialized work together. title: Manager, Data Engineering & Analytics
jd_text: About the Role We are looking for a Manager, Data Engineering & Analytics to own the architecture, delivery, and evolution of our enterprise data platform. This is a hybrid leadership and hands-on role: you’ll manage a team of data engineers while staying close to the data modeling, pipeline architecture, and business automation work that keeps the platform running. You will act as the bridge between business stakeholders and technical execution — scoping requirements, architecting scalable solutions in Google BigQuery and dbt, orchestrating integrations through SnapLogic, and overseeing our Tableau environment. Responsibilities Team Leadership & Agile Delivery Manage and mentor a team of data engineers, providing regular feedback, technical coaching, performance reviews, and career development support. Own the team’s Jira board and lead Agile/Scrum ceremonies, including backlog grooming, sprint planning, task estimation, and delivery tracking. Build a culture of technical excellence, accountability, clear documentation, and continuous learning. Data Architecture, Engineering & Business Automation Architect and maintain our data transformation layer in dbt, ensuring modular, tested, and well-documented data models. Manage and optimize our enterprise data warehouse in Google BigQuery, including performance tuning, cost management, and access controls. Build and monitor ELT pipelines and automated workflows using SnapLogic and REST APIs to connect core SaaS platforms and enterprise systems. Design and run proof-of-concepts to evaluate emerging technologies and architectural enhancements. Platform Administration & Governance Administer Tableau, including server/site governance, user permissions, licensing, performance monitoring, and content promotion. Establish and champion best practices for data modeling, version control (Git), CI/CD, and technical documentation. Ensure data integrity, reliability, and security compliance across all ingestion and reporting layers. Business Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement Partner directly with cross-functional business leaders to translate strategy into technical data roadmaps and actionable user stories. Coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and validate data deliverables alongside business partners. Maintain SOPs and data dictionaries to drive data literacy across the organization. Qualifications Required: 5+ years in Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, or Enterprise Data Solutions. 2+ years of formal people management, or demonstrated experience leading engineering squads, sprint planning, and managing backlogs in Jira. Production-level experience designing, optimizing, and managing a cloud data warehouse (Google BigQuery or Snowflake preferred). title: Principal Product Manager, Compliance and Payments (New Markets)
jd_text: We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to join Procore's Product & Technology organization, supporting our Procore Pay business . In this role, you'll identify, size, and validate the next set of markets and segments for Procore's Compliance and Payments products, turning early signals into fully formed strategies backed by evidence. Your primary goal is to determine where Procore Pay can win next — and to prove product-market fit in those markets before we scale investment behind them. As a Principal Product Manager , you'll partner with Engineering, UX, Product Marketing, Sales, Finance, Risk & Compliance, and Payments leadership to move opportunities from a hypothesis to a funded, launched, revenue-generating product line. Use your opportunity assessment and market sizing rigor, customer discovery expertise, and ability to operate independently in ambiguity to expand the Procore Pay product and open new revenue streams for Procore. This is a rare chance to shape a strategically critical, high-growth part of Procore's business with real autonomy and executive visibility — apply today. This position reports into the Director of Product Management, Procore Pay and will be based in our Austin, TX office . We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead opportunity assessments for new markets and segments, sizing the opportunity and making a clear, defensible recommendation on whether and how Procore should enter. Validate product-market fit for existing Procore Pay capabilities in new markets, defining the discovery plan, entry criteria, and evidence required before we commit resources. Craft the vision, opportunity assessments, and product briefs for your area, explaining the "why" with sound logic that holds up to executive scrutiny. Take large, ambiguous strategic initiatives and break them into logical, sequenced phases that deliver value to customers along the way. Drive go-to-market readiness with Marketing, Sales, Enablement, Support, Risk, and Compliance, designing release plans that generate fast learning through pilots and betas. Define initiative-level customer and business outcomes, track progress against them, and communicate results in a compelling way across Procore. Mentor product managers and contribute to hiring panels, raising the bar for product craft across the team. What we're looking for: 7+ years of product management or equivalent experience, including ownership of a large or strategically important product area. Demonstrated track record of new market or new product entry: taking a small, unproven idea and developing it into a funded, launched, revenue-generating initiative. Expertise in opportunity assessment, market sizing, and product-market fit validation, with the judgment to recommend against an opportunity when the evidence doesn't support it. Expert command of discovery techniques through customer interviews, market and competitive analysis, prototype testing, and the ability to synthesize findings into trends others can act on.
