We are growing rapidly and looking for a strong, autonomous Regional Operations Manager (AM) who doesn't wait for perfect direction, but instead steps in to identify issues, align resources, and drive action for their doctors and clinical teams. Purpose of the Role The Regional Operations Manager is the critical connector, translator, and operator between our clinics and the Solutions Center. This role doesn’t exist to micromanage from a computer screen; it exists to help our doctors and teams succeed. You will implement the operational infrastructure that allows clinics to perform consistently, creating visibility and developing practice leaders before operational problems become crises. Core Responsibilities & Pillars Operational Leadership: Maintain a pulse on clinic performance, staffing, morale, and operational risks. You will get into clinics early and often, identifying trends and moving issues quickly toward resolution. Leadership Development: Develop Practice Managers into strong operational leaders. Your job is not to personally fix everything, but to coach teams through accountability and execution—building capability instead of dependency. Doctor Partnership: Build deep trust and credibility with our doctors. You will ensure they feel supported, heard, and informed, removing operational barriers so they can focus entirely on patient care. KPI Accountability: Use performance data to drive meaningful conversations, understand the root drivers of performance (not just the outcomes), and ensure clinics are focused on the right priorities. Solutions Center Partnership: Act as the bridge between the field and support teams. Escalate issues early and clearly, ensuring the right teams are solving the right problems to drive company initiatives forward. What "Great" Looks Like in This Role The best Regional Managers make the role their own and leave every clinic stronger than they found it. You are a great fit if you can seamlessly balance relationships (to create trust) with data (to create clarity) , and can communicate clearly at any given moment: Which clinics are winning, which are at risk, and why . Which leaders need development, and which are ready for the next step. What operational issues or KPIs are moving and what is driving them. What to Avoid: If you prefer managing from a distance, relying solely on email communications, or waiting for perfect instruction before taking action, this is not the role for you. Qualifications 3+ years of multi-unit operations management experience (Dental, Orthodontic, or healthcare hospitality preferred). Proactive Ownership: A proven track record of showing initiative and ownership of a region, learning a business deeply, and driving action without a micromanaging leader. Data Literacy: Ability to look past the surface numbers to understand operational drivers and apply analytics to process improvement. Strong Communication & Presence: Exceptional face-to-face relationship-building skills with both administrative staff and doctors. Travel: Ability to travel 60% – 70% of the time to be present in your clinics within the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area. Benefits & Culture We promote a healthy work-life balance and provide a supportive environment built on mutual respect and leadership development. Our benefits package includes: Employer-contributed health insurance. 401(k) with company match (eligible after one year). Paid Time Off (PTO) with no waiting period. Holiday pay with no waiting period. Performance-Based Bonus: Tied directly to operational outcomes within the region.

jd_text: About Us Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. Job Summary The Principal Architect works across data engineering, data visualization, data governance, and AI rather than within a single technical area. On large, multi-disciplinary engagements, this role orchestrates a unified technical approach across technical area leads, each of whom owns depth within their own discipline. Alongside that delivery leadership, this role carries the practice maturation agenda: the delivery standards, accelerators, engineering practices, evaluation rubrics, and advisory frameworks that make delivery consistent and repeatable as the practice scales. The Principal Architect may be billable on engagements where specific technical depth or cross-discipline technical leadership is required. Role Description Cross-Practice Delivery Leadership Lead the technical delivery approach on large, multi-disciplinary engagements spanning data engineering, data visualization, data governance, and AI. Orchestrate a unified solution approach across capability leads, integrating each discipline’s technical direction into one coherent delivery plan with clear sequencing, dependencies, and shared standards. Own delivery approach rather than solution design within any single discipline: how the work is structured, sequenced, staffed, and de-risked, and where the technical decision points sit. Identify delivery risk early and intervene on engagements drifting on approach, quality, or coherence across workstreams. Practice Maturation Priorities are set with the Practice Manager, each carried from assessment through to an adopted standard. Delivery Excellence: baseline delivery standards, reusable accelerators and templates, engineering practices informed by DORA capabilities, and adaptive delivery approaches that balance program predictability with the experimentation required by data and AI projects . Talent and Engagement Model: technical interview standards and calibration, a consistent hiring bar, skills inventory and workforce visibility, and engagement health practices that protect consultant focus. Scoping and Advisory Excellence: structured recommendation frameworks, strategic opportunity framing that translates vague asks into clarified business problems, and clearer engagement pathways between delivery, presales, and the PMO. Data and AI Fluency: capability assessment, targeted learning pathways mapped to assessment outcomes and to the pace of Microsoft platform change, and improved use of internal data for practice decision-making. Build capabilities so they outlast the person driving them, with documented standards, named owners, and adoption evidence . AI-Accelerated Delivery Apply AI tooling and agentic patterns to how the practice delivers value , improving the speed, consistency, and quality of consulting work across all engagements . Evaluate where AI meaningfully changes delivery economics and where it introduces review overhead without net gain and build the evidence to distinguish the two. Fold proven patterns into delivery standards and accelerators so that gains are structural to the practice rather than dependent on individual habit . Practice Leadership and Capability Growth Coach architects and consultants across disciplines on delivery approach, consulting judgment, and technical decision-making. This is a player-coach role without direct reporting relationships. Influence the priorities of technical leads where cross-practice coherence, engagement risk, or the practice maturation agenda requires it. Behaviors and Competencies ​ This role sits at the top of the technical career architecture and is expected to demonstrate expert-level capability across the following. Subject Matter Expertise: Recognized depth in one discipline and sufficient working command of others to lead delivery, evaluate technical decisions, and identify risk outside their primary area. Facilitation: Leads discovery, architecture review, and executive working sessions to a decision, including where stakeholders disagree or the problem is poorly defined at the outset. Communication: Explains complex technical trade-offs to executive, business, and technical audiences, and enables effective communication between groups that do not naturally align. Relationship Management: Builds durable trust with client executives, internal leadership, partners, and delivery teams, and sustains it through difficult engagements. Collaboration: Works in the open across technical disciplines , presales, PMO, and partner organizations, treating shared outcomes as the measure of success. Collaborates closely with Principal Architects from other delivery teams to enable consistent delivery approach and continuous improvement within SHI Services. Problem Solving: Anticipates systemic problems, addresses root causes rather than symptoms, and proposes solutions that hold up as the practice scales. Skill Level Requirements We are looking for candidates who demonstrate strength across these areas. Deep expertise in every technology listed is not expected. Candidates should not self-select out if they do not meet all of them. Bachelor’s degree in a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience. Ten or more years delivering enterprise data or AI solutions, including substantial experience in a consulting or professional services environment. Expert-level depth in one of data engineering, data visualization, or data governance, with working proficiency in at least two of the others sufficient to lead delivery and evaluate technical decisions across them. title: Principal Architect - Databricks
jd_text: About Us Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services. Over 17,000 organizations worldwide rely on SHI’s concierge approach to help them solve what’s next. But the heartbeat of SHI is our employees – all 7,000 of them. If you join our team, you’ll enjoy: Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S. Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities. Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family. World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours. Job Summary We are expanding our Databricks capability within the Data and AI practice and are looking for a Principal Solutions Architect to lead the technical side of it. You will work directly with customers from the outset, qualifying opportunities, conducting technical discovery with customer architects and data leaders, designing target-state platforms, and owning the technical win. Much of the work ahead involves platform build-out, migration, and consolidation, helping enterprises move to the Databricks Lakehouse from Hadoop and Spark estates, legacy analytics platforms, established data warehouse and appliance environments, and other cloud platforms. The role also supports AI and machine learning initiatives that Databricks is designed to enable. This is a senior individual contributor position with significant influence over the solutions we build and bring to market. It is ideal for someone who wants to shape a capability rather than operate within one that is already defined. Role Description Own the Technical Side of Databricks Pursuits Lead qualification, technical discovery, target architecture design, effort estimation, and risk assessment. Develop technical content for proposals and Statements of Work (SOWs). Build and maintain technical relationships with customer architects and stakeholders. Provide customers with realistic and accurate assessments of migration complexity, implementation effort, AI workload readiness, and associated risks. Provide Architectural Oversight Through Delivery Review architecture decisions throughout project delivery. Confirm that the delivered solution aligns with what was originally scoped and proposed. Surface technical risks and issues early in the engagement. Remain closely involved throughout delivery to ensure accountability for architecture and outcomes. Shape Databricks Service Offerings Define the technical content of market-facing Databricks offerings. Establish what is included in scope, how success is measured, and what evidence validates successful completion. Create repeatable delivery standards and frameworks that teams can execute consistently. Partner with Databricks Engage directly with Databricks field teams and specialist architects on joint customer accounts. Build productive relationships with Databricks technical teams. Effectively collaborate and navigate technical challenges, feedback, and differing viewpoints from vendor architects and specialists. Behaviors and Competencies Willingness to Learn: Can apply new learning to daily work, encourage and facilitate learning in others, and actively make changes to work based on feedback. Self-Development: Can demonstrate a commitment to continuous learning and adaptability to new ideas and methods. Leadership: Can take ownership of complex team initiatives, collaborate with others in decision-making processes, and drive team performance. Strategic Thinking: Can analyze complex situations, anticipate future trends, and align and integrate strategies across departments or functions. Problem-Solving: Can proactively identify and take ownership of complex problem-solving initiatives, initiate preventative measures, collaborate with others to find solutions, and drive successful outcomes. Analytical Thinking: Can use advanced analytical techniques to solve complex problems, draw insights, and communicate the solutions effectively. Prioritization: Can take ownership of complex task management, collaborate with others to align priorities, and drive team efficiency. Customer-Centric Mindset: Can take ownership of customer-centric initiatives, ensuring products and services align with customer needs. Collaborates with cross-functional teams to integrate customer feedback into product development. Organization: Can oversee complex projects with multiple moving parts, ensure team alignment with organizational systems, and adapt to changing priorities. Communication: Can effectively communicate complex ideas and information to diverse audiences, facilitate effective communication between others, and mentor others in effective communication. Interpersonal Skills: Can communicate effectively, build relationships, resolve conflicts, influence others, and support others in developing their interpersonal skills in major situations. Skill Level Requirements Lakehouse Platform and Architecture Account and workspace design Unity Catalog and metastore architecture Compute strategy across interactive, jobs, and serverless workloads Open table format decisions Cost architecture and design choices that affect long-term scalability and affordability The ability to design platforms that remain technically and financially sustainable at enterprise scale is critical. Migration and Consolidation Migrating organizations from Hadoop and Spark environments Modernizing legacy analytics and statistical platforms Consolidating established warehouses and appliance-based solutions Migrating workloads from other cloud platforms Key areas of expertise include: Platform assessments Wave planning and migration strategy Workload and code conversion Reconciliation and parity validation Cutover planning and execution This is expected to represent a significant portion of the work within the practice and requires genuine expertise rather than general familiarity. Data Engineering and Pipelines Batch data ingestion Streaming data ingestion Declarative pipeline development Workflow orchestration Testing and validation frameworks Data quality instrumentation Building and operating reliable, production-ready data engineering solutions Machine Learning and AI Engineering Feature engineering Experiment tracking Model registry and serving Evaluation and validation frameworks Retrieval and grounding architectures Agent development This represents one of Databricks’ key differentiators and is an area where many customers require assistance moving from proof-of-concept solutions to production-grade, supportable implementations. Governance at the Perimeter Catalog-based access controls Data classification Data masking Data lineage and governance frameworks Candidates should understand how Databricks governance integrates with enterprise governance strategies and be able to address challenges that exist across organizational and platform boundaries. Consumption Economics Compute sizing strategies Workload placement optimization Serverless versus classic compute trade-offs Consumption attribution and chargeback models Cost management and optimization practices Candidates must be comfortable discussing platform costs with customers and providing practical guidance on controlling and forecasting consumption. Technical Depth Expectations Candidates do not need to be equally strong across all six areas; however, they must possess: Deep expertise in lakehouse architecture and platform design Deep expertise in migration and consolidation Deep expertise in data engineering Sufficient proficiency in the remaining areas to recognize when specialist support should be engaged Other Requirements Databricks Expertise Substantial hands-on Databricks experience gained through: A Databricks partner organization Databricks directly Managing a significant Databricks Lakehouse environment internally This role requires Databricks-specific expertise rather than general data platform leadership experience. Enterprise Migration and Consolidation Experience Proven success delivering enterprise-scale migration and consolidation initiatives. Ability to discuss at least one major migration project in detail, including lessons learned and outcomes. Production Machine Learning and AI Experience Experience operating and supporting production machine learning or AI solutions. Expertise beyond proof-of-concept implementations. Demonstrated understanding of the operational, governance, and maintenance considerations required for production AI workloads. Principal-Level Technical Leadership Proven success operating at Principal Architect level or equivalent. Recognized as the senior technical authority in customer engagements. Trusted to commit organizations to scopes, architectures, and technical approaches. Presales Experience Experience in presales environments, or Delivery leadership experience demonstrating the ability to: Lead customer discussions Define scope and solution approaches Develop proposals and Statements of Work Stand behind technical commitments made during the sales process Vendor Collaboration Comfortable working with and being challenged by vendor architects and technical specialists. Certifications Databricks certification preferred. Ability to obtain certification quickly if not currently certified. Certification support and funding are provided. The estimated annual pay range for this position is $195,000 - $250,000 which includes a base salary and bonus. The compensation for this position is dependent on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location and, therefore, will vary from individual to individual. Benefits may include, but are not limited to, medical, vision, dental, 401K, and flexible spending. Equal Employment Opportunity – M/F/Disability/Protected Veteran Status

jd_text: Overview Who we are Collaborative. Respectful. A place to dream and do. These are just a few words that describe what life is like at Toyota. You’ll also be responsible for Identifying and supporting improvement efforts of existing best practices (Kaizen) through the effective implementation of Toyota Business Practices and TPS Principles. Reporting to the SPO, Inventory Planning Manager, the person in this role will support the Inventory Planning and Demand Forecasting short, mid and long-range goals to right size inventory, minimize costs & improve profitability while maintaining customer satisfaction performance goals for our Lexus, Toyota and Private Distributor Dealers around the world. title: Staff Technical Program Manager - Vision AI
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Most TPM roles focus on tracking timelines, coordinating milestones, and driving execution against an established plan. This role is different. You’ll own the operational backbone of a vision AI data program, ensuring ideas move seamlessly from hypothesis to data capture to validation to a governed dataset to a commercial product. You’ll sit at the center of a complex ecosystem spanning a lean founding engineering team, capture hardware and annotation vendors, frontier AI and robotics companies, academic partners, and internal Legal, Site Operations, and Finance teams. Your mandate is to create operational continuity across these interfaces, remove friction, accelerate decisions, and maintain a disciplined path from experimentation to validated, production ready outcomes. Stord Labs is an innovation center designed to evaluate emerging logistics technologies and help redefine the future of fulfillment. Within a live micro fulfillment environment, you’ll orchestrate the full lifecycle of technical experiments, ensuring promising concepts are rigorously tested, clearly validated, and efficiently transitioned into production when they demonstrate measurable business value. This role is built for a systems oriented program leader who has operated in computer vision, ML, AI, robotics, or data intensive environments and can translate fluently between research, engineering, and warehouse operations without sacrificing speed or precision. You’ll be equally comfortable working with engineers and researchers, coordinating external partners, navigating operational constraints, and communicating outcomes to executive stakeholders. The goal isn’t simply to manage the program. It’s to build the operating system that allows a new vision AI capability to move from idea to validated data product at scale. What You'll Do: Own the evaluation lifecycle: Govern the end to end pipeline of experiments, ensuring every initiative starts with a clear hypothesis, measurable success criteria, and structured evaluation framework. Drive disciplined decisions to kill, iterate, or scale based on evidence. Run hardware and vendor evaluations: Lead structured, evidence based evaluations across capture devices, depth sensors, gloves, edge compute, and data and annotation vendors. Own RFPs, scorecards, evaluation frameworks, and vendor selection. Orchestrate the cross functional ecosystem: Serve as the primary integration point between the engineering pod and Legal, Site Operations, Finance, and warehouse operations. Coordinate requirements around consent, associate participation, scheduling, floor logistics, cost modeling, and operational readiness. Manage the data pipeline program: Drive the path from pilot capture through annotation, validation, and secure buyer delivery. Own annotation throughput and QA cadence while establishing and tracking data quality, capture yield, and delivery metrics. Manage partners and buyers: Coordinate technical and operational engagement with frontier AI and robotics companies and academic partners such as Georgia Tech. Translate customer requirements into clear program priorities and ensure datasets meet the standards required for validation and delivery. Keep governance and risk on track: Ensure consent, privacy, and data rights requirements are addressed with Legal before and throughout capture activities. Identify and retire program risks while keeping executive sponsors informed of progress, tradeoffs, and decisions. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related technical discipline. 8+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Engineering Management, or complex cross functional delivery roles. Demonstrated experience running computer vision, ML, or data pipeline programs end to end, including data collection, annotation, model training pipelines, or data platform delivery. Proven experience managing both hardware and data or annotation vendors, including RFPs, structured evaluations, scorecards, and strategic partnerships. Comfortable operating in deeply technical CV, ML, and data environments and translating between research, engineering, and operations without losing precision. Strong execution discipline and experience operating in agile, sprint based, or similar environments. Demonstrated judgment in making and driving kill, iterate, or scale decisions based on data and outcomes. High ownership and comfort operating in ambiguous, 0 to 1 environments. Bonus Points: Experience in innovation labs, R&D environments, or advanced automation programs. Familiarity with egocentric or robotics datasets, annotation platforms such as Scale, MLOps, or delivering datasets to external customers. Experience with data governance, privacy, or consent programs, including BIPA, GDPR, or CCPA requirements. Familiarity with warehouse data ecosystems and architectures, including WMS, OMS, WES, and WCS. Exposure to digital twin or simulation initiatives. Domain knowledge in warehouse automation, robotics integration, or fulfillment operations. Experience working with frontier AI companies, robotics companies, academic research institutions, or other emerging technology partners.

title: Compliance Program Manager
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Role Overview The Program Manager, Compliance is a strategic driver of Stord’s operational strength and commercial growth. This role is responsible for scaling enterprise compliance programs across OSHA, EPA, GMP, and adjacent regulatory regimes -- building the infrastructure that enables Stord to operate with confidence, win in the market, and deliver on the compliance commitments that today’s leading brands require from a fulfillment partner. A mature, well-run compliance program is not just a risk management function at Stord; it is a competitive differentiator that unlocks customer revenue, supports network expansion, and protects the business at scale. Reporting to the Director of Health, Safety & Security, this is an enterprise-level, network-wide role that operates at the intersection of compliance, operations, and growth. The Program Manager partners closely with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Finance to ensure compliance capabilities are a strength Stord leads with -- enabling the business to pursue regulated customer segments, scale into new markets, and demonstrate the program maturity that top-tier brands demand. The work product of this role is what the entire organization is built around: scalable written programs, audit frameworks, certification standards, reporting infrastructure, and regulatory intelligence systems that grow stronger as Stord grows. What This Role Owns This role owns the enterprise compliance program architecture -- the standards, written programs, audit frameworks, and governance mechanisms that define what ‘compliant’ looks like at every Stord facility. The work product of this role is what the rest of the organization is held accountable to. Specifically: Enterprise compliance program design, construction, and ownership across OSHA, EPA, GMP, GDP, DOT, and applicable state and local regulatory frameworks -- building programs from the ground up where gaps exist and elevating inconsistent standards to enterprise-grade. Regulatory intelligence: continuously monitoring rulemaking, agency guidance, and enforcement trends; converting regulatory change into updated enterprise programs before gaps become violations. Enterprise audit and inspection framework: designing the internal audit program architecture, defining scope and methodology, and building the tools and cadences that keep the network inspection-ready -- not conducting site audits, but building the system that governs them. Enterprise compliance documentation infrastructure: designing and owning the system of record for all written programs, SOPs, training requirements, certifications, and regulatory correspondence -- the single source of truth for compliance across the network. Customer and industry certification programs: GMP, GDP, CTPAT, TAPA, and other regulated operating standards required by Stord’s customer base. Regulatory agency relationships: serving as the primary compliance point of contact for OSHA, EPA, and other agencies at the program level. Enterprise compliance reporting, data, and dashboards: building the metrics infrastructure that gives the Head of HSS, senior leadership, and the broader business real-time visibility into compliance performance, risk posture, and program health across the network. Enterprise compliance training architecture: defining what training is required, for whom, at what frequency, and in what format -- building the content and governance framework that regional and site teams deliver against. Key Responsibilities OSHA Compliance Program Management Build and own Stord’s enterprise OSHA compliance program -- designing the written program architecture, establishing network-wide standards, and creating the governance mechanisms that ensure consistent compliance across every facility regardless of size, volume, or operational complexity. Maintain and update OSHA-required written programs: Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout, Respiratory Protection, Emergency Action Plans, Powered Industrial Truck programs, and others as applicable. Oversee OSHA recordkeeping standards across the network -- establishing recordkeeping protocols, auditing site-level logs for accuracy, and managing 300A summary posting requirements. Serve as the primary internal resource for OSHA compliance questions, inspection preparation, and citation response -- coordinating with Legal and the Head of HSS on formal agency interactions. Track OSHA rulemaking, enforcement priorities, and National Emphasis Programs relevant to warehouse and fulfillment operations; update programs proactively. Develop and maintain OSHA compliance self-assessment tools for use by Regional Managers and Site Managers. EPA and Environmental Compliance Build and own Stord’s enterprise EPA compliance program -- designing the framework that covers applicable Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, EPCRA, and Tier II reporting obligations across the network and scales as the facility footprint grows. Maintain environmental compliance calendars for all sites, ensuring permit renewals, required inspections, and mandatory reporting deadlines are met without exception. Manage Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans and storm water pollution prevention programs where applicable. Coordinate with Facilities and Operations on environmental requirements triggered by site construction, expansion, or changes in chemical inventory. Serve as the point of escalation for environmental incidents, regulatory notifications, and corrective actions related to EPA-regulated activities. Monitor EPA regulatory changes and enforcement activity relevant to Stord’s operations; assess impact and update compliance programs accordingly. GMP, GDP, and Regulated Operating Standards Build and own Stord’s enterprise GMP and GDP compliance programs -- designing the standards, SOPs, and qualification frameworks that enable Stord to onboard and serve regulated customers at scale across health, wellness, supplement, and pharmaceutical-adjacent accounts. Develop and maintain GMP/GDP-aligned SOPs, documentation standards, and control requirements applicable to regulated fulfillment operations. Lead readiness activities for GMP and GDP customer audits and third-party certifications -- managing pre-audit assessments, coordinating site preparation, and tracking corrective action plans post-audit. Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Operations to assess GMP/GDP requirements for new customer onboarding and ensure facilities are qualified before regulated product is received. Maintain working knowledge of FDA guidance, NSF, and other applicable standards that intersect with Stord’s customer base and product handling requirements. Build and maintain a GMP/GDP compliance library: training materials, audit checklists, SOP templates, and certification documentation for use across the network. Hazmat and Chemical Compliance Build and own Stord’s enterprise Hazardous Materials compliance program -- designing the program for our fulfillment locations, OSHA Hazard Communication, EPA chemical reporting, and state-specific requirements across the full facility network. Maintain the enterprise Hazmat program: classification standards, handling and storage requirements, labeling, SDS management systems, and spill response frameworks. Establish and maintain Hazmat acceptance criteria and screening processes to ensure sites are equipped to handle regulated materials received from customers. Coordinate Hazmat compliance requirements with Transportation, Operations, and Facilities during new site launches, customer onboarding, and facility modifications. Manage DOT compliance requirements for sites involved in the outbound transportation of regulated materials, including proper shipping papers, packaging, and labeling standards. Audit Program and Inspection Readiness Architect the enterprise internal compliance audit program from the ground up -- establishing audit scope, methodology, scoring frameworks, and corrective action workflows that give the organization a consistent, repeatable mechanism for identifying and closing compliance gaps. Conduct or coordinate compliance audits across the network, producing written findings, risk ratings, and actionable corrective action plans for site and regional leaders. Manage the enterprise corrective action tracking system for compliance findings, ensuring closure within defined timelines and verifying effectiveness. Prepare the network for external regulatory inspections and customer audits -- developing site-readiness checklists, conducting pre-audit walkthroughs, and providing on-site support during inspections where required. Maintain an inspection and audit calendar for all sites, tracking regulatory visit history, findings, and corrective action status in a centralized compliance management system. Produce regular compliance performance reporting for the Head of HSS and senior leadership, including audit scores, open findings, and trend analysis. Regulatory Intelligence and Policy Development Establish and operate a systematic regulatory intelligence function -- monitoring federal and state activity across OSHA, EPA, FDA, and DOT to identify proposed rules, final rules, and enforcement trends before they affect Stord’s operations. Translate regulatory changes into policy updates, program revisions, and implementation plans; communicate impacts clearly to the Head of HSS, Regional Managers, and site teams. Own Stord’s compliance policy library: drafting, reviewing, updating, and version-controlling all compliance-related policies and written programs. Serve as subject matter authority for compliance questions from Regional Managers, Site Managers, Operations, Legal, and Customer Success. Contribute compliance expertise to new site launch processes, automation deployments, and major operational changes to ensure regulatory requirements are built in from the start. Reporting, Data & Dashboards Build the enterprise compliance reporting infrastructure from the ground up -- designing the metrics framework, data architecture, and dashboard suite that give the Head of HSS and senior leadership a real-time, accurate view of compliance performance across the network. Define the enterprise compliance KPI set selecting the leading and lagging indicators that most accurately represent program health, regulatory risk, and operational compliance posture -- and ensuring those metrics are collected consistently across all sites. Design and own compliance dashboards that surface OSHA recordable rates, audit scores, corrective action aging, training completion rates, certification status, and regulatory inspection outcomes in a format that is actionable at the executive, regional, and site levels. Build data collection standards and reporting protocols across the network -- establishing how compliance data is captured, validated, and submitted from sites and regions to ensure the enterprise view is reliable and comparable. Develop regular compliance performance reporting cadences for the Head of HSS, Operations leadership, and the Safety and Security Steering Committee -- translating raw data into clear narratives, trend analysis, and risk-flagged summaries that drive decisions. Identify systemic compliance risks and program gaps through data analysis -- surfacing patterns across sites, regions, and regulatory domains that individual site or regional reports would not reveal in isolation. Partner with Operations, Finance, and Technology to integrate compliance data into broader business reporting platforms, ensuring compliance metrics are visible alongside operational and financial performance indicators. Maintain a compliance metrics library and reporting archive that provides the organization with historical performance data, audit trails, and the documentation needed to demonstrate program maturity to regulators, customers, and insurers. Training Governance and Compliance Capability Building Build the enterprise compliance training architecture: designing the training matrix, specifying required topics, applicable employee populations, delivery methods, and completion frequencies across all regulatory domains -- the standard that governs what compliance training looks like at every Stord site. Develop compliance training content and supporting materials for use by site and regional teams -- including written programs, quick reference guides, audit checklists, and SOP templates. Govern training completion compliance across the network through record audits and gap reporting; escalate systemic deficiencies to Regional Managers with a remediation timeline. Build and maintain a compliance resource library accessible to site and regional HSS teams, enabling consistent program delivery without requiring centralized instruction. Required Qualifications Experience 7+ years of experience in regulatory compliance, EHS program management, or a related discipline in a warehouse, fulfillment, manufacturing, or logistics environment. Demonstrated expertise across multiple regulatory domains -- OSHA, EPA, and GMP/GDP -- with hands-on program ownership experience in each. Experience managing compliance programs across a multi-site network, including audit program design and regulatory agency interaction. Track record of translating complex regulatory requirements into practical, scalable operational programs. Technical Knowledge Deep working knowledge of OSHA General Industry standards, recordkeeping requirements, and enforcement processes. Strong familiarity with EPA compliance obligations applicable to warehouse and fulfillment operations, including Tier II, SPCC, and RCRA. Working knowledge of GMP and GDP standards as they apply to regulated fulfillment, distribution, and third-party logistics. Experience with DOT Hazmat regulations (49 CFR) governing the handling, storage, and transportation of regulated materials. Proficiency with compliance management systems, audit platforms, document control tools, and regulatory tracking resources. Credentials (Preferred) CSP, ASP, or equivalent safety certification preferred. CHMM (Certified Hazardous Materials Manager) or equivalent preferred. REHS, REM, or equivalent environmental compliance credential a plus. GMP/GDP auditor certification or equivalent regulated industry compliance credential preferred. OSHA 500 or OSHA 30-hour General Industry required; advanced OSHA coursework preferred. Who You Are A regulatory expert, not a generalist -- you have deep knowledge in at least two of the core compliance domains and the intellectual curiosity to go deep in the others. A program architect -- you build compliance infrastructure that scales across dozens of sites without requiring your personal presence at each one. Your programs are self-sustaining by design. Proactive and ahead of the curve -- you’re tracking rulemaking before it becomes a requirement and updating programs before an inspector identifies the gap. A credible advisor -- Regional Managers and site teams bring you their hardest compliance questions because you give clear, practical answers grounded in the actual regulation. Detail-oriented without losing the thread -- you can manage a 30-site audit calendar and still see the systemic risk patterns that individual findings represent. A strong written communicator -- your policies are readable, your audit reports are actionable, and your regulatory summaries make complex requirements understandable to operators.

title: VP, Fulfillment Planning and Optimization
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Stord is looking for a VP, Fulfillment Planning & Optimization to lead the end to end process of translating customer demand into operational readiness across our fulfillment network. This leader will own Stord’s Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process, turning customer and order forecasts into a clear operating plan for the labor, infrastructure, training, and support required to meet demand. Sitting at the intersection of Customer Experience, Operations, and Operations Support, this leader will program manage the full planning cycle from demand forecasting and operational requirements through resource deployment, performance tracking, and reforecasting, ensuring the network is positioned to deliver against customer commitments efficiently and at scale. What You'll Do: S&OP & Demand Planning: Own Stord's S&OP process across the fulfillment network, creating a single operating view of expected customer demand and the resources required to support it. Partner with CX and customers to understand expected order volume, promotions, launches, seasonality, and other demand drivers. Translate customer forecasts into site, process, shift, and time specific operating requirements. Validate customer forecasts using leading operational indicators, including inbound inventory and historical demand patterns. Identify forecast risk early and develop clear scenarios for expected, upside, and downside demand. Establish a consistent planning cadence across customers, sites, and support functions. Labor Planning : Translate demand into a comprehensive workforce plan across Stord's fulfillment network. Determine labor requirements by site, shift, process path, and planning horizon. Partner with Operations and People teams to ensure hiring, staffing, scheduling, and training plans can support forecasted demand. Track labor demand against actual labor delivery and surface gaps early enough to intervene. Build planning models that account for productivity, attendance, attrition, ramp curves, seasonality, and other operational realities. Continuously improve the accuracy and responsiveness of Stord's labor planning models. Operational Readiness : Translate the operating forecast into clear requirements for the teams responsible for enabling Operations. The forecast should trigger a coordinated readiness plan across: MHE: Equipment, capacity, maintenance, and material handling requirements. EHS & Facilities: Building readiness, safety requirements, space, and facility capacity. Procurement: Supplies, packaging, equipment, and other operating inputs. Industrial Engineering & Continuous Improvement: Capacity, process design, building layout, productivity, and future state operating models. Training: Training capacity, onboarding requirements, cross training, and workforce readiness. Ensure these teams understand what is coming, what Operations will require, when it is needed, and whether delivery is on track. Readiness Program Management : Own the program management layer connecting S&OP to execution. Translate the S&OP plan into specific requirements, owners, milestones, and delivery dates across support functions. Maintain a single view of operational readiness across the network. Track dependencies and escalate risks before they become operational failures. Hold teams accountable for delivering the resources required to support forecasted demand. Create clear executive visibility into where the network is ready, where it is at risk, and where intervention is required. Actuals, Feedback & Continuous Replanning : Close the loop between planning and reality. Once volume begins flowing through the network, this leader owns the process for understanding: What did we forecast? What actually happened? Why was it different? What needs to change now? Monitor actual inbound and outbound volume against forecast. Measure forecast accuracy by customer, site, and planning horizon. Use actual inbound volume and other leading indicators to continuously validate and refine outbound forecasts. Determine whether forecast misses were driven by customer forecast accuracy, internal planning assumptions, labor delivery, productivity, or operational execution. Feed those learnings back into S&OP and continuously adjust labor and resource plans. Build a planning organization that becomes increasingly accurate and responsive as Stord scales. Basic Qualifications: Significant experience owning S&OP, workforce planning, labor planning, capacity planning, or network planning at scale within a complex fulfillment, distribution, retail, manufacturing, or logistics network. Deep understanding of how order forecasts translate into labor hours, productivity requirements, equipment, space, training, and operating capacity. A track record operating in environments where demand shifts quickly and planning decisions have immediate operational and financial consequences. Strong analytical skills paired with an operator's instinct. You are comfortable challenging assumptions across both Operations and planning teams and are focused on whether the plan actually works on the floor. Exceptional cross functional program management skills, with the ability to drive accountability across senior leaders and create structure across functions without directly managing every team involved. Experience building planning processes, systems, and teams that can scale with a rapidly growing business.

title: VP, Inventory Control & Quality Assurance
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. About the Role Stord is looking for a Vice President of Quality to build and lead the quality function across our fulfillment network. This leader will own the systems, standards, and operating mechanisms that ensure inventory is accurate, processes are followed, and every order moves through our network the way it was designed to. The mandate spans the full lifecycle of inventory inside our buildings from inbound receipt and putaway through picking, packing, sorting, and outbound shipment. This is an independent quality function. While our Operations teams are responsible for delivering volume efficiently, the VP of Quality is responsible for ensuring we never achieve speed, growth, or cost improvements by compromising inventory integrity or execution quality. This leader should be an inventory and fulfillment quality expert at heart — someone who understands how inventory moves through a complex fulfillment operation, knows where process breakdowns create downstream failures, and is relentless about identifying and eliminating root causes. What You'll Own Inventory Health & Accuracy Own inventory health and accuracy across Stord's fulfillment network. Establish the standards, controls, and operating mechanisms required to maintain book-to-floor and floor-to-book inventory integrity. Own cycle counting, inventory reconciliation, adjustment governance, and inventory variance reduction. Build mechanisms to identify inventory defects early and systematically eliminate their root causes. Establish network-level metrics and reporting that make inventory health visible and actionable. Fulfillment Process Quality Own process adherence across inbound, receiving, putaway, picking, packing, sorting, and outbound operations. Define the critical quality controls for each process path and ensure sites consistently execute against them. Build audit mechanisms that identify process drift before it becomes a customer or inventory issue. Partner with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Data to eliminate systemic sources of defects. Develop a clear view of transaction volume, exception rates, and defect rates by process path to identify where quality is breaking down. Lot Control & Regulatory Compliance Own lot, expiration-date, and inventory-attribute accuracy across applicable customers and facilities. Establish controls for FIFO, FEFO, lot traceability, recalls, quarantine, and other regulated inventory requirements. Ensure Stord's operating processes meet applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual quality requirements. Build a quality organization capable of supporting increasingly complex and regulated categories as Stord grows. Continuous Improvement Build a rigorous root-cause and corrective-action discipline across the fulfillment network. Turn recurring defects into permanent process, system, or training improvements rather than repeatedly solving individual incidents. Identify network-wide trends and deploy standardized improvements across sites. Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure recurring operational defects inform the technology roadmap. Create a culture where defects are surfaced quickly, investigated objectively, and permanently resolved. Quality Organization Build and lead Stord's network Quality and Inventory Control organization. Establish clear ownership and accountability between Quality and Operations. Develop site and regional quality leaders capable of independently auditing operational performance. Serve as the executive escalation point when inventory integrity, regulatory compliance, or fulfillment quality is at risk. Maintain an independent point of view and be willing to stop, challenge, or redesign processes when quality standards are not being met. What We're Looking For We are looking for someone who has spent their career inside large, complex fulfillment or distribution operations and understands inventory at a level most operators do not. The ideal candidate: Has 12+ years of experience across fulfillment quality, inventory control, operational excellence, distribution, or supply chain operations, including significant leadership experience. Has led quality or inventory control across a multi-site fulfillment or distribution network . Comes from a scaled 3PL, retailer, e-commerce fulfillment network, food distribution company, or similarly complex physical operation. Is deeply fluent in inventory control, WMS-driven processes, cycle counting, reconciliation, lot control, and inventory accuracy . Understands the mechanics of inbound, putaway, pick, pack, sort, and outbound processes — and how defects in one process create downstream failures elsewhere. Has built quality systems based on data, audits, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and measurable defect reduction. Is comfortable challenging Operations leadership when execution does not meet the required standard. Has operated in environments where quality and compliance cannot be traded for throughput or cost . Ideally brings experience from food, grocery, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another environment with rigorous lot, expiration, traceability, or regulatory requirements. Can operate strategically at the executive level while still being willing to go onto the warehouse floor, trace an inventory discrepancy through a WMS, and understand exactly where a process failed.

Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. Field Service Engineer - Process Diagnostics & Control (PDC) Be the Eyes of the Fab. Power the Future of Technology. Our equipment is used to produce virtually every advanced chip in the world, and we're looking for talented engineers to help keep those systems performing at their best. These systems are often referred to as the "eyes of the fab" because they monitor, measure, and help control critical manufacturing processes that determine wafer quality and production success. title: Retail Insights Manager (Sales Engineer)
jd_text: Description: SPS Commerce is a leading provider of cloud-based supply chain management solutions, serving a global network of retail trading partners. We foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment where innovation and continuous improvement are highly valued. Join SPS Commerce and be part of a dynamic team that's transforming the global retail supply chain! Position Summary: As a Retail Insights Manager (Sales Engineer), you’ll be the customer-facing subject matter expert on retail deductions, chargebacks, and compliance — the person suppliers trust in the room. Partnering side by side with Account Executives and Account Managers, you’ll co-pilot deals from first demo through close, translating deep retailer knowledge into clear, compelling business cases that help suppliers protect revenue and recover deductions. This is a highly external, sales-facing role: you’ll spend the majority of your time on demos, discovery, and data presentations, acting as the technical account leader who speaks to the platform, interprets audit findings, and builds the ROI story. You came up on the supplier side managing deductions and compliance — now you’ll bring that expertise to the table for suppliers who were once in your shoes. If you thrive on meeting new people, thinking on your feet, and turning complex retail data into a story that closes business, this role puts you at the heart of how SPS Revenue Recovery drives growth for suppliers. What You'll Do: Sales-cycle co-pilot: Partner with Account Executives and Account Managers as the technical expert across the full deal cycle — first call, discovery, demo, data presentation, and contract negotiation — owning the deductions and retailer expertise the salesperson can’t carry alone. Product demos & presentations: Present and demo the SPS Revenue Recovery platform to prospects ranging from Fortune 100 suppliers to small businesses, showing deep retailer knowledge and answering questions with command and credibility. Data presentation & business case: Interpret audit and deduction analysis, pull out the insights that matter, and build the ROI and value story — then deliver it clearly to stakeholders up to and including CFO-level decision-makers . Deal strategy: Prep with reps on huddles and prep calls, strategize on messaging and outreach voice, and proactively push deals forward — weighing in on what’s best for the deal at any given moment. Retailer subject matter expertise: Serve as the go-to SME on deduction codes, compliance programs, and root-cause analysis across multiple retailers — Walmart, Amazon, Target and beyond (CVS, Walgreens, Kohl’s, Home Depot, Lowe’s, UNFI, and others we support). Cross-functional partnership – Marketing , Product Customer Success : Work close ly with Marketing — translating the voice of the supplier, advising on feature priorities, escalating data questions, and representing the retailer domain internally and externally . Hosting webinars and lead in person -events related to Revenue Recovery . Product Development : Work closely with the Revenue Recovery Product Managers to advise on feature prioritization . Sitting in on customer research calls to “ translate” user feedback . Providing insights and feedback on the product b ased on experience . Advising on potential feature opportunities and technological advancements in the platform as an SME. Thought leadership & enablement: Contribute to article creation, host webinars, support events, and help build out platform functionality as an SME — elevating the team’s external voice in the revenue recovery space. Confidentiality & trust: Handle sensitive client and revenue data with discretion and integrity while influencing strategic decisions across teams. Perform other duties as assigned. What You'll Bring: Proven Experience: Bachelor’s degree plus 2+ years of relevant experience (or equivalent education and work experience), ideally on the supplier side managing deductions, chargebacks, and retailer compliance — within a B2B SaaS, CPG, retail, or supply chain environment. Multi-Retailer Knowledge (must-have): Deep, hands-on expertise across at least two of the big three — Walmart, Target, and Amazon — with Amazon strongly preferred. Amazon-only is not sufficient; this role requires breadth across multiple retailers, as you’ll be expected to be the expert on any retailer a supplier brings to the table. Revenue Recovery Expertise: Expert-level understanding of the retailer deductions space — deduction codes, compliance programs, root-cause efforts, and how it all impacts suppliers’ day-to-day operations, including EDI and how supplier operations work. External & Sales-Facing Command: Comfortable and confident presenting to new people you’ve never met — from analysts to CFOs — and speaking to ROI on high-value contracts. Able to step into and out of complex supply chain sales cycles with high impact and credibility. Clear, Confident Communicator: Clear, concise, and confident verbal, non-verbal, and written communication — including altering vocal tone and inflection, active listening, and writing relevant, engaging content. No wallflowers: you jump in when the moment strikes. Tech-Savvy: Proficient in Microsoft Excel and Office Suite (advanced Excel — pivot tables, formulas — a plus ). Multitasking Under Pressure: Able to juggle multiple demos, presentations, and requests in a single day in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment where the calendar is rarely your own — prioritizing quickly and setting boundaries with reps. Self-Driven & Collaborative: Proactive, high-ownership, and able to work autonomously with minimal supervision, while collaborating closely and communicating well over Slack and Zoom with a distributed team. Preferred Qualifications: Knowledge of additional retailers we support (CVS, Walgreens, Kohl’s, Home Depot, Lowe’s, UNFI, and others). Power BI and/or Tableau experience. CRM tools (Salesforce) experience. Familiarity with AI tools (e.g., Claude) to support analysis, decks, and process efficiency. Mid-level ERP knowledge (most integrations involve pre-built adapters). Prior CPG, retail, supply chain, or SPS Commerce / SupplyPike experience. Where You'll Work: This role is either hybrid out of one of our offices in Minneapolis, MN, Rogers, AR or open to remote. title: Corporate Counsel
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. About the role: Stord is seeking a Corporate Counsel to support Stord’s commercial contracting growth as the company scales its sales pipeline by over 50%. This role will primarily focus on sales, partnerships, and commercial relationships, including reviewing, advising, and negotiating customer agreements, partner agreements, vendor contracts, amendments, and NDAs. This role will leverage AI tools alongside strong legal judgment to drive efficiency. Critical skills for this role include agility, comfort operating in ambiguity, attention to detail, and the ability to be resourceful while managing multiple initiatives. This role will work within Stord Legal and directly with the business team to understand objectives and develop business-centric strategies that mitigate risk while enabling the business to move quickly. This role will assist in providing day-to-day advice to the business team on a range of matters, including contract interpretation, strategic advice, and general inquiries. Stord is looking for a self-starter with a bias for action who thrives in a high-growth environment. What You'll Do: Partner with the Sales and Partnerships teams to review, negotiate, and execute commercial contracts, including customer agreements, reseller and referral agreements, strategic partnership agreements, and vendor contracts, while collaborating cross-functionally with the Operations, Finance, and Product teams. Own and continuously refine Stord's contract playbooks and negotiation guardrails, including fallback positions, escalation thresholds, and approval authority, to drive consistency and speed across the sales pipeline. Partner with Sales Operations and other cross-functional stakeholders to help build out Stord's contract management infrastructure as it scales, including template libraries, workflow tools, and process documentation. Support and guide the sales team and various business teams on deal structure, contract negotiations, and risk assessment, balancing legal risk with business objectives. Serve as a legal point of contact for the Sales and Partnerships teams, enabling deal velocity while managing risk. Identify opportunities to improve the contract management process to drive operational efficiencies and process standardization throughout Stord. Address internal inquiries regarding contractual questions, obligations, and compliance. Stay up to date on relevant industry, commercial, intellectual property, privacy and compliance issues. Basic Qualifications: 3+ years of experience with commercial transaction experience in the ecommerce or logistics space Experience negotiating, drafting, and solving issues for various types of commercial contracts, including those relating to warehousing and logistics, with demonstrated business judgment and ability to provide practical, risk-balanced advice. Proven ability to ramp quickly and take ownership of a contract portfolio in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with legal technology, including AI-assisted contract review tools and CLM platforms (Ironclad experience a plus) J.D. from an accredited law school and membership in at least one state bar required. Preferred Qualifications Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal, with a collaborative approach Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently to prioritize work, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines. Comfort building and refining process and structure where none fully exists yet, rather than relying solely on an established system. Logistics experience; in-house experience. Experience with warehouse liens, bailment law, or UCC Article 7 (warehouse receipts and documents of title). Familiarity with FMCSA broker regulations, transportation law, or logistics compliance requirements. Experience with data privacy agreements, technology contracts, or software licensing arrangements.

Includes but not limited to moving furniture or fixtures, changing lights, light carpentry, painting, light plumbing, changing of light bulbs, repair of minor electrical devices Battery Maintenance duties will include battery charger repairs, battery changes for MHE, repair of plugs and tips of batteries and chargers, watering and washing batteries, acid spill clean up, battery rack cleaning, battery area sweeping and cleaning, setting equalizing charge on batteries Participate in departmental on-call program, as designated Responsible for logging time and materials into the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) on a daily basis in the form of work orders, P.M.s, etc. Responsible for housekeeping, clean up of all maintenance areas/work areas on a daily basis. Maintain all tools and equipment in clean, safe, working order Adhere to all safety requirements and wear the proper Personal Protective Equipment required by the job Respond to emergency situations to ensure employee and facility safety Champion overall safety in the department Comply with OSHA, and other local, state and federal regulations Adhere to Organization and the Facilities Department policies and procedures including appropriate attire, grooming, and attendance Interact effectively, build relationships, and demonstrate a high level of cooperation QUALIFICATIONS Education High School diploma or general education degree (GED); Tech school or equivalent is preferred (2 years) Experience Two years in an MHE maintenance position preferred (No experience required) Professional Skills Ability to read, analyze and interpret technical procedures, or governmental regulations Ability to add, subtracts, multiply, and divides into all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals Certificates, Licenses, and Registrations Must possess a valid state Driver's License and provide proof of liability coverage meeting Company standards. Complete a Sysco approved the defensive driving program Obtain a Powered Industrial Equipment Certification from Sysco within 3 months MHE 8 hour maintenance tech certificate from MHE manufacturer (IE: Crown, Raymond, Hyster, etc.) preferred Physical Demands While performing the duties of this job, the associate is regularly required to talk or hear. The associate is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms and climb or balance. The associate is occasionally required to stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The associate must occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. Working Conditions While performing the duties of this job, the associate is occasionally exposed to wet, hot, extreme cold and/or humid conditions; and moving mechanical parts and may be required to work in confined spaces. The associate works non-traditional business hours including evenings, nights, weekends, holidays and on-call. The associate may occasionally be required to travel to other Operating Companies or the corporate office as business needs dictate (i.e. training, business continuation, etc.). The associate is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places and confined spaces. The associate is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Actively observes and provides feedback, holding team members accountable while recognizing great guest experience moments.
