title: VP of Internal Systems & IT
jd_text: Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. The Opportunity Stord is made up of two complicated businesses under one roof. We build and run software at scale, and we operate an international, multi-site fulfillment and parcel network. Our enterprise systems have to carry both, which makes them as complex as anything in the product. These systems were built for a smaller company than the one we are now. This role is responsible for elevating this system. There are two direct domains. Business Operations owns the enterprise systems Stord runs on, the processes sitting on top of them, and the quality of the business data inside them. IT owns identity, devices, access, and end-user experience for a company adding headcount monthly, as well as the physical network and device infrastructure inside every fulfillment and parcel site we run. In partnership with Procurement you own Stord's SaaS estate company-wide. Engineering's tooling is also in that scope: R&D chooses it, you administer it. You report to the SVP of Product & Engineering, sit alongside the Head of Engineering, the VP of Data, and the VP of Security as peers, and work daily with leadership across Finance, Revenue, People, Legal, and Operations. This is not a blank slate, nor should you want one. What currently exists is here because it has to be: we are already a scaled operation, billions in GMV across hundreds of brands, and the systems carrying that are load-bearing. You inherit a capable team and a stack that works. What’s missing is architecture, clear ownership, and someone with a point of view on both. The test is what comes next. Taking an operation already at this scale and building it for the future, without slowing anything down. Plenty of leaders can add control to a fast company. We are hiring the one who can add control while maintaining necessary speed. How We Think About This Role IT is a product, not a ticket queue. We measure this function by whether a Stord employee can do their job on day one and every day after, not by SLA attainment on tickets that should never have existed. A well-run IT function makes most of its own tickets disappear. Sophisticated application of AI Before we add a person, buy a tool, or build an integration, the first question is whether an agent can do the work. You own making AI the normal way your own functions operate, and being the person who can tell a genuine agentic workflow from a thin wrapper around an API call if a vendor is selling you one. One system of record per domain. Customers, vendors, products, locations, employees. If a team is keeping a shadow spreadsheet, that is a defect in your architecture. Tool sprawl is a tax, and you are the person who collects it. Every SaaS application at Stord gets a named owner, a renewal date, a utilisation number, and a security posture. R&D will continue to decide the tools they need. You own everything after that decision, from the contract and the licence count to who has access and what happens at renewal. Bring the same rigor to a $200k observability contract as we bring to a $200k ERP module, and give Procurement a technical counterpart who knows what the contract is actually for. Build, buy, or cut, decided deliberately. We will support a build when the process is ours and nothing off the shelf fits it. We will not back a build that exists because a configuration was hard. We should cut as often as we build or buy. Process before automation. Automating a broken process buys you a faster broken process. We would rather you delete a step than script it. If you read that and disagreed with any of these, tell us when we talk. That is a better conversation than agreement. What You'll Own Enterprise systems and architecture The strategy, architecture, and roadmap for Stord's business technology stack across CRM, ERP, HRIS, CLM, Procurement, and Customer Success platforms Integration and data-flow decisions between those systems, and the ownership model that keeps them from drifting apart again A documented architecture with named owners, prioritised by business impact and not by who asked loudest Business process and master data Governance for the domains that matter most: customers, vendors, products, locations, employees. Defined once and sourced once The standards and quality frameworks that make business data something the company can build on, in close partnership with the VP of Data whose platform consumes it The source-system side of metric consistency. Data sets the canonical definition; you make sure the CRM, ERP, and HRIS capture it that way, so three teams asking the same question get the same number Finding the processes creating the most drag across Finance, People, Legal, Support, and Operations, and rebuilding them instead of automating the old shape IT, corporate and on site IT strategy and day-to-day operations: identity and access management, device lifecycle, end-user support, and the corporate network The physical network and device estate across our fulfillment and parcel sites: handheld scanners, label and packing-station printers, floor wifi coverage, switching and routing, ISP circuits and failover. If the network drops in a fulfillment center, orders stop shipping, and that outage is your responsibility Standing IT up for a new site or a new country on the timeline Operations commits to The endpoint, identity, and access controls themselves, operated by your team to the standards the VP of Security sets. You run them, Security governs them, and the two of you agree what good means before an auditor does Onboarding and offboarding that are fast, complete, and boring, at the pace of a company adding headcount monthly and entering new countries An IT function that gets ahead of problems, with the operating rhythm and metrics to show it SaaS and vendor portfolio Company-wide ownership of the SaaS estate, run jointly with Procurement. Engineering tooling is in scope for administration, contracts, licensing, access, and renewals; R&D keeps the selection call Renewal calendar, utilization data, consolidation plan, and a recommendation at every renewal instead of an auto-renew Third-party and sub-processor diligence across the estate. Every tool touching employee or customer data is reviewed before it is bought and re-checked at renewal, to the standard Security and Legal set Security and compliance review for new tooling, including AI tools adopted anywhere in the company, and IT administration for AI platforms company-wide: procurement, provisioning, access, and licence management Privacy and compliance Privacy operations sit with IT today, because IT is where the systems are. You inherit GDPR, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework certification, records of processing, DSARs, retention schedules, and vendor data processing agreements on day one As the VP of Security builds out GRC, program ownership moves there alongside SOC 2 and ISO 27001. Running it well in the meantime and handing it over cleanly is part of this job. We would rather tell you that now than after you join What stays with you permanently is enforcement: data residency, retention, and deletion in the business systems. Where an employee or customer record lives, how long it stays, and how it is removed when it should be. Access reviews, segregation of duties, and change control across the financial and HR systems, built to survive an audit and, in time, SOX IT general controls Evidence on demand. When an auditor, an enterprise customer's security review, or a regulator asks how a control works, the answer comes out of your systems rather than a spreadsheet someone assembled that week AI adoption inside your own functions Make IT and BizOps the proof case for how Stord works with AI, actually measured against the projected value Partner with the functions you serve so their operating processes get AI-native treatment, and with R&D leadership where an internal need warrants purpose-built software instead of configuration M&A systems integration Business systems integration when Stord acquires: get the acquired company onto Stord's stack and standards on a predictable timeline, not left running as a permanent side system Partner with Corporate Development on technical and operational due diligence for future targets Team Lead and grow a team across IT and Enterprise Systems, including an established Director of IT Build the rigor and follow-through that makes other functions want you in the room Earn trust well outside your reporting line. This role only works if people change how they work because you asked them to How This Role Works With Its Peers These seats are distinct on purpose, and the seams between them matter more than the boxes. VP of Security. Security owns the strategy, the security program, the security team, detection and response, and the control standards. You own the operation of the controls that live inside IT: identity, endpoints, device posture, access lifecycle. Security says what good looks like; you make it true across every laptop and every account, and you bring the evidence to audits. Security also builds the GRC function that will take privacy program ownership from you, so an early piece of this partnership is getting that handover right. This partnership fails when it turns into a negotiation at audit time. It works when the two of you agree on the standard before the tooling is bought. VP of Data. Data owns the data platform, analytics, BI, decision science, and AI-first access to Stord's data. You own the business systems that are among the most important sources feeding it, and the governance of the master data inside them. Data owns what a metric means; you own whether the systems capture it that way. If a number is wrong, Data will usually find it and you will usually be the one who can fix it at source. You are jointly accountable for the business trusting that number. Procurement and Finance. Procurement owns the commercial process, supplier relationships, and negotiation. You own the technical evaluation, the architecture fit, the security posture, and the honest utilisation picture that tells Procurement what leverage they have. Legal. Legal owns the legal calls: lawful basis, controller and processor posture, contract and DPA language, and what we say to a regulator. You own the operational program today and the systems enforcement permanently. Expect to be the person who tells Legal what the systems can and cannot do, rather than waiting to be told. Head of Engineering. Engineering owns customer-facing software, the production estate, and our applied AI work, and chooses the tooling its teams build with. You are their internal counterpart, not their competitor. You administer the tooling they choose, you hold them to the same portfolio discipline as every other function, and when an internal problem needs software built instead of bought, you bring the case and they help you resource it. What Success Looks Like In your first year: Stord has a documented enterprise systems architecture with named owners and a prioritized roadmap the executive team has actually agreed to Business leaders trust the numbers coming out of our systems, and the shadow spreadsheets are measurably fewer The SaaS estate is fully inventoried with owners, renewals, and utilization visible, and you have rationalised a meaningful portion of it with the savings attached IT gets ahead of problems instead of reacting to them. Onboarding and offboarding are fast and complete, and employees say so Identity, access, and endpoint controls meet the standard the VP of Security has set, and hold up under audit without a scramble Privacy operations are in better shape than you found them, and the program has either transitioned cleanly to GRC or has a dated plan to At least two functions outside R&D are running a materially better process than a year earlier, with AI doing work a person used to do and numbers to show it If we closed an acquisition this year, its business systems are on Stord's stack rather than bolted on the side You have a leadership team you trust and a function known for getting things done What We're Looking For Experience 10+ years leading enterprise systems, business technology, corporate IT, or a combined function, with direct budget and hiring ownership Has owned a complex multi-system business technology ecosystem end to end: CRM, ERP, and HRIS at minimum, through a migration or consolidation and not steady-state administration Has run corporate IT as a proactive function at a company growing fast, ideally through international expansion Has owned IT for distributed physical sites and not only offices and remote workers: floor networking, handheld devices, connectivity, and the operational stakes that come with them Has owned a SaaS portfolio company-wide and worked properly alongside Procurement, with consolidation and savings you can point to Has run or materially supported a privacy or compliance programme in practice: GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent. You do not need to be a privacy lawyer, but you need to have been accountable for evidence that held up Has integrated business systems following an acquisition and can describe what got merged into one operating model, not what was left running in parallel Background in technology or tech-enabled businesses. Logistics or operations experience is a plus, not a requirement AI An AI adoption story from inside an operating function, measured after the fact. We will ask what changed, who stopped doing what, and how you knew Working knowledge of the current AI and agentic tooling landscape, sharp enough to make build-versus-buy calls yourself instead of relying on a vendor's deck A view on where AI changes a back-office process and where it is theater. We would rather hear one honest "that didn't work" than five polished case studies Technical depth Deep fluency in enterprise application architecture, integration patterns, and master data management Solid grounding in IT operations, identity management, and endpoint and access controls. You do not have to do the work yourself, but you need to know when it is being done well Enough technical credibility to read an integration design, push back on an approach, and hold your own with senior engineers and with the VP of Data Leadership Earns trust across functions. Finance, Engineering, Revenue, People, and Operations all want you involved Change management that sticks: you can get a Sales or Support team to adopt a new way of working, not just tolerate a mandate Clear communicator who can take a systems problem to an executive team as a business decision Comfortable operating in the seams between peer VPs without needing the org chart to resolve every question for you Bonus points You have taken a company through IPO readiness or operated inside a public company, including SOX IT general controls. We don’t know our future but we want the rigor of a public company You have supported international expansion: multi-entity ERP, multi-country HRIS and payroll, data residency You have supported a business with a physical operation, where a systems failure means something does not ship You have been on the receiving end of an acquisition as well as the acquiring side This Role Is Not For Everyone The scope is deliberately bounded. You will not own our AI engineers, our forward-deployed engineering team, or our security program. Those are separate seats. If your ambition is to build a product engineering organization, this is not that role and we would be wasting each other's time. What you get instead is an unambiguous mandate over the systems the whole company depends on, at a business doubling in size, acquiring, and expanding internationally with both a physical and virtual team. Nobody here needs convincing that this function matters, which is an argument most people in this job spend their first year losing somewhere else. If you have worked somewhere that talked about systems excellence but never funded it, this is your opportunity to realize that dream.

title: Manager of Health, Safety, & Loss Prevention
jd_text: ABOUT STORD Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like True Classic, Native, Seed Health, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Role Overview The Site Manager, Health, Safety & Security is the primary HSS presence on the floor. This role is responsible for executing Stord's safety and security program at the site level -- embedded in daily operations, visible to employees and operators, and directly accountable for building a safe and secure working environment across an assigned set of facilities. Reporting to a Regional Manager of Health, Safety & Security, the Site Manager owns the day-to-day delivery of the HSS program: conducting safety observations, managing incident response, driving corrective actions to closure, and partnering closely with site General Managers and operations leaders to embed safety into every shift. Across their sites, they are the face of safety -- the person employees’ approach, leaders lean on for guidance, and the Regional Manager depends on for ground-level execution. This is not a desk role. It demands consistent physical presence, operational credibility, and the ability to influence behavior and culture. What This Role Owns The Site Manager is the execution layer of Stord's HSS program. They translate regional and enterprise standards into what happens on the floor, every shift, at every site they cover. This role owns: Day-to-day safety and security program delivery at assigned sites, including full compliance with enterprise standards and applicable regulations. Incident response and investigation -- first on scene, responsible for documentation, root cause analysis, and driving corrective action closure. Proactive identification and mitigation of site-level risks -- physical, behavioral, and systemic -- that could lead to injury, financial loss, or operational disruption. Physical security ownership: setting and enforcing access control, CCTV, perimeter, and visitor management standards across assigned sites -- ensuring controls are operational, documented, and audit-ready. Loss prevention and integrity: inventory shrink, behavioral observation, fraud and integrity investigations, and escalation of theft or policy violations. Employee-facing safety culture: visible floor presence, coaching, near-miss reporting, and reinforcing speak-up behaviors every shift. Site audit readiness -- facilities are always inspection-ready for both internal reviews and regulatory visits. Regulatory compliance at the site level: OSHA adherence, state and local requirements, Hazmat standards, and readiness for customer-required certifications. Key Responsibilities Daily Site Operations and Floor Presence Conduct regular safety walks, behavioral observations, and hazard identification sweeps across all assigned facilities. Partner with shift supervisors, operations managers, and General Managers to address safety concerns in real time. Monitor safety conditions during peak periods, shift transitions, and high-traffic operational windows. Serve as the on-site point of contact for all safety, security, and loss prevention matters during operating hours. Deliver immediate coaching on unsafe behaviors and conditions; document and track corrective actions to verified closure. Maintain a visible, consistent presence that makes safety feel operational -- not bureaucratic. Incident Management and Investigation Lead the immediate response to all site-level incidents, including injuries, near-misses, security events, and property damage. Conduct thorough investigations using root cause analysis methodology and document findings in Stord's safety management system. Coordinate with the Regional Manager, HR, and Legal as appropriate for significant incidents or sensitive investigations. Ensure all OSHA recordkeeping, regulatory notifications, and mandatory reporting are completed accurately and on time. Drive corrective and preventive actions to verified closure; follow up with site operations leaders to confirm implementation. Lead post-incident reviews with site leadership and translate findings into durable operational improvements. Safety Program Execution Execute all enterprise and regional safety programs, standards, and procedures at assigned sites consistently and completely. Ensure all required safety training programs -- including PIT certification, LOTO, ergonomics, PPE, and emergency response -- are in place, current, and completed by required populations; govern through audit and record. Prepare and maintain site safety documentation: OSHA 300 logs, inspection records, training logs, and corrective action trackers. Participate in site leadership meetings to represent HSS priorities and conduct pre-shift safety briefings in coordination with operations supervisors. Ensure pre-shift safety briefings are conducted consistently by operations supervisors and that site leadership meetings include a standing HSS agenda item -- hold leaders accountable for delivery. Physical Security and Loss Prevention Monitor and enforce physical security controls at assigned sites, including access control systems, visitor protocols, and CCTV coverage. Conduct inventory integrity checks and partner with operations to investigate and resolve shrink, damage, or variance trends. Conduct inventory integrity checks and partner with operations to investigate and resolve shrink, damage, or variance trends. Lead integrity and fraud investigations at the site level -- including internal theft, employee misconduct, vendor fraud, and inventory manipulation -- managing the full investigation lifecycle from detection through resolution and corrective action. Gather and preserve evidence, maintain chain of custody, and produce investigation documentation that meets internal and legal standards -- coordinating with HR, Legal, and the Regional Manager throughout. Serve as the primary site-level liaison with law enforcement -- managing police responses, coordinating active investigations, and building ongoing relationships with local agencies to support loss prevention and security outcomes. Identify behavioral and operational indicators of theft, fraud, or policy violations; escalate findings to the Regional Manager and HR with documented evidence and a recommended course of action. Perform periodic security assessments and surface vulnerabilities in perimeter, access, or procedural controls to the Regional Manager. Ensure security awareness is embedded in employee onboarding and reinforced through daily operational routines. Regulatory Compliance Maintain full compliance with applicable OSHA standards, state and local regulations, and Stord internal policies at assigned sites -- with no exceptions or deferred action items. Serve as the site-level point of contact for regulatory inspections, agency visits, and compliance inquiries -- coordinating responses with the Regional Manager and Legal as needed. Manage all OSHA recordkeeping obligations accurately and on time, including OSHA 300/300A logs, required postings, and mandatory incident notifications. Govern site-level Hazmat compliance through audits and documentation reviews: verify proper classification, storage, labeling, SDS management, spill response readiness, and regulatory incident documentation in accordance with DOT, OSHA, and EPA requirements. Own site readiness for customer-required certifications and audits including GMP, GDP, CTPAT, and TAPA where applicable -- maintaining current documentation, training records, and control evidence at all times. Conduct internal compliance self-audits on a defined cadence, identifying gaps before external inspections or customer audits surface them. Track and close all compliance-related corrective actions within required timelines, escalating unresolved gaps to the Regional Manager with a clear remediation plan. Monitor regulatory updates affecting site operations and coordinate with the Regional Manager to implement any required changes to procedures, training, or controls. Employee Engagement and Safety Culture Build trusted, visible relationships with employees at all levels -- approachable, consistent, and credible. Champion near-miss and hazard reporting programs; coach employees on why reporting matters and how to do it. Recognize and reinforce safe behaviors; address at-risk behaviors through coaching-first approaches before escalating. Support site safety committee development and maintain an active network of floor-level safety champions. Model and reinforce a no-retaliation culture by demonstrating that safety concerns are taken seriously and resolved. Reporting and Communication Provide regular site-level performance updates to the Regional Manager, including TRIR, near-miss rates, corrective action status, and security incidents. Maintain site-level safety dashboards and ensure data is current, accurate, and actionable. Escalate emerging trends, unresolved compliance gaps, or systemic risks to the Regional Manager with supporting data and a recommended path forward. Communicate HSS expectations clearly to site General Managers and operations leaders, ensuring priorities are understood and supported within site operating plans. Required Qualifications Experience 4+ years of experience in health and safety, loss prevention, or operations compliance in a warehouse, fulfillment, or manufacturing environment. Experience carrying safety and security accountability across more than one facility simultaneously preferred. Proven track record of hands-on incident response, structured investigation, and corrective action management. Experience delivering frontline safety training and measurably influencing employee behavior and site culture. Technical Knowledge Solid working knowledge of OSHA standards and recordkeeping requirements, including OSHA 300/300A log management. Familiarity with physical security systems, access control, and foundational loss prevention practices. Hands-on experience with PIT/MHE safety programs, LOTO, PPE standards, and ergonomics in high-volume fulfillment settings. Hazmat awareness and handling knowledge applicable to warehouse and fulfillment operations. Proficiency with safety management systems, incident tracking tools, and operational reporting platforms. Credentials (Preferred) OSHA 30-hour General Industry certification required; OSHA 500 or equivalent preferred. ASP or active pursuit of a safety credential preferred. First Aid, CPR, and AED certified, or willing to obtain upon hire. Loss Prevention Qualified (LPQ) or Loss Prevention Certified (LPC) preferred. Wicklander-Zulawski (WZ) interview and interrogation certification preferred. Essentials of Retail Asset Protection Certificate preferred. Who You Are Operationally credible -- you've worked in fast-moving, high-volume environments and employees trust your judgment because you understand the work. Visible and present -- you're on the floor, not behind a desk, and people know who you are and what you stand for. A clear communicator -- you can walk a seasonal employee through a safety procedure and brief a General Manager on site risk with equal clarity. Detail-oriented with follow-through -- you don't just flag problems, you own them until they're solved. Calm under pressure -- incidents happen; you respond with focus and steadiness and help your site do the same. Growth-oriented -- this role is a development path toward regional responsibility, and you're building the skills, credibility, and results to get there.

jd_text: ABOUT STORD Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission. By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale. With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order. Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like True Classic, Native, Seed Health, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures. Position Description - Night Shift (WED-SAT) Wed hours: 5 pm - 3:30 am / Thu-Sat hours: 7 pm - 5:30 am The Operations Lead will be responsible for overseeing the handling of customer products, including the loading, unloading, picking, and packing of product. This leadership role will be responsible for assigning work and work functions to all warehouse associates as necessary to meet the needs of the customer. Following company and site-specific safety policies, and encouraging other associates to do the same, is of great importance to this position. What You’ll Do Assign tasks to warehouse personnel through written and/or oral instruction, including: unloading, outbound staging and loading, verifying and labeling of freight, picking and packing. Supervise tasks performed by warehouse personnel. Complete reports and records in a timely manner. Troubleshoot machine and equipment malfunctions and report them to maintenance personnel. Advise associates on care and preservation of product, use of equipment in handling, storing, maintaining, shipping stock, and related problems. Ensure high-quality customer service through assisting associates in warehouse functions when help is needed. Take action and speak to associates when proper safety, quality, and productivity procedures are not being followed. Work cooperatively and productively with other warehouse associates and leadership Adhere to company or site-specific safety policy and guidelines to ensure safe working conditions for self and others. Additional duties may be assigned by the supervisor. What You'll Need Must be eighteen (18) years of age or older. High school diploma or equivalent. Minimum of two (2) years’ experience working in a warehouse environment. Must be able to perform any physically exerting duties in a warehouse environment, which may be non-air conditioned or heated, meaning the indoor temperature fluctuates with the seasons. Must be able to pass pre-employment drug screening and background check. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite. Previous leadership experience. Experience working with a warehouse management system (WMS).

Position Overview The People Administrator plays a critical role in managing and monitoring both full-time employee (FTE) and contingent hourly labor headcount across sites within the Region. This role ensures accurate attendance tracking, proactive workforce planning, and effective labor delivery management in partnership with on-site Operations Leaders, HR, and external staffing partners. The ideal candidate brings a strong HR & Staffing foundation with working knowledge of co-employment laws, particularly those applicable within the region, to manage hourly labor effectively while driving compliance and operational excellence. Key Responsibilities Regional Workforce Planning & Delivery Monitor FTE and contingent labor headcount across Region to align daily/weekly staffing with volume and SLA targets. Manage FTE and contingent labor delivery tracking across multiple regional sites; rebalance labor based on forecast, cancellations, or volume shifts. Track New Hire Orientations (NHOs) by site; ensure delivery rates and show-up percentages meet regional goals and are reflected in forecasts. Vendor & Partner Management Partner with staffing vendors and co-employment partners to review performance, fill-rate, quality, and compliance; develop corrective and proactive action plans. Assess vendor capacity and scalability specific to regional needs (seasonality, client mix, shift profiles). Data, Systems & Reporting Maintain and continuously improve regional demand tracking tools/dashboards to support the Regional Leadership Team (RLT) decision-making. Analyze workforce trends (Attrition, Overtime/Mandatory overtime, Voluntary Time Off / Voluntary overtime, call-offs, cancellations) and recommend actions to stabilize delivery and cost. Deliver recurring and ad hoc reporting (daily/weekly site rollups, NHO conversion, quality of hire, vendor fill-rate, cancellation reasons, error/audit logs). Execution & Compliance Utilize HRIS and VMS platforms (e.g., Workday) for requisitions, hiring events, timekeeping audits, and headcount moves. Support Managed Service Provider (MSP) in planning, setup, and breakdown of regional hiring events based on labor projections. Conduct post-event audits; resolve errors (timecard, roster, PO/billing, rate codes) within SLA. Monitor workforce activity (VTO, VOT, MOT, canceled shifts) and adjust demand plans; escalate emerging risks early. Ensure compliance with state and local employment regulations within the region (breaks, meal periods, scheduling, minor labor, sick leave). Maintain critical supplies (incl. PPE) for assigned sites; coordinate replenishment according to safety and budget guidelines. Support special projects and pilot programs as assigned by the manager. Qualifications Required High school diploma or equivalent. 1+ years in a fast-paced, customer-oriented environment (operations, administrative support, customer service, retail, hospitality, staffing, recruiting, HR, or related). Strong organization and prioritization skills with high attention to detail. Excellent customer service and discretion; able to handle confidential information. Clear written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to groups. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and company communication tools (e.g., email, Slack). Experience with data entry, auditing, and producing data-driven reports. Role may require time on the warehouse floor (walking/standing); ability to lift up to 25lbs on occasion. On-site presence at Home Site with periodic travel to regional sites; occasional evenings/weekends. Ability to travel to support sites as needed. Preferred Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field. HR background with knowledge of co-employment and contingent labor management. Experience in workforce planning, staffing vendor/MSP management, or fulfillment/distribution environments. Proficiency with iOS, Excel (lookups/pivots), and Workday (or similar HRIS). Experience with VMS platforms. Analytical problem-solver able to identify trends and recommend actions. Demonstrated ability to build effective partnerships with site teams and external vendors.

They are experts of operations, process and efficiency. This team leads food and food services including replenishment, inventory accuracy, food safety, presentation, ensuring price accuracy and promotional signing processes for all Food & Beverage areas of the store. At Target, we believe in our leaders having meaningful experiences that help them build and develop skills for a career. The role of a Food & Beverage Team Leader can provide you with the skills and experience of: Guest service fundamentals and experience building a guest-first and freshness culture on your team. Food & Beverage business fundamentals, including department sales trends, freshness, food safety and quality, inventory management, item reliability, guest shopping patterns and pricing and promotions strategies. Planning department(s) daily/weekly workload to support Food & Beverage priorities and deliver sales goals. Leading a team of hourly team members, including skills in interviewing, training, coaching, evaluating, retaining and developing talent. As a Food & Beverage Team Leader, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities: Consistently deliver guest experience commitments to create an Easy, Inspiring and Friendly guest experience. Ensures every team member understands, is trained, and consistently delivers on Target’s guest experience commitments and consistent operations. Actively observes and provides feedback, holding team members accountable while recognizing great guest experience moments. Reviews area guest, financial, and team outcome metrics to identify opportunities, takes action to improve, and aligns team on the right behaviors and execution, celebrates wins, drives results that deliver outcomes and elevates the guest experience. Understand sales goals, plan and execute daily/weekly workload to deliver on department and store sales goals and guest engagement, including merchandising, pricing, changes to salesfloor merchandise displays, sampling and promotions. With guidance from your direct leader, lead a guest-focused, efficient Food & Beverage team that strives to deliver the Food & Beverage standards by completing the Food & Beverage Daily Standards walk. Assess backroom and sales floor areas of Food & Beverage and Food Service on a daily basis by walking the Target Food & Beverage Standards. Prioritize your business needs and identify workload tasks for the team; review reporting to identify business trends for follow-up. At the guidance of your direct leader, establish clear goals and expectations and hold team members accountable to those expectations. Be a partner to the store leadership team through communication and collaboration to influence current sales performance and workload deliverables, leverage check-in and check-outs as daily connection points. Maintain a fresh, full and food safe area during all operating hours leveraging strong inventory management, area routines and Food Safety policies and procedures. Assign daily tasks to TMs based on planned workload and guest traffic patterns, ensuring alignment with weekly and monthly business priorities set by your direct leader. Validate and follow-up on team members’ progress against their assigned prioritized workload tasks, production area routines, and application of best practices. Lead and demonstrate a culture of executing all best practices; help close skill gaps through development, coaching, training, and team interactions. Lead team huddles to communicate focuses and trends, leveraging store reporting and HQ communications. Develop and maintain partnerships with vendors to ensure clear expectations are established, brand standards (such as delivery and merchandising) are being met and areas are reliably in-stock. Ensure product is available for guests by placing store-initiated orders according to best practices (where applicable). Remain up-to-date on relevant trends and products to educate team members. Support your leader in the hiring and onboarding process of new team members. Participate in team hiring and onboarding processes. Support guest services such as back-up cashier, order pick up (OPU) and Drive-up (DU) and maintain a compliance culture while executing those duties, such as compliance with federal, state, and local laws. Support Become a subject matter expert in federal, state and local adult beverage laws as they apply to your business and protect the store’s liquor license (if applicable). Lead your team to uphold and maintain all Starbucks and Pizza Hut Brand Standards and foster a productive partnership with your Starbucks district manager, following up on key takeaways from their time in your store (if applicable). In addition to Food Safety Manager Certification, complete all Starbucks and/or Pizza Hut training requirements or certifications (if applicable). Foster a productive relationship with your Starbucks district manager DM (if applicable), attend required in-store planning and business meetings and follow-up on key takeaways from their time in your store. Demonstrate a culture of ethical conduct, safety and compliance; lead team to work in the same way and hold others accountable to this commitment. Lead and demonstrate a safety culture through modeling and recognizing safe behaviors, identifying and correcting hazards, holding team accountable to following safety expectations, assisting with incident response, and reporting/investigating injuries timely and accurately. Model the execution of physical security processes in order to enhance the instore security culture. Support merchandise protection strategies across the total store, including ordering, storage and application as directed by best practices. Demonstrate inclusivity by valuing diverse voices and approaches, being authentic and respectful, and creating equitable experiences. As a key carrier, follow all safe and secure training and processes. Occasionally assume store-level leadership on duty (LOD) responsibilities to enable the guest experience for the store during assigned shifts based on store needs. Address all store emergency and compliance requirements. All other duties based on business needs. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR This may be the right job for you if: You enjoy interacting and helping others - including guests that shop our store and fellow team members you work with. You thrive in a fast-moving, highly active and physically demanding role, where teamwork, flexibility, and creative problem solving are key to success. You are open to working a variable work schedule with varying hours, days or shifts (including nights, weekends, holidays, closing shifts and other peak shopping times). The good news is that we have some amazing training that will help teach you everything you need to know to be a Food & Beverage Team Leader. jd_text: Starting Hourly Rate / Salario por Hora Inicial: $17.75 USD per hour ALL ABOUT TARGET Working at Target means helping all families discover the joy of everyday life. We bring that vision to life through our values and culture. Learn more about Target here. ALL ABOUT ASSETS PROTECTION Assets Protection ( AP ) teams function to keep our guests, team and brand secure and lead through crisis events. They protect profitable sales by mitigating shortage risks, preventing, and resolving theft and fraud to ensure product is available for our guest . They also build relationships inside and outside of Target , including store leaders and public safety officials, inclusive of law enforcement. At Target , we believe in our team members having meaningful experiences that help them build and develop skills for a career. The role of a Target Security Specialist can provide you with the skills and experience of : U sing intelligence-led tactics to keep team members and guests safe and secure C risis response, safety and crowd management; providing support to both guests and team members D e-escalation as well as experience with physical security controls and culture Using Target's video surveillance system T imely and accurately document ing cases using case management system s As a Target Security Specialist , no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities: Create an Easy, Inspiring and Friendly guest experience by delivering on the following commitments: Greet: 10ft: be friendly – smile, make eye contact, or wave 4ft: greet the guest, smile and initiate a warm, helpful interaction Help guests find what they need and/or resolve issues to ensure a smooth, easy shopping experience End every guest transaction with a sincere thank you Actively support team efforts and assist peers in other areas while maintaining a positive and respectful attitude Adjust to business and guest needs to deliver an easy and inspiring guest experience Promote a physical security culture for our team members and guests by assessing and maintaining safe and secure standards throughout the store, including exterior property . R espond to and accurat ely document security incidents in a timely manner . Appropriately respond to guest issues to provide a safe and secure environment for our team members and guests . Leverage d e- e scalation tactics and resources when responding to security incidents across the store . Conduct merchandise theft recoveries and provide theft apprehension support as needed, strictly adhering to AP polic ies . Prevent theft and shortage at the front of store by performing merchandise receipt checks while adhering to AP policies, as well as recognizing and communicating trends . Submit appropriate documentation in the case management system for all incidents following AP policy and procedures . Understand and appropriately use Target's video surveillance system . Work in a safe manner at all times ; comply with all safety policies , best practices , and training; report hazards and correct where possible . All other duties based on business needs . title: Energy Risk Engineering Consultant
jd_text: Exec Consultant Risk Eng - KR07HE Sr Consultant Risk Engineering - KR08DE We’re determined to make a difference and are proud to be an insurance company that goes well beyond coverages and policies. Working here means having every opportunity to achieve your goals – and to help others accomplish theirs, too. Join our team as we help shape the future. At The Hartford, our Risk Services organization exists to help people and businesses thrive by working directly with customers to assess risk, improve resilience, and deliver practical risk mitigation solutions that make a measurable difference. We partner with customers throughout their lifecycle to identify exposures, reduce losses, and strengthen operational performance—combining consultative expertise, technology enabled risk solutions, and data driven insights to improve outcomes before and after a loss. By integrating risk assessment, prevention, and recovery with the broader insurance experience, we help customers protect what matters most while building trust, long-term value, and sustainable advantages for both our customers and our enterprise. As an Energy Risk Engineering Consultant, you will provide direction and oversight for all assigned Energy accounts (Specifically oil and gas and sustainable/renewable energy) assuring that best-in-class services are targeted for our customers. Specific focus on battery energy storage systems, onshore wind turbines, EV charging, photovoltaic systems, open pit mining, fuel cells, electrical cooperatives, gas and electric utilities, transmission, upstream and midstream oil and gas. You will provide and implement formal service planning and direct initiatives to assure the delivery of exceptional energy specific risk engineering services that mitigate risk and increase client retention. In addition, the role will include technical evaluation of new business and existing written accounts for the Energy Unit where evaluation of risk and exposure identification and hazard/control assessment are required. Join us to continuously learn, expand your technical and consultative capabilities, and shape the future of risk engineering while delivering meaningful outcomes for customers and the enterprise. This role offers a remote work arrangement but requires the candidate to reside in Houston, TX to effectively support regional operations, clients, and partners. consultants as appropriate by role level Education, Professional Credentials and Experience – where appropriate 5+ Years progressive experience in energy specific risk engineering, loss control, Energy related sciences, Engineering OR equivalent combination of education and experience. jd_text: Sr PI Field Sales Rep - SD08AE We’re determined to make a difference and are proud to be an insurance company that goes well beyond coverages and policies. Technologically savvy (e.g., Microsoft tools such as Sales Force, Teams, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint). Ability to travel within assigned territory. title: Account Executive Officer, Senior Underwriter, Commercial Accounts
jd_text: Who Are We? Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it. Job Category Underwriting Compensation Overview The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards. Salary Range $109,300.00 - $180,200.00 Target Openings 1 What Is the Opportunity? Commercial Accounts offers a wide array of guaranteed-cost products to mid-size businesses. Total account solutions include General Liability, Property, Automobile, Workers' Compensation, and Lead Umbrella. The Account Executive Officer (AEO), Commercial Accounts will partner with agents and brokers to provide property, general liability, commercial auto, and/or workers' compensation coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource. As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers. What Will You Do? Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business. Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability. Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities. Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings. Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills. Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans. May assist in the training and mentoring of less experienced Account Executives. Perform other duties as assigned. What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have? Bachelor’s degree. Six to eight years of relevant underwriting experience with experience in commercial lines. Deep knowledge of commercial lines products, the regulatory environment, and the local insurance market. Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to proactively identify underwriting, marketing, or financial challenges and analyze available information to make timely decisions in alignment with our risk appetite. Excellent communication skills with the ability to successfully negotiate in difficult situations with agents and brokers. CPCU designation. What is a Must Have? Four years of underwriting, claim, operations, risk assessment, actuarial, sales, product, or finance experience. What Is in It for You? Health Insurance : Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment. Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers. Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays. Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs. Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice. Employment Practices Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions. If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you. Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting. To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/ .

title: Director of Business Development

You'll own security diligence on future targets and the integration playbook that gets acquired environments to our standard on a predictable timeline. Product and customer trust. Partner with Product and Engineering on secure-by-default design across Logistics, Brands, and Commerce. Own penetration testing and our bug bounty program. Be the executive voice in enterprise security reviews and questionnaires — the ones that decide whether a deal closes this quarter or next. Resilience. Own business continuity and disaster recovery for an operation where downtime means orders don't ship. Prove recovery works by testing it, not by documenting it. Team. The role of a Store Director can provide you with the skills and experience of: Managing a large team of hourly team members and leaders as well as leaders of leaders Recruiting, selecting, talent management and talent planning across all departments of the store Guest service fundamentals and experience building and leading a guest first culture across the store Retail business financials (e.g. payroll, profit and loss) and driving sales growth Creating store specific strategies and managing your team to deliver results Retail business fundamentals for total store: understanding sales trends, inventory management, guest shopping patterns and satisfaction, pricing and promotions strategies and specialty businesses Setting and planning total store quarterly business priorities and managing a team to deliver on sales goals Making business decisions by assessing market competition, understanding guest insights and feedback As a Store Director, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities: Cultivate a guest-centric and engaged team Lead a talent culture through taking an active role in the onboarding, development and growth of your leaders. Drive accountability through clear expectations and consistent performance management. In partnership with HR, create and deliver on sustainable and equitable talent strategies to fuel career progression and continued team growth. Be approachable and available for your team, lead a culture where leaders and team members are able to share and issues are quickly resolved. Recruit, hire and retain a passionate team for area specific knowledge and expertise. Oversee the scheduling process to ensure schedules meet the needs of your business, while providing a consistent guest experience and aligning with team member availability and desired hours. Own and implement leadership schedules that align to guest and business needs (including weekends, mornings, evenings, overnight and appropriate seasonal adjustments). Demonstrate and promote inclusivity by valuing diverse voices and approaches, being authentic and respectful, and creating equitable experiences. Invest in and follow up on personal and team training to enhance skills and capabilities, follow up to consistently achieve timely completion of required training. Model creating a welcoming experience by greeting guests as you are working. Demonstrate how to engage with guests when assistance is needed; engage with guests in a welcoming way and help solve their specific needs. Lead by thanking guests and let them know we’re happy they chose to shop at Target. Drive a guest-obsessed culture balancing the in-store and digital guest to deliver on store sales goals and operational goals while ensuring your team can inform, educate and promote the suite of benefits, featuresand offerings that reward our guest and/or enhance their shopping experience (including the Target App, Target Circle Card, Target Circle, Drive Up, Order Pick Up and Circle 360 same day delivery). Own your store’s overall business to drive efficiency, safety and grow sales Build and execute plans to run an efficient operation to fund future growth. Lead and create a culture of executing all best practices by understanding where operational shortage can occur throughout the building, build routines and action plans to resolve opportunities, and establish clear goals and expectations to hold team accountable. Leverage your reports (financial, operational, safety, food safety, team and guest) to understand the business and make decisions. Lead a culture of financial accountability through following your sales trends, leadership headcount guideline, payroll management and hourly overtime guidance and teaming each team how to understand their role in driving sales growth and total store profitability. Know and assess the competition; leverage guest insights and feedback to drive the business and be the destination of choice for our guests. Build relationships that are important to the store’s community to address the most pressing local needs. Leverage field support partners to help you solve problems and drive continuous operational improvement. Set clear priorities for the team through balancing competing priorities and demands. Own the safety culture and performance for the store through modeling and recognizing safe behaviors, identifying and correcting hazards, assisting with incident response, validating investigations effectively drive sustainable solutions, and own total store accountability to safety. Validate an instore security culture by focusing on deterrence, response and resolution in order to improve physical security processes. Validate that merchandise protection strategies across the total store are being executed according to best practices. As a key carrier, follow all safe and secure training and processes Addressing all store emergency and compliance needs Always demonstrate a culture of ethical conduct, safety (including food safety) and compliance; Lead and hold the team accountable to work in the same way WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR This may be the right job for you if: You enjoy interacting and helping others - including guests that shop our store and fellow team members you work with. You thrive in a fast-moving, highly active and physically demanding role, where teamwork, flexibility, and creative problem solving are key to success. You are open to working a flexible work schedule with varying hours, days or shifts (including nights, weekends, holidays and other peak shopping times). The good news is that we have some amazing training that will help teach you everything you need to know to be a Store Director. But there are a few skills you should have from the get-go: 4-year degree or equivalent experience Strong interpersonal and communication skills Team leadership and engagement Strong cognitive skills, including problem analysis, decision making, financial and quantitative analysis Manage conflict and lead and hold others accountable Relate well with and interact with all levels of the organization Welcoming and helpful attitude Manage workload and prioritize tasks independently Capability to remain focused and composed in a fast-paced environment and accomplish multiple tasks within established timeframes Ability to communicate on multiple frequency devices and operate handheld scanners, and other technology equipment as directed We are an awesome place to work and care about our teams, so we want to make sure we are clear on a few more basics that we expect: Access all areas of the building to respond to guest or team member issues Interpret instructions, reports and information Accurately handle cash register operations as needed Climb up and down ladders as needed Scan, handle and move merchandise efficiently and safely, including frequently lifting or moving merchandise up to 44 pounds without additional assistance from others Capable of working in and exposure to varying temperatures, humidity, and other elements while performing certain job duties including but not limited to Drive-Up, carryout, etc. Ability to remain mobile for the duration of a scheduled shift (shift length may vary) Flexible work schedule (e.g., nights, weekends and holidays) and reliable and prompt attendance necessary Benefits Eligibility Please paste this url into your preferred browser to learn about benefits eligibility for this role: https://tgt.biz/BenefitsForYou_F Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) In compliance with state and federal laws, Target will make reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. Reporting to the Director of AI & ML Platforms and partnering closely with the AI Governance team, Cybersecurity, Model Risk, Legal, Privacy, and the business, you will own the technical foundation for how AI use cases and agents move from idea to production. A typical week spans three kinds of work: shaping the governance framework and lifecycle controls (roughly half your time), hardening the security posture of our AI and agentic platforms (about a quarter), and embedding directly with use-case teams to design, build, and ship the controls they need to launch (about a quarter). You'll balance governance rigor against engineering velocity so teams can innovate within guardrails instead of around them. production monitoring and retirement Operationalize lifecycle gates: intake, risk classification, control design, approval workflows, monitoring, and remediation Define risk tiers and controls proportional to use-case risk, extending model risk management to AI/ML and GenAI in line with SR 11-7, NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, and ISO/IEC 42001 Own the Agent Registry and AI inventory as the authoritative source of truth — registration, versioning, and prevention of shadow-AI deployments Translate governance policy into repeatable, testable engineering controls, partnering with the AI Governance team to move controls from observation to staged enforcement AI Security (≈25%) Perform AI-specific threat modeling and risk assessments — prompt injection, data poisoning, adversarial attacks, model theft, and data exfiltration — and design mitigations across the data, model, application, and infrastructure layers Design guardrail, isolation, and least-privilege controls for agents — sandboxed execution, non-human identity, secrets management, and mediated tool access through the MCP registry Build AI-specific incident response playbooks, drive red-team exercises, and embed security into the AI/ML lifecycle (DevSecOps for AI) with audit logging into enterprise SIEM Forward Deployed Engineering (≈25%) Embed with use-case, product, and platform teams to design and ship the executable controls they need to launch AI and agentic solutions within governed boundaries Build reusable, production-grade capabilities hands-on: guardrail services, evaluation pipelines, agent/MCP registrations, and human-in-the-loop approval flows — using AWS, Bedrock/AgentCore, Cedar policies, and Lambda/Step Functions Lead design reviews, set engineering standards, and mentor engineers across the governance and security control stack What you bring 12+ years of software engineering experience and demonstrated experience with AI/ML/Data Governance and associated information-security of AI/ML Designing and implementing enterprise AI or data governance frameworks and operational governance processes in production Translating security, risk, privacy, and compliance requirements into executable controls, measurable tests, and working software Deep understanding of AI/model risk and responsible-AI principles, with working knowledge of SR 11-7, NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, and preferred) and modern CI/CD Strong communication — able to explain technical AI risk and control gaps to both engineers and senior executives Added bonus if you have Direct experience governing or securing enterprise AI/GenAI programs in financial services or another regulated industry Hands-on experience with AWS AI services (Bedrock, AgentCore, Bedrock Guardrails), policy-as-code (e.g., Cedar), and LLM/agent evaluation and guardrail frameworks (LLM-as-judge, trajectory evaluation, NeMo Guardrails, Llama Guard) Relevant certifications — CISSP, CCSP, CRISC, CISA, a Certified AI Security/Governance credential, or a model-risk certification What we’ll bring During your interview process, our team can fill you in on all the details of our industry-leading benefits and career development opportunities. title: Senior Implementation Consultant (Supply Chain Risk Management)
jd_text: Sphera is a leading global provider of enterprise software and services that enables companies to manage and optimize their environmental, health, safety and sustainability. Our mission is to create a safer, more sustainable and productive world. Sphera is a portfolio company of Blackstone, a U.S.-based alternative asset investment company that focuses on private equity, technology and innovation, and more. Blackstone businesses succeed through strong partnerships, a personalized approach and a commitment to exceptional performance with uncompromising integrity. Sphera and Blackstone are leaders in the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) space. We are guided by our core values of Customer Centricity, Accountability, Bias to Action, Innovation, and Collaboration. These values help us recruit the right talent to join our rapidly expanding team of around the globe. It is important to us that each and every Spherion is not only eager to challenge themselves and knows how to get work done but is an awesome addition to our company culture. As a Senior Implementation Consultant, you will play a key role in helping Sphera customers successfully implement and maximize the value of our supply chain risk management solutions. You will own customer implementation projects from kickoff through to completion, working closely with customers to understand their business requirements, configure and enable the solution, provide training and guidance, and ensure they are able to achieve meaningful value from the platform. We are looking for someone who combines strong supply chain expertise with project management and client-facing consulting skills. Experience in supply chain risk management is particularly valuable, as you will bring subject matter expertise into customer engagements while developing a deep understanding of Sphera's solutions. This is a key role within the team, and we are looking for someone who can bring a high level of expertise and professionalism, share best practices and help raise the standard across the wider implementation team. What You’ll Do Lead Customer Implementations Own customer implementation projects from initial kickoff through to successful completion. Typically manage implementation projects , ensuring projects are delivered on time, within scope and to a high standard. Lead customer meetings and workshops to understand business requirements, processes and objectives . Translate customer requirements into effective solution configurations and implementation approaches. Provide customer training and guidance, helping users understand how to effectively use the platform and maximize its value. Act as a trusted advisor throughout the implementation, using your supply chain expertise to provide practical recommendations and guidance. Manage project timelines, deliverables, risks and customer expectations. Supply Chain & Subject Matter Expertise Apply your knowledge of supply chain management and, ideally, supply chain risk management (SCRM) to customer engagements. Understand supply chain processes, procurement , supplier management and global supply chain risks and how these can be managed through technology. Bring industry knowledge and best practices into customer projects. Project Management & PMO Apply strong project management and PMO principles across customer engagements. Manage project planning and project backlog s identifying project risks and dependencies and proactively manage them through to resolution. Maintain accurate project documentation and contribute to internal implementation best practices. Work closely with internal teams, including Customer Care, Product and other delivery functions, to continuously improve processes and the customer experience. Pre-Sales & Commercial Support Support the Sales team during the pre-sales process, bringing implementation and supply chain expertise to prospective customers. Contribute to solution scoping, project estimates, proposals and implementation planning. Participate in customer discussions and demonstrations where your subject matter expertise can add value. Help ensure that proposed solutions are realistic, achievable and aligned with customer requirements. Team & Continuous Improvement Share knowledge, best practices and implementation approaches with colleagues. Contribute to improving implementation methodologies, templates, documentation and processes. What You’ll Bring Essential Strong professional experience in Supply Chain Management, with experience in areas such as procurement, supplier management, sustainability , supply chain operations or supply chain risk. Experience working in a client-facing consulting, implementation, project management or similar role. Strong understanding of supply chain processes and challenges. Demonstrable experience managing projects, workstreams or customer engagements from start to finish. jd_text: SNC's Military Fellowship Program partners with programs such as SkillBridge and Hiring Our Heroes to provide fellowship opportunities to service members transitioning to the civilian workforce. Staffed out of Supply Chain and assigned to a program or proposal, Supply Chain Program Managers (SCPMs) are the primary experts for both Supply Chain Program Management and Technical responsibility of a Supplier’s SOW. As a SCPM, you may oversee daily operations for multiple lower-level SCPMs and/or Supply Chain Project Coordinators (SCPCs). You will collaborate with assigned Subcontract Leads, Purchasing Agents, Program Office staff, Engineering teams, Operations personnel, and Business Management to develop strategies that meet program missions.
