The role involves consolidating supply chain risks at the program level while mitigating them effectively. You will also act as a key voice in developing supplier requirements during proposals. This role may require the following responsibilities: Leadership and Team Supervision • Supervise a team of SCPCs and SCPM 1, providing daily oversight and guidance on SNC's tools, procedures, and processes. • Participate in and occasionally lead programmatic and technical meetings with subcontractors and suppliers. • Attend Program Reviews with subcontractors to provide updates, communicate needs and status, and request program-driven changes Strategic Supply Chain Management and Planning • Develop the Program-level Supply Chain Management Plan, outlining supply chain strategies, reporting, and communication plan. • Develop a cohesive strategy for forming effective teaming within our supply chain network which encompasses a robust framework that ensures seamless integration. • Develop comprehensive negotiation strategies to facilitate the formalization of strategic agreements with key suppliers. • Create tailored sourcing strategies that address each category's unique requirements and actively engage cross-functional teams in collaborative planning sessions. • Evaluate the performance and capabilities of current suppliers and the supply chain, forecast future needs, and develop negotiation strategies that promote sustained collaboration. • May be responsible to lead make / buy assessments from supply chain perspective. • May be assigned as the subcontract Program Manager for a large or complex subcontract, executing the role of Program Manager. • If assigned to a platform, product line, Business Unit (BU) or product support team, collaborate and communicate potential long-term investment strategies to reduce lead-time and cost. • Identify and coordinate the need for alternate or additional sources to enhance competition and leverage. Act as the supply chain architect and liaison for the proposal or program, ensuring a competitive, capable, and compliant supply base • Lead business requirements, technical evaluations, risk assessments, and Basis of Estimate (BOE) strategies in support of proposals and new pursuits. • Provide supply chain strategy and status to internal and external customers • Support SNC's Design for Excellence (Dfx) initiatives by leading the Design for Supply Chain (DFSC) efforts, including implementing Design to Product Target Cost (DPTC) methodologies for development programs. • Support department goals, objectives and supply chain Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), such as on-time delivery, negotiations, and purchase requisition processing time Supply Chain Communication and Coordination • Act as the liaison between the Supply Chain management team and the program to ensure alignment of prime requirements (i.e., CDRLs to SDRLs) and timely resolution of problems. • Initiate the Purchase Requisition (PR) to Purchase Order (PO) process by developing the Material and Service Request (MSR) or Advanced Purchase Requisition (APL). • Create and update Supply Chain Program Review Charts, dashboards, highlighting the current cost, technical, and schedule performance of each program. • Coordinate between supply chain teams (procurement, subcontract management, and the program) to ensure timely schedules and milestone delivery. • Communicate supply chain status, identify/manage risk and opportunity. • Champion and present status of recovery plans to all stakeholders at the program level or to senior supply chain leadership. Program Management and Control Account • Manage the cost, technical, and schedule aspects of supply chain for a given proposal or program as the Program Management representative. • Track progress against the Supply Chain schedule, identifying and addressing any deviations. • Lead the development of Supplier/Subcontractor Statements of Work (SSOW), Supplier Data Requirement Lists (SDRLs), and other requirements flow downs. • Identify potential risks within program specific supply chain (subcontractors and procured parts) and present mitigation plans to address risk. • May be delegated Control Account Manager (CAM) responsibilities by the Program Manager, requiring SCPM to obtain SNC’s CAM Certification. • Use Earned Value Management (EVM) techniques to assess project performance • Monitor actual costs against budgeted costs and report variances. • Calculate, track and report out on key EVM metrics, such as Cost Performance Index (CPI) and Schedule Performance Index (SPI), to all stakeholders. • Prepare regular status reports on cost, schedule, and performance metrics. Maintain comprehensive documentation related to all aspects of the control account. • Analyze causes behind significant variances from planned values in terms both time/costs recommending corrective actions where necessary. Additional SCPM proposal/pursuit responsibilities: As an SCPM supporting pursuits and proposal activities, you will ensure SNC is well-positioned with an achievable solution and a competitive, compliant, and capable supply base to win new business. Specific tasks may include: • Collaborate with supply chain team to; o Identify potential supply sources to mitigate risks, identify opportunities and meet program objectives. o Develop source selection strategies, criteria, and planning, including participation in Make/Buy assessments at the program level. • Create and document labor and non-labor Basis of Estimates (BOE). • Develop program/technical requirements documents. • Support technical evaluation of proposals for content and quality. • Lead or support the development of source selection plans, mitigating risks by qualifying multiple sources, and practice split awards when possible. Present business cases to Program Management and Supply Chain Leadership. • Provide subcontractor and critical procurement-related input into customer proposals. • Ensure subcontractors' milestone payment plans align with program expectations, budget, and schedules. • Develop a preliminary Supply Chain Management Plan that includes resources for successful new program start-up. jd_text: Work Schedule Second Shift (Afternoons) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer. The Inventory Control Specialist is responsible for maintaining accurate inventory records, ensuring material availability, supporting inventory transactions, and driving continuous improvement throughout inventory management processes. This role serves as the primary subject matter expert for inventory activities while working closely with Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality and Finance to ensure inventory accuracy and operational efficiency. The ideal candidate possesses SAP inventory management experience, a deep understanding of manufacturing processes, excellent problem-solving skills, a willingness to teach and willingness to learn. Monitor inventory levels and identify potential shortages, excess inventory, and obsolete materials. Conduct cycle counts on a regular basis and actively supports physical inventory activities. Investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies, variances, and transaction errors. Analyze inventory movements and recommend corrective and preventative actions to improve accuracy. Support inventory reconciliation activities between physical inventory and ERP system records. SAP Inventory Control Execute and monitor SAP inventory transactions, including: Goods Receipts (GR) Goods Issues (GI) Transfer Postings Stock Transfers Inventory Adjustments Cycle Count Processing Physical Inventory Documentation Ensure SAP master data accuracy related to: Material Masters Storage Locations Inventory Parameters Units of Measure Batch Number Controls Troubleshoot inventory-related SAP transaction issues and collaborate with IT or SAP support teams, as needed. Work in developing and maintaining SAP reports, queries, and inventory performance metrics. Inventory Analysis & Reporting Generate and distribute inventory status reports and KPI dashboards. title: Senior Project Manager
jd_text: STV is seeking a Senior Project Manager, for our PM/CM group in Texas. The Senior Project Manager is responsible for overseeing the planning, design, execution, and completion of construction projects, ensuring that they meet quality standards, timelines, budgets, and regulatory requirements. This role involves collaborating with architects, contractors, vendors, school administrators, and local government entities to deliver safe, functional, and sustainable educational environments for students and staff. Key Responsibilities: Project Planning & Coordination: · Manage the entire lifecycle of construction projects. · Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and resource allocation plans. · Lead pre-construction meetings to ensure project goals and expectations are clearly defined. Budget and Financial Management: · Prepare and manage project budgets, tracking expenses and ensuring the project stays within budget. · Review and approve project invoices and payment applications. · Provide regular financial reporting to stakeholders, highlighting potential cost overruns or savings. Team Leadership & Communication: · Lead and supervise project teams, including architects, engineers, construction workers, and subcontractors. · Serve as the primary point of contact between all project stakeholders (school district, contractors, consultants, local authorities, and the community). · Organize and lead regular project meetings, providing updates on progress, challenges, and upcoming milestones. Regulatory Compliance & Safety: · Ensure all construction activities comply with local, state, and federal regulations, including building codes, zoning laws, and environmental standards. · Ensure all safety standards and procedures are followed on-site to protect workers, students, and staff. · Obtain necessary permits and approvals before commencing construction. Risk Management & Problem Solving: · Identify potential project risks and develop mitigation strategies to address them. · Resolve issues and conflicts that arise during construction, ensuring minimal impact on project timelines and quality. · Ensure any changes to project scope, schedule, or budget are documented and communicated to stakeholders. Quality Assurance: · Monitor construction work to ensure it meets established quality standards and specifications. · Conduct regular site visits to assess progress, resolve issues, and maintain quality control. · Ensure that final construction is thoroughly inspected and completed to satisfaction before handover. Post-Construction & Handover: · Ensure all necessary documentation, warranties, and manuals are provided at project completion. · Coordinate post-construction inspections and punch lists for project close-out. title: Customer Onboarding and Learning Systems Specialist
jd_text: Job Description:  Customer Onboarding & Learning Systems Specialist Department Customer Success Location Remote / Hybrid Reports To Director of Customer Success Type Full-Time Role Overview EZFacility is seeking a Customer Onboarding & Learning Systems Specialist to serve as both a hands-on software trainer and an architect of our next-generation onboarding experience. This is a pivotal role that bridges two critical needs: delivering high-quality, personalized training to new EZFacility clients while simultaneously helping us transition from a live-session-heavy model to a scalable, self-guided onboarding ecosystem. Today, new customer onboarding relies primarily on live Zoom training sessions totaling approximately six hours per client. Our goal over the next 12 months is to cut that in half through structured digital learning, in-app guidance, and AI-powered resources — freeing our training team to focus on higher-value, consultative support. This is a builder-and-doer role ideal for someone who enjoys working directly with customers, creating engaging learning experiences, and experimenting with technology to improve how clients learn and adopt software. Key Responsibilities Deliver Client Training & Onboarding Serve as a software expert across all EZFacility products, guiding new clients through the critical first months of implementation. Assess each client's goals and business needs; develop customized training plans that ensure they are set up for success. Conduct live (Zoom-based) training sessions for both basic and advanced software usage, adapting your approach to each client's technical comfort level. Collaborate with Sales and Account Management to ensure onboarding is completed on schedule and aligned with client timelines. Demonstrate patience and professionalism when working with clients to resolve outstanding questions or issues. Make product recommendations based on clients' overall business objectives and act on opportunities to enhance their experience. Build a Scalable Self-Guided Onboarding Program Design and implement structured self-guided onboarding tracks tailored to different customer segments and use cases. Develop a scalable library of learning resources including short training videos, step-by-step tutorials, self-guided courses, and knowledge base articles. Create learning paths for new customer onboarding, advanced product usage, and new feature releases. Reduce reliance on live training sessions by replacing feature walkthroughs with high-quality digital content. Implement Digital Adoption & Learning Tools Own and optimize our digital adoption platform (Userpilot) to deliver in-app guidance, product tours, and contextual help experiences. Implement and manage a Learning Management System (LMS) for structured, trackable training delivery. Design guided product walkthroughs that help users learn the platform in the flow of their work. Integrate AI into Customer Education Content creation and maintenance Use AI to quickly update training materials after each product release, so customer-facing content never lags the platform. Turn recorded onboarding sessions into searchable summaries, short how-to clips, and FAQ entries. Build reusable AI prompt templates for common content types, such as release notes, help articles, and session recaps, to keep output consistent across the team. Personalized onboarding Use AI to analyze a new customer's setup, industry, and goals before kickoff, and tailor the training plan to match. Identify customers who are falling behind in onboarding, based on product usage and engagement signals, and trigger targeted learning content or outreach. Design adaptive learning paths that adjust to a customer's progress and proficiency. Self-service and support deflection Partner with Support to mine ticket data for the top recurring questions, and prioritize new training content based on what the data shows. Audit knowledge base content regularly with AI to find outdated, duplicate, or missing articles. Build contextual in-app guidance that surfaces the right help article or walkthrough at the moment a customer needs it. Collaborate Cross-Functionally Partner with Customer Success, Support, and Product teams to identify friction points in onboarding and design solutions that shorten time-to-value. Work closely with the Training Team Lead to coordinate onboarding activities and share best practices. Leverage Salesforce to track client training progress, document feedback, and streamline training initiatives. Evaluate and document client feedback for the product development team's review. Ensure all education content aligns with current product capabilities and best practices. Measure & Continuously Improve Track key metrics including onboarding completion rates, time-to-first-value, training engagement, and reduction in live training hours. Brainstorm and execute client engagement and retention initiatives such as video tutorials, webinars, and user guides. Continuously refine learning programs based on data, customer feedback, and evolving product capabilities. Qualifications Required 2+ years of experience in software training, customer onboarding, customer success, or a related field. Previous software training, customer service/support, and basic technical experience. Experience creating or delivering structured learning programs, training plans, or onboarding flows. Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate complex product functionality into simple, approachable learning experiences. Ability to prioritize, multi-task, and work independently with minimal supervision in a fast-paced environment. Strong work ethic and the ability to meet deadlines while managing multiple client relationships. A patient, client-first mindset with a genuine commitment to resolving issues and driving client success. Preferred Experience with Digital Adoption Platforms (Userpilot, WalkMe, Pendo, Appcues, or similar). Experience implementing or managing a Learning Management System (LMS). Familiarity with AI tools for content creation, knowledge management, or training personalization. Knowledge of Salesforce for tracking training progress and client data. Video editing experience for producing training and tutorial content. Prior experience in the SaaS industry; familiarity with the sports, fitness, or recreation industry is a strong plus. Experience working with SaaS customer success or training teams. Skills & Attributes Strong systems thinking and process design — you see patterns and build solutions that scale. Instructional design sensibility — you know how to structure information so people actually learn it. Comfortable experimenting with new tools and technologies, and sharing what you learn with the team. Data-driven mindset — you use metrics to inform decisions and demonstrate impact. Collaborative and communicative — you build strong relationships with clients and teammates alike. Organized and detail-oriented — you can manage multiple client implementations simultaneously without dropping the ball. What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months) Within your first year, you will: Successfully onboard a full book of new clients while delivering high-quality, personalized training. Reduce average live training hours per client from 6 hours toward 3 hours through self-guided content. Launch a structured self-guided onboarding program with supporting video, tutorial, and LMS content. Stand up and optimize our digital adoption platform to deliver in-app onboarding guidance. Introduce AI-powered knowledge and learning resources that measurably reduce support inquiries. Enable the broader training team to shift focus from feature walkthroughs to consultative, high-value onboarding. Why Join EZFacility EZFacility is a leading software platform serving sports facilities, gyms, and membership-based businesses worldwide. Our customers rely on our platform to run and grow their operations — and our team is committed to making that experience as smooth and successful as possible. As we scale, we are investing in modern onboarding and education experiences that empower customers to learn faster, adopt our platform more effectively, and realize value sooner. This role offers a unique opportunity to be both on the front lines with clients and at the center of building the future of customer education at EZFacility.                                                                                      Business Unit:  EZ Facility- USA                                                                                      Scheduled Weekly Hours: 40                                                                                      Number of Openings Available:  1                                                                                      Worker Type:  Regular More About Jonas Software: Jonas Software is a leading provider of enterprise management software solutions, serving a wide range of vertical markets including hospitality, healthcare, construction, education, personal care, fitness, leisure, moving and legal services, to name a few. Within these markets, Jonas is comprised of over 65 distinct brands, each a respected leader in its domain. Jonas’ vision is to be the branded global leader across these verticals and to be recognized by customers and industry stakeholders as the trusted provider of “Software for Life.” We are committed to technology, product innovation, quality, and exceptional customer service. Jonas Software supports over 60,000 customers in more than 30 countries. We employ over 6,000 skilled professionals, including industry experts and technology specialists. Across our broader network, we support a global workforce of more than 30,000 employees. Headquartered in Canada, Jonas Software has a global footprint with offices around the world. We’re a 100% owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., based in Toronto, publicly listed on the TSX (CSU.TO), and a member of the S&P/TSX 60 Index.

Evaluate and leverage learning management systems and other learning technologies to support program administration, training delivery, learner engagement, tracking and reporting. Measurement, Analytics & Continuous Improvement (20%) Establish and manage program measurement strategies that evaluate participant experience, learning effectiveness, behavioral adoption, and business impact. Analyze program data, assessment results, participation trends, and stakeholder feedback to identify opportunities for improvement and increased effectiveness and impact. Develop executive-ready dashboards, scorecards, and reports that communicate program performance, business impact and recommendations for future enhancements. Continuously refine program design, delivery practices, and measurement methodologies to drive greater organizational impact and learner engagement and outcomes. jd_text: Job Title Diabetes Education Program Manager Agency Texas A&M University Health Science Center Department TAMHSC McAllen Campus Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location McAllen, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description Our Commitment Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences. Operates and manages the clinical side of DEP, which includes overseeing inventory and requisition of necessary medical program supplies, medications, equipment, etc. Maintains a close working relationship with the Director and keeps well informed of all DEP activities, changes, issues, data collection/analysis, and/or concerns. Attend meetings with Director to discuss planning, program review, program development, grant acquisition, budget evaluation, and program effectiveness. Assists in developing short/long term goals, objectives and strategic planning. Assists in the development of special reports and/or information requested by the Director. Supervises and provides directions to program staff and other clinicians to include student assistants/interns. Maintains a regular and consistent meeting schedule with the entire DEP staff to ensure quality and outstanding care and service to our participants and community partners/stakeholders. Develops and maintains working relationships with community partners/stakeholders and DEP participants which includes marketing/outreach activities and attending seminars, conferences, training, etc. Evaluates the content, teaching methods, and performance of all program educators and assistants. Oversees and manages all program data collection, analysis and evaluation to support program efficiency and effectiveness. Travels to various locations within the service area of the Rio Grande Valley (Starr, Hidalgo, Cameron and Willacy Counties) for program activities in a personal or University vehicle. Occasional travel to Corpus Christi and/or College Station, TX for training, meetings, etc. Manages the social media/marketing activity for DEP. Stays well versed in new trends of evidence-based practice in diabetes and other chronic illnesses. Works closely with other staff to ensure the diabetes education program meets the American Diabetes Association (ADA) standards and program recognition is maintained within the field and at the community and state levels. Works closely with Coastal Bend Regional DEP leadership, county public health officials, and other staff as appropriate for best practice and curriculum adjustments, etc. Develops educational program material, learning resources, and evaluation tools for specific educational clinical interventions. Prepares and delivers presentations to our participants and community partners/stakeholders. Completes health screenings for program participants, to include, but not limited to: HbA1c, cholesterol, blood pressure, hip and waist circumference, and body mass index (BMI). Master’s degree in a health-related field. Fluent in English and Spanish. Valid driver’s license. Skill in facilitating cooperative group decision making among assorted organizations and individuals serving on planning committees. Ability: Ability to work with frequent interruptions and changes in priorities. Ability to quickly recognize and analyze irregular events. Ability to establish and maintain good working relationships with other stakeholders within and outside the University. Ability to exercise good judgment, tact, and diplomacy in all dealings and maintain confidentiality as required. Ability to understand and explain complex issues to stakeholders and to establish and maintain effective communication and working relationships with City employees, community leaders, and the public. title: Academic Technology Operations Coordinator
jd_text: Job Title Academic Technology Operations Coordinator Agency Texas A&M University - Kingsville Department Instructional Technology Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Kingsville, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description About Texas A&M University–Kingsville Texas A&M University–Kingsville (TAMUK), the oldest institution of higher learning in South Texas and a proud member of the Texas A&M University System, stands as the region’s premier university. TAMUK offers the widest range of academic programs and degrees in South Texas, provides exceptional learning and residential facilities, conducts impactful research, awards substantial scholarships, and has awarded more than 80,000 degrees in the institution’s 100-year history. The university is recognized for its unwavering commitment to student success, meaningful research, and deep community engagement. With a welcoming campus culture and strong regional partnerships, TAMUK offers faculty and staff a unique opportunity to make a lasting difference in the lives of students and the broader South Texas region. Location: The University is located in historic Kingsville, a friendly, safe city of 25,000 that is the home of the legendary King Ranch. Corpus Christi and its beaches are just 40 miles to the northeast, and the border with Mexico is 120 miles to the south at Brownsville or 119 miles to the west at Laredo. For more information, click here . Position Overview The Academic Technology Operations Coordinator, under direction, routinely manages large, complex academic technology projects and operations that support the University’s academic mission, teaching, learning, and innovative technology environments. The position coordinates academic technology operations across classrooms, conference spaces, digital learning environments, and other institutional facilities. Collaborates with academic leadership, the Institutional Facilities Project Manager, Campus Operations, ITS, campus stakeholders, and external partners to plan and implement innovative, accessible, and technology-enabled learning environments. Performs limited specialized technical duties while advancing operational excellence, emerging technologies, and continuous improvement in support of the University’s academic community within the Division of Academic Affairs. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Operations and Service Delivery Collaborates with the Center for Academic Technology team to promote innovative approaches and support high-quality service delivery across instructional technology, academic classrooms, audio-visual systems, digital learning spaces, and institutional workforce innovation environments. Directs day-to-day operations of academic technology services across classrooms, conference spaces, digital signage, satellite locations, and workforce innovation environments. Oversees operational processes and service delivery models, including preventative maintenance, incident response, and technology lifecycle management. Serves as the primary point of contact for academic technology operations, providing consultation, issue resolution, and support for faculty, staff, and campus partners. Develops, implements, and maintains standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure consistency, compliance, and operational effectiveness. Cultivates collaborative partnerships with campus leadership, Campus Operations, ITS, Event Planning, Facilities, and external vendors to support integrated technology solutions. Strategic Planning, Project Management, and Resource Administration Leads and collaborates in the coordination, prioritization, and execution of work with Campus Operations, establishing service expectations, schedules, and resource allocations. Manages the planning and implementation of academic technology initiatives, including classroom technology upgrades, AV integrations, and emerging technology deployments. Applies formal project management methodologies to define scope, timelines, milestones, risks, and resource requirements, ensuring successful project delivery. Administers budgets in collaboration with Center for Academic Technology leadership and coordinates the procurement, evaluation, selection, and deployment of instructional and AV technologies. Ensures fiscal responsibility, resource optimization, and alignment with institutional priorities and standards. Innovation, Emerging Technologies, and Continuous Improvement Advances the integration and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within academic technology operations, supporting AI-enabled teaching and learning tools, service automation, and data-informed decision-making. Promotes human-centered, ethical, accessible, and compliant AI practices aligned with institutional priorities and emerging higher education trends. Monitors service metrics and implements continuous improvement strategies to enhance operational efficiency and user experience. Promotes ongoing professional development and continuous learning related to emerging technologies, accessibility requirements, AI-enabled teaching and learning, and workforce innovation environments. Identifies and supports innovative solutions that enhance teaching, learning, collaboration, and institutional effectiveness. Other Duties Assigned The above represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned. Qualifications Required Education Bachelor’s Degree in applicable field or equivalent combination of education and experience Required Experience Three Years of Related Experience Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Knowledge Knowledge of academic and instructional technology operations, including classroom A/V systems, digital learning spaces, conference technology, digital signage, and emerging technologies. Knowledge of project and operations management principles, including project scope, schedules, milestones, resource allocation, risk management, budgeting, and project delivery. Knowledge of audio-visual and classroom technology systems, integration practices, preventative maintenance, troubleshooting, and technology lifecycle management. Knowledge of IT service management practices, including incident response, service delivery, performance metrics, continuous improvement, and ITIL principles. Knowledge of technology procurement and vendor management, including product evaluation, selection, purchasing, implementation, and coordination with external partners. Knowledge of IT security, institutional compliance, and digital accessibility requirements applicable to higher education technology environments. Knowledge of Artificial Intelligence and emerging technology trends, including responsible, ethical, accessible, and human-centered applications of AI in academic and operational environments. Knowledge of standard productivity applications, including word processing, spreadsheets, documentation, reporting, and data analysis tools. Skill s Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to coordinate multiple complex technology initiatives simultaneously. Strong technical troubleshooting and problem-solving skills related to academic technology, A/V systems, and technology-enabled learning and work environments. Strong analytical and decision-making skills with the ability to evaluate operational needs, service metrics, technology solutions, and resource requirements. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical information effectively to faculty, staff, administrators, vendors, and other stakeholders. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills with an emphasis on responsive, collaborative, and solutions-oriented support. Strong planning, prioritization, documentation, and process-improvement skills. Skill in developing and maintaining standard operating procedures, technical documentation, service expectations, and operational workflows. Skill in coordinating cross-functional teams, campus partners, contractors, and technology vendors. Abilities Ability to manage and coordinate complex academic technology operations across classrooms, conference spaces, digital signage environments, satellite locations, and institutional learning and workforce environments. Ability to work closely with the Institutional Facilities Project Manager to coordinate academic technology requirements within renovation, construction, infrastructure, and learning-space improvement projects. Ability to collaborate effectively with institutional stakeholders, including academic leadership, Campus Operations, Facilities, ITS, Event Planning, faculty, staff, external vendors, and other campus partners. Ability to coordinate technology requirements with stakeholders throughout project planning, design, implementation, installation, testing, and completion. Ability to plan, prioritize, and deliver multiple academic technology and A/V projects within established scope, timelines, budgets, and institutional requirements. Ability to assess academic technology needs and recommend scalable, sustainable, accessible, and innovative solutions aligned with institutional priorities. Ability to communicate technical requirements, project expectations, timelines, risks, and operational needs effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to respond effectively to technology incidents, changing priorities, project requirements, and operational demands while maintaining high-quality service. Ability to analyze operational and service data to improve processes, resource allocation, preventative maintenance, technology lifecycle planning, and customer experience. Ability to exercise independent judgment, initiative, discretion, and sound decision-making within established institutional policies and procedures. Ability to adapt to and continuously learn new technologies, A/V systems, accessibility standards, AI-enabled tools, and emerging higher education technology practices. Ability to multitask, establish priorities, and work cooperatively in a collaborative, customer-focused academic environment and represent the Center for Academic Technology Leadership in the division of Academic Affairs in meetings. Other Requirements Physical Requirements Ability to perform primarily office-based work with periodic work in academic classrooms, conference rooms, learning spaces, and other campus facilities. Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, stoop, reach, and move throughout campus facilities as necessary to coordinate academic technology operations and projects. Ability to operate computers, A/V equipment, control systems, and other standard academic technology equipment. Ability to visually inspect academic technology and A/V installations and identify operational or equipment issues. Ability to occasionally move, position, or assist with technology equipment and related materials in accordance with institutional safety practices. Ability to travel between buildings and institutional locations as necessary to inspect projects, coordinate installations, and support academic technology operations. Ability to work in active construction, renovation, classroom, and technology installation environments when coordinating projects with the Center for Academic Technology Leadership, Team, Institutional Facilities Project Manager, contractors, vendors, and campus stakeholders. Other Requirements and Factors Must maintain a customer-service-oriented, collaborative, and professional approach when working with faculty, staff, administrators, students, contractors, vendors, and institutional stakeholders. Must be able to coordinate and prioritize multiple academic technology projects, operational needs, and service requests in a dynamic higher education environment. Must work collaboratively with the Center for Academic Technology Leadership, Team, Institutional Facilities Project Manager, Campus Operations, Facilities, ITS, Event Planning, academic units, external vendors, and other institutional stakeholders on technology-related projects and initiatives. Must be able to work across academic classrooms, conference spaces, digital learning environments, satellite locations, and institutional workforce environments as operational and project needs require. May require occasional work outside normal business hours to support technology implementations, scheduled maintenance, upgrades, installations, projects, or time-sensitive operational needs. Must demonstrate sound judgment and professionalism when handling institutional technology resources, operational information, project documentation, budgets, and vendor relationships. Must maintain current knowledge of academic technology, A/V systems, accessibility requirements, cybersecurity considerations, Artificial Intelligence, and emerging higher education technology trends. Must participate in ongoing professional development and continuous learning relevant to academic technology operations, project management, accessibility, and emerging technologies. Must adhere to applicable University, Texas A&M University System, information technology, safety, accessibility, procurement, and security policies and procedures. Must be able to adapt to changing institutional priorities, technology environments, project requirements, and operational demands while maintaining timely and high-quality service. This position is security sensitive This position will require export-control authorization prior to starting employment. This position requires compliance with state and federal laws/codes and Texas A&M University System/TAMU policies, regulations, rules and procedures All tasks and job responsibilities must be performed safely without injury to self or others in compliance with System and University safety requirements Why Join the Javelina Nation? No matter where you're located—on campus or online—you are part of a mission that transforms lives and makes a difference across the state of Texas and beyond. ________________________________________________________________________ Important Immigration Information: A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. This role works closely with the Continuous Improvement team, Enterprise Applications, and functional departments to translate operational needs into practical system solutions that improve efficiency, consistency, and user experience. Position is located on the Tarleton State main campus with normal work hours of Monday to Friday; 8am to 5pm or as work requirements indicate. Serves as Campus Security Authority (CSA). Key Responsibilities Translate business requirements into technology solutions. Configure, implement, and support solutions across institutional technology platforms. Design and maintain workflow automation and low-code/no-code solutions. Partner with stakeholders to improve business processes through technology. Collaborate with Enterprise Applications and IT teams to deliver scalable solutions. Support evaluation, testing, and implementation of AI-enabled features within approved institutional platforms. Identify opportunities to apply automation and AI-enabled tools to improve business processes, reduce manual effort, and enhance service delivery. Conduct testing, troubleshooting, and solution validation activities. Document requirements, configurations, and implementation outcomes. Evaluate technology capabilities and recommend solution approaches. Communicate technical concepts and solution impacts to stakeholders. Participate in process discovery, solution design, and implementation planning. Support training, adoption, and continuous improvement activities. Manage multiple projects and priorities in a collaborative environment. Perform other duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Education and Experience Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Business Administration, Computer Science, Educational Technology, or a related field required. Five years of experience in business systems analysis, technology implementation, enterprise applications, workflow automation, or related roles. Experience working with platforms such as Salesforce, Banner, Canvas LMS, Kuali Build, Microsoft Power Platform, or similar technologies. title: Principal Product Manager, Member Experience
jd_text: Join the team leading the next evolution of virtual care. At Teladoc Health, you are empowered to bring your true self to work while helping millions of people live their healthiest lives. Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens. Summary of Position You'll own the vision and strategy for the core member software experience across the full care journey, from the moment a member first discovers what care is available through getting care and following up afterward. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who thinks in systems, has strong product design sense, and uses data and user research to decide what to build and why. You'll turn ambiguous, cross-cutting problems into clear direction, set a vision that delights members while working within the realities of a complex, regulated healthcare environment, and earn trust with partners from engineering leads to senior executives. You operate with a high degree of autonomy and are the person we point at a complex, high-priority problem to chase down end to end. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Set the vision and strategy: define a multi-year vision and roadmap for the core member-facing software experience across the full care journey, and prioritize smartly among competing efforts to deliver the greatest value for members. Think in systems: map the complete member journey end to end, break down ambiguous, cross-cutting problems into clear requirements, and drive alignment across engineering, design, data science, clinical, operations, and marketing. Champion great design: partner with design as a strategic differentiator, contribute directly to design reviews and critiques, push back where warranted, and hold a high bar on craft and attention to detail, connecting the smallest interaction elements into a coherent end-to-end experience, especially where metrics don't fully capture what members feel. Drive outcomes with data and research: use user research, behavioral data, and A/B testing to inform decisions and pivot or stop work when the evidence demands it; define success metrics, and counter-metrics focused on activation, engagement, retention, and lasting member value. Take ideas from concept to impact: convert opportunities into well-scoped projects, lead the team through prototyping, launch, and iteration, and hold the team to a high standard of execution. Lead up, down, and across the organization: serve as a credible senior product voice with engineers and executives alike, synthesize complexity into a simple, persuasive narrative, create clarity without pretending certainty by communicating what we believe, what we've learned, and what remains unknown, and carry complex conversations independently. Raise the bar for product: mentor other product managers on product craft, systems thinking, and analytical rigor. The time spent on each responsibility reflects an estimate and is subject to change dependent on business needs. Supervisory Responsibilities No Qualifications Expected for Position 12+ years of product management experience at a senior level in consumer-facing products at meaningful scale, with enough breadth and variety of problems to think from first principles. Direct ownership of at least one consumer product experience from ambiguous problem to measurable adoption, with evidence of discovering product direction rather than only delivering against an established roadmap. Strong command of B2C product dynamics, including onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, and habit formation across multi-step user journeys. Strong product analytics proficiency, including experience with product analytics tools and SQL; able to combine qualitative and quantitative insight to make sound decisions with incomplete information, tell signal from noise, and explain what was learned beyond which number moved. Strong technical fluency, including an understanding of how modern software applications work, APIs, data flows, and system dependencies; able to collaborate effectively with engineering and understand technical constraints and trade-offs without requiring deep platform or architectural expertise. Executive presence and a proven ability to build trust with business and engineering stakeholders and to influence senior leaders in a matrixed organization without formal authority. Empathy for users navigating health concerns and genuine conviction about the role technology can play in improving healthcare access and outcomes; experience in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated, high-stakes categories is a plus but not required. Exceptional written and verbal communication; fluency at both altitudes, from articulating a differentiated vision to working through the detailed tradeoffs required to ship it; low ego and high ownership; the judgment to balance collaborative openness with decisive vision-setting, and comfort advocating for a direction among ambiguous options in fast-moving environments where the answer isn't handed to you. Travel: Up to 10% Travel expectations are approximate and subject to change based on business needs. Bonus Qualifications Strong product design sense: fluent in design language, able to give structured, differentiated critique and bring taste and craft to design conversations; experience working in design-forward product organizations. jd_text: Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period! For more information about our benefits, see below! We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet." Overview We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Sr. Manager, Data Scientist to lead a team of talented data scientists focused on advancing our marketing analytics capabilities. This role will be instrumental in translating complex marketing challenges into data-driven solutions, driving insights that optimize campaign performance, enhance customer understanding, and maximize ROI. The ideal candidate will possess a strong blend of technical expertise in data science, proven leadership abilities, and a deep understanding of marketing strategies and analytics. Duties & Responsibilities Team Leadership & Management Lead, mentor, and develop a team of 2-3 data scientists, fostering a collaborative and high-performing environment. Set clear goals, provide regular feedback, and conduct performance reviews for team members. Support the professional growth of team members through training, conferences, and challenging assignments. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify opportunities for leveraging data science to create business value. Manage competing priorities across multiple projects while ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards. Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of data science projects, from ideation and prototyping to production and monitoring. Conduct rigorous reviews of statistical and optimization models to ensure they meet business needs, technical standards, and ethical guidelines. Executive Presence including excellent communication and presentation skills, written and verbal and ability to communicate at all levels within large organizations. Technical Execution & Innovation Apply a strong understanding of statistical modeling, machine learning algorithms, and experimental design. Oversee the end-to-end data science lifecycle, including data collection, cleaning, feature engineering, model development, validation, deployment, and monitoring. Ensure the integrity and accuracy of data used for analysis and modeling. Contribute to the development of scalable data pipelines and analytical infrastructure in collaboration with data engineering teams. Hands-on experience deploying models from development through production in a modern data science stack Champion the use of cutting-edge data science techniques to solve challenging marketing problems. Strategic Marketing Analytics & Insights Partner closely with marketing leadership and stakeholders to understand business objectives and identify opportunities for data science to drive impact. Define and execute the roadmap for marketing analytics initiatives, aligning with overall business strategy. Lead the design, development, and implementation of advanced analytical models (e.g., attribution modeling, customer lifetime value (CLTV),, segmentation, propensity modeling, personalization algorithms, media mix modeling (MMM)). Develop and implement A/B and multivariate testing frameworks and methodologies to measure the impact of marketing initiatives. Stay abreast of industry trends and emerging technologies in data science and marketing analytics. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams including Marketing, Product, Sales, IT, and Data Engineering. Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for marketing teams and senior leadership. Act as a subject matter expert in data science and marketing analytics within the organization. Education Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field. Experience 10+ years of progressive experience in data science, with at least 2-3 years in a leadership or management role, leading a team of data scientists. Extensive experience with ML predictive analytics, optimization algorithms, and large-scale data processing frameworks. Significant experience working in cross-functional teams and influencing stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Demonstrable experience with many of the following: Demand Forecasting, Segmentation, Testing, Predictive Customer Response, Price Optimization, Marketing Mix Modeling, Customer Journey Analytics, Next Best Product/Offer, Customer Elasticity (Market Response Modeling), Skills & Competencies Expert proficiency in Python (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch) and/or R. Strong SQL skills for data extraction and manipulation. Experience with big data technologies (e.g., Spark, Hadoop) and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure). Solid understanding of statistical inference, experimental design, and causal analysis. Proven ability to build, deploy, and monitor machine learning models in production environments. Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels. Strong problem-solving abilities and a strategic mindset. jd_text: Texas Capital is built to help businesses and their leaders. Our depth of knowledge and expertise allows us to bring the best of the big firms at a scale that works for our clients, with highly experienced bankers who truly invest in people’s success — today and tomorrow. While we are rooted in core financial products, we are differentiated by our approach. Our bankers are seasoned financial experts who possess deep experience across a multitude of industries. Equally important, they bring commitment — investing the time and resources to understand our clients’ immediate needs, identify market opportunities and meet long-term objectives . At Texas Capital, we do more than build business success. We build long-lasting relationships. Texas Capital provides a variety of benefits to colleagues, including health insurance coverage, wellness program, fertility and family building aids, life and disability insurance, retirement savings plans with a generous 401K match, paid leave programs, paid holidays, and paid time off (PTO). Headquartered in Dallas with offices in Austin, Fort Worth, Houston, Richardson, Plano and San Antonio, Texas Capital was recently named Best Regional Bank in 2024 by Bankrate and was named to The Dallas Morning News ’ Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex Top Workplaces 2023 and GoBankingRate’s 2023 list of Best Regional Banks. For more information about joining our team, please visit us at www.texascapitalbank.com . Overview This Financial Systems Senior Analyst role is a vital member of the Enterprise Business Management (EBM) Office that provides direct oversight of enterprise finance platforms and data workflows across Texas Capital Bank. This high-profile role combines data integration expertise with platform governance in support of the EBM Office's expanding charter. The position provides opportunities to work directly with finance, technology, and business leadership in designing data flows, managing platform configurations, and ensuring data usability across downstream systems. This role has a strong systems and data focus and will require a self-motivated, action-oriented strategic thinker who can prioritize, communicate, and collaborate to build relationships across departmental lines and drive platform initiatives to successful completion. Responsibilities · Be a key partner to the Enterprise Finance Leadership Team; supporting enterprise business management capabilities across several models, projects and their reporting in Apptio. · Design and document data flow architecture; identify integration points, data dependencies, and handoff sequences. · Establish data mapping standards and master data governance across platforms to ensure consistency in definitions, hierarchies, and dimensions. · Contribute to the development of data governance policies and practices for platforms facilitated by the EBM Office. · Support the establishment of data quality standards, validation rules, and remediation workflows; track SLAs for data completeness, accuracy, and timeliness. · Document platform capabilities, data schemas, and business rules; maintain current documentation of platform configuration and data lineage. · Identify manual processes and redundant data entry across finance systems; design and implement automated workflows to reduce rework and improve timeliness. · Act as a liaison between the EBM Office, Corporate Finance, IT, and business units on platform, data, and allocation matters. · Monitor data integration health, latency, and quality; proactively identify and resolve integration failures or data anomalies. Requirements · An undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Finance, or related field. · A minimum of 5 years of related experience in data integration, ETL, data governance, or enterprise systems administration. · Initiative to identify data quality issues, scope and logically structure an analysis, extract relevant insights, and communicate with a point of view. · Strong technical foundation: SQL, relational databases, and data modeling; ability to read and interpret technical documentation. · Expertise in data governance frameworks, master data management, or information architecture. · Problem solver attitude with a curious mindset. · Self-motivated, results-oriented self-starter. · Ability to build relationships with, and provide thought leadership to, officers of TCB. · Experience thriving in a dynamic and fast-moving work environment. · Experience effectively managing several work streams and projects concurrently. · Superior analytical skills and attention to detail. · Strong communication (written and oral) and partnering skills. · Strong PC skills, including proficiency in Excel and experience sourcing data from database applications. Preferred · Familiarity with Apptio or relevant platform data models. · Experience with technology business management (TBM), enterprise business management (EBM), financial planning and analysis (FP&A), or enterprise finance. · Hands-on experience with ETL tools (e.g., Informatica, Talend, MuleSoft) or API-based integration patterns. · Experience with data governance tools or metadata management platforms. · Prior experience supporting a technology organization. · Certification in ITSM, data management, governance, or relevant platform (e.g., Apptio Training). · MBA/MIS or similar degree/certification. The duties listed above are the essential functions, or fundamental duties within the job classification. The essential functions of individual positions within the classification may differ. Texas Capital Bank may assign reasonably related additional duties to individual employees consistent with standard departmental policy.Texas Capital is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Senior Manager, Retail Operations
jd_text: Your Opportunity as the Senior Manager, Retail Operations This role leads the strategy, governance, and execution model for national retail coverage across J.M. Smucker Company priorities. This position is accountable for strengthening the company’s partnership with Acosta and other retail partners, improving the effectiveness of the retail coverage model, increasing accountability for retail investment, and ensuring retail activity translates into measurable business value. The role connects retail execution, customer priorities, display management, reporting, financial governance, and data-led on-shelf availability. Working across Sales, Procurement, Finance, Deduction Management, Transportation, category teams, external broker partners, and customer-facing teams, this leader establishes clear processes, improves execution, and directs resources toward the highest-value opportunities. Location: Working Remote, USA and residing near a major airport Work Arrangements: Approximate travel 50% or as business needs require. In this role you will: Lead Retail Operations strategy and execution. · Develop and continuously refine the national retail broker model across Food and Beverage, Hostess, convenience, and other priority retail channels, including dedicated and syndicated coverage, convenience-store support, back-office support, and customer-specific retail programs. · Set retail execution strategy across selling, merchandising, distribution correction, promotional execution, in-aisle activity, secondary displays, and total-company display execution. · Prioritize retail resources using account-level needs, store productivity, execution requirements, and expected return. · Support Perfect Store, 360 Selling, seasonal limited-time offers, shipper deployment, display management, and customer-specific execution initiatives. Strengthen retail partner governance and accountability. · Serve as a primary point of contact for Acosta and other retail partner relationships, ensuring activities, coverage levels, costs, and expected outcomes are clearly defined. · Lead scorecards, monthly and quarterly business reviews, customer coverage reviews, and recurring performance discussions that connect field activity with customer priorities and measurable business results. · Challenge coverage levels and redirect resources when productivity, execution requirements, or expected return do not support the investment. · Partner with Procurement, Finance, Sales, and Deduction Management to define broker services, negotiate appropriate rates, validate billing, monitor variances, and connect costs with services delivered. Advance data-led retail execution and on-shelf availability. · Use customer-specific data, Circana insights, real-time out-of-stock scanning, and authorized-item reporting to identify high-value distribution and availability opportunities before representatives enter stores. · Translate alerts, scorecards, and key performance indicator reporting into actionable priorities for retail representatives and sales teams. · Support customer initiatives such as Kroger On-Shelf Availability by connecting store-level corrections with customer ordering processes and broader retail productivity goals. · Measure execution impact across store visits, out-of-stocks, void correction, cases influenced, cases packed out, display execution, and priority-program performance. Improve planning discipline and field communication. · Drive earlier communication among Sales, Retail Operations, customers, and broker partners to improve execution windows, reset readiness, and store-level awareness. · Establish recurring customer coverage reviews focused on shipment and key performance indicator tracking, planogram compliance, retail tools, and 90-day retail planning calendars. · Facilitate ad hoc requests from internal sales teams, field teams, and category partners while ensuring ownership and priorities are clear. · Lead internal share-out meetings to communicate progress, risks, opportunities, and required follow-up actions. Manage display, freight, and retail investment governance. · Maintain oversight of the Hostess display-management relationship, budget, ordering, deployment, inventory, and shipment planning. · Establish disciplined financial review, return-on-investment evaluation, and approval processes before deploying display equipment or retail resources. · Identify opportunities for cost avoidance, improved financial control, reduced freight exposure, and stronger accountability for retail investment. Lead cross-functional problem solving and process improvement. · Coordinate Sales priorities, field execution, Procurement discussions, Finance requirements, deduction-management needs, display production, analytics, transportation considerations, and customer-specific requirements. · Diagnose execution challenges by identifying whether root causes involve coverage, communication, inventory, reporting, store authorization, timing, ownership, or process gaps. · Partner with Pet and other counterpart teams to develop standard operating procedures, best practices, execution strategies, and consistent ways of working. What we are looking for: Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree. 10+ years of experience in consumer packaged goods (CPG), retail operations, sales strategy, customer execution, broker management, or related commercial roles. Experience directing a national retail agency or broker partner and managing retail coverage models, services, costs, billing, resource allocation, scorecards, and performance reviews. Strong knowledge of retail management, broker operations, customer execution, store-level merchandising, planograms, display and promotional execution, distribution correction, and on-shelf availability. Experience translating customer, syndicated, store-level, and operational data into field priorities, measurable outcomes, and practical actions. Strong commercial and financial acumen, including evaluating retail investments and prioritizing resources based on customer needs, productivity, execution requirements, and expected return. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes and create clear operating processes that connect field activity, customer priorities, reporting, and financial governance. Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives and working effectively across Sales, Procurement, Finance, Deduction Management, Transportation, category and analytics teams, external partners, and customer-facing organizations. Strong communication, facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, including the ability to establish accountability and influence senior leaders without direct authority. Ability to lead through ambiguity, make sound decisions, balance immediate execution with long-term operating-model improvements, and create effective planning, governance, and executive-update routines. Additional skills and experience that we think would make someone successful in this role: Master of Business Administration, other relevant advanced degree, or certification in retail analytics, project management, process improvement, or financial management. Experience working with Acosta, Advantage Solutions, or a comparable national retail agency across food, beverage, convenience, or other consumer packaged goods retail channels. Experience with Perfect Store, 360 Selling, seasonal programs, display deployment, planogram compliance, and on-shelf availability initiatives. Experience overseeing display management, freight, deduction management, or related retail investment processes. Experience using customer-specific, Circana, authorized-item, out-of-stock, or comparable retail analytics tools. #LI-MR1 The Right Place for You We are bold, kind, strive to do the right thing, we play to win, and we believe in a strong community that thrives together. Our culture is rooted in our Basic Beliefs , and we believe in supporting every employee by meeting their physical, emotional, and financial needs. Stay connected with us on LinkedIn® We're an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, age, national origin, disability status or protected veteran status.

Monitor Optimizely Opal credit consumption and report run rate to the Senior Marketing Operations Manager.
