title: Area Credit Manager
jd_text: Position Purpose: The Area Credit Manager role at SRS exists to safeguard and expedite recovery of the company's assigned account receivable portfolio, under the oversight of the Regional Credit Manager. The incumbent will handle collection calls, customer account reviews, provide guidance on account status to internal teams, process credit applications and job accounts, while also maintaining diligent notes on clients within the company system. This role also necessitates strategic collaboration with both internal and external stakeholders, and involves direct training for progression into a Regional Credit Manager role, strengthening the company's overall financial management practices. Key Responsibilities: Oversee and manage the company's accounts receivable portfolio, ensuring timely collection and safeguarding of assets, under direction from the Regional Credit Manager and the Director of Credit. Make consistent collection calls on due and overdue accounts receivable, documenting each interaction within the company's digital systems for record keeping and company-wide transparency. Regularly review and release orders from ticket holds after careful evaluation. Process and approve credit applications, extending and maintaining credit lines within authority level. Provide continuous oversight of lien and bond rights, requiring thorough knowledge of notices, mechanics liens, and bond claim processes to ensure collection of job balances. Communicate proactively with both internal and external clients, including the sales team and management, to ensure clear understanding of account statuses, credit applications, and company's credit policy. Conduct thorough customer account reviews, providing recommendations on account handling to internal stakeholders as necessary. Track and reconcile any deductions, overseeing joint-check payments and enforcing company credit policy consistently. Participate fully in credit team meetings, learning from interactions and regularly contributing to department-wide discussions for continuous improvement. Direct Manager Direct Reports: The Area Credit Manager at SRS reports directly to the Regional Credit Manager and/or the Director of Credit. The manager utilizes these key supervisory relationships to formulate decisions on credit lines, lien enforcement, and credit policy, while also seeking guidance for continued professional development towards a Regional Credit Manager role. This position does not oversee any direct reports as it is largely independent, although the manager is expected to engage actively and routinely with the Sales team and the Credit team. The successful execution of this role involves comprehensive communication skills, dedicated teamwork with peers, and accurate and timely reporting to superiors. Despite having no direct managerial responsibilities, the Area Credit Manager is required to guide and educate others, including Sales team and customers. They are also expected to uphold the highest standards of credit policy enforcement and provide valuable input in credit team meetings and key performance indicator reviews, ensuring the smooth running of the Company's overall financial operations. Travel Requirements: The Area Credit Manager's role at SRS necessitates domestic travel, primarily for in-person meetings with regional teams, customer visits, or important company events, as directed by the Regional Credit Manager and/or Director of Credit. Physical Requirements: The Area Credit Manager role at SRS generally operates in a professional office environment and as such requires the ability to use standard office equipment such as computers and phones. The ability to remain stationary for extended periods of time, intermittently stand, walk, bend, reach, and perform manual tasks, such as filing or lifting up to 20 pounds, is expected in regular office operations. Good visual acuity and proficiency in reading, writing, and communicating effectively in English is necessary for the satisfactory completion of the essential functions of this position. As an employer committed to ADA principles, the Company is prepared to make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. While performing the duties of this job, reasonable accommodations may include adjustment of the workspace, modifying material or presentations, providing additional technology aids or offering flexibility in work schedule to enable the performance of essential job functions. We encourage candidates to discuss potential accommodations with us and assure that all discussions related to accommodations will remain confidential. At the Company, it is our policy to treat all employees and job applicants fairly and without regard to physical abilities. We aim to maintain a work environment that is inclusive and respectful to all, reinforcing our commitment to equal opportunities. We appreciate your interest in the Area Credit Manager role and look forward to receiving your application. Working Conditions: As the Area Credit Manager at SRS, you will operate in a hybrid environment; remote work is standard with local travel to branches and infrequent air travel for Credit or corporate meetings. This role is characterized by a fast-paced, deadline-driven atmosphere that requires diligence and high levels of concentration. You will find yourself working closely alongside various team members, including the Regional Credit Manager and the Director of Credit, escalating matters to them as necessary. You will also have regular interaction with internal and external customers, calling for exceptional interpersonal and communication skills. Additionally, this role requires a substantial amount of time spent on computer-related activities such as processing credit applications, reviewing account information, maintaining notes and tracking deductions. You will be expected to monitor critical deadlines related to Notices, mechanics' liens, and bond claims, requiring a high level of organization and attention to detail. Furthermore, you may be required to participate in cash application interactions and attend both credit team meetings and key performance indicator reviews. Overall, this position demands a professional who thrives under pressure, possesses excellent problem-solving abilities, and upholds the highest standards of credit policy enforcement. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum 5 years of experience in Credit Management, preferably within a similar industry. Credentialed as a Credit Business Associate (CBA) from the National Association of Credit Management is preferred. Proven experience with the protection and collection of account receivable (AR) portfolios, including making collection calls and providing lien/prelien support. Demonstrated excellence in communication and negotiation skills to effectively liaise with internal and external stakeholders. Proficiency in evaluating and releasing orders from ticket hold, and maintaining accurate notes in company computer systems. Experience in processing and approving credit applications and establishing credit lines within authority level. Demonstrated abilities in deduction tracking and reconciliation, handling joint check reviews and enforcing credit policies. Proficient in guiding and educating sales teams and customers, in addition to coordinating with the sales team and credit team. Experience in monitoring deadlines for Notices, mechanics liens and bond claims. Exceptional analytical ability and attention to detail. Adept at working independently without close oversight, but also a team player who productively collaborates with immediate team and across functions. Proficient with MS Office Suite, especially Excel; experience with company-specific software would be beneficial. Excellent business acumen, professional demeanor, and strong ethical judgement. Ability to meet assigned deadlines, including strong multitasking and organizational skills, and learning agility. Familiarity with cash application interaction and participation in credit team meetings as well as key performance indicator reviews is preferred. Preferred Qualifications: Proven experience as a Credit Manager or a similar role in the finance sector. A minimum of 5 years' experience in credit management is desirable. Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, or a related field. A Master's degree or professional certification such as NACM's CBA would be advantageous. Proven proficiency with corporate accounting software systems for managing account receivables. Familiarity with the specific software used by the Company will be a plus. Demonstrable ability to evaluate and establish credit lines, preferably within a large business or corporate setting. Familiarity with credit applications and approval process within the terms of authority level is a must. Superior written and verbal communication skills with an ability to communicate effectively with sales teams and interact professionally with both internal and external customers. Strong understanding of financial laws and regulations, particularly regarding liens, bond claims, and other aspects related to credit and collections. Experience in deduction tracking and reconciliation, joint check review and enforcing credit policies within a corporate setting. Proficient in Microsoft Office suite, especially in data analysis and presentation tools such as Excel and PowerPoint. Strong leadership skills with a commitment to lead regular credit team meetings and conduct key performance indicator reviews. Experience in training and guiding sales teams, customers, or junior staff members would be beneficial. Exceptional organizational skills and an ability to work under pressure, maintaining accuracy even while handling multiple tasks and meeting strict deadlines. Demonstrated ability to compile, verify, and sort information to prepare source data for computer entry. Proven experience in enhancing the financial health of a company by effectively overseeing account collections and managing credit policies. Ability to interpret agreements, financial statements, and credit reports. A strong sense of integrity and confidentiality. Minimum Education: The Minimum Education required for the position of Area Credit Manager includes a Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field. Professional certification such as Certified Credit Professional (CCP) is desirable. Prior experience in a credit management role and comprehensive knowledge of credit-related laws and regulations are essential. Proficiency in credit management software and advanced skills in Microsoft Office Suite are also a requirement. Exceptional analytical abilities, sound judgment, and excellent communication skills are expected. Preferred Education: The preferred academic qualification for the Area Credit Manager role at the Company extends beyond minimum requirements to include a Master's Degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field, complemented by relevant industry certifications. Minimum Years Of Work Experience: Candidates applying for the role of Area Credit Manager should bring a substantial tenure of relevant professional experience. A minimum of 5 years in a credit management role, preferably within a comparable industry, is required. This timeframe is non-negotiable, as it ensures that the individual in this position possesses a robust understanding of best practices in credit management, as well as a demonstrable track-record of success in protecting significant accounts receivable portfolios. Certifications: None required. A Credit Business Associate (CBA) or Credit Business Fellow (CBF) certification from the National Association of Credit Management (NACM) is preferred. Competencies: Credit Management Expertise: Knowledge and understanding of the credit process, from evaluating credit applications to initiating credit lines, as well as handling AR collections, is crucial for success in this role. Exceptional Communication Skills: The ability to communicate efficiently and professionally with both external and internal stakeholders is required to interpret and enforce credit policies, as well as to guide and educate sales teams and customers. Strong Analytical Skills: The credit manager needs to have strong analytical skills to evaluate creditworthiness and make informed decisions. Organizational Skills: This role requires exceptional organizational abilities to manage necessary timelines for notices, track deductions, complete lien waivers and perform joint check reviews. Technical Aptitude: Mastery of corporate computer systems, the ability to maintain detailed account notes, and engagement with cash application interaction is necessary. Regulatory Understanding: A solid grasp of mechanics liens, bond claims, and associated legal processes is crucial to this position. Collaborative Leadership: The credit manager should participate in team meetings, be capable of guiding others, and work closely with the Regional Credit Manager. Instructional Skills: The capacity to educate the sales team and customers on credit policy, account procedures, and other critical responsibilities is another significant competency for an area credit manager. title: Manager, IT Support Services
jd_text: Position Purpose: The Manager, IT Support Services is responsible for leading and overseeing the Service Desk Team, ensuring the delivery of exemplary customer service and technical support to employees across our Corporate Campus and Branches. This role requires strategic leadership to manage the Team effectively, ensuring compliance with established processes and procedures while fostering an environment of continuous development through mentorship and training. The Manager collaborates with senior IT leadership to align technology needs with business objectives and supports executive-level requests, contributing to critical IT projects and providing insightful KPI and metrics reports to the Director, IT Operations. Key Responsibilities: Provide strategic leadership and mentorship to the IT Service Desk Team, fostering a culture of self-sufficiency and teamwork to enhance overall operational efficiency. Ensure strict adherence to established Service Desk processes and Change Management policies, maintaining high standards of compliance and operational integrity. Offer advanced technical direction and innovative problem-solving strategies to the Team, enhancing their ability to tackle complex troubleshooting scenarios with efficiency. Oversee and optimize the IT Service Management (ITSM) ticket assignment and escalation process, ensuring thorough documentation, accurate routing, and prompt resolution to meet service level agreements. Develop and implement ongoing training and development programs to nurture talent and advance the skill sets of Team members, supporting their professional growth. Efficiently manage workforce planning, ensuring comprehensive coverage across all support channels, including overseeing scheduling, approving overtime, and facilitating leave management. Collaborate effectively with IT Leadership to strategically forecast and procure necessary hardware and software resources, aligning with organizational needs and future demands. Deliver insightful KPI and metrics reports to the Sr. Director, IT Operations, providing data-driven recommendations for continuous improvement and service excellence. Direct Manager Direct Reports: The Manager, IT Support Services reports directly to the Sr. Manager or Director, IT Infrastructure & Operations. This role is responsible for leading and providing strategic direction to the Service Desk Team, ensuring that top-tier customer service and support are delivered to Corporate Campus and Branch employees across various divisions. The Manager does not hold any direct reports; instead, the position involves collaborative partnerships with the Team and Sr. IT Leadership to enhance IT support services. Duties include monitoring service compliance, overseeing ITSM processes, and participating in strategic IT projects. The Manager also plays a key role in metrics reporting and resource forecasting, working closely with the broader IT Leadership Team. title: IT Portfolio and Demand Management Specialist
jd_text: Pay range: $106,787 - $160,180 annually, based on experience. In addition, this role is eligible to work remotely from an approved state by St. Charles (please refer to the list). If you do not reside in an approved listed state (or do not plan to relocate to an approved listed state) we request, you do not apply for this particular position. Approved states by St. Charles: Oregon, Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Idaho, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah, and Wisconsin. This position comes with a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, and a generous Earned Time Off (ETO) program. ST. CHARLES HEALTH SYSTEM JOB DESCRIPTION TITLE: IT Portfolio and Demand Management Specialist REPORTS TO POSITION: IT Manager Customer Experience DEPARTMENT: Information Technology DATE LAST REVIEWED: September 2026 OUR VISION: Creating America’s healthiest community, together OUR MISSION: In the spirit of love and compassion, better health, better care, better value OUR VALUES: Accountability, Caring and Teamwork DEPARTMENT SUMMARY: The Information Technology (IT) department helps improve the work of our caregivers by providing efficient systems, comprehensive training, and stellar customer service. We do this by taking pride in the integrity of our workflows, data security, and training delivery. We partner with our customers to best leverage various technologies to achieve the best patient outcomes possible by implementing new hardware and software solutions, upgrading existing environments, protecting the data we store, and integrating different solutions to achieve a seamless experience. POSITION OVERVIEW : The IT Portfolio and Demand Management Specialist facilitates the IT demand management function by overseeing the intake, evaluation, and prioritization of technology-related requests across the organization. This role partners closely with business and IT leaders to ensure proposed initiatives align with strategic priorities, operational objectives, compliance requirements, and available resource capacity. The position establishes intake standards, facilitates decision-ready business cases, maintains clear visibility into the demand pipeline, and supports portfolio decisions that optimize the delivery of IT services, enhancements, and projects. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES: Facilitate the IT demand management process by capturing, evaluating, and prioritizing incoming requests from business units to ensure alignment with organizational strategy, operational needs, and resource capacity. Establish and enforce intake standards to ensure demands are accurately classified as service requests, enhancements, optimization efforts, or projects, enabling efficient routing and decision-making. Develop, maintain, and communicate portfolio dashboards, executive summaries, scorecards, and pipeline reports that provide transparent visibility into demand intake, prioritization, status, portfolio health, resource capacity, and decision points. Partner with business and IT stakeholders to organize, validate, and mature business cases; define scope, objectives, benefits, assumptions, dependencies, funding considerations, and the appropriate path for each request, including conversion to project work, operational support, optimization, or other intake channels. Ensure business cases are complete and decision-ready by coordinating required inputs such as approvals, level-of-effort estimates, discovery findings, architectural review, and stakeholder alignment. Facilitate cross-functional assessment of regulatory, security, technical, and operational risks associated with new demands to support informed prioritization and governance decisions. Monitor and administer the demand intake lifecycle, ensuring requests progress through defined stages such as submission, triage, discovery, estimation, approval, deferral, rejection, or conversion to project or operational work. Coordinate the assignment and tracking of non-project work to the appropriate operational pathways, ensuring accurate categorization, accountability, and follow-through for intake items that do not become formal projects. Ensure proposed initiatives are reviewed for compliance with legal, regulatory, privacy, and organizational requirements prior to approval and execution. Govern the demand pipeline and portfolio backlog to ensure initiatives are scored, ranked, prioritized, and sequenced in alignment with enterprise strategy, operational priorities, technical dependencies, financial stewardship, risk, and available organizational capacity. Define, implement, and continuously refine prioritization criteria, scoring methods, and review practices that support consistent portfolio and demand management decisions. Facilitate recurring demand and portfolio review forums by preparing agendas, decision materials, scoring summaries, capacity views, tradeoff options, and follow-up actions for leadership review and direction. Maintain portfolio data quality within demand and portfolio management tools, ensuring request records, stage gates, approvals, benefit statements, priority scores, resource estimates, and disposition decisions remain accurate and current. Leverage ServiceNow Strategic Portfolio Management capabilities, including demand management, portfolio planning, resource management, project portfolio management, reporting, and workflow automation, to support consistent intake, tracking, prioritization, and portfolio decision-making. Partner with the PMO to track active portfolio health and ensure that approved demands are delivering their intended strategic value. Monitor resource capacity across IT functions and provide recommendations on timing, sequencing, and tradeoff decisions to balance incoming demand with current commitments and operational support needs. Design and maintain tools, templates, and intake frameworks that support project managers and leaders in resource planning, effort estimation, and demand transparency. Partner with project and operational leaders to monitor portfolio execution, identify resource constraints, and adjust allocations or priorities as needed to support successful delivery. Provides and oversees team’s delivery of customer service in a manner that promotes goodwill, is timely, efficient, and accurate. Supports the vision, mission, and values of the organization in all respects. Provides and maintains a safe environment for caregivers, patients, and guests. Collaborates with teams to review processes and identify/implement opportunities for improvements, applying Lean principles, concepts, and tools. Conducts all activities with the highest standards of professionalism and confidentiality. Complies with all applicable laws, regulations, policies and procedures, supporting the organization’s corporate integrity efforts by acting in an ethical and appropriate manner, reporting known or suspected violation of applicable rules, and cooperating fully with all organizational investigations and proceedings. May perform additional duties of similar complexity within the organization, as required or assigned. EDUCATION: Required: Bachelor’s degree or combination of education, related industry certification, and experience to perform the full scope of the position. Preferred: LICENSURE/CERTIFICATION/REGISTRATION: Required: N/A Preferred: ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Strategic Portfolio Management (CIS-SPM) or completion of ServiceNow Strategic Portfolio Management training preferred. At least one (1) IT or professional certification such as ServiceNow, ITIL, PMP, Agile, Lean, or portfolio management certification. EXPERIENCE: Required: Minimum of five (5) years of IT or similar professional experience, including recent experience, preferably within the last three to five years, supporting demand intake, portfolio coordination, project intake, operational prioritization, or resource capacity planning in a healthcare, clinical, hospital, ambulatory, affiliate, or similarly regulated environment. Preferred: ServiceNow experience is highly preferred, particularly experience with ServiceNow Strategic Portfolio Management, ServiceNow Demand Management, Project Portfolio Management, Resource Management, reporting, workflow automation, resource visibility, intake scoring, prioritization, and portfolio decision support. Experience with similar enterprise portfolio management platforms may be considered. ADDITIONAL POSITION INFORMATION: Travel: Ability to travel to business functions / trainings / meetings for all St. Charles Health System’s sites and affiliate sites as required. Occasional overnight travel will be required. General Skills: Manages a high volume of work with efficiency: Has a system for keeping tasks from slipping through the cracks. Able to juggle competing demands and prioritize without sacrificing quality. Identify deadlines and create plans to achieve deadlines. Resourceful : Consistently overcomes challenges and leverages resources to creatively solve problems. Proposes solutions to issues without much guidance. Proactively asks for help, anticipates problems, and course-corrects where needed. Attention to detail: Notices and corrects errors that others might overlook. Accountability: Acknowledges mistakes and turns them into learning opportunities. Strong sense of ownership, flexibility, and resilience : Plans ahead and find alternative paths to get to the finish line. Bounces back from setbacks and rejections. Holds self to high standards even when things are hectic. Ready to take advantage of unexpected opportunities; adapt quickly as things change. Attentive, empathetic leadership : Enthusiasm for meeting and engaging with people. Empathize with the teams we serve. Listen closely to understand needs or concerns and take steps based on that input. Take pride in providing clear, helpful information. Inclusive leadership and management : Brings a clear vision and recognizes the value of divergent perspectives. Approaches leadership with a mindset of “power with” rather than “power over” and regularly includes others in planning and decision-making. Able to make and communicate difficult decisions in the best interest of the organization. Creates plans for staff development, retention, strategy, and improving culture. Proactive problem solving: Proactively develop solutions to challenges, including by constantly looking at big-picture progress on the programs team, and by flagging any potential upcoming challenges in the organization overall. Mathematical Skills: Performs intermediate to advanced math (analysis, statistics, significant data, or number manipulation). Language Skills: Reads, writes, and speaks English. Computer Skills : Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, and Visio), database management, and document preparation. Demonstrated ability and experience in computer applications for project management and use of electronic medical record keeping systems Experience using ServiceNow or similar enterprise workflow, ITSM, demand management, or portfolio management platforms is highly preferred. title: Sr. Manager, Information Security
jd_text: Responsible for leading the day-to-day operations of a team of Information Security Analysts responsible for frontline monitoring and response to security alerts and incidents. Will work closely with IT leadership, security leadership, enterprise architecture, and business stakeholders to ensure the organization maintains effective, risk-based security practices that support business objectives. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Security Operations Leadership Lead and manage a team of Information Security Analysts responsible for monitoring, triaging, and responding to security alerts and incidents. Serve as an escalation point and actively participate in incident response activities to ensure rapid containment and resolution of security events. Establish and reinforce a culture of urgency, accountability, and continuous improvement within the security operations team. Drive improvements in detection, response processes, playbooks, tooling, and operational effectiveness. Challenge the status quo and identify opportunities to strengthen the organization’s defensive capabilities. Program Leadership & Execution Partner with leaders across Development, IT, Product, Operations, HR, Accounting, and Marketing to implement and operationalize the enterprise Information Security strategy. Own and manage key components of the Information Security program, ensuring consistent execution across business units. Translate strategic security objectives into actionable roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Support cross-functional teams in addressing security risks and strengthening security practices across the organization. Governance, Risk & Compliance Stay informed on emerging vulnerabilities and threats and partner with IT teams to ensure timely remediation. Operationalize the Information Security policy, standards, and guidelines framework. Support the implementation and ongoing operation of the Information Security Management System (ISMS) aligned to recognized frameworks (e.g., NIST, SOC, SOX, COBIT). Manage internal and external audit activities including security questionnaires, evidence collection, remediation tracking, and audit readiness. Metrics, Reporting & Continuous Improvement Develop and maintain security metrics and reporting that measure the effectiveness and maturity of the Information Security program. Provide regular reporting and insights to senior leadership and governance committees, escalating risks and gaps when appropriate. Identify and lead initiatives to improve security controls, processes, and operational maturity. Awareness, Resilience & Risk Management Oversee and mature the Security Awareness and Training program to strengthen the organization’s security culture. Partner with IT and business leaders to support the maturity of Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) programs. Monitor emerging information security threats, risks, and regulatory trends, communicating relevant impacts to leadership. Leadership & Culture Mentor and develop Information Security Analysts, helping them grow technically and professionally. Promote a proactive security culture by encouraging collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning. title: Application Support Specialist III
jd_text: Position Summary The Application Support Specialist III is a senior technical support professional responsible for providing advanced technical expertise in the support, maintenance, troubleshooting, and optimization of Dark Matter applications and supporting technologies. W orking with a high degree of independence, this role leads the investigation and resolution of complex client and production issues, coordinates critical incident response, performs root cause analysis, and drives sustainable corrective and preventive actions. Provides technical guidance concerning application support, business processes, integrations, and emerging AI-enabled solutions. Responsibilities are based on depth and scope of support expertise, client impact, and complexity of issue resolution. Job Responsibilities Provide advanced Tier 3 application support to clients and internal users, resolving complex functional, technical, configuration, integration, and data-related issues within established service-level and severity guidelines. Serve as a technical escalation point for critical incidents and high-severity production issues; assess impact and urgency, coordinate responders, maintain clear stakeholder communications, and support restoration of service. Reproduce reported issues in appropriate test environments; isolate contributing factors; document findings; and distinguish application defects from configuration, data, infrastructure, integration, or user-process issues. Lead root cause analysis for recurring or significant incidents and partner with Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, and other teams to implement corrective and preventive actions. Use SQL to investigate incidents, validate data, reconcile results, and support troubleshooting while following data-access, privacy, and security requirements. Review application logs, code paths, and system interactions; apply working knowledge of .NET and C# to debug issues and collaborate effectively with development teams. Monitor application health, availability, performance, and operational trends to identify service risks and recommend preventive improvements. S upports application deployments, releases, upgrades, maintenance activities, and change management processes. Analyze APIs, integrations, distributed services, and business process flows to identify dependencies, failure points, and downstream impacts. Create and maintain accurate knowledge articles, runbooks, troubleshooting guides, known-error records, and operational procedures. Identify opportunities to automate repetitive support activities, improve observability, reduce recurring incidents, and strengthen the client and user experience. Provide technical coaching and knowledge transfer to less experienced specialists without direct people-management responsibility. Handle other related responsibilities consistent with the role. AI Support & Innovation Responsibilities Supports AI-enabled applications, copilots, intelligent automation solutions, and machine learning-powered products utilized by Dark Matter and its clients. Monitors AI solution performance, usage trends, and operational effectiveness. Investigates and resolves issues related to AI-generated outputs, workflow failures, prompts, integrations, and data quality concerns. Assists with AI feature testing, validation, and user acceptance activities to ensure quality, accuracy, and business alignment. Collaborates with Product and Engineering teams to evaluate AI enhancements and recommend improvements. Document AI support procedures, governance requirements, best practices, and troubleshooting methodologies. S upport responsible AI practices by following established requirements for privacy, data security, regulatory compliance, human oversight, and appropriate use. Use approved AI tools in day-to-day work to improve research, analysis, troubleshooting, documentation, communication, and process efficiency while validating outputs before use. jd_text: GROW WITH US: Tandem Diabetes Care creates new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and their healthcare providers through a positively different experience. We’d love for you to team up with us to “innovate every day,” put “people first,” and take the “no-shortcuts” approach that has propelled us to become a leader in the diabetes technology industry. STAY AWESOME: Tandem Diabetes Care is proud to manufacture and sell the Tandem Mobi system and t:slim X2 insulin pump with Control-IQ+ technology — an advanced predictive algorithm that automates insulin delivery. But we’re so much more than that. Our company’s human-centered approach to design, development, and support delivers innovative products and services for people who use insulin. Because many of our own team members live with diabetes, or have a loved one impacted by diabetes, the work is personal, and we are committed to the cause. Learn more at tandemdiabetes.com A DAY IN THE LIFE: The Senior Digital Marketing Manager is responsible for leading integrated digital marketing strategies that build awareness, engage priority audiences, and drive measurable business results. This role connects paid media, email, web, audience activation, campaign measurement, and optimization into a cohesive customer experience across the full funnel. The position translates brand, product, and business objectives into audience-led strategies, scalable campaign plans, measurement frameworks, and clear optimization recommendations. The Senior Digital Marketing Manager partners closely with Analytics, Brand, Product Marketing, Brand Operations, Brand Experience, Sales, IT, Legal, Regulatory, Privacy, international teams, and external agencies to deliver effective digital programs in a fast-paced, regulated environment. A Senior Digital Marketing Manager's at Tandem are also responsible for: Leads integrated digital marketing strategy and execution across paid media, email, web, audience activation, and emerging digital channels in support of brand, product, launch, and business objectives. Translates audience insights, customer journeys, market priorities, and business goals into channel strategies, campaign briefs, media plans, testing roadmaps, and measurable performance goals. Owns digital campaign performance, including budget pacing, channel effectiveness, funnel progression, conversion, cost efficiency, and return on marketing investment. Builds measurement frameworks and dashboards with Analytics and Marketing Operations; synthesizes data into decision-ready insights, risks, tradeoffs, and optimization actions for senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders. Leads experimentation across audiences, creative, messaging, offers, landing pages, media mix, and campaign sequencing to improve performance and customer experience. Partners with Brand, Product Marketing, Creative, Web, CRM, Sales, Marketing Operations, IT, and other cross-functional teams to deliver coordinated omnichannel programs and consistent customer experiences. Supports international and multi-market launches by establishing scalable digital strategies, launch playbooks, channel requirements, timelines, measurement standards, and localization guidance for language, culture, media behavior, regulatory requirements, approved claims, and market-specific business needs. Manages external agencies, technology partners, direct reports, and/or project teams by setting clear scope, priorities, roles, deliverables, budgets, performance expectations, feedback, and accountability. Strengthens campaign enablement in partnership with Marketing Operations and technology teams, including audience activation, lead management, tracking, tagging, consent, and data quality. Ensures digital initiatives comply with company policies and applicable legal, regulatory, privacy, accessibility, and promotional review requirements, including Privacy/HIPAA where relevant. Monitors digital marketing trends, platform changes, competitive activity, and emerging technologies; recommends practical opportunities to improve reach, relevance, efficiency, and differentiation. WHEN & WHERE YOU’LL WORK: Remote: This position is fully remote and open to candidates within the United States. Equipment for the role will be provided and training will occur virtually. WHAT YOU’LL NEED: Demonstrated expertise in integrated digital strategy, paid media, lifecycle/email marketing, web experiences, audience activation, and campaign optimization. Deep expertise in integrated digital strategy, paid media, lifecycle/email marketing, web experiences, audience activation, campaign optimization, and full-funnel measurement. Strong knowledge of major advertising, analytics, tag management, and marketing automation platforms, with the ability to apply data to improve performance and customer experience. Ability to connect business objectives, audience insights, channel strategy, creative, media, measurement, and optimization into a cohesive plan. Strong analytical, project management, and program leadership skills, including the ability to manage multiple campaigns, launches, markets, agencies, budgets, and deadlines simultaneously. Proven ability to lead through influence, manage agencies or team members, collaborate across global and regional teams, and communicate strategies, insights, and recommendations clearly. EXTRA AWESOME: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Business, Communications, Digital Media, Analytics, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and applicable experience. Advanced degree or relevant digital marketing certifications preferred. 12-15 years of progressive digital marketing experience, including ownership of integrated, full-funnel campaigns across multiple digital channels. Experience leading complex campaigns, product launches, media budgets, agencies, vendors, and/or cross-functional teams. Experience supporting international or multi-market launches, including localization, regional coordination, and adaptation to market-specific requirements. Experience in medical devices, healthcare, or another regulated industry is preferred. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS: The starting base pay range for this position is $ 141,800 - $177,300 annually. Base pay will vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience and may also fluctuate depending on candidate’s location and the overall job market. In addition to base pay, Tandem offers a competitive compensation package that includes bonus and a robust benefits package. Tandem offers health care benefits such as medical, dental, vision available your first day, as well as health savings accounts and flexible saving accounts. You’ll also receive 11 paid holidays per year, a minimum of 20 days of paid time off (with accrual starting on day 1) and you will have access to a 401k plan with company match as well as an Employee Stock Purchase plan. Learn more about Tandem’s benefits here ! Tandem has good cause to conduct a review of criminal history information of candidates for this position, as this role may involve access to proprietary, sensitive and/or confidential information, including customer protected health information. This review is required to ensure that individuals in such roles uphold high standards of trust and integrity so as to protect the interests of our customers, employees, and stakeholders. SPONSORSHIP: Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE: At Tandem, we believe joy fuels excellence. That's why we've built a workplace that celebrates your achievements and supports your well-being. Our team thrives on pushing boundaries and fostering growth, all while maintaining a spirit of fun and camaraderie. This is just one of the ways we stay awesome! Explore the benefits and reasons to love Tandem at https://www.tandemdiabetes.com/careers . BE YOU, WITH US! We embrace the value that every single one of us brings to the table. But sometimes we forget that when we don’t meet 100% of a job description’s criteria – maybe you’re feeling that way right now? We encourage you to apply anyway. Because we want you to be you, with us. Tandem is firmly committed to being an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, sex, race, religion or belief, gender identity or expression, marriage/civil partnership, pregnancy/maternity, or sexual orientation. If you know someone who would be a great fit for this position, please share! title: Sr Operations Manager AV
jd_text: About TaskUs: TaskUs is a provider of outsourced digital services and next-generation customer experience to fast-growing technology companies, helping its clients represent, protect and grow their brands. Leveraging a cloud-based infrastructure, TaskUs serves clients in the fastest-growing sectors, including social media, e-commerce, gaming, streaming media, food delivery, ride-sharing, HiTech, FinTech, and HealthTech. The People First culture at TaskUs has enabled the company to expand its workforce to approximately 60,000 employees globally. Presently, we have a presence in twenty-three locations across twelve countries, which include the Philippines, India, and the United States. It started with one ridiculously good idea to create a different breed of Business Processing Outsourcing (BPO)! We at TaskUs understand that achieving growth for our partners requires a culture of constant motion, exploring new technologies, being ready to handle any challenge at a moment’s notice, and mastering consistency in an ever-changing world. What We Offer: At TaskUs, we prioritize our employees' well-being by offering competitive industry salaries and comprehensive benefits packages. Our commitment to a People First culture is reflected in the various departments we have established, including Total Rewards, Wellness, HR, and Diversity. We take pride in our inclusive environment and positive impact on the community. Moreover, we actively encourage internal mobility and professional growth at all stages of an employee's career within TaskUs. Join our team today and experience firsthand our dedication to supporting People First. &#xa;&#xa; Salary Range: $97,000.00 - $145,000.00 per year.&#xa;&#xa; Pay Transparency Statement: The base salary range represents the low and high end of the anticipated salary range for this position across our US locations. The "pay scale" provided is a good faith estimate of the range the employer reasonably expects to pay for the position at the time of hire. Actual salary will be determined based on various factors including, but not limited to, the candidate's qualifications, experience, skills, and specific geographic location. Application Window: This position is expected to remain open until 11-30-2026 . We recommend that interested candidates apply within 7 days of the posting date to ensure consideration.&#xa;&#xa; Job Description: Job Description What does a Senior Operations Manager really do? Think of yourself as someone who will manage day-to-day business operations, including performance, billing, and PNL, so not everyone can qualify for this role. We make sure we hire the best of the best, after all, we are a ridiculously good company so we make sure our employees are top-notch. So come on, now we need your full concentration because it’s time to imagine what it’s like being a Senior Operations Manager. Responsibilities: As a Senior Operations Manager of the AV Rider Assistance & Dispatch unit, you will manage day-to-day operations business, including performance, billing, P&L and resource forecasting for a growing fleet. Manage a high-performing team of Operations Managers and Team Leads, ensuring they are coached in both leadership and AV technical literacy. Design and scale response frameworks that accommodate unique AV challenges, including software-defined edge cases, hardware failures, and environmental obstacles. Drive KPI excellence across specialized AV metrics, balancing technical Resolution Rates and Safety Benchmarks with business metrics like CSAT and AHT. You will meet with Senior Management and clients as needed to continue business growth. Ensure compliance with evolving regulatory and legal standards specific to autonomous transportation. We need someone who has the proven ability to scale operations, drive performance management, and foster employee retention. Own the hiring and talent development pipeline, identifying candidates with the "top-notch" analytical skills required to thrive in a fast-paced technology environment. Foster an organizational culture that prioritizes safety, innovation, and rapid adaptation to technological change. Requirements: Two-plus years of experience as a Senior Operations Manager or seven-plus years of experience as an Operations Manager in high‑stakes or safety‑critical environments (e.g., transportation, automotive, aviation). Autonomous Vehicle Experience is must . BA/BS degree preferred. Experience managing supervisors, as well as coaching and developing Teammates. 20% travel required to support market launches, conduct field audits, and meet with regional stakeholders. Location On Site - Metro Detroit How We Partner To Protect You: TaskUs will neither solicit money from you during your application process nor require any form of payment in order to proceed with your application. Kindly ensure that you are always in communication with only authorized recruiters of TaskUs. DEI: In TaskUs we believe that innovation and higher performance are brought by people from all walks of life. We welcome applicants of different backgrounds, demographics, and circumstances. Inclusive and equitable practices are our responsibility as a business. TaskUs is committed to providing equal access to opportunities. If you need reasonable accommodations in any part of the hiring process, please let us know. EEO: TaskUs is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We celebrate and support diversity; we are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. TaskUs people first culture thrives on it for the benefit of our employees, our clients, our services, and our community. We invite you to explore all TaskUs career opportunities and apply through the provided URL https://www.taskus.com/careers/ .

jd_text: Opportunity awaits those up to the challenge of developing transformative therapies across a broad range of debilitating diseases. Summary: The Sr. Manager, Commercial Learning & Development – Operations will lead the infrastructure, processes, and standards that enable the Commercial Learning & Development function to operate with efficiency, compliance, and scalability. This individual will serve as the operational backbone of the team, ensuring consistent execution across the Biogen franchise portfolio. The role requires exceptional organizational and systems expertise, strong project management skills, and the ability to partner cross-functionally to establish standards and governance that ensure Commercial Learning & Development delivers with excellence on behalf of the business. Roles and Responsibilities: Own the operations and governance model for Commercial Learning & Development, establishing standards, processes, and documentation that drive consistency and accountability. Create, optimize, and maintain standard training class schedules, including Integrity Selling class schedules, coordinating facilitators, participants, and logistics across therapeutic areas. Support the structure and stand-up of the new learning management system (LMS), and manage and continuously improve systems and tools (e.g., LMS, Veeva, certification tracking) to ensure compliance, efficiency, and accuracy. Standardize training surveys and lead reporting and analytics (survey aggregation, metrics, dashboards) to monitor performance and inform business decisions. Develop and oversee the Commercial Learning & Development calendars, scheduling, and project trackers, ensuring alignment and transparency across stakeholders and cross-functional partners. Support Training Managers with scheduling, calendar invitations, and territory and field organization activities to enable efficient, well-coordinated training delivery. Provide hands-on support for training initiatives as needed, stepping in on delivery and execution to maintain continuity and quality. Serve as the liaison between administrative support and cross-functional teams, ensuring clear communication, timely handoffs, and coordinated execution. Standardize communications and templates to improve stakeholder engagement and efficiency. Provide operational leadership for onboarding, vendor management, and meeting coordination, ensuring a professional and seamless learner experience. Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to implement future-forward solutions (intranet, governance policies, advanced analytics) that enable scalability as the organization grows. Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Director, Global Commercial Learning & Development, on process improvement and infrastructure, ensuring operational discipline and freeing leadership capacity for strategic initiatives. Education, Registration & Certification: Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in business or related discipline preferred. Experience: 7+ years of experience in project management, training operations, or commercial excellence within Life Sciences. Demonstrated experience implementing and governing learning systems, tools, and processes in a commercial organization. Proven success establishing infrastructure and standards that scale within a growing biotech or specialty pharma company. Skills, Knowledge & Abilities: Strong project management expertise with ability to design, implement, and sustain operational frameworks. Deep knowledge of learning management systems (LMS) and related digital platforms. Highly organized with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Exceptional collaboration and communication skills; able to partner across Sales, Market Access, HR, and other stakeholders. Strategic problem-solver with a continuous improvement mindset. Comfortable navigating ambiguity and building new processes in a fast-paced, evolving environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, Teams) and experience with project management tools (e.g., Smartsheet, Asana, Monday.com, or equivalent). Ability to quickly learn and adapt to new systems and technologies that enable operational efficiency. This role involves some domestic travel (field engagements, meetings, HQ collaboration) and regular in-office engagement to support team and cross-functional collaboration. jd_text: Let’s search for your next career at TEL. Use the form below to search our current opportunities and then apply. Job Description Tokyo Electron US Holdings is a subsidiary of Tokyo Electron Limited (TEL), a global, multi-billion-dollar corporation and a leader in the semiconductor industry is seeking a Mgr./Sr. Mgr. Facilities Operations . We engineer success. Tokyo Electron U.S. Holdings, Inc. is the holding company of TEL’s U.S. subsidiaries. We oversee the intensely innovative development and production of cutting-edge products that are used globally in the electronics industry. Our employees work closely with chip manufacturers, material suppliers, and other equipment suppliers to pursue common goals and learn collectively in a pre-competitive manner, ensuring timely solutions to the technology roadmap of the semiconductor industry. Here at Tokyo Electron, we take pride in our diverse culture. Technology Enabling Life. The Day to Day (Responsibilities): Manages the design, planning, construction and maintenance of equipment, machinery, buildings, and other facilities. Plans, budgets, and schedules facility modifications, including estimates on equipment, labor, materials and other related costs. Designs and develops organizational policies relevant to the facilities department. Oversees the coordination of building space allocation and layout, communication services and facilities expansion. May have responsibility for establishing and overseeing health and safety standards. Selects, develops, and evaluates personnel to ensure the efficient operation of the function. Must Haves (minimum qualifications): Requires a Bachelor's degree and 8 years of related experience. Supervisory and/or Leadership Responsibilities: Establishes operational objectives and work plans, and delegates assignments to subordinates. Senior management reviews objectives to determine success of operation. Involved in developing, modifying and executing company policies that affect immediate operations and may also have company-wide effect. Works on issues where analysis of situations or data requires an in-depth knowledge of organizational objectives. Implements strategic policies when selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining results. Establishes and assures adherence to budgets, schedules, work plans, and performance requirements. Regularly interacts with senior management or executive levels on matters concerning several functional areas, divisions, and/or customers. Requires the ability to change the thinking of, or gain acceptance from, others in sensitive situations, without damage to the relationship. Manages activities of two or more sections or departments. Provides technical oversight for the application of and compliance with technical standards. Completes reports and summaries for management and users including project status reports, problem reports, and progress summaries. Responsibilities: Provide leadership and strategic direction for data analysis activities across a portfolio of public health and nutrition research projects, ensuring alignment with organizational and research goals. Supervise, mentor, and support data analysts and junior statisticians; delegate tasks, facilitate professional development, and provide technical guidance and quality assurance. Oversee the design, implementation, and continual optimization of data analysis workflows, ensuring best practices are established and maintained across projects. Demonstrated experience leading the preparation of research manuscripts and securing grant funding. Excellent verbal and written communication skills with ability to effectively communicate with faculty and staff. title: Operations Manager, Space Institute
jd_text: Job Title Operations Manager, Space Institute Agency Texas A&M Engineering Department Space Institute Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Houston, Texas Job Type Staff Job Description Why work for Texas A&M Engineering? Engineering has been part of Texas A&M University since its opening in 1876 as the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas. Today, the College of Engineering is the largest college on the College Station campus with more than 25,000 engineering students enrolled in 15 departments. Its mission is to serve Texas, the nation and the global community by providing engineering graduates who are well-founded in engineering fundamentals, instilled with the highest standards of professional and ethical behavior, and prepared to meet the complex technical challenges of society. As the research arm of Engineering, the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station (TEES) is a state agency within the Texas A&M University System with a mission to improve lives through basic and applied engineering research, workforce development and technology transition. Our collaborations with industry, academia and government provide cutting-edge solutions to global technical challenges. We are deeply committed to recruiting and retaining a talented workforce that embraces our core values of Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Service, by offering competitive salaries, an array of benefits, an extensive support network, and above all, an enriching and highly collaborative working community that is deeply passionate about our vision for higher education, research, and public service. Job Description Purpose: The Operations Manager, under direction, leads and oversees facility operations, maintenance, and infrastructure support for the Texas A&M University Space Institute in Houston. This position is responsible for ensuring that facilities are safe, secure, functional, and capable of supporting a dynamic, multi-tenant environment. The Operations Manager contributes to the overall effectiveness of the Institute by maintaining high operational standards, supporting tenant needs, and ensuring facility and equipment readiness to support high-quality facility operations in a fast-paced and evolving environment. Responsibilities: Oversees preventative, corrective, and planned maintenance, including mechanical, electrical, HVAC, custodial, and grounds operations. Oversees day-to-day facility operations to ensure the building is safe, secure, functional, and maintained in accordance with university policies and applicable regulations. Serves as primary point of contact for facility-related issues, and service requests ensuring timely response and resolution. Coordinates and manages vendor services, contractors, and maintenance providers to ensure quality performance and compliance. Oversees building access control, key management, badging, tenant onboarding, and facility usage processes; conducts regular reviews of access permissions to ensure appropriate and secure access. Leads facility safety, emergency preparedness, and business continuity efforts, including safety training, fire drills, evacuation procedures, emergency response planning, corrective actions, and participation in on-call response activities. Assigns and coordinates facility proctors, safety monitors, and other personnel as required to support daily operations, events, and specialized activities. Oversees the operation, maintenance, enhancement, and reconfiguration of specialty environments, including the Moon and Mars analog scapes, utilizing and coordinating the operation of heavy equipment and specialized machinery. Coordinates with business operations staff on supply ordering, equipment service requests, purchase documentation, and related administrative processes. Establishes processes and maintains records of maintenance activities, work orders, inspections, and performance metrics. Supports space utilization planning and assists with coordination of facility modifications or improvements such as new equipment installation. Provides communication and guidance to staff and tenants regarding facility operations and procedures. Monitors facility performance and identifies opportunities for operational improvements. Coordinates with internal university departments and external partners to support facility operations. Performs other duties as assigned. What We Need: Bachelor’s degree in Facility Management, Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Five (5) years of related experience in facility operations, maintenance, or project coordination. Other Requirements: This position is security sensitive and requires United States Citizenship only. What Is Helpful: Experience working in higher education, research, or complex multi-tenant facilities. Experience coordinating vendors, service contracts, and maintenance activities. Knowledge of building systems, maintenance practices, and safety standards. Work Location: Houston, TX. About The Texas A&M Space Institute: The Texas A&M University Space Institute will advance commercial, government, military, and academic research and development partnerships in support of national and international space endeavors. With a $200 million investment from the State of Texas, a 400,000 square foot facility is under construction at NASA-Johnson Space Center's Exploration Park. This unique facility, featuring the world's largest indoor climate-controlled landscapes to emulate surface operations on the moon and Mars, is expected to open in the fall of 2026 and will support space system research, testing, training, and workforce development initiatives. Options for Vision , Dental , Life , and Long-Term Disability insurance. A defined benefit retirement plan with the Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS) with 8.25% employer contribution. Additional Voluntary Retirement Programs: Tax Deferred Account 403(b) and a Deferred Compensation Program 457(b). Flexible spending account options for medical and childcare expenses Generous paid time off with holidays , vacation and sick leave . Robust free training access through LinkedIn Learning plus professional development opportunities. Tuition assistance and Educational release time to further your academic pursuits. Access to Engineer Your Wellness programs that provide opportunities for employees to engage in health and fitness. Wellness release time offered to employees to promote work/life balance. Recognize and reward exceptional performance based on individual and team contributions to the growth and success of Texas A&M Engineering. jd_text: Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period! For more information about our benefits, see below! We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet." What do our Pest Control Technicians do? The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for residential customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions . Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following: Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Implement a phased enforcement approach for DLP (visibility → user education → controlled override → targeted enforcement) to reduce false positives and operational friction. Define exception processes, review cadence, and tuning workflows so data protection does not become “set-and-forget” shelfware. Partner with IT, risk, privacy, legal, compliance, and business data owners to align protection controls to real data flows and regulatory expectations. 2) Security architecture leadership Lead a team of security architects responsible for the security architecture blueprint , including reference architectures, control standards, and reusable patterns. Experience managing 3rd party cybersecurity risk program including due diligence, contract language, ongoing monitoring, and incident response. Cloud security architecture experience (major cloud provider environments) and endpoint data controls integration. title: Administrative Coordinator for CDO Operations & Data
jd_text: Job Posting Location: Claremont, CA Job Posting Title: Administrative Coordinator for CDO Operations & Data Job Description: ABOUT POMONA COLLEGE: Located near Los Angeles, California, Pomona College is widely regarded as one of the nation's premier liberal arts colleges. Established in 1887, Pomona College is known for small classes, a challenging curriculum, close relationships between students and faculty, and a range of student research and leadership opportunities. Pomona is a member of The Claremont Colleges. JOB PURPOSE: The Administrative Coordinator for CDO Operations & Data plays a central role in supporting the operations, administration, and assessment efforts of the Career Development Office (CDO). This position provides high-level administrative support to the Senior Director, manages the logistics and execution of the office's major events and programs, and oversees key financial and operational processes. The Administrative Coordinator also supports the CDO's data-informed approach to student services by collecting, analyzing, and reporting on qualitative and quantitative data. This includes conducting research, benchmarking peer institutions, developing reports and dashboards, and translating data into actionable insights that inform decision-making and demonstrate the impact of the office's programs and services. Success in this role requires the ability to think strategically across all functions of the CDO, connect operational activities to broader departmental goals, and present complex information in clear, accessible formats for a variety of audiences. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Reporting directly to the Associate Dean and Senior Director, Career Development Office, the Administrative Coordinator will provide a broad range of support to the Career Development Office (CDO). Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Office Operations & Administrative Tasks (25%) ● Provide administrative support to Senior Director. ● Oversee front desk coverage to ensure CDO is a welcoming space for externals, students and colleagues; meet and greet visitors, students, faculty and staff and field general questions. ● Work collaboratively with the other administrative staff ensure smooth operations, including facilities, housekeeping, deliveries, furniture/supplies, etc. ● Support logistics for large-events, including booking locations, arranging caterers, securing vendors, tracking responses, process payments, etc. Serve as one of the primary technology contacts between the CDO and the web-based recruiting system (presently Handshake) for troubleshooting issues; liaise with ITS to upload student information. ● Design and implement organization systems and processes to improve office functioning and service delivery. ● Arrange travel and hotel accommodation for staff and visitors. ● Schedule/arrange meetings, answer the phone, sort physical mail and inboxes, photocopy and prepare materials for meetings and presentations; provide logistical arrangements for internal and external meetings and videoconferences. Financial Tasks (30%) ● Monitor and administer the departmental budget, track expenditures, process financial transactions, reconcile accounts, and ensure compliance with institutional policies for individual staff, departmental programs and gifts. ● Assist the Senior Director in tracking costs, expenses and budgets of the departments and programs overseen by the Senior Director. ● Identify appropriate vendors for supplies, resources and services; negotiate rates and manage shipments/services rendered. ● Manage office subscriptions and resources. ● Prepare and track business reimbursements; enter purchase requisitions into the institution’s electronic procurement system. Data Management (30%) ● Analyze assessment and benchmarking data and streamline into comprehensive reports for internal and external stakeholders. ● Compile, analyze, and report mid-year and annual data, drawing strategic insights related to student engagement, ofﬁce operations, past performance, and future planning. ● Analyze and report on monthly trends using visual dashboards to communicate operational performance. ● Serve on First Destination and Annual Impact Report teams, support efforts to collect knowledge through outreach, and assist in the data analysis process. ● Educate and train CDO staff around data tracking responsibilities and procedures. ● Create and customize reports, providing data for senior management that will be utilized to increase service and program effectiveness and to inform various constituents about how the CDO is essential to carry out the College’s mission and CDO’s Strategic Plan . Other (15%) ● Serve on CDO Communications team; support Manager of Communications & Digital Media with CDO social media accounts, newsletters, emails, and event marketing. ● The Administrative Coordinator will also assist with special projects and other tasks, as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Bachelor’s degree in business administration or liberal arts is preferred, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience: A minimum of 2 years of administrative experience with increasing responsibility is preferred. At least 2 years of experience at an academic institution is preferred. At least 2 years of data collection and analysis experience preferred. REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE AND CRITICAL SKILLS: This position must possess the knowledge, skills and abilities to be able to successfully perform the essential functions of the position or be able to demonstrate how the essential functions will be performed, with or without reasonable accommodation, using other skills and abilities not listed below. 1. Deploy professional skills in office management, in collaboration with colleagues to best promote the College’s strategic interests. a. Able to exercise good judgment with limited guidance. b. Possess a friendly demeanor that creates a welcoming environment for visitors. c. Possess a professional and flexible demeanor that thrives in an intense, deadline-filled environment, where multi-tasking under pressure is essential. d. Provide good customer service to students, employers, staff, and faculty through a positive attitude, listening to needs, and following up as promised. e. Able to collaborate effectively with all constituents (faculty, staff, colleagues, students, employers) with a good sense of humor, team spirit and positive attitude. f. Knowledgeable of how to supervise and work with students in a liberal arts setting. g. Knowledgeable about CDO resources h. Able to manage events with multiple constituents. i. Able to work well on a variety of projects with a strong team orientation. j. Able to manage and prioritize high levels of email correspondence. 2. Demonstrate effective, accurate and clear communication with excellent verbal, written, interpersonal, reading, and phone skills. Follow all written and verbal instructions, asking questions as needed for clarification of projects/tasks/duties/assignments. 3. Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, etc.) and the ability to quickly learn and effectively use other software platforms and technologies, such as Handshake, Slack, Tableau, Canva, Workday, recruiting systems, databases, and web-based applications. Utilizes assigned technology and equipment to support departmental operations while maintaining confidentiality and data security 4. patience, discretion, good judgment, courtesy and tact while working with people from a wide variety of backgrounds. 5. Prioritize and perform multiple projects/tasks, meet deadlines/timelines, respond to others in a timely manner, and work both independently and as a collaborative member of the College with a high standard of integrity and ethics, in support of the College’s strategic vision and the division’s/department’s annual goals. 6. Use exceptional organizational, administrative and time management skills to complete work with accuracy and a keen attention to detail in a fast-paced environment with constant interruption. 7. Operate the College’s vehicles safely for campus-related work and meet all insurance-related requirements. To apply, please upload the materials below: Cover Letter Resume REQUIRED HOURS: The regular hours for this full-time position are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday – Friday. Overtime, holiday, weekend and evening work hours may be required. Travel may be required. Regular hours may vary due to needs of the College or division HOURLY RATE: The hourly rate for this role is $27.00 to $33.00 per hour with a competitive benefits package. The specific factors that the College will consider when offering a salary to an individual will include, but not be limited to: education, training, relevant prior experience, and performance in prior roles. All staff positions are ineligible for visa or permanent resident card sponsorship. As a California employer, Pomona College requires all employees to be residents of California.
