title: Artificial Intelligence (BS Program), Department of Information Technology - Adjunct Faculty
jd_text: Adjunct Faculty – Artificial Intelligence (BS Program) Department of Information Technology | University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) This position is specifically to teach remotely for stateside applicants. Local applicants only; UMGC does not sponsor logistical support for this role. At UMGC, we don’t just teach; we empower . Founded in 1947, UMGC is an open-access, minority-serving institution serving over 90,000 nontraditional learners worldwide, including a proud, large military-affiliated population. Our students are mature, highly dedicated, and balancing careers, families, and service. As an Adjunct Faculty member, you are the essential partner helping them bridge the gap between classroom theory and real-world career success. Why Teach with UMGC? Focus on Students, Not Course Design: All courses follow a standardized, pre-designed, unified course model. Standardized rubrics, OER materials, library resources, and digital textbooks are fully provided at no cost to you. You get to focus 100% of your energy on mentoring, facilitating, and providing high-quality feedback—no unpaid course-building required. True Asynchronous Flexibility: Teach with flexibility, on your own schedule. As long as you meet weekly grading, responsiveness, and engagement milestones, your daily hours are entirely up to you. Ongoing Growth: We invest in you. All newly hired faculty receive comprehensive online orientation, alongside ongoing, cost-free professional development opportunities. The Rhythm of Your Week (Key Responsibilities) Adjunct faculty bring our pre-built curriculum to life through real-world expertise and active mentorship. Classroom Engagement & Presence Be Visible: Maintain an active classroom presence at least 5 days per week, introducing yourself with a welcome announcement and driving discussions. Bridge Theory & Practice: Enrich the pre-built curriculum with your own professional expertise and real-world examples. Build Belonging: Foster an inclusive, culturally responsive environment where adult learners feel supported and motivated. Responsiveness & Feedback Stay consistently engaged with learners throughout the course by responding to inquiries, returning feedback, and posting final grades within the expected timeframe. Proactive Support & Collaboration Monitor Progress: Use available data tools to track student engagement and conduct proactive outreach to at-risk students. Team Up: Partner with success coaches, academic staff, and portfolio directors to refer struggling students to UMGC support resources. Stay Connected: Participate in UMGC's vibrant faculty community, including the Program Hub and ongoing training. Course Structure & Time Commitment Format: 100% Online & Asynchronous Term Length: 8-week sessions (3-credit courses) Class Size: Typically, 25–35 students (smaller sections for select courses) Time Commitment: The adjunct faculty role requires a substantial commitment throughout the term focusing not only on academic success but also the social, personal, and professional growth of students Minimum Qualifications: Education: Master’s degree in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Data Analytics, or related field from an accredited institution of higher learning. Experience: 3-5 years of professional experience in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Data Analytics. Legal Status: Applicants must have and be able to maintain their own legal status in the country in which they apply to teach. The Mindset: A deeply student-centered approach rooted in empathy, flexibility, professional integrity, and cultural responsiveness. Preferred Qualifications: Industry Certifications in ML, AI, Data Science from Microsoft, IBM, AWS. Experience teaching adult learners in an online, asynchronous environment. Prior postsecondary teaching experience. Active engagement in your discipline's professional community. Materials needed for submission Resume/ Curriculum Vitae Cover letter highly preferred Unofficial Transcripts If selected, candidates with international degrees may be required to submit a translation/degree evaluation from a NACES approved vendor All submissions should include a cover letter and resume . The University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal and state laws regarding nondiscrimination. UMGC is committed to a policy of equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, religion, ancestry, political affiliation or veteran status in employment, educational programs and activities, and admissions. Workplace Accommodations: The University of Maryland Global Campus Global Campus (UMGC) is committed to creating and maintaining a welcoming and inclusive working environment for people of all abilities. UMGC is dedicated to the principle that no qualified individual with a disability shall, based on disability, be excluded from participation in or be denied the benefits of the services, programs, or activities of the University, or be subjected to discrimination. For information about UMGC’s Reasonable Workplace Accommodation Policy or to request an accommodation, applicants/candidates can contact Employee Accommodations via email at employee-accommodations@umgc.edu . Benefits Package Highlights: Health Coverage: Access to health care, medical with vision, dental, and prescription plans for both individuals and families, effective from the 1st of the month following your hire date. NOTE: Adjuncts are not eligible for the State of Maryland subsidized rates. Adjuncts would be responsible for the total cost if enrolled. Insurance Options: Term Life Insurance and Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance. Supplemental Retirement Plans : include 401(k), 403(b), 457(b), and various Roth options. The university does not provide matching funds. For additional information please see: SS Adjunct Faculty_2020.pdf (umgc.edu) Hiring Range by Rank and Degree: Instructor: No Terminal Degree: Step 1 $806 - Step 11 $1,050 per credit hour Assistant Adjunct Professor: No Terminal Degree Step 1 $877 - Step 11 $1,127 per credit hour Assistant Adjunct Professor: Terminal Degree Step 1 $1,023 - Step 11 $1,288 per credit hour Associate Adjunct Professor: No Terminal Degree Step 1 $947 - Step 11 $1,205 per credit hour Associate Adjunct Professor: Terminal Degree Step 1 $1,202 - Step 11 $1,483 per credit hour Adjunct Professor: No Terminal Degree Step 1 $1,023 - Step 11 $1,288 per credit hour Adjunct Professor: Terminal Degree Step 1 $1,347 - Step 11 $1,645 per credit hour

jd_text: BSN SPORTS, A VARSITY BRANDS COMPANY - THE RECOGNIZED LEADER IN TEAM ATHLETIC GEAR For over 50 years, BSN SPORTS has been the largest team sporting goods equipment and apparel distributor of choice in the United States . Our 3,000 BSN SPORTS employees strive to support the Heart of the Game by putting valuable time back into the day of coaches and administrators through excellent service platforms. Our company mission is simple: Save coaches and administrators time with everything they do off the field so they have more time to impact young lives on it. WORK TYPE: On Site LOCATION DETAILS: 13700 Benchmark Dr , Farmers Branch , TX 75234 WORK HOURS: Monday-Friday 5:30AM - 2:00 PM (OT as needed to meet production needs and during peak operations from June-Dec). HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT As a member of the Warehouse team , the Warehouse Associate is a critical role within our warehouse department and the Inventory Control department is responsible for making sure all inventory is accounted for accurately and placed in the most efficient locations for the Distribution Center's flow. WHAT YOU WILL DO Warehouse Associates ensure products are stocked, selected, packed, and shipped to customers. You’ll work in one of the following roles: Picking, Packing, Shipping, Inventory. General responsibilities include: Receiving, picking, sorting, and labeling orders. Pack, fold, and arrange garments. Scanning shipping orders, and inputting into inventory system. Research and correct displaced, mislabeled, and missing products, perform replenishments, cycle counts, stock checks, and resolving inventory and order discrepancies. QUALIFICATIONS KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES High energy, great attitude, and aptitude for leadership Great attention to detail and organization skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills Computer literate with knowledge and proficiency in Microsoft Office Ability to work in a structured and process-oriented environment Ability to multi-task and problem solve Ability to work seasonal mandatory OT as needed and maintain excellent attendance Read and comprehend documents, instructions, and correspondence in English to perform job duties efficiently. Communicate effectively with team members, clients, and stakeholders in spoken English, ensuring clarity and understanding. Participate in meetings, discussions, and presentations requiring proficient spoken English skills. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, providing valuable insights and feedback in English. Learn tasks quickly, accuracy driven, personable, team oriented, and punctual with excellence in attendance. Ability to add, subtract multiply and divide numbers. . EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE Previous warehouse experience is a bonus Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a bonus Preference will be given to candidates with previous related experience. At least 2-3 years of continued work experience 2 years in-depth SAP experience Learn tasks quickly, is detailed, accuracy driven, personable, team oriented, and punctual with excellent attendance. Must be very comfortable with Microsoft Office, with extensive experience with Microsoft Excel. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand for long periods of time. Repetitive movement of the body is required on a regular basis. The position requires lifting of no less than 15-50 lbs. on a regular basis. Must be able to tolerate working in a non-climate-controlled environment. #LI-NU1 Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Respect - We earn it by giving it. Because everyone deserves it. Innovation - We never stop striving to be better. For ourselves and our community. Transparency - We are committed to openness and honesty in everything we do. OUR BENEFITS We are committed to putting you and your families first. For benefits eligible roles, we offer a variety of choices and costs as well as program enhancements that align with our responsibility to elevate the employee experience. title: Technical Consultant
jd_text: Imagine yourself… Doing meaningful work that makes an everyday impact on the world around you. Joining a company with a proven track record of success and an exciting future. It’s possible with a role at ChemTreat . ChemTreat, a Veralto company, is the nation’s largest and fastest-growing specialty chemical company dedicated solely to industrial water treatment. We understand and respect the awe-inspiring power of water to impact industries, and to sustain and enhance lives. Our 2,000 associates across North and South America maximize this power for our customers— from power producers to food and beverage companies to the automotive industry— helping them grow their businesses while protecting people and the environment. When you join the ChemTreat team and the broader Veralto network, you’ll have the chance to shape the future of our planet and the future of your career. You’ll have opportunities to build new skills and invest in your development, all while doing meaningful work that makes an everyday impact on the world’s vital water resources. Learn more about how our team is maximizing the power of water: https://wi.st/3vH5OUK This role requires approximately 60% –75% travel, primarily across the continental United States, typically three to four days per week with no regular weekend travel expected. We are seeking a Technical Consultant to partner with field sales teams and customers across the United States. In this high-impact role, you will apply your industrial water treatment expertise to solve complex customer challenges, influence strategic sales opportunities, and improve system performance across a range of industries and applications. Conduct plant audits, system assessments, and operational reviews to identify performance improvement opportunities. Relevant industries include food and beverage, power, chemical processing, refining, or other industrial environments. Strong communication , customer-facing, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain technical recommendations clearly to sales teams and customers. Willingness and ability to travel 60%–75%, primarily throughout the continental U.S. Technical sales experience or experience partnering closely with commercial teams is preferred. title: Systems Architect Supervisor (P109)
jd_text: Job Description Summary: Salary: $133,952.00 - $200,928.00 annually The Systems Architect Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the comprehensive enterprise architecture design, development, and deployment of TRWD’s IT systems and infrastructure. This includes managing disaster recovery, cloud infrastructure, server compute and storage, as well as Identity and Access Management (IAM). They ensure that systems meet employee and business requirements while maintaining sustainability, scalability, security, and resilience. Additionally, they evaluate, select, and test technology products critical for solution delivery, and lead the setup, implementation, and documentation of technology integrations or migration strategies. Alongside supervising a small team of Cloud and Systems Engineers, they provide essential technical guidance across the Information Services organization. Job Description Essential Functions and Responsibilities: The duties listed below are intended only as illustrations of the various types of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to this position. Responsibilities include: Enterprise Architecture Design and Development : Lead the design and development efforts to architect IT systems that align with organizational objectives and future growth plans. Employ a strategic approach to ensure systems are adaptable, scalable, and capable of meeting evolving business needs. Act as part of the Enterprise Architecture Review Board to ensure technology solutions across all technical stacks are implemented to effectively meet business goals. Technology Evaluation and Selection : Evaluate emerging technologies and tools to determine their suitability for integration into TRWD’s IT infrastructure. Conduct thorough testing and analysis to assess the performance, reliability, and security of potential solutions. Supervision and Team Leadership : Manage and mentor a team of Cloud and Systems Engineers, providing guidance and support to foster their professional growth and development. Coordinate team efforts to achieve project milestones and deliverables effectively. Technical Guidance and Collaboration : Serve as a technical authority within the Information Services organization, offering expertise and insights on complex architectural decisions. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align technology initiatives with business objectives and requirements. Website Portfolio Management : Oversee the hosting and management of TRWD’s portfolio of websites, ensuring optimal performance, reliability, and security. Collaborate with web development teams to implement best practices and leverage innovative solutions for website optimization. Identity and Access Management (IAM) : Implement and maintain robust IAM policies and procedures to safeguard sensitive data and resources. Ensure proper authentication, authorization, and access controls are in place to protect against unauthorized access and data breaches. Cloud Architecture and Services (Microsoft Azure) : Design and implement cloud architecture solutions leveraging Microsoft Azure services. Ensure scalability, reliability, and security of cloud-based infrastructure while optimizing cost and performance. Cost Management : Monitor and optimize infrastructure costs to ensure efficient resource utilization and alignment with budgetary constraints. Implement cost-saving measures and identify opportunities for optimization to maximize ROI. Disaster Recovery/Business Continuity : Develop and maintain disaster recovery and business continuity plans to mitigate the impact of potential disruptions. Implement robust backup and recovery strategies to ensure data integrity and availability in the event of system failures or disasters. Telemetry Management : Oversee the collection, analysis, and interpretation of telemetry data to monitor system performance, identify potential issues, and optimize resource utilization. Utilize telemetry insights to make data-driven decisions and drive continuous improvement efforts around capacity, vulnerability, and performance management. Vulnerability Management : Implement and oversee vulnerability management processes to identify, prioritize, and remediate security vulnerabilities across the IT infrastructure. Collaborate with security teams to implement patches and updates in a timely manner, ensuring the organization remains protected against potential threats. Incident, Problem, and Change Management : Establish and enforce incident, problem, and change management processes for infrastructure components. Ensure timely resolution of incidents and problems while minimizing the impact of changes on operations. Documentation and Knowledge Management : Maintain detailed documentation of architecture designs, integration plans, and technology evaluations. Facilitate knowledge sharing and best practices dissemination to enhance team efficiency and effectiveness. Required Experience: A minimum of ten (10) years progressive experience involving IT systems administration and engineering within a virtualized Windows Server and Azure Cloud environment. Previous supervisory experience involving diverse and highly technical teams. Demonstrated automation and infrastructure as code (IaC) experience (e.g. PowerShell, Ansible, ARM templates, Bicep, Azure CLI). Expertise in implementing and deploying VMWARE ESXi, VMWare Virtual Center and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure, Hyper V, and other enterprise virtualization solutions. Serverless hosting using containerization (Docker, K8, etc.) Experience managing both native Microsoft Azure and hybrid cloud solutions using Azure Arc. Identity and Access Management in hybrid Active Directory/Entra environments. Previous management of enterprise storage solutions such as SAN, NAS, SDS, Azure Storage Accounts Capacity, performance, and security analysis using telemetry repositories such as Elastic or Splunk. Technical documentation of complex IT systems. Advanced knowledge of data security administration principles, method, and techniques including firewalls, network, intrusion detection systems, file integrity monitoring, anomaly detection, and DLP rules. Identify training budget needs Performance review alignment Job description review Maintain familiarity with strategic District levels of service Continuous improvement monitoring and innovation efforts Perform other duties as required Required Education/Certification/License: Bachelor’s degree in a related field of study. An additional five (5) years of work experience in the enterprise technology industry can be used in lieu of degree. Must pass a Texas DPS/FBI Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) criminal history background check and maintain CJIS eligibility Valid Texas driver’s license Desired Education/Certification/License: TOGAF, Zachman, or equivalent enterprise architecture certification Microsoft Azure certification ITIL or COBIT certification VMware VCDX, VCAP Success Factors/Job Competencies: Detailed technical documentation skills Adhering to and creating policies and procedures Excellent problem-solving ability and second order strategic thinking Strong attention to detail to diagnose resolve systemic problems Ability to work outside regular working hours as needed by the client, including evenings and weekends Self-motivated, ability to learn new technologies quickly and independently Planning – ability to think ahead and plan over five (5) years Strong team player Physical Demands and Work Environment The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Physical demands : While performing duties of job, employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hand to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; stoop; talk and hear. Must not be afraid of heights. Must be able to drive necessary distances when required. Employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Work environment: While performing the duties of this job, the employee typically resides within an office or cubicle and may have occasional fieldwork that will expose the employee to weather conditions prevalent at the time.

jd_text: Drive Innovation for Investors Everywhere At Vanguard, we put investors first - and that means putting innovation at the center of everything we do. As part of the Application Development track, you’ll design and build technology solutions that power our business and improve outcomes for our clients. title: Financial Business Intelligence Manager
jd_text: When you’re the best, we’re the best. We instill an environment where employees feel engaged, satisfied and able to contribute their unique skills and talents while living and working as their authentic selves . We provide extensive opportunities for personal and professional development, building both employee competence and organizational capability to fuel exceptional performance through an inclusive environment both now and in the future. Summary: In this role, you will lead the design and development of advanced finance analytics, business intelligence, and reporting solutions that support corporate targets and informed decision-making. You will independently build complex Power BI dashboards and data visualizations from the ground up, source and model data from Databricks and other data sources, and translate complex financial information into clear, actionable insights. This role sits at the intersection of Finance, Data Analytics, and Business Intelligence. The ideal candidate brings strong financial acumen together with hands-on technical expertise in Power BI development, data modeling, visualization design, and analytics solution delivery. Your work will support senior executives, the Finance Committee, the Board of Directors, investors, and internal business partners. Responsibilities: Independently design, build, test, deploy, and maintain complex Power BI dashboards, reports, and data visualization solutions from the ground up. Develop scalable Power BI solutions using advanced features such as data models, calculated measures, interactive slicers, drill-through functionality, and row-level security. Source, transform, model, and validate data from Databricks and other enterprise data sources to support finance reporting and analytics needs. Translate complex financial and operational data into intuitive visualizations, management insights, and executive-level financial narratives. Partner with Finance leaders and business stakeholders to gather requirements, define key performance indicators, and convert business needs into effective analytics solutions. Produce monthly and quarterly consolidated reporting and dashboards for senior executives, the Finance Committee, the Board of Directors, investors, and internal partners. Perform data reconciliation, validation, and quality assurance to ensure the accuracy and integrity of dashboards, reports, calculations, and underlying data. Collaborate with Accounting, Financial Systems, and technical partners to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve source-data, logic, integration, and reporting issues. Support FP&A team members with business-unit reporting, financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and performance insights. Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting, improve dashboard performance, streamline analytics processes, and strengthen self-service reporting capabilities. Qualifications: Relevant degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Business Administration, Economics, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field preferred. Advanced degree desired. Five or more years of experience in finance analytics, financial business intelligence, FP&A reporting, data visualization, or a related area. Demonstrated experience independently designing and building complex Power BI dashboards and reporting solutions from initial requirements through deployment and ongoing maintenance. Advanced hands-on Power BI development experience, including data modeling, DAX calculations, interactive visualizations, slicers, drill-through functionality, and row-level security. Experience sourcing, transforming, validating, and modeling data from Databricks or a comparable cloud-based enterprise data platform. Strong understanding of financial reporting, FP&A processes, financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, key performance indicators, and business-performance analysis. Experience translating financial and business requirements into scalable analytics, reporting, and visualization solutions. Ability to analyze complex data, recognize trends and anomalies, and communicate clear, actionable recommendations to business and executive audiences. Experience troubleshooting data-quality, reporting-logic, calculation, and source-system issues in partnership with finance and technical teams. Strong attention to detail with a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy, integrity, documentation, and quality assurance. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex financial and technical information to senior-level stakeholders. Willingness to travel. #LI - AC1 Estimated Hiring Range: At Vizient, we consider skills, experience, and organizational needs in our compensation approach. Geographic factors may adjust the range estimate and hires typically fall below the top range. Compensation decisions are tailored to individual circumstances. title: Data Engineering Manager
jd_text: <p><strong>About OpenSesame</strong></p> <p>OpenSesame is transforming workforce development with an AI-powered marketplace of skill-building courses and learning pathways. We help organizations build skills and stay compliant through a high-quality content catalog, seamless LMS/LXP integrations, and advanced capabilities like skills-based curation and multilingual content creation. More than 2,000 companies, including 150+ of the Global 2000, rely on OpenSesame to develop the world's most productive and admired workforces.<br>Learn more: <a href="http://www.opensesame.com/about" target="_blank">www.opensesame.com/about</a></p> <p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>The Data Engineering Manager will guide and grow a lean, focused data engineering team. The team’s mission is to build and scale an AI-ready data foundation that enables reliable analytics, operational reporting, governance, enterprise system integrations, and future AI initiatives across the company. This role partners closely with analysts, business leaders, engineering teams, product management, and data consumers company-wide to improve the accessibility, trust, and usability of enterprise data assets.</p> <p><strong>About the Role&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>As a Data Engineering Manager I, you will combine direct people management, team stewardship, operational execution, and technical decision-making. You will own the Data Governance &amp; Accessibility program while serving as the managerial and architectural lead responsible for designing scalable data systems, improving pipeline reliability, and enabling analysts through robust, specialized data solutions.</p> <p>Success in this role requires balancing high-impact people management (1:1s, performance management, career development) with strategic planning, cross-functional stakeholder management, agile process facilitation, and technical leadership.</p> <p><strong>Core Responsibilities &amp; Management Expectations</strong></p> <p><strong>People Management &amp; Mentorship</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Direct Supervision:</strong> Conduct effective 1:1s, set clear goals, deliver regular performance feedback, and manage career growth for direct reports.</li> <li><strong>Engineering Culture:</strong> Foster a psychologically safe team environment built on trust, transparency, continuous improvement, and a growth mindset.</li> <li><strong>Team Upskilling:</strong> Actively mentor engineers in data engineering best practices, design patterns, testing strategies, and operational discipline.</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;Team Leadership &amp; Process Stewardship</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Delivery &amp; Execution:</strong> Act as a team steward, driving execution, managing team velocity, breaking down bottlenecks, and maintaining operational sustainability.</li> <li><strong>Agile &amp; Work Management:</strong> Facilitate planning, standups, and prioritization; partner with data analysts and business leaders to translate business needs into well-defined, incremental stories.</li> <li><strong>Process Critique &amp; Improvement:</strong> Regularly evaluate team processes to refine norms and eliminate friction.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Cross-Functional Collaboration &amp; Stakeholder Alignment</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Stakeholder Enablement:</strong> Serve as the primary technical contact for analytics and business leaders to ensure data enablement across departments.</li> <li><strong>Project Communication:</strong> Maintain radical transparency on team roadmaps, risks, delays, and progress.</li> <li><strong>Business &amp; Strategy Alignment:</strong> Translate complex technical concepts into business terms for cross-functional partners and leadership.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Technical Governance &amp; Architecture Leadership</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>AI-Ready Platform Architecture:</strong> Direct the design and scale of our Snowflake-based data platform, ingestion architecture, and AI interface layers.</li> <li><strong>Enterprise Integrations:</strong> Oversee seamless data ingestion from core systems (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Zendesk, Jira, Confluence) into a centralized, queryable source of truth.</li> <li><strong>Data Governance &amp; Observability:</strong> Establish company-wide standards for data ownership, access management, lineage visibility, testing/validation, and automated pipeline monitoring.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Performance Objectives</strong></p> <p><strong>Within 30 Days</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Team &amp; Management Foundation:</strong> Establish recurring 1:1s with direct reports, assess team dynamics and individual skill sets, and align on individual goals and development paths.</li> <li><strong>Stakeholder Mapping:</strong> Build working relationships with key cross-functional stakeholders to map out current data dependencies, pain points, and reporting workflows.</li> <li><strong>Full Data Ecosystem Audit:</strong> Conduct a comprehensive audit of the end-to-end data stack (<strong>Snowflake, Fivetran, dbt, Looker, etc.</strong>) to evaluate cloud spend, pipeline reliability, data transformations, data quality gaps, and constraints for future AI initiatives.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Within 60 Days</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Operational Execution:</strong> Refine team operating rhythms (planning, standups, retro) and prioritization processes to improve delivery transparency and reduce operational friction for analytics requests.</li> <li><strong>Standards &amp; Quick Wins:</strong> Define foundational engineering standards (code review, dbt testing/modeling guidelines, monitoring/alerting) and implement 1–2 quick wins to improve immediate pipeline reliability.</li> <li><strong>Architectural Options Drafting:</strong> Draft initial proposals for a modernized, cost-effective data architecture across ingestion, transformation, and storage, evaluating trade-offs between current tooling, usage-based pricing, and AI integration requirements.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Within 90 Days</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Architecture Recommendation: </strong>Deliver a formal, well-documented recommendation for a modernized data architecture across the entire stack that optimizes tool and infrastructure costs, improves processing efficiency, and provides a scalable foundation for AI solutions.</li> <li><strong>Self-Service &amp; title: Manager, IT Project Management
jd_text: Are you someone who strives for excellence, values accountability, provides the best service, all while reflecting unwavering integrity? Our talented team members across the state follow the behaviors, beliefs and outcomes of these core values to ensure that our vision is met. If you're ready to join the TSTC family and make great memories please complete our application process. Job Description The Manager of IT Project Management provides leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight for the planning, execution, governance, and delivery of technology projects across Texas State Technical College. This position leads the IT Project Management team and is responsible for establishing consistent project management practices, strengthening institutional accountability, improving portfolio visibility, and ensuring technology initiatives align directly with College priorities. Reporting to the Director of IT Operational Services, the Manager collaborates closely with IT leadership, technical teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to manage scope, resources, schedules, dependencies, risks, and organizational change. The Manager fosters a culture of delivery excellence by balancing structured governance with agile, scalable practices adapted to project size and complexity. Essential Functions The employee will demonstrate TSTC’s Core Values of Excellence, Accountability, Service, and Integrity with internal and external stakeholders, customers, students, and community members. Team Leadership & Capability Development Provides direct leadership, mentorship, and operational supervision to the IT Project Management team by setting clear performance expectations, conducting regular evaluations, and fostering ongoing professional development. Fosters a collaborative and accountable team culture that emphasizes customer service, continuous capability growth, and disciplined project execution across all technology initiatives. Project Portfolio Governance & Reporting Establishes, implements, and continuously refines institutional IT project management standards, methodologies, templates, and performance metrics across predictive, Agile, and hybrid delivery frameworks. Monitors overall portfolio health, resource capacity, and schedule milestones while delivering transparent, data-driven reporting and actionable recommendations to executive and IT leadership. Project Execution & Technical Integration Oversees the end-to-end execution of complex, cross-functional technology initiatives involving enterprise software, cloud platforms, infrastructure, data analytics, and cybersecurity. Collaborates with technical engineering teams and functional stakeholders to ensure project deliverables, system integrations, and technical requirements remain aligned throughout the project lifecycle. Stakeholder Management & Organizational Change Partners with academic, administrative, and operational leaders to align technology solutions with departmental needs while actively managing project scope, risks, and conflicting priorities. Integrates structured organizational change management practices into project delivery to facilitate effective communication, end-user training, operational adoption, and sustainable transition to operational support. Project Intake, Prioritization & Continuous Improvement Leads the project intake, evaluation, and prioritization processes to assist leadership in assessing business value, technical complexity, budget impact, and resource feasibility. Directs post-implementation reviews and project retrospectives to systematically capture lessons learned, eliminate delivery roadblocks, and drive institutional process improvements. Education & Experience Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, Project Management, Management Information Systems, or a related field. 5+ years of progressively responsible experience managing enterprise technology projects, programs, or project portfolios. 2+ years of leadership, supervisory, or significant team lead experience with responsibility for coaching and mentoring project professionals. Preferred Qualifications 7+ years of progressively responsible IT project or portfolio management experience, including three or more years of direct supervisory experience. Demonstrated experience leading a Project Management Office or enterprise technology portfolio within higher education or a complex public sector environment. Professional certification such as Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), or PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP). Demonstrated experience managing enterprise SaaS platforms, ERP systems, system integrations, and multi-campus technology migrations. Relevant experience may be considered in lieu of formal education where appropriate, consistent with TSTC’s equivalency philosophy. Skills & Abilities Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and supervise professional project management staff to achieve high-quality project outcomes. In-depth knowledge of project and portfolio management frameworks across Agile, predictive, and hybrid delivery models. Strong enterprise technology acumen with the ability to bridge technical concepts and operational requirements for diverse audiences. Advanced analytical and problem-solving capabilities to identify dependencies, evaluate operational risks, and recommend sound solutions. Exceptional interpersonal, negotiation, and conflict-resolution skills to drive cross-functional alignment where direct reporting lines do not exist. Proven capability to lead organizational change management initiatives that support technology adoption and operational readiness. Strong organizational and prioritization skills to balance competing initiatives across a multi-campus college environment. Proficiency with enterprise work management and tracking platforms to maintain accurate project records and executive dashboards. Core Competencies Leadership & Team Development Leads with purpose, clarity, and visible commitment to institutional values while empowering team members to achieve high-performance results. Provides meaningful coaching, constructive feedback, and professional growth opportunities to build team capabilities and foster a resilient, service-oriented culture. Job Knowledge & Job Performance Applies deep technical and operational project management expertise to guide teams, solve complex institutional challenges, and deliver high-quality technology solutions. Maintains current knowledge of emerging industry standards, enterprise technologies, and governance practices to continually elevate departmental performance. Ownership & Accountability Takes ownership of team and portfolio outcomes, establishing clear expectations and holding project teams accountable for commitments, timelines, and budgets. Proactively navigates project challenges, makes sound risk-adjusted decisions, and maintains disciplined focus on institutional objectives. Teamwork & Service Cultivates cross-functional partnerships across academic, operational, and statewide departments to ensure shared understanding and customer satisfaction. Encourages an inclusive, collaborative team dynamic grounded in mutual respect, transparency, and responsive service delivery. Planning & Execution Translates organizational strategy into actionable project portfolio roadmaps while optimizing resource allocation and capacity management. Anticipates delivery bottlenecks, manages complex dependencies, and executes structured project plans with urgency, accuracy, and operational discipline. Technology Acumen & Innovation Applies a strong understanding of enterprise applications, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and system architecture to guide informed technology decisions. title: Lead AI Research Scientist II - Digital Safety Research Institute
jd_text: Job Description We have an exciting opportunity for a Lead AI Research Scientist II a t UL Research Institutes. This is a remote based opportunity. The Lead AI Research Scientist II directs advanced research across specialized areas including natural language processing (NLP); computer vision (CV), signal processing (SP), and AI reasoning. This role leads AI safety research including literature surveys, AI safety experimental design, AI/software engineering, data acquisition, data analysis, and documentation necessary to execute comprehensive experimental studies. The Lead AI Research Scientist II defines concepts and criteria to resolve major problems in current programs or approaches. Projects require substantial knowledge of state-of-the-art AI and software engineering principles and theories and use professional concepts and procedures to solve a wide range of research-based problems. UL Research Institutes: At UL Research Institutes (ULRI) , we expand the boundaries of safety science to create a more secure and sustainable world. For more than a century, we have studied the unintended consequences of innovation, designed solutions to mitigate risk and shared our findings with academia, scientists, manufacturers, and policymakers across industries. We identify critical safety and sustainability issues, asking the tough questions because we believe a safer world begins with knowledge. Build a safer, more secure, and sustainable future with us. Join us and work with our Digital Safety teams who conduct the research required to produce that knowledge and put into practice. Digital Safety Research Institute: The Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI) addresses unresolved safety risks and emerging dangers in the world’s digital ecosystem. We aim to help protect people from unwanted access to personal devices and privacy, algorithm, and disinformation threats by working to create a new digital safety ecosystem. DSRI is committed to sharing digital safety insights, collaborating with key stakeholders, and offering extensive outreach and education to help support safer digital environments for people everywhere. What you’ll learn and achieve: As the Lead AI Research Scientist II, you will play a key role in the rapid growth of UL as you: Formulate, design, and manage independent test and evaluation research programs to protect the public from AI systems harms – focusing on testing systems enabling the most public harm. Lead and contribute to the development of competitive research proposals, including using the Heilmeier criteria to define scope, methodology, and deliverables, to secure funding for independent AI test and evaluation research programs. Serve as a principal investigator for Digital Safety’s’ independent test and evaluation research programs in their specialty area. Apply intensive and diverse knowledge of technology and AI/software engineering concepts to execute and manage specific research programs. Analyze experimental results to determine causes of problems and develop solutions, and evaluates technical specifications and factors related to process or design objectives. Plan, design, and complete initial and follow-up procedures as needed to validate the testing and evaluation results. Plan, design, and execute research challenges, using and improving DSRI’s evaluation tools, to lead their AI specialty community to solve problems of importance to transition partners. Propose and host workshops at leading research conferences in AI safety where research challenge winning methods and their comparative results are discussed to move the field forward in producing results that can have impact in public safety. Stay ahead of changing technologies in the field by reading papers and scientific publications and attending academic conferences. Contribute to and/or lead other department specific and cross-functional initiatives. What you’ll experience working at UL Research Institutes: We have pursued our mission of working for a safer, more secure, and sustainable world for nearly 130 years, embedding conscientious stewardship into everything we do. People : Our people make us special. You’ll work with a diverse team of experts respected for their independence and transparency and build a network, because our approach is collaborative. We collaborate across disciplines, organizations, and geographies to build the global scientific response that today’s global challenges require. Interesting work : Every day is different for us here. We see what’s on the horizon and use our expertise to build the foundations of a safer future. You’ll have the opportunity to push the boundaries of human understanding as part of a team working to advance the public good. Grow and achieve : We learn, work, and grow together through targeted development, reward, and recognition programs. Values . Four core values guide our work: collaboration, respect, integrity, and beneficence. By living our values, we inspire the trust essential to fulfilling our mission and foster the partnerships that enable us to pursue a beneficent future in which we all can thrive. Total Rewards : All employees at UL Research Institutes are eligible for bonus compensation. We offer comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans and a generous 401k matching structure of up to 5% of eligible pay. Moreover, we invest an additional 4% into your retirement saving fund after your first year of continuous employment. Depending on your role, you may be able to discuss flexible working arrangements with your manager. We also provide employees with paid time off, including vacation, holiday, sick, and volunteer days. What makes you a great fit: While no one candidate will embody every quality, the successful candidate will bring many of the following professional competencies and personal attributes: Demonstrated general knowledge of AI and software engineering disciplines. Demonstrated experience securing research funding through competitive proposal development. Demonstrated ability to write and win proposals for leading research workshops. Demonstrated ability to attract invitations to give keynote presentations. Excellent communication skills required. Advanced AI engineering, software engineering, and data analysis skills. Ability to collaborate effectively with research scientists, engineers, team members, and external partners to deliver research outcomes. Ability to publish research results at leading academic conferences. Professional education and experience requirements for the role include: PhD in Computer Science with a focus in the applicable AI area of specialty plus 8 or more years of directly related research experience. About UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement UL Research Institutes and UL Standards & Engagement are nonprofit organizations dedicated to advancing safety science research through the discovery and application of scientific knowledge. We conduct rigorous independent research and analyze safety data, convene experts worldwide to address risks, share knowledge through safety education and public outreach initiatives, and develop standards to guide safe commercialization of evolving technologies. We foster communities of safety, from grassroots initiatives for neighborhoods to summits of world leaders. Our organization employs collaborative and scientific approaches with partners and stakeholders to drive innovation and progress toward improving safety, security, and sustainability, ultimately enhancing societal well-being. Our affiliate, UL Solutions, stands alongside us in working for a safer and more sustainable world. UL Solutions conducts testing, verification and certification, and provides training and advisory services, along with data-driven reporting and decision-making tools, for customers around the world. To learn more, visit our website UL.org and ULSE.org . Salary Range: $144,304.94-$198,419.29 Pay Type: Salary

title: Accounting and CyberAccounting, Department of Operations, Innovation, and Leadership - Adjunct Faculty
jd_text: Adjunct Faculty – Accounting & Cyber-Accounting Department of Operations, Innovation, and Leadership | University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) This position is specifically to teach remotely for stateside applicants. Local applicants only; UMGC does not sponsor logistical support for this role. Accounting Information Systems (ACCT 618): A study of the use of information systems in the accounting process, with an emphasis on computer systems and internal controls. Focus is on the analytical tools necessary to evaluate users' accounting information needs and to design, implement, and maintain an accounting information system to support business processes and cycles. Topics include the components of contemporary accounting information systems; security and internal controls, particularly within Internet and e-commerce environments; traditional flow charts and data-flow diagrams; computer networks; theory and application of relational databases; and relational database management systems. Assignments include designing an accounting information system using a commercial database software package. CyberAccounting: Management and Compliance (ACCT 620): An applied study of the principles of information systems management and their integration within private-sector organizations served by accounting professionals. Emphasis is on developing strategic cyber accounting initiatives to increase cybersecurity awareness inside organizations, with organizations in its supply chain, and with other stakeholders. Topics include cybersecurity compliance requirements issued by federal and state regulatory agencies and voluntary cybersecurity standards, such as the G-7 Fundamentals of Cybersecurity for the Financial Sector; and the AICPAs Cybersecurity's Risk Management Framework. Cyber Forensics in Accounting (ACCT 645): An applied study of the tools, techniques, and technologies used in forensic accounting investigations, data analytics, and litigation. Focus is on disentangling obscure evidence discovered during fraud investigations using data analytics. Activities include conducting a forensic accounting investigation, performing analytical tests on financial data, preparing written forensic accounting reports for legal proceedings, and serving as an expert witness providing testimony supported by evidence and analytical tests. Information Technology Auditing (ACCT 660): This course integrates subject matter from accounting and information systems program courses. Advanced principles, techniques, and theories are applied through the analysis and presentation of case studies by student teams. Assignments include a research paper that comprehensively assesses an important current issue or emerging trend in the fields off accounting and information systems. CyberAccounting: Risk Management (ACCT 670): A capstone exploration of the principles of risk management as practiced by federal, state, and local entities. Discussion examines cyber accounting risks management as promulgated by professional accounting organizations such as the AICPA. Risk management techniques are applied to cybersecurity issues confronting professional accounting service providers. Focus is on developing skills in assessing client risks, designing, and developing cybersecurity controls to mitigate cyber-attacks on client data, and conducting penetration tests to identify potential cyber accounting vulnerabilities. At UMGC, we don’t just teach; we empower . Founded in 1947, UMGC is an open-access, minority-serving institution serving over 90,000 nontraditional learners worldwide, including a proud, large military-affiliated population. Our students are mature, highly dedicated, and balancing careers, families, and service. As an Adjunct Faculty member, you are the essential partner helping them bridge the gap between classroom theory and real-world career success. Why Teach with UMGC? Focus on Students, Not Course Design: All courses follow a standardized, pre-designed, unified course model. Standardized rubrics, OER materials, library resources, and digital textbooks are fully provided at no cost to you. You get to focus 100% of your energy on mentoring, facilitating, and providing high-quality feedback—no unpaid course-building required. True Asynchronous Flexibility: Teach with flexibility, on your own schedule. As long as you meet weekly grading, responsiveness, and engagement milestones, your daily hours are entirely up to you. Ongoing Growth: We invest in you. All newly hired faculty receive comprehensive online orientation, alongside ongoing, cost-free professional development opportunities. The Rhythm of Your Week (Key Responsibilities) Adjunct faculty bring our pre-built curriculum to life through real-world expertise and active mentorship. Classroom Engagement & Presence Be Visible: Maintain an active classroom presence at least 5 days per week, introducing yourself with a welcome announcement and driving discussions. Bridge Theory & Practice: Enrich the pre-built curriculum with your own professional expertise and real-world examples. Build Belonging: Foster an inclusive, culturally responsive environment where adult learners feel supported and motivated. Responsiveness & Feedback Stay consistently engaged with learners throughout the course by responding to inquiries, returning feedback, and posting final grades within the expected timeframe. Proactive Support & Collaboration Monitor Progress: Use available data tools to track student engagement and conduct proactive outreach to at-risk students. Team Up: Partner with success coaches, academic staff, and portfolio directors to refer struggling students to UMGC support resources. Stay Connected: Participate in UMGC's vibrant faculty community, including the Program Hub and ongoing training. Course Structure & Time Commitment Format: 100% Online & Asynchronous Term Length: 8-week sessions (3-credit courses) Class Size: Typically, 25–35 students (smaller sections for select courses) Time Commitment: The adjunct faculty role requires a substantial commitment throughout the term focusing not only on academic success but also the social, personal, and professional growth of students Minimum Qualifications: Education: ​ A terminal degree (i.e., PhD, JD, DBA) in Business, Accounting, or a related field from an accredited institution of higher learning At least one certification in the cyber-security area from professional organizations, such as the ISACA-issued CISA Experience: Professional cybersecurity, auditing, compliance management, accounting, finance, and/or business experience Legal Status: Applicants must have and be able to maintain their own legal status in the country in which they apply to teach. The Mindset: A deeply student-centered approach rooted in empathy, flexibility, professional integrity, and cultural responsiveness. Preferred Qualifications: CPA, CIA, CFE, or equivalent certification Experience teaching adult learners in an online, asynchronous environment. Prior postsecondary teaching experience. Active engagement in your discipline's professional community. Materials needed for submission Resume/ Curriculum Vitae Cover letter highly preferred Unofficial Transcripts If selected, candidates with international degrees may be required to submit a translation/degree evaluation from a NACES approved vendor All submissions should include a cover letter and resume . title: Director, Procurement Intelligence & Predictive Analytics, Global
jd_text: About Vantage Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands. Global Procurement & Supply Chain Governance Department The Global Procurement & Supply Chain Governance team supports procurement, source-to-pay processes, supply chain performance, supplier management, working capital visibility, and enterprise decision-making. The team partners closely with Finance, Operations, IT/Data, and procurement stakeholders to improve data quality, build trusted analytics, and translate business needs into measurable operational improvements. Position Overview This role is based remotely in the United States. Vantage is seeking a Director, Procurement Intelligence & Predictive Analytics, Global to lead the strategy, development, and adoption of advanced analytics capabilities across Procurement, Supply Chain, and Finance. This role will drive enterprise-wide data-driven decision making by transforming complex global data into actionable insights that improve operational performance, optimize working capital, mitigate risk, enhance supplier outcomes, and support executive and strategic business decisions. The Director will define and execute the global roadmap for procurement analytics, predictive and prescriptive modeling, machine learning, and decision intelligence solutions across Demand-to-Delivery, Source-to-Pay, supplier performance, spend analytics, inventory and asset management, and cash flow forecasting. Working closely with senior leaders across Procurement, Finance and Technology and Business Functions, this role establishes scalable analytics capabilities, data governance standards, and reporting frameworks that enable informed decision-making and deliver measurable business value worldwide. Essential Job Functions Own and lead the global strategy, roadmap, and governance for procurement analytics, data science, and decision intelligence capabilities that enhance procurement performance, supplier management, sourcing effectiveness, contract compliance, and spend optimization. Serve as a strategic advisor to Procurement, Finance, Technology and executive leadership by translating complex procurement, supplier, inventory, and supply chain data into actionable insights, business strategies, and measurable outcomes. Lead the design and deployment of predictive and prescriptive analytics capabilities, leveraging machine learning, statistical modeling, optimization, forecasting, and decision intelligence to drive enterprise value using both internal and external data sources. Oversee the development and implementation of analytical models supporting demand forecasting, supplier risk management, capacity planning, inventory optimization, lead-time prediction, anomaly detection, and cash flow forecasting. Establish and champion executive dashboards, supplier scorecards, KPI frameworks, and reporting standards that provide visibility into procurement, supply chain, fulfillment, and project performance across the organization. Drive enterprise-wide working capital and cash flow optimization initiatives through advanced analytics of purchasing activity, payment timing, inventory investments, accruals, supplier terms, and capital project spending. Partner with senior leaders across Finance, Procurement, Operations, Technology, and business functions to improve forecasting accuracy, scenario planning, capital allocation, operational efficiency, and supplier performance. Lead transformation initiatives across Source-to-Pay processes by identifying strategic opportunities for automation, compliance improvement, process optimization, and operational excellence. Advance procurement analytics capabilities that increase guided buying adoption, spend visibility, purchase order compliance, invoice matching accuracy, goods receipt management, and overall procurement effectiveness. Establish and maintain global procurement data governance standards, including data quality frameworks, master data management, metadata, lineage, controls, and stewardship practices. Drive a culture of data-driven decision making by promoting analytics adoption, enhancing self-service capabilities, and ensuring analytical insights are embedded into business operations and strategic planning. Influence enterprise data and analytics strategy through collaboration with technology and data teams, ensuring scalable solutions, strong governance, and sustainable business impact. Mentor and develop analytics talent while fostering best practices, innovation, and continuous improvement across the analytics organization. Additional duties as assigned by Management. Job Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, Supply Chain, Finance, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree (MS, MBA, or equivalent) preferred. 10+ years of experience in data science, advanced analytics, business intelligence, analytics engineering, quantitative strategy, or a related discipline, including experience leading enterprise-scale analytics initiatives. 5+ years of experience supporting or partnering with Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, Operations, or other enterprise business functions, with demonstrated influence at the leadership level. Proven experience developing and executing analytics strategies, roadmaps, and operating models that drive measurable business outcomes and organizational transformation. Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and translate complex analytical insights into strategic recommendations, business decisions, and investment priorities. Deep expertise in advanced analytics, machine learning, statistical modeling, forecasting, optimization, and modern cloud data platforms such as Azure Synapse, Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, or similar technologies. Experience leading the development of enterprise reporting, KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, and self-service analytics capabilities using Power BI, Tableau, or similar technologies. Strong understanding of procurement operations, strategic sourcing, supplier management, spend analytics, working capital optimization, Demand to Delivery, Source-to-Pay, Asset & Inventory, and supply chain performance management. Familiarity with procurement and ERP platforms such as Coupa, SAP Ariba, Oracle, Workday, Yardi, SAP ERP, or similar enterprise systems. Expertise in data governance, master data management, data quality, metadata management, lineage, stewardship, and enterprise data management best practices. Experience integrating and leveraging procurement, finance, supplier, inventory, contract, project, ERP, and payment data to drive strategic insights and operational improvements. Preferred experience in data center infrastructure, construction, capital projects, procurement analytics, finance analytics, supply chain analytics, or other CAPEX-intensive environments. Demonstrated success leading cross-functional teams, large-scale transformation initiatives, and enterprise data programs in complex, high-growth organizations. Experience building, mentoring, and developing analytics, business intelligence, or data science talent preferred. Professional certifications such as CDMP, CPSM, CIPS, PMP, or related credentials are preferred. Travel up to 20%, with flexibility to increase as business needs evolve. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Additional Details Salary Range: $180,000-200,000 Base + Bonus (this range is based on Colorado market data and may vary in other locations) This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits. This role leads a shared-services Center of Excellence that partners with regional marketing, product marketing, sales, customer experience, IT and commercial teams to improve the end-to-end customer journey, modernize digital platforms, increase discoverability, enable ecommerce and digital marketing channel growth, and translate data into actionable business insight. This position is responsible for the leadership and development of digital marketing experience, analytics, CRM, marketing operations and related team members. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Develop and execute the multi-year strategy and operating roadmap for digital experience, marketing operations, CRM, analytics, marketing technology, AI-enabled capability building and digital channel enablement across the Americas. Own the strategy for Watts digital properties, including customer journey design, user experience, search discoverability, conversion optimization, personalization, accessibility and site performance. Advance ecommerce and digital channel growth by partnering with sales, channel, product and commercial teams to improve product content, digital merchandising, lead capture, customer acquisition and engagement. Build executive-level dashboards, attribution models and reporting structures that connect digital engagement, campaign performance, pipeline influence, customer behavior and marketing investment to business results. Establish scalable operating models, governance frameworks, service level expectations and intake/prioritization processes that enable consistent support for stakeholders across brands, regions and functions. Drive AI and automation adoption to improve productivity, speed to market, campaign effectiveness, content creation, insight generation and customer engagement. Serve as a strategic partner to regional and global stakeholders, translating commercial priorities into digital capabilities, measurable initiatives and clear execution plans. Manage agency, consulting and technology partnerships, including scopes of work, budgets, performance expectations and continuous improvement opportunities. Champion Watts values of Integrity, Accountability, Continuous Improvement, Innovation and Transparency through leadership actions, team development and cross-functional collaboration. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Analytics, Information Systems or related field; equivalent experience considered. 12+ years of progressive leadership experience in digital marketing, digital experience, ecommerce, marketing operations, analytics, CRM, marketing technology or customer experience. 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leading managers, developing talent and building high-performing cross-functional teams. Proven experience building or transforming a digital marketing, ecommerce, customer experience or marketing operations function in a complex, multi-brand or matrixed environment. Demonstrated ownership of website strategy, user experience, customer journey optimization, SEO/SEM, digital campaign performance and conversion improvement. Hands-on leadership experience with CRM, marketing automation, analytics platforms, web content management systems, data governance practices and marketing technology/vendor ecosystems. Strong ability to connect digital activity to business outcomes through dashboards, attribution, financial analysis, executive reporting and actionable insights. Executive communication, change leadership, stakeholder management and cross-functional partnership skills, with the ability to influence sales, marketing, product, IT, finance and operations leaders. Experience supporting ecommerce growth, digital merchandising, product information management, distributor/channel enablement or marketplace optimization. title: Digital Product Strategy & Delivery Director
jd_text: At TruStage, we’re on a mission to make a brighter financial future accessible to everyone. We put people first, and work hand in hand with employees and customers to create a diverse and inclusive environment. Join a team that has received numerous awards for being a top place to work: TruStage awards and recognition Job Purpose: Leads the strategy, performance, and long-term direction of a portfolio of digital products and experiences. Guides Digital Product Owners in shaping product visions and roadmaps, participating directly in business strategy and performance discussions, and leading cross-functional product teams to deliver digital experiences that drive measurable business, customer, operational, and enterprise results. Leverages and strengthens a product-centric operating model that brings Product, Design, Technology, Analytics, and business partners together around shared outcomes. Uses this model to enable Digital Product Owners to lead with clear accountability, build effective cross-functional teams, and move work from strategy through delivery, measurement, and continuous improvement. Job Responsibilities: Portfolio Strategy & Outcomes Set the portfolio vision, strategy, measures, and long-term capability direction in line with enterprise and business priorities. Take responsibility for overall portfolio performance and ensure product strategies and roadmaps add up to the expected results. Turn enterprise goals, business opportunities, customer needs, operating challenges, compliance requirements, and platform needs into a coherent set of digital capabilities and experiences. Balance immediate outcomes with modernization, maintenance, stability, compliance, accessibility, technical health, and long-term sustainability. Recommend portfolio investments and resolve tradeoffs among cross-functional product teams when demand exceeds capacity. Guide business leaders in understanding how digital experiences, data, customer insight, and emerging capabilities can expand what the business is trying to achieve. Position Digital Product Owners as the primary point of engagement for capability and experience decisions within their cross-functional product teams. Portfolio Governance Organize each cross-functional product team around clear outcomes and provide the recurring capabilities it needs to carry work from opportunity through sustained performance. Give Digital Product Owners room to lead while maintaining clear escalation points, portfolio alignment, and accountability for results. Build effective cross-functional teams by assembling the skills and capacity needed from across the organization and establishing shared accountability for operating as a single, autonomous delivery team. Resolve dependencies and decisions across cross-functional product teams at the lowest practical level without sacrificing shared capabilities or long-term commitments to short-term priorities. Product Management & Talent Leadership Lead, coach, and develop Digital Product Owners and other managers and professional staff, building leadership depth and succession readiness across the portfolio. Develop Digital Product Owners who act as trusted business partners, lead across functions, make sound product decisions, and remain accountable for results and long-term value. Establish clear Product Owner accountability for product vision, strategy, roadmaps, priorities, sequencing, backlog decisions, and results across the full product lifecycle. Set consistent expectations for discovery, research, experimentation, analytics, prioritization, value realization, and ongoing product health without limiting Product Owner autonomy. Strengthen the Product Management competency and build needed organizational capabilities through shared practices, coaching, talent development, succession planning, and continuous improvement. Innovation & Future Capability Development Monitor emerging technologies, customer expectations, market shifts, and digital practices and identify where they create practical opportunities for the portfolio. Bring forward ideas that can improve results, raise business ambition, or create new value. Test and adopt new capabilities through the appropriate cross-functional product teams, with clear ownership from concept through measurement. Move successful ideas into durable product roadmaps and operating ownership. The above statement of duties is not intended to be all inclusive and other duties will be assigned from time to time. Job Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in related field, or equivalent combination of education and/or related professional work experience. 12+ years of progressive experience in digital strategy, product management, customer experience, marketing, servicing, analytics, technology-enabled transformation, or a related field. 7+ years of leadership experience, including developing leaders, leading cross-functional teams, and building organizational capabilities. A record of leading a portfolio of digital products or capabilities and delivering measurable business, customer, operational, strategic, or enterprise results. Experience making Product Owners and cross-functional product teams active participants in business strategy, planning, and performance management. Experience establishing product-centered operating models, cross-functional product teams, product roadmaps, decision rights, and lifecycle practices. Ability to lead through influence and align senior leaders across business, Product, Design, Marketing, Analytics, Architecture, Engineering, Creative, and other functions. Strong business and digital judgment, with the ability to shape strategy, challenge assumptions, prioritize investment, manage competing needs, and make decisions that advance enterprise objectives. Strong communication, relationship management, organizational leadership, and executive presentation skills. Preferred Experience in a financial services organization or heavily regulated industry. jd_text: Adjunct Faculty – Operations Management Department of Operations, Innovation, and Leadership | University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) This position is specifically to teach on-site in San Antonio, Texas. Data, Cybersecurity, and AI in Business Strategy (BMGT 250): An interdisciplinary introduction to data analysis, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence (AI) in business operations and decision-making. The goal is to collect, process and analyze business data, identify cybersecurity threats; and explore AI fundamentals for business applications. Topics include data processing techniques, cybersecurity risk analysis, and practical AI tools. Operations Management (OPMG 300): A comprehensive study of the design and management of business operations, with an emphasis on building competitive advantage. Objectives include the optimization of both product and service operating processes. Topics include product development, process analysis, project management, quality management and the supply chain. Sustainability Management (OPMG 310): An introduction to the principles, strategies, and practical applications of sustainable business practices.¿ Going beyond traditional profit incentives, this course also integrates social responsibility, environmental stewardship, sustainable resource utilization and economic stability into organizational decision making. Topics include environmental, social, and economic impacts of business, emerging trends and innovation, sustainable business strategies that contribute to long-term profitability. Quality in the Value Chain (OPMG 320): A study of tools and methodologies for improving quality across the organizational value chain with a goal to identify, analyze and reduce inefficiencies while enhancing customer satisfaction. Apply quality management techniques across different stages of the value chain to improve overall customer satisfaction and performance. Topics include quality assessment, quality improvement initiatives and applying quality management techniques to improve the value chain. Supply Chain (OPMG 340): An applied study of procurement processes with an emphasis on utilizing project management techniques. The objective is to effectively manage procurement activities through supplier selection, contract management, negotiation strategies, and risk management. Topics are explored through case studies, interactive simulations, and practical exercises. At UMGC, we don’t just teach; we empower .
