title: Sr. Full Chip Physical Verification Engineer (Silicon Engineering)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR.&nbsp;</strong><strong>FULL CHIP PHYSICAL VERIFICATION ENGINEER (SILICON ENGINEERING)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking a motivated, proactive, and intellectually curious engineer who will work alongside world-class cross-disciplinary teams (systems, firmware, architecture, design, validation, product engineering, ASIC implementation). In this role, you will be developing cutting-edge next-generation silicon for deployment in space and ground infrastructures around the globe. These chips are enabling connectivity in places it has previously not been available, affordable or reliable. Your efforts will help deliver cutting-edge solutions that will expand the performance and capabilities of the Starlink network.&nbsp; &nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Own and execute full-chip DRC, LVS, ESD, PERC and antenna signoff using industry standard tools like Calibre, ICV, or Pegasus</li> <li>Develop, maintain, and optimize physical verification flows for advanced node SoC’s.</li> <li>Interpret and implement foundry Design Rule Manuals (DRM) — translate rule updates into verified flow changes</li> <li>Debug and resolve complex DRC/LVS violations across hierarchical full-chip designs</li> <li>Perform ESD verification — validate protection strategies, current paths, and CDM/HBM compliance</li> <li>Drive tapeout readiness by coordinating signoff across block and top-level and Hard IP design teams</li> <li>Engage directly with foundry teams to resolve DRM ambiguities and waiver requests.</li> <li>Develop/modify design flows as needed to meet the overall design quality of results and chip integration requirements.Leverage AI agents to automate rule deck validation, violation triage, and signoff reporting workflows</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering or computer science</li> <li>5+ years of ASIC and/or physical design flow development experience in industry</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience and deep understanding of SOC top level physical design flows (floor-planning, I/O, bump &amp; jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>RF ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation that provides fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Starlink RF Engineer, you will fully own all phased array, Wi-Fi, and other RF systems for this customer-facing hardware. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. In addition, you will own advanced parabolic antenna systems for our gateways/ground stations, which we deploy regionally throughout the world. You will design, implement, and verify small router antennas, phased arrays, and reflector antenna systems. You will interact regularly with senior leadership to influence the fundamental operation of our constellation and network while collaborating with electrical, silicon, software, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to steer this project from initial concept development to full-scale production.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, fabricate and characterize prototypes of antennas, feed systems and RF front ends for next-generation phased arrays, gateways, and consumer wireless products</li> <li>Create electromagnetic simulation models of hardware (antennas, filters, PCB layout) to design and evaluate performance</li> <li>Work in close collaboration with EE, ME, DSP and software engineers to design and validate RF systems</li> <li>Create and test phased array alignment solutions</li> <li>Rapidly develop design validation and production test solutions for our high-volume consumer products</li> <li>Write automation software in python to interact with units under test, test equipment, instrumentation, and documentation systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional RF experience with antennas or communication systems (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)</li> <li>1+ years professional experience with radio test equipment such as spectrum analyzers, vector signal analyzers, vector signal generators, and network analyzers</li> <li>1+ years of professional programming experience in Python, C#, C++, or MATLAB</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in electrical engineering with emphasis in RF/antenna engineering</li> <li>Experience designing wireless communications systems</li> <li>Experience with basic principles of antenna theory</li> <li>Understanding of link budgets and analysis related to communications</li> <li>Thorough understanding of RF active and passive components</li> <li>Experience characterizing radio performance at microwave frequencies</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal</li> <li>Passion for problem solving</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work in a highly cross-functional role</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Aerodynamics Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AERODYNAMICS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Starship Aerodynamics team is responsible for predicting the aerodynamics and aerothermal environments booster and ship experience during all phases of their missions. Aerodynamics engineers use engineering models, simulations and wind-tunnel testing in order to provide the most accurate predictions ahead of flight validation. The team works closely with the GNC (guidance, navigation, and control) team to enable them to safely land and recover both Starship stages once their mission is accomplished. Moreover the team supports engineers responsible for vehicle structures during their design efforts. Aerodynamics engineers are expected to have a clear understanding of the flow fields experienced by our vehicles through the various flight regimes, from subsonic through hypersonic, and apply this understanding while they operate our prediction tools.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prepare, mesh, run, and post process CFD models</li> <li>Review post-flight data and compare to pre-flight estimates</li> <li>Interface with responsible engineers, providing them inputs to their designs and ensuring they have a clear understanding of the physical phenomena they are dealing with</li> <li>Write code and scripts in a variety of languages, making sure they share common interfaces and can be part of a mostly automated workflow</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS &amp; EXPERIENCE</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree in aerospace or mechanical engineering</li> <li>Experience with lower-order, engineering-level analysis tools</li> <li>Proficiency creating watertight 3D models and CFD grids, running CFD on Linux/Unix systems, and post-processing data with Tecplot or ParaView</li> <li>Experience with solvers used by NASA for entry vehicles, e.g. FUN3D, Loci/CHEM, DPLR</li> <li>Experimental testing experience</li> <li>Data processing and analysis in MATLAB or Python</li> <li>Strong background in external, compressible fluid dynamics</li> <li>Self-motivated, with strong organizational, communication and documentation skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ANTENNA ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AUTOMATED WELDING TECHNICIAN (STARSHIP)</strong><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>As an Automated Welding Technician specializing in Starship and Super Heavy Booster fuselage and tank sections, you will operate advanced machinery to fabricate, assemble, and inspect high-precision components critical to spacecraft structures. These sections form the body of the fuselage and the tanks, requiring expertise in metal forming, welding preparation, and quality control to meet stringent aerospace standards for strength, weight, and durability. This role demands attention to detail, safety adherence, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, innovative environment focused on fully reusable space vehicles.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Operate and utilize advanced manufacturing equipment such as robots, welders, and manufacturing software.</li> <li>Set up and calibrate machinery based on engineering blueprints, CAD models, and production specifications to ensure precise dimensions (e.g., tolerances within microns for structural integrity under extreme conditions).</li> <li>Perform material handling, including loading raw materials (e.g., steel coils or gores) and unloading finished sections for further assembly or stacking.</li> <li>Conduct in-process inspections using tools like calipers, laser scanners, and non-destructive testing (NDT) methods to verify quality, detect defects, and ensure compliance with NASA/AS9100 standards.</li> <li>Prepare surfaces and edges of barrel sections for welding and assembly, including cleaning, grinding, beveling, and deburring to ensure optimal joint quality, adhesion, and structural integrity.</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers, welders, and assembly teams to troubleshoot issues, optimize processes, and implement continuous improvements in fabrication techniques, including working with weld development and engineering teams to refine welding parameters, materials, and methodologies for enhanced performance and efficiency.</li> <li>Perform routine preventative maintenance on fabrication equipment, including inspections, lubrication, and minor repairs, to ensure operational reliability, minimize downtime, and extend equipment lifespan.</li> <li>Maintain a clean and organized workspace according to 5S, adhering to safety protocols for handling heavy machinery, hazardous materials, and high-pressure environments.</li> <li>Document production data, including machine logs, quality reports, and maintenance records, using digital systems for traceability.</li> <li>Participate in shift rotations, overtime, and rapid prototyping efforts to support aggressive production timelines for the Starship programs success.</li> <li>Check work after completion of each operation in job and/or completed job to ensure it is complete per drawing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate.</li> <li>1+ years of experience in hardware assembly, test, maintenance, material handling, machine operator, and/or installation; OR certificate from an accredited trade skills program in welding, A&amp;P, manufacturing, and/or electronics.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Technical certification in machining, fabrication, or welding preferred (e.g., AWS Certified Welder or CNC Operator certification).</li> <li>Experience in operating fabrication machinery in a manufacturing setting, ideally in aerospace, automotive, or heavy industry.</li> <li>Proficiency with tools and software such as CNC programming (e.g., G-code), CAD/CAM systems, and quality management software.</li> <li>Strong mechanical aptitude, with knowledge of metalworking processes like rolling, bending, stamping, and heat treatment for aerospace-grade materials.</li> <li>Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings, blueprints, and specifications.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work all shifts (day shift, 6 AM - 6 PM title: Automation & Controls Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AUTOMATION &amp; CONTROLS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX's Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket (collectively referred to as Starship) represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. Starship will be the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, with the ability to carry in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth orbit. We are looking for an automation &amp; controls engineer to help SpaceX develop and build a great variety of automated solutions for Starship Production. This role will be hands-on in designing and activating hardware and software systems for the machines that make up the Starship production line. The role will also support transport and storage solutions for Starship vehicles. The successful applicant will join and be supported by a highly talented team of automation and control engineers with an amazing track record in developing any&nbsp;automated solution imaginable.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Participate in initial equipment conceptual development and carefully balance product specifications, process requirements, layout complexity, cost, and lead-time limits.</li> <li>Lay out new industrial electrical control panels that are NFPA79/NEC/UL508A compliant and create electrical, pneumatic, and fluid schematics.</li> <li>Architect, write, and debug PLC code, emphasizing generating organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable code for manufacturing applications.</li> <li>Develop robot systems to aid in the automated manufacturing of various vehicle sub-components.</li> <li>Implement (ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant) control reliable safety systems for safeguarding robots, gantries, conveyors, and other manufacturing equipment.</li> <li>Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens for complex machinery while providing sufficient feedback for troubleshooting.</li> <li>Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, pneumatic and fluid plumbing.</li> <li>Select and size electrical and electromechanical components such as servo motors and controllers.</li> <li>Deploy automated processes and equipment into production.</li> <li>Set, implement, and maintain schedules and budgets to ensure project completion.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years experience in the design and commissioning of automation and controls systems for industrial applications.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Process integration and electromechanical/mechatronic systems experience.</li> <li>Experience in a variety of robotic weld applications (Kuka, ABB &amp; Fanuc).</li> <li>Robot and PLC simulation experience.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience working with National Instruments software and hardware.</li> <li>Electrical schematic CAD experience using EPlan.</li> <li>C#, .NET, python and/or SQL experience.</li> <li>PLC programming experience, preferably Siemens TIA Portal &amp; Beckhoff TwinCat 3.</li> <li>HMI and SCADA programming experience.</li> <li>Field bus networks, serial communication and Ethernet communication.</li> <li>Hands-on experience building and commissioning high quality electrical control panels and electro-mechanical systems.</li> <li>Knowledge of NEC, NFPA 79, UL508A codes.</li> <li>Exposure to a wide variety of production machinery, industrial sensors, and equipment (vision systems, dispense systems, temperature controllers, laser distance sensors, Nut-Runners, etc).</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.</li> <li>Experience in fast-paced iterative design and manufacturing environments.</li> <li>Experience solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed.</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day.</li> <li>Sit: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) between 1 to 2 hours per day.</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 1 hour per day.</li> <li>Walk: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to 25lbs. (unassisted) between 1 to 2 hours per day.</li> <li>Climb (ladder/stairs): up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Kneel/Crouch: up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Upper body twist: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees: up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description.</li> <li>Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.&nbsp;</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Automation & Controls Engineer, Assembly Manufacturing (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AUTOMATION &amp; CONTROLS ENGINEER, ASSEMBLY MANUFACTURING (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the world.</p> <p>As a member of this team you will lead creative, multi-disciplinary projects spanning machine design, robotics, motion systems, and factory health monitoring that all come together to form the innovative, high-rate factories that allow us to deliver internet to those that need it most.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and manage automation projects - this includes initial factory ideation, machine commissioning, proof of rate capability, and eventual hand-off to operational teams&nbsp;</li> <li>Architect, write, and debug PLC code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for high-volume manufacturing applications&nbsp;</li> <li>Keep our factory safe and and then motivate the team to achieve them&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering, physics, or computer science discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in one or a combination of the following: <ul> <li>Professional or internship experience in industrial or factory automation design and implementation</li> <li>Involvement with a project team designing and building electro-mechanical/robotic/automated systems or products beyond classroom assignments &nbsp;</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED <li>Experience with electromechanical systems</li> <li>Electrical sizing of motors, cables, circuit protection, VFD’s, motor starters, various other motion systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Design of fail-safe electrical circuits using both safety logic controllers and safety-rated relays&nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience troubleshooting industrial electrical systems using tools like multimeters, oscilloscopes, EMI probes</li> <li>Proficiency in understanding and creating electrical schematics and single line diagrams (EPLAN preferred)</li> <li>Field bus networks, serial communication, and Ethernet communication</li> <li>Hands-on experience designing and commissioning high quality electrical panels and electro-mechanical systems with appropriate safety considerations in mind</li> <li>Knowledge of NEC, NFPA, UL508A codes with ability to ensure compliance with control system safety standards&nbsp;</li> <li>PLC programming, preferably Beckhoff TwinCAT structured text programming&nbsp;</li> <li>Programming and implementing machine safety software through the use of safety PLC’s&nbsp;</li> <li>HMI, SCADA, IoT (MQTT, OPC-UA), Ignition systems with focus on user friendly navigation and machine health monitoring and control&nbsp;</li> <li>Field Bus Networking protocols, preferably EtherCAT, Profinet, Profisafe, Ethernet/IP&nbsp;</li> <li>Robotics programming, preferably ABB</li> <li>Industrial software application to mechanical assemblies, electrical systems, sensors, pneumatics/hydraulics, including how to safely checkout these interdisciplinary systems prior to production implementation&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical title: Automation & Controls Engineer, Launch Pad (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AUTOMATION &amp; CONTROLS ENGINEER, LAUNCH PAD (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX’s Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket, collectively known as Starship, is a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We are looking for an automation &amp; controls engineer to develop and build launch and test systems for Starship, focusing on electrical control systems for the launch mount, integration tower, and orbital propellant farm, including input/output (I/O), motion systems, drive controls, and supporting infrastructure. The successful candidate will join a highly talented team of engineers with a proven track record of developing advanced automated solutions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <p>Electrical systems:</p> <ul> <li>Architect, design, integrate, and commission control systems for the Starship launch pads</li> <li>Design industrial electrical control panels that are National Fire Protection Association 79 (NFPA 79)/National Electrical Code (NEC)/Underwriters Laboratories 508A (UL 508A) compliant</li> <li>Design control and data acquisition systems</li> <li>Design and author electrical schematics</li> <li>Design electrical conveyance and distribution systems (e.g., raceways, cables, wiring methods)</li> <li>Work closely with other disciplines; interface control systems with high-power equipment and communication equipment</li> <li>Design electrical systems for hazardous environments</li> </ul> <p>Control software:</p> <ul> <li>Architect, write, and debug programmable logic controller (PLC) code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for similar applications</li> <li>Configure, commission, and tune variable frequency drives (VFDs) for open- and closed-loop control system applications</li> <li>Generate aesthetically simple human-machine interface (HMI) screens for complex machinery while providing sufficient feedback for troubleshooting</li> <li>Commission devices using a variety of industrial communication protocols</li> <li>Set up and tune proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers for continuous processes</li> </ul> <p>Mechanical integration:</p> <ul> <li>Add detail for electrical assemblies to computer-aided design (CAD) models to plan out installation for cable tray, conduit, panel mounting, etc.</li> <li>Design systems that are robust to the mechanical stresses of Starship launch</li> </ul> <p>General responsibilities:</p> <ul> <li>Participate in initial equipment conceptual development and carefully balance product specifications, requirements, layout complexity, cost, and lead-time limits</li> <li>Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, and conveyance installs</li> <li>Set, implement, and maintain schedules and budgets to ensure project completion</li> <li>Document control system built for handoff to pad operators</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in the design and commissioning of control systems for industrial applications (internship experience qualifies)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Electrical schematic CAD experience using EPLAN</li> <li>Mechanical design experience with CAD, such as Siemens NX or SolidWorks</li> <li>Field bus networks, serial communication, and Ethernet communication</li> <li>Hands-on experience building and commissioning high-quality electrical control panels and electro-mechanical systems</li> <li>Knowledge of NEC, UL 508A codes</li> <li>Experience in fast-paced iterative design and test environments</li> <li>Experience solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> <li>Strong work ethic and drive to succeed as part of a high-functioning team</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment</li> <li>Ability to thrive in ambiguity, independently drive project progress, and manage multiple priorities</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of engineering principles behind electronic equipment, instrumentation, and commonly used industrial equipment</li> <li>Experience designing and installing instrumentation and control systems in hazardous areas (National Fire Protection Association 70 (NFPA 70) Section 500 installations); Class 1, Division 1 and Division 2 environments or International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) equivalence</li> <li>Experience with electrical power distribution, working knowledge of NFPA 70 and NFPA 70E</li> <li>Experience with industrial bus protocols such as Modbus, Profinet, and EtherNet/IP</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Must be willing to travel for extended periods, up to 100% during system activation</li> <li>Ability to travel to other SpaceX or third-party facilities (up to 20%)</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 50 lbs. (unassisted) between 1 and 2 hours per day</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Walk: Up to 10 hours per day</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to 25 lbs. (unassisted) between 1 and 2 hours per day</li> <li>Climb (ladder/stairs): up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Kneel/Crouch: up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Upper body twist: Up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees: up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description.</li> <li>Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Automation & Controls Engineer, Solar Cell Factory (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AUTOMATION &amp; CONTROLS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.&nbsp;</p> <p>The Solar Cell team is revolutionizing power generation for space applications through advanced solar cell manufacturing. We're scaling production of high-efficiency solar cells to support sustainable energy solutions for Starlink constellations, launch vehicles, and beyond. As a Solar Cell Factory Automation and Controls Engineer, you will design, build, and optimize controls and automation systems for the production of solar cell manufacturing equipment and material movement mechanisms. This role requires a detail-oriented engineer passionate about safe electrical design, writing robust and elegant control code, and taking on total ownership of existing systems for optimization in addition to development of novel equipment, all while minimizing risks and maximizing efficiency in our cutting-edge solar cell factory.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and manage automation projects - including initial factory ideation, machine commissioning, proof of rate capability, and eventual hand-off to operational teams &nbsp;</li> <li>Architect, write, and debug PLC code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for high-volume manufacturing applications &nbsp;</li> <li>Keep our factory safe and reliable by implementing ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant systems for robots, gantries, conveyors, and other manufacturing equipment&nbsp;</li> <li>Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens to make complex machines easy to understand, operate, and troubleshoot&nbsp;</li> <li>Integrate individual equipment pieces into master SCADA and MES systems</li> <li>Design electrical systems compliant to NEC, NFPA, &amp; UL508A regulations&nbsp;</li> <li>Stay organized by creating schedules and budgets, and then motivate the team to achieve them &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or chemical discipline &nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of experience with high-speed manufacturing, controls and automation, and/or programming (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Excited by a quick and iterative design and manufacturing role&nbsp;</li> <li>Proven ability to solve complex problems with simple solutions in both design and implementation stages&nbsp;</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal, with the ability to make plans and directional recommendations collaboratively and cross-functionally&nbsp;</li> <li>Ability to engineer creative, new approaches to problems while adhering to ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA safety requirements to keep a factory safe &nbsp;</li> <li>Hazardous process expertise in an aerospace, oil and gas, or chemical industry where high pressure or hazardous systems for fluids or gasses were in use</li> <li>Experience with at least one of the specific disciplines listed below. The ideal candidate is interested in learning at least the fundamentals of the other areas they are not yet strong in</li> </ul> <p><em>Electrical/Industrial Controls: &nbsp;</em></p> <ul> <li>Electrical sizing of motors, valves, pneumatics, cables, circuit protection, VFDs, motor starters, various other motion systems &nbsp;</li> <li>Design of fail-safe electrical circuits using both safety logic controllers and safety-rated relays &nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience troubleshooting industrial electrical systems using tools like multimeters, oscilloscopes, EMI probes&nbsp;</li> <li>Proficiency in understanding and creating electrical schematics and single line diagrams (EPLAN preferred)&nbsp;</li> <li>Field bus networks, serial communication, Profinet and Ethernet communications&nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience designing and commissioning high quality electrical panels and electro-mechanical systems with appropriate safety considerations in mind&nbsp;</li> <li>Knowledge of NEC, NFPA, UL508A codes with ability to ensure compliance with control system safety standards &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><em>Industrial Software: &nbsp;</em></p> <ul> <li>PLC programming, preferably Siemens TIA Portal or Beckhoff TwinCAT structured text + ladder&nbsp;</li> <li>HMI, SCADA, IoT (MQTT, OPC-UA), ignition systems with focus on user friendly navigation and machine health monitoring and control &nbsp;</li> <li>Field Bus Networking protocols, preferably EtherCAT, Profinet, Profisafe, Ethernet/IP &nbsp;</li> <li>Robotics programming, preferably ABB&nbsp;</li> <li>Industrial software application to mechanical assemblies, electrical systems, sensors, pneumatics/hydraulics, including how to safely checkout these interdisciplinary systems prior to production implementation &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: &nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones &nbsp;</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Automation & Controls Specialist

title: Automation and Controls Engineer, Gateways (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">AUTOMATION AND CONTROLS ENGINEER, GATEWAYS (STARLINK)</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">One key component of SpaceX’s success so far is our commitment to keeping all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision making, and speedy deliverables. Automation and Controls Engineers at our Bastrop site are hyper-focused on designing and developing&nbsp;full&nbsp;factory solutions for&nbsp;novel technologies&nbsp;that are critical to our mission of connecting the unconnected. As a member of this team, you will lead creative, multi-disciplinary projects spanning machine design, robotics, motion systems, and factory health monitoring that all come together to form the innovative, high-rate factories that allow us to deliver internet to those that need it most. </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><strong><span title: Automation Build Engineer, Development (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>AUTOMATION BUILD ENGINEER, DEVELOPMENT (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.</p> <p>As a build engineer on the Development Operations team, you will be responsible for leading large-scale projects, developing standardized procedures, and optimizing fabrication and integration processes to drive overall efficiency inside our shop, across our internal customer base and strategic partnerships with local vendors.</p> <p>Working in concert with Starlink engineering product teams, supply chain, materials management, and leadership, you will coordinate ownership across these multi-disciplinary teams. You will collaborate daily, driving meaningful changes to processes, procedures, planning, and organization to improve fabrication and integration workflow. You will take extreme ownership of deliverables, schedule adherence, and alignment with overall program milestones.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as the primary liaison between automation, supply chain, production, and development operations to ensure factory infrastructure is built and deployed to meet program milestones</li> <li>Ideate and implement new manufacturing processes and workflows within the development operations team to increase shop throughput, efficiency and personnel safety</li> <li>Manage the build, configuration and instillation of all modular automation assets within the team’s catalog from raw material purchase to complete cell build and handoff to automation/production</li> <li>Work with peer engineering and support teams to drive design updates in response to manufacturing issues, part obsolescence, and system requirement changes</li> <li>Prepare engineering documentation necessary for the transition from development to production including assembly procedures, integration instruction and manufacturing bills of materials</li> <li>Work with supplier and internal vendors to fabricate piece parts and sub-assemblies at rate to meet production needs or supplement internal capacity</li> <li>Contribute to design reviews acting as an expert in design for manufacturability, design for reliability, design for maintenance, supplier capabilities assessments, quality control, etc.</li> <li>Spearhead cost reduction efforts and implement initiatives to meet and exceed departmental objectives while not compromising on quality</li> <li>Design, develop, validate, and implement tooling to ensure repeatability and efficiency</li> <li>Primary point of contact for non-conforming product (cells, panels &amp; tooling), troubleshooting, root cause, failure investigations and corrective actions</li> <li>Develop training requirements for built technician personnel and work to elevate overall team capability and productivity</li> <li>Work creatively and innovate to support SpaceX's goals by always being prepared to challenge the status quo</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ years of experience in design, manufacturing, and/or production of mechanical or electrical hardware systems (internship and collegiate extracurricular engineering project experience qualifies)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of experience implementing design for manufacture for electromechanical systems</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in design and/or production of mechanical or electronics hardware systems</li> <li>Ability to create and deliver presentations for design and manufacturing readiness reviews</li> <li>Experience transitioning products from design to manufacturing as part of a cross-functional team in a fast-paced iterative design environment</li> <li>Experience modeling with 3D CAD software such as: NX, Catia, Solidworks or equivalent</li> <li>Working proficiency with DFMEA and PFMEA methodology and implementation</li> <li>SPC (Statistical Process Control) knowledge and experience applying statistical methods to track process capability</li> <li>Competency with SQL databases</li> <li>Demonstrated experience designing tooling in a manufacturing environment</li> <li>Hands-on engineer with a passion for continuous improvement</li> <li>Capable of solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> <li>Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>BAW DEVICE ENGINEER (STARLINK/AKOUSTIS)</strong></p> <p>Akoustis is now operating as a wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX, providing industry leading RF filters using patented XBAW technology to help drive the mission of making human life multi-planetary and connecting the world through Starlink.&nbsp;We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game-changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</p> <p>XBAW technology utilizes MEMS-based thin film transfer process, enabling a broad range of piezoelectric material synthesis and compositions tailored for specific application needs with enhanced material properties and an optimized resonator performance including superior figure of merit from coupling and Q factor. Our Device Engineers plays a critical role in developing and improving XBAW resonators and supporting filter designs. This person will perform FEM simulations and experimental DOE to improve the figure of merit of BAW resonators, with an emphasis on developing efficient process integration and reduced cycle time for lean filter development.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and improve FEA setups (COMSOL, HFSS) for BAW resonator simulations and optimization</li> <li>Improve the as short cycle time</li> <li>Support BAW filter design with dimensions and process integration</li> <li>Define and generate resonator equivalent circuit models to be used in filter design</li> and yield improvement</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience with semiconductor devices, RF, title: BIM Specialist
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We are currently seeking a BIM Specialist to lead the integration and coordination of Building Information Modeling (BIM) across fast-paced multidisciplinary projects, ensuring project objectives are met through effective model management and collaboration. This position will serve as a key technical resource, supporting project teams and fostering strong BIM practices throughout the project lifecycle.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and maintain detailed 3D BIM models using industry-standard software (Revit, Navisworks, AutoCad) for architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), and other engineering disciplines</li> <li>Perform clash detection, model coordination, and constructability reviews to identify and resolve conflicts early in the design and construction phases</li> <li>Lead BIM coordination efforts for multi-disciplinary projects, ensuring the seamless integration of models and data. The ideal candidate will have owned BIM coordination through construction administration on multiple large scale projects and have a solid understanding of means and methods of construction</li> <li>Experience in aerospace, high-tech manufacturing, or mission-critical facilities projects.</li> <li>Proficiency in BIM authoring and coordination tools, including Revit (advanced level), Navisworks, and related plugins; jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>BUILD ENGINEER (STARSHIP)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>As a build engineer on the Starship team, you will be responsible for developing and qualifying processes for high-rate, mixed-product manufacturing of propulsion, avionics, and welded structural assemblies. Focus will be on design for manufacturing, implementing poka-yoke systems, increasing product yield, and automation as required to minimize takt and cycle times.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and perform acceptance testing of manufacturing processes, techniques, and tools to enable efficient and high-rate manufacturing</li> <li>Design and implement precision tooling to eliminate assembly error, improve quality, and minimize cycle time</li> <li>Automate novel processes to ensure repeatability on high-rate manufacturing lines</li> <li>Work closely with design engineering teams to influence flight design and vehicle architecture with design for manufacturing improvements</li> <li>Develop and/or automate in-situ inspection techniques to increase yield and decrease cycle time</li> <li>Manage transition of parts and assemblies from development to high-rate production</li> <li>Challenge and simplify requirements to optimize processes and reduce overhead</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's or advanced degree in aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of manufacturing and process design experience (internship and academic experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>Hands-on project experience with mixed value stream or high-rate manufacturing lines, focusing on maximizing yield and increasing rate</li> <li>Proficiency in mechanical assembly methods, testing, failure mode effects analysis, and troubleshooting</li> <li>Experience with integration and testing of propulsion, thermal, electrical, and/or structural systems</li> <li>Prior experience with developing, maintaining, and improving weld processes and weld inspection techniques, inclusive of automation</li> <li>Experience using SQL or other data management structures to inform priorities and measure performance</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Flight hardware typically is built in tight quarters and physical dexterity is required</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Flexibility to travel to remote build sites, up to 10%</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 30 minutes to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Walk: Up to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to 25lbs. (unassisted) 30 minutes to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Kneel/Crouch: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees 6 hours or greater per day</li> <li>Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description</li> <li>Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Build Reliability Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>BUILD RELIABILITY ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a Build Reliability Engineer, you will be part of a widely interdisciplinary team developing global manufacturing procedures, maximizing quality through efficient production. You will employ “reliability by any means necessary”, stretching your expertise in fabrication methods, work instructions, tooling design, inspection procedures, data gathering/visualization, and broad collaboration. You will build new processes from the ground up, and routinely grade/improve execution of existing processes, driving continuous production improvement and ultimately be responsible for build-induced vehicle risk.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop manufacturing, integration, assembly, welding, NDE, cleanliness, and checkouts processes from the ground up, then enforce consistency across different work centers.</li> <li>Design and implement tooling for work access, mechanical/avionics/propulsion testing, build fixturing, lifting &amp; rigging, and fluids.</li> <li>Define and document inspection requirements and procedures.</li> <li>Create training for production and inspection processes.</li> <li>Author planning, test plans, and training to execute processes and collect data, ensuring efficient and stable quality at increasing production volumes.</li> <li>Contain non-conforming hardware in collaboration with quality, production, and design groups to ensure systemic issues are corrected, and risk is managed for the fleet.</li> <li>Work closely with design teams to improve DFM and requirement fulfillment. Aggressively modify requirements and manufacturing process where design intent and production rate are incompatible.</li> <li>Conduct build quality reviews to identify repeat and high impact issues. Drive corrective action within and outside of your work center.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, materials engineering, manufacturing engineering, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, or engineering physics.</li> <li>1+ years in manufacturing, quality, and/or design engineering role (student project team or internship experience qualifies).</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with the build, assembly, or integration of structures, avionics, valves, fluid system components, actuators, thermal protection systems, or other aerospace components.</li> <li>Mechanical tooling or component design and design for manufacturability.</li> <li>Proficiency with 3D CAD Software such as NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA.</li> <li>Knowledge of mig, tig, laser, stud, spot, or robot welding techniques, as well as visual, penetrant, x-ray, EMAT, or other NDT processes.</li> <li>Involvement in a collegiate or hobby design project (Formula SAE, rocketry, etc).</li> <li>Proficiency with SQL and Power BI or other database/query/data visualization suite.</li> <li>You thrive in a hands-on environment and are hungry to step out of the office, onto the shop floor.</li> <li>Knowledge of metallic manufacturing techniques, processes, and equipment related to machining, bending, forming, casting, additive manufacturing, fastening, drilling, and/or bonding.</li> <li>Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate with partners/customers from a diverse set of engineering disciplines.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Through root-cause analysis, escalations ownership, and line optimization, the role enables the production rates and structural integrity needed for Starship’s high flight cadence.&nbsp;</span></p> title: Build Supervisor (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>BUILD SUPERVISOR (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Build Supervisor is responsible for leading a team of fabricators, welders, and technicians building the primary and secondary structures for the Starship and Super Heavy vehicles. The Build Supervisor is the most influential person on-site to drive progress on an hour-by-hour and day-by-day basis. The Supervisor of the team will take technical direction from the engineering team and turn it into reality by building, retaining, and managing their team effectively; distributing labor resources, prioritizing certain aspects of the build, and setting headcount requirements where necessary. The Supervisor is also a key enabler to a productive, fun, and hard-working culture. For this role specifically, it is highly important that the Supervisor is an inspiring leader, oftentimes working side by side with their build team.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supervise shop floor activity, including daily schedules and workflow</li> <li>Lead and manage a staff of ~30 technicians including all performance management related tasks</li> <li>Review work instructions and make change recommendations when needed</li> <li>Assess and vet appropriate skillsets as needed</li> <li>Identify training needs and develop training programs</li> <li>Provide required data and reporting to support departmental metrics and improvement objectives</li> <li>Monitor labor hours and overtime, and implement improvement plans and time management with staff</li> <li>Accomplish production results by communicating job expectations; planning, monitoring, appraising job results</li> <li>Effectively organize, assign and track work/deliverables for the team, ensuring seamless progression through multi-shift work schedules</li> <li>Initiate and foster a spirit of cooperation within and between departments</li> <li>Ensure product quality and conformance to specifications</li> <li>Maintain tooling and consumable supply inventory</li> <li>Improve area safety and efficiency through regular auditing and continuous improvement</li> <li>Continuously improve process and manpower efficiency, utilization and productivity</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree or 5+ years of experience in final assembly production: aviation, aerospace, mechanical systems</li> <li>2+ years of experience in leading a team or a project</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>A&amp;P license</li> <li>Experience applying lean manufacturing principles and efficiency methods</li> <li>8+ years of experience in final assembly and production in a fast paced manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience bringing teams and processes from development to production highly desirable</li> <li>Familiarity with design for manufacturability, kaizen, lean manufacturing, six sigma, and failure mode effects analysis</li> <li>Ability to effectively communicate (verbal and written) with Engineering and Production</li> <li>Able to adapt to constant changing work assignments and fast paced work environment</li> <li>Excellent concentration and attention to detail with outstanding work efficiency and accuracy</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends, which varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Must be available to work 1st shift or 2nd shift</li> <li>Must be able to travel for short and extended trips as needed</li> <li>Stand: Up to 10 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 1 hour</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. The Supervisor of the team will take technical direction from the engineering team and turn it into reality by building, retaining, and managing their team effectively; distributing labor resources, prioritizing certain aspects of the build, and setting headcount requirements where necessary. The Supervisor is also a key enabler to a productive, fun, and hard-working culture. For this role specifically, it is highly important that the Supervisor is an inspiring leader, oftentimes working side by side with their build team.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supervise shop floor activity, including daily schedules and workflow</li> <li>Lead and manage a staff of ~30 technicians including all performance management related tasks</li> <li>Review work instructions and make change recommendations when needed</li> <li>Assess and vet appropriate skillsets as needed</li> <li>Identify training needs and develop training programs</li> <li>Provide required data and reporting to support departmental metrics and improvement objectives</li> <li>Monitor labor hours and overtime, and implement improvement plans and time management with staff</li> <li>Accomplish production results by communicating job expectations; planning, monitoring, appraising job results</li> <li>Effectively organize, assign and track work/deliverables for the team, ensuring seamless progression through multi-shift work schedules</li> <li>Initiate and foster a spirit of cooperation within and between departments</li> <li>Ensure product quality and conformance to specifications</li> <li>Maintain tooling and consumable supply inventory</li> <li>Improve area safety and efficiency through regular auditing and continuous improvement</li> <li>Continuously improve process and manpower efficiency, utilization and productivity</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree or 5+ years of experience in final assembly production: aviation, aerospace, mechanical systems</li> <li>2+ years of experience in leading a team or a project</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>A&amp;P license</li> <li>Experience applying lean manufacturing principles and efficiency methods</li> <li>8+ years of experience in final assembly and production in a fast paced manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience bringing teams and processes from development to production highly desirable</li> <li>Familiarity with design for manufacturability, kaizen, lean manufacturing, six sigma, and failure mode effects analysis</li> <li>Ability to effectively communicate (verbal and written) with Engineering and Production</li> <li>Able to adapt to constant changing work assignments and fast paced work environment</li> <li>Excellent concentration and attention to detail with outstanding work efficiency and accuracy</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends, which varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Must be available to work 2nd shift (6:00pm - 6:00am)</li> <li>Flight hardware is typically built in tight quarters and physical dexterity is required</li> <li>Physical effort including sitting or standing for extended periods of time and lifting and carrying weight such as materials or equipment (up to 25 lbs. unassisted)</li> <li>Work performed in an environment with exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Occasionally exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments (heat, cold, rain)</li> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends, which varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Must be able to travel for short and extended trips as needed</li> <li>Stand: Up to 10 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 1 hour</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) 30 minutes to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Overhead reach: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Walk: Up to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Lift/Carry: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 30 minutes to 1 hour per day</li> <li>Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Kneel/Crouch: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees 6 hours or greater per day</li> <li>Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Business Development Manager, US & Canada (Starlink Product Growth)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT MANAGER, US &amp; CANADA (STARLINK PRODUCT GROWTH)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is a revolutionary satellite constellation, delivering low-latency broadband internet around the world—bringing an unprecedented opportunity to significantly impact communities, businesses, and governments worldwide. The Product Growth Team is seeking a Business Development Manager to drive consumer growth through commercial collaborations with adjacent products, services, industries, and affiliate channels. This person will play a key role in shaping how Starlink scales beyond its core service, including exploring innovative ways to reach consumers through digital platforms, affinity groups, and new go-to-market approaches.<br><br>The ideal candidate will have a strong background in business development &amp; partnerships in consumer technology, telecommunications, and/or subscription-based services, with a proven track record of building and executing new business models, structuring commercial opportunities, and scaling revenue. This role requires creativity, strategic thinking, and strong execution skills to translate ideas into market-ready offerings that accelerate adoption of Starlink.<br><br>This is a unique opportunity to work at the cutting edge of connectivity technologies with a world-class team focused on connecting every household and traveler.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Execute business development strategies to expand Starlink’s consumer presence in the US and Canada, with a focus on adjacent products, bundled offerings, and new go-to-market models</li> <li>Identify and evaluate emerging customer acquisition channels to reach consumers (e.g., affiliates, membership programs, utilities, content providers, affinity groups) and build initiatives that scale access and adoption</li> <li>Drive deal execution from opportunity identification through to commercial agreements, ensuring alignment with Starlink’s growth and profitability objectives</li> <li>Represent Starlink in external discussions with prospective commercial relationships</li> <li>Collect and synthesize customer and channel feedback to influence product offering development, pricing strategies, and go-to-market approaches</li> <li>Report on progress of business development initiatives, presenting insights and recommendations directly to Starlink leadership</li> <li>Collaborate with sales, product, marketing, engineering, and finance teams to structure offerings that combine technical feasibility with strong commercial impact</li> <li>Develop business cases for bundled offerings with Starlink (e.g., devices, content, services), including customer value analysis and pilot execution</li> <li>Conduct ongoing market and competitive analysis to identify consumer trends, channel opportunities, and emerging technologies relevant to Starlink’s ecosystem</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, engineering, or a related field</li> <li>5+ years of experience in business development, sales, or partnership management involving consumer technology, telecommunications, utilities, or other subscription-based services</li> <li>3+ years of experience negotiating commercial agreements and managing execution of revenue-driving initiatives</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven experience developing and scaling consumer-focused business models &amp; partnerships in technology, telecommunications, utilities, real estate, or consumer electronic sectors</li> <li>Strong understanding of the US and Canadian consumer markets, particularly in the rural areas, with experience expanding into new channels and solidifying partnerships, bundles, and affiliate deals</li> <li>Demonstrated success in structuring complex business commercial opportunities and driving them to completion</li> <li>Independently motivated with a track record
