title: Dangerous Goods Lead
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p class="s3" style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 13.3333px;"><strong>DANGEROUS GOODS LEAD</strong></span></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a highly motivated Dangerous Goods (DG) Lead, known internally as a Global Logistics Lead to join the Logistics team. This role owns the planning, execution, and continuous improvement of DG policies, controls, and processes to ensure safe, compliant, and scalable transportation of dangerous goods across air, ocean, and ground networks.</p> <p>You will partner closely with internal teams, carriers, consultants, and regulators to drive safety and compliance across the company while enabling new transportation models that support Starlink’s rapid growth. Success in this role requires strong regulatory expertise, operational judgment, and the ability to turn complex requirements into clear, scalable processes.</p> <p class="s3" style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><strong><span class="s2">RESPONSIBILITIES:</span></strong></span></p> <div class="s6" style="line-height: 1.2;"> <ul> <li>Develop, implement, and continuously improve DG policies, procedures, and controls for air, ocean, and ground transportation</li> <li>Serve as the subject matter expert on IATA, 49 CFR, IMDG, and related U.S. and international DG regulations</li> <li>Conduct internal audits of processes and documentation to ensure full regulatory compliance</li> <li>Drive scalable solutions and metric-based continuous improvement that reduce risk and support business growth</li> <li>Build and maintain strong relationships with regulators, industry associations, and key partners</li> <li>Partner with senior leadership across organizations to align policy, risk posture, and operational controls</li> <li>Support new business opportunities and transportation models with clear regulatory guidance</li> </ul> </div> <p class="s3" style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><strong><span class="s4">BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</span></strong></span></p> <div class="s6" style="line-height: 1.2;"> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree We design, build, test, and operate the full stack — satellites, user terminals, and the software that ties it all together.</p> <p style="line-height: 1.2;">As a Data Engineer on the Starlink Enterprise team, you will improve the quality of data flowing into our commercial systems and build the integrations and AI agents that turn that cleaner data into better decisions and faster execution — from pipeline generation through closed revenue and ongoing enablement. You will partner with Enterprise sales, channel and reseller operations, sales ops, and enablement to fix messy inputs, reduce manual cleanup, and ship automations that make go-to-market workflows more reliable.</p> <h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Improve data hygiene and quality across go-to-market systems — title: Design Criteria Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DESIGN CRITERIA ENGINEER (STARSHIP)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>The design criteria team is responsible for ensuring that hardware and operations lead to the mission's successful completion and meet or exceed requirements. This engineer will be industry-unique, stepping into an agile system engineering team, facilitating cross-disciplinary action and problem-solving across all SpaceX programs and engineering staff.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Drive improvements to vehicle design by being closely integrated with hardware teams.</li> <li>Provide critical peer review and approval of hardware designs during design reviews; confirm acceptance and qualification test campaigns.</li> <li>Drive the development of tools and methods to ensure accurate and well-disseminated design criteria.</li> <li>Ensure a cohesive evolution of designs and operations across the different technical teams: avionics, propulsion, structures, launch, manufacturing, analysis, and test.</li> <li>Work with a team to perform rapid conceptual design, analysis, and testing cycles on development hardware (may include CAD modeling and testing oversight as needed).</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years of experience with mechanical design, manufacturing, and/or analysis (internship experience qualifies).</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with aerospace structure systems: design, analysis, testing, and fabrication for use in high-performance or safety critical applications.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with fatigue, vibration, and thermal testing of mechanical assemblies.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with various industry standard manufacturing tools, techniques and processes, including mills, lathes, electronics assembly, composite layup, etc.</li> <li>Experience with material selection and make vs. buy decisions for system components.</li> <li>Experience with solid modeling (Siemens NX) and finite element analysis software (FEMAP).&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience performing closed-form and numerical stress analysis, title: Dynamics Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>DYNAMICS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Starship Dynamics team is responsible for induced vehicle environments, system dynamics and vehicle dynamics on the Starship and HLS vehicles. The dynamics group is focused on defining forcing functions acting on the vehicle, predicting vehicle and system response, and ensuring hardware is qualified for ground testing and flight. The group has a wide range of responsibilities that include structural dynamics, fluid system dynamics, random vibration, engine dynamics and multibody dynamics. Dynamics engineers are expected to have a strong intuition of physics first principles, frequency domain analysis, and a broad range of engineering disciplines, in addition to having solid software and analytical skills.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Resolve dynamics problems through analysis, test and the use of flight data</li> <li>Build finite element and lumped element models of launch vehicle systems</li> <li>Execute dynamic testing from start-to-finish (pre-test analysis, sensor selection &amp; installation, testing, data analysis, signal processing and model correlation)</li> <li>Own system level analysis and drive hardware modifications or vehicle operations across vehicle engineering teams</li> <li>Perform analyses using commercial and in-house codes as well as write new code</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience with structural or fluid dynamics via full-time employment, outside the classroom projects, or lab work</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience either analyzing data or building hardware</li> <li>Experience with frequency-based and/or time-history vibration analysis</li> <li>Experience with vibration, shock, and modal testing (system-identification experience a plus)</li> <li>Experience with data processing and analysis in Python and MATLAB</li> <li>Experience with solving ordinary differential equations</li> <li>Experience with turbomachinery, combustion dynamics, fluid system modeling, or structural-fluid coupling pogo problems</li> <li>Working knowledge of structural analysis and test, including a fundamental understanding of strength, stability and fatigue failure mechanisms</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Position may require extended work hours and weekend work</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. Starlink also designs, builds, and delivers high-volume consumer hardware that allows users to connect to these satellites within minutes of unboxing, as well as our advanced gateways that we deploy regionally throughout the world. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game-changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</p> <p>As an Electrical Design Engineer on the Starlink team, you will have complete ownership over the development of millions of customer-facing products and devices that we ship directly to end users (Starlink dishes/user terminals, Wi-Fi routers, etc.). Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. You will be responsible for the design, implementation, and verification of the entire electrical system for these products. You could also be responsible for the design and performance of next-generation gateways - ultimately ensuring that our ground station antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class&nbsp;engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As an electrical engineer on the Starlink hardware reliability team, you'll sit at the intersection of electrical, firmware, RF, and manufacturing engineering. You will be responsible for hardware failure analysis, root cause, and driving for design and process changes to improve hardware reliability across our various devices. Your focus will be on product launches and field returns. The team works on a wide range of technical disciplines including high-speed digital communication, RF systems, power electronics, PCBA manufacturing, cabling, connectors, and test boards for electrical piece part failure analysis.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own qualification and test of new electrical designs and SMT manufacturing lines for high volume production</li> <li>Perform hands-on debugging to drive to root cause and corrective action of failed phased-array antenna, Wi-Fi router, power supply PCBAs, and cables. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.&nbsp;</p> <p>As an Electrical Test &amp; Manufacturing Engineer on Starlink, you will spearhead state-of-the-art production processes for our printed circuit boards (PCBs). This position is responsible for the development and implementation of all equipment, facilities, tooling, and manufacturing process technologies necessary to scale production to high volumes. You will design and implement advanced manufacturing processes and automation, owning your projects from conception and factory design through machine installation, commissioning, factory ramp, and process optimization. You will design and run large, hands-on process design of experiments (DOE), optimize complex mechanical and chemical process equipment, and interact regularly with senior leadership during critical design phases.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p>Your work will form the backbone for millions of next generation consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. title: Electrical Hardware Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICAL HARDWARE ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>We are seeking best-in-class Electrical Hardware Engineers to own the full lifecycle of the electronics that make Starmind possible. You’ll apply deep electrical engineering skill sets at the intersection of power conversion and distribution, high-speed digital communications, analog design, network integration, thermal management, signal integrity, and on-orbit compute to create the hardware backbone for next-generation space-based AI infrastructure.</p> <p>We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system. Your work sits at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal analysis, software, and networking engineering that enables orbital compute capability. Challenges range from high-speed digital communications, analog, network system integration, power electronics, RF/optical devices, and high-performance compute electronics for space. Your work will include everything from system design and schematic capture to PCB layout oversight; as well as hardware troubleshooting to driving requirements for the underlying silicon and complete product production and test. This also includes driving successful business outcomes across interdisciplinary subsystems of the satellite, inclusive of mechanical and software engineering peers among other engineering disciplines. Sub-teams include:</p> <p><strong>Avionics</strong>: The backbone of Starmind satellites are the bus avionics systems which control the vehicle, convert and distribute kilowatts of power, route high-speed vehicle and user/compute traffic, and connect satellites to each other via our state-of-the-art Space Lasers! The team is responsible for the design, development, and ultimate success of these avionics systems from concept to grave.</p> <p><strong>Payload</strong>: The Payload team is responsible for the design of custom AI compute electronics that push the forefront of AI chip performance, interconnectivity, and cluster size. Everything from high-power AI chips to high throughput network switching to high density storage conversion. The team owns the design, development, and ultimate success of this hardware from concept to grave.</p> <p>Your placement on these teams will be determined throughout the interviewing process after factoring in technical fit, expertise, and your personal preference.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Rapidly develop high-reliability electronics for satellites and title: Electrician, Medium Voltage (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ELECTRICIAN, MEDIUM VOLTAGE (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As a Medium Voltage Electrician, you will support the installation, inspection, testing, maintenance, and repair of electrical equipment in substations and power grid facilities to ensure safe, reliable power delivery. This role focuses on basic tasks under direct supervision, working with energized equipment up to 260 volts initially, progressing to higher voltages (above 750 volts) after training. You will assist higher-classified personnel in high- and medium-voltage environments, following strict safety standards. This position combines core responsibilities from substation technician and station electrician roles, emphasizing hands-on learning and team collaboration.<br><br><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Assist in installing, inspecting, maintaining, and repairing substation equipment, including breakers, transformers, switches, relays, buswork, control systems, and batteries.</li> <li>Perform basic routine maintenance on high- and medium-voltage electrical systems, such as cleaning, lubrication, and visual inspections (e.g., checking oil levels, lights, heaters, and connections).</li> <li>Conduct entry-level electrical testing, including using voltmeters, ohmmeters, ammeters, insulation meggers, and assisting with insulation resistance, relay, transformer, and circuit breaker tests.</li> <li>Read and interpret basic electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, schematics, wiring diagrams, and work orders with guidance.</li> <li>Troubleshoot simple electrical, mechanical, and control system issues under supervision.</li> <li>Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), grounding, clearance procedures, and safety protocols (e.g., PPE, emergency rescue techniques like steel/aerial lift rescue).</li> <li>Assist in station switching, de-energizing equipment, placing grounds, and coordinating with operators, engineers, and utility crews during outages or Operations.</li> <li>Help with physical tasks: digging/backfilling trenches, installing conduit/pipe/cable/wire, uncrating materials, painting structures, climbing ladders/structures (up to 50+ ft), and operating hand/power tools, portable generators, blowers, and pumps.</li> <li>Support emergency responses to outages, faults, and call-outs for prompt service restoration.</li> <li>Document work performed, test results, and observations accurately; maintain records and prepare basic reports.</li> <li>Replace simple components like lamps, switches, outlets, dry cells; assist with oil sampling/handling and signal/communication systems.</li> <li>Participate in training sessions, assist in training others, and become familiar with company safety rules, First Aid.</li> <li>Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).</li> <li>Perform similar or less skilled incidental duties as assigned.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate.</li> <li>3+ years of experience working as a licensed electrician.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate degree in electrical, mechanical, industrial maintenance technology.</li> <li>Basic understanding of electrical principles (AC/DC circuits, safety standards).</li> <li>Ability to read basic prints/drawings and use common test tools.</li> <li>Proficiency with hand/power tools and physical tasks (lifting 50+ lbs, working at heights/confined spaces, outdoors in all weather).</li> <li>Strong safety focus, attention to detail, and ability to work independently or in teams.</li> <li>Knowledge of print reading for drawings, manuals, and one-lines.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs and flexibility required regarding frequent overtime/weekend support.</li> <li>Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.</li> <li>Stand: Up to 6 hours per day.</li> <li>Sit: Up to 3 hours per day.</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We design, build, manufacture, and operate all parts of the system including thousands of satellites, hundreds of gateways, and millions of customer kits. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. While users can get online within minutes almost anywhere in the world, we’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential. We are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for individuals, communities, and businesses. Below are just some of the focus areas for software teams on Starlink:&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Develop software running on custom hardware that is deployed to millions of devices around the world</li> <li>Create infrastructure and tools for rapid and reliable deployment of our code to our customers no matter where they are</li> <li>Write software for Starlink’s custom phased array and modem silicon</li> <li>Radically improve the user experience of satellite internet</li> <li>Develop a telemetry system that scales to millions of devices with trillions of data points</li> <li>Build robust systems that are resistant to adversarial attacks</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and implement highly available, fault-tolerant consumer devices and gateways that operate for long periods of time with minimal maintenance for millions of users</li> <li>Participate in architecture, design, and code reviews</li> <li>Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints</li> <li>Work with the Starlink factory to manufacture devices in-house</li> <li>Write quality Linux based software for common processors and microcontrollers (e.g. ARM, RISC V, etc.)</li> <li>Develop systems that allow for test execution across multiple environments such as virtualized hardware or real hardware-in-the-loop simulations</li> <li>Invent new tools that enable more frequent and reliable software deployment, test execution, and data analysis as part of a continuous integration and release system</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or a STEM discipline and 1+ years of professional experience in software engineering; title: Engineering Manager, Wastewater Treatment & Ultrapure Water (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ENGINEERING MANAGER, WASTEWATER TREATMENT &amp; ULTRAPURE WATER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink will continue to spearhead the next era of space infrastructure as we prepare to launch next-generation connectivity satellites, strive to scale our userbase to 100 million users globally, and begin development on large-scale AI data centers in orbit. Our Bastrop, TX site has multiple manufacturing processes consuming ultrapure water (&gt;18mOhm) and generating complex waste streams, representing &gt;10,000 gallons per minute of total capacity across 24/7 operations. This includes one of the largest PCB manufacturing lines in North America and soon to be one of the largest solar cell manufacturing facilities in the world. To support this mission, we are seeking an Engineering Manager to lead the design, construction, commissioning, and operation of multiple large scale, state of the art (fully closed loop/zld) ultrapure and wastewater treatment plants.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the full lifecycle of UPW and wastewater treatment facilities, from conceptual design through commissioning, startup, and ongoing operations, ensuring compliance with all environmental regulations (e.g., EPA, NPDES)</li> <li>Support wastewater treatment systems for vertically integrated (ingot/wafer/cell) multi-GW thin-film solar PV, PCB, and silicon packaging manufacturing lines</li> <li>Ensure 100% compliance with ultra-pure water reuse goals and hazardous waste minimization</li> <li>Develop and manage design specifications for advanced treatment processes, including chemical precipitation and clarification, membrane filtration (TMF/UF/RO), EDI and IX, membrane degasification systems, advanced oxidation processes (AOP), and solids handling tailored to a variety of effluents (e.g., high COD, heavy metals, fluoride, solvents, silica, etc.)</li> <li>Lead cross-functional teams for ZLD systems, including advanced RO, evaporation, and crystallization systems (mechanical vapor recompression, forced circulation, etc.)</li> <li>Oversee and collaborate with title: Environmental Health & Safety Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH &amp; SAFETY ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>As part of a small, hardworking team of technicians and engineers, you will provide technical expertise and assist in the implementation of all environmental, health and safety programs at the Starship rocket development &amp; test site. The ideal candidate is highly skilled with both environmental and occupational safety fields, hands-on, and works well in a fast-paced environment. We work as a highly integrated team and job responsibilities will include helping other programs to ensure the overall success of SpaceX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Work closely with test engineers and technician teams to perform detailed safety reviews of complex hazardous operations to ensure safe execution</li> <li>Lead or assist in all aspects of incident investigations, including initial follow-up, root cause analysis, and corrective action development and closure</li> <li>Develop and maintain compliance with all applicable regulations and/or title: Equipment Engineering Manager - Solar Cell Factory (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MANAGER, EQUIPMENT ENGINEERING (SOLAR CELL MANUFACTURING</strong>)</p> <p>SpaceX is seeking a highly motivated Equipment Engineering Manager to lead the development, installation, qualification, and sustainment of advanced manufacturing equipment for our next-generation solar cell production lines. In this role, you will drive equipment strategy, reliability, and performance to enable high-volume, high-efficiency solar cell manufacturing that supports SpaceX’s energy goals. Your scope will span initial factory turn-on, execution of ambitious factory ramps, and driving of equipment strategy to support continuous solar cell technology and performance improvements.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Grow, lead, and mentor a team of equipment engineers responsible for solar cell manufacturing tools including wet chemical benches, PECVD deposition systems, PVD/sputtering tools, metrology/inspection systems, and beyond</li> <li>Own equipment lifecycle management from installation and process qualification through high-volume production, including preventive maintenance strategies, spare parts optimization, and continuous improvement of overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).</li> <li>Drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions for equipment downtime, yield excursions, and process drift using structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, FMEA, DOE).</li> <li>Collaborate with process engineering, manufacturing, and facilities teams to define equipment specifications, acceptance criteria, and capacity expansion roadmaps for solar cell technologies</li> <li>Develop and execute equipment roadmaps that improve throughput, reduce cost per watt, and increase cell efficiency while maintaining world-class uptime</li> <li>Establish and enforce equipment safety, cleanroom protocols, and change control processes in a high-volume semiconductor-style manufacturing environment.</li> <li>Partner with vendors and internal SpaceX designers to evaluate, qualify, and integrate new equipment platforms and drive performance improvements on existing tools</li> <li>Track and report key performance metrics (MTBF, MTTR, yield impact, cost of ownership) to senior leadership and drive data-driven decisions</li> As production develops and increases rate, the Maintenance Engineer's primary goal is to achieve maximum asset and system up-time by implementing and executing plans to minimize production losses, unpredictable asset behavior, and unusually high costs for system maintainability. In addition, the Maintenance Engineer acts as the accountable engineering resource in driving the design, build, and installation stages of new and modified assets as well as provides technical support to maintenance management, technicians, and production personnel to prevent and mitigate operational issues of critical equipment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work technical personnel</li> <li>Manage production requests for asset improvement, control functions, and data collection</li> <li>Apply value analysis to repair/replace, repair/redesign, and make/buy decisions</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, systems, or manufacturing engineering</li> <li>1+ years of title: Equipment Maintenance Technician, Silicon Assembly (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN, SILICON ASSEMBLY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven technicians to drive manufacturing output and yield.&nbsp;</p> <p>As a semiconductor equipment maintenance technician, you will be responsible for the upkeep, preventative, and unscheduled maintenance of the production equipment for the custom silicon packaging team at Starlink. This is a versatile and highly skilled, hands on manufacturing job. The position will require extensive collaboration and critical thinking to troubleshoot unique equipment issues and develop quick solutions in a demanding environment. The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a fast-paced cleanroom setting, has a wide array of complementary skills, and is motivated by Starlink’s mission to provide high speed, low latency connectivity across the globe.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform preventative maintenance and unplanned (Andon) maintenance repairs of production line equipment that includes photolithography, die prep, grind and polish, AOI, reflow, die bonding, compression molding, convection and vacuum curing ovens, tape mount, microsaw and die singulation equipment, physical vapor deposition (PVD) systems, electrochemical plating, wet/dry etch, dry films, metrology and back end semiconductor (RF) test equipment</li> <li>Read and utilize schematics (mechanical/electrical/pneumatic) to troubleshoot systems down to the component level</li> <li>Read and safely execute lockout tagout (LOTO) procedures</li> <li>Utilize diagnostic equipment to monitor equipment performance, diagnose root cause, and develop/implement solutions</li> <li>Use schematics, hand tools, electrical gauges and common test equipment for calibration, diagnosis, and repair of machinery or peripheral equipment</li> <li>Communicate with suppliers, specify requirements, obtain quotes, and submit purchase requisitions to procure necessary items to reduce/eliminate equipment downtime</li> <li>Provide feedback, work with equipment reliability, process engineering, and vendor teams to identify root cause of failures associated with equipment downtime and drive jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>EQUIPMENT RELIABILITY ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 4M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. As production develops and increases rate, the Equipment Reliability Engineer's primary goal is to achieve maximum asset and system up-time by implementing and executing plans to minimize production losses, unpredictable asset behavior, and unusually high costs for system maintainability. In addition, the Equipment Reliability Engineer acts as the accountable engineering resource in driving the design, build, and installation stages of new and modified assets as well as provides technical support to maintenance management, technicians, and production personnel to prevent and mitigate operational issues of critical equipment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work with project engineering to ensure the reliability and sustainability of new and modified installations</li> <li>Guide efforts to ensure consistency and maintainability of critical equipment, processes, utilities, facilities, controls, and safety/security systems</li> <li>Own equipment improvement plans for more responsive and developed preventative maintenance strategies, equipment effectiveness, and minimization of production downtime</li> <li>Define, design, develop, monitor, and refine an asset maintenance plan that includes value-added preventive maintenance tasks, minimization of high-cost low-value repairs, effective utilization of predictive, and other non-destructive testing methodologies</li> <li>Prepare asset documentation package for review of system mechanical design, controls, and software</li> <li>Develop engineering solutions to repetitive failures and equipment-specific problems that adversely affect plant operations including capacity, quality, cost, or regulatory compliance issues</li> <li>Work with production to perform analyses of assets including asset utilization rate, overall equipment effectiveness, remaining useful life, operational restrictions, and other parameters that define the operating condition, reliability, and costs of assets</li> <li>Provide technical support to production, maintenance management, and technical personnel</li> <li>Manage production requests for asset improvement, control functions, and data collection</li> <li>Apply value analysis to repair/replace, repair/redesign, and make/buy decisions</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, systems, or manufacturing engineering</li> <li>1+ years of methods</li> <li>Demonstrates critical thinking and problem-solving skills</li> <li>Detail-oriented, organized, and able to demonstrate a high sense of urgency</li> <li>Experience working with CMMS jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FACTORY BUILD ENGINEER (STARLINK PRODUCTION)</strong></p> <p>One of the most ambitious missions that SpaceX has undertaken to date, the Starlink network is our solution to providing reliable internet to the entire world. We are looking for a talented engineer to help design processes and systems for factories that will output millions of Starlink user terminals, silicon packaging chips, and solar cells.</p> <p>The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, and security of the products that we deliver. If you seek a fast-paced, dynamic environment; if you thrive on solving difficult problems where resolutions have a high impact; and if you love the challenge of building something from scratch, then this role will be an ideal next career step.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop Starlink factory design on a physical and digital level, including building requirements, facility resources, and part flow to meet production rate of millions of units/year</li> <li>Ownership of floor layouts, capacity studies, and product flow analysis to ensure on-time product delivery</li> <li>Coordinate and schedule construction activities with internal SpaceX teams and external general/sub-contractors</li> <li>Develop and maintain project schedules and budgets for capital projects, monitoring progress and addressing deviations in real time</li> <li>Define new business processes and systems for high volume production, including manufacturing execution, inventory management, nonconformance resolution, configuration management, material traceability, process control, and maintenance</li> <li>Act as subject matter expert in multiple Starlink production processes and systems, enabling complex data gathering, troubleshooting, and problem solving</li> <li>Implement data acquisition and tracking for production and quality metrics, as well as environmental, testing, and safety controls</li> <li>Assist production/engineering leadership team to identify trends and opportunities for optimizing product output, quality enhancements, and cost of manufacturability</li> <li>Consistently contribute effort, leadership, and creative thinking to solving complex problems in a collaborative fashion and under tight deadlines</li> <li>Collaborate across disciplines including Engineering, Production, Test, Inventory, Quality, Supply Chain, and Customer Experience to ensure efficiency and consistency across the organization</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, software, industrial, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in manufacturing or industrial project management (collegiate extracurricular engineering projects such as lab projects, Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Design Build Fly team, competitions, or internships qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High-volume production experience (consumer goods, automotive, etc.)</li> <li>Project management experience, particularly related to title: Failure Analysis Engineer, Microelectronics (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FAILURE ANALYSIS ENGINEER, MICROELECTRONICS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is SpaceX’s ambitious goal to bring high-quality internet to the globe by building a constellation of thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) using our Falcon 9 and Starship reusable rockets. We are developing millions of devices for end users to link our customers to our satellites.</p> <p>As a Failure Analysis Engineer on the Starlink team, you will perform detailed root cause failure analysis on microelectronic components and packaging to support high-volume manufacturing, qualification, and field returns. You will leverage advanced laboratory tools and physics-of-failure techniques to identify failure mechanisms and drive corrective actions that improve the reliability of our satellite constellation and user terminals.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end root cause failure analysis investigations on microelectronics failing in manufacturing, test, and field, from initial failure characterization through final corrective action verification</li> <li>Conduct advanced electrical fault isolation and characterization using curve trace, TDR, RF characterization, Lock-in Thermography, OBIRCH, EBIRCH, EBAC, nanoprobing, and related techniques to precisely localize defects in complex devices</li> <li>Perform advanced physical failure analysis using SEM, FIB, EDS, SAM, cross-sectioning, and related techniques to identify failure mechanisms in silicon, packaging, and interconnects</li> <li>Apply physics-of-failure principles and deep knowledge of semiconductor failure modes (electromigration, thermal fatigue, delamination, EOS/ESD, solder joint fatigue, etc.) to determine root causes</li> <li>Drive corrective actions by working directly with silicon design, packaging, and manufacturing teams to implement and validate design or process changes based on FA findings</li> <li>Author detailed technical reports documenting failure modes, root cause conclusions, supporting data, and corrective action effectiveness</li> <li>Develop and improve failure analysis techniques and workflows to support new packaging technologies and advanced materials</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in materials science, electrical engineering, physics, chemical engineering, or other STEM discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience in microelectronics failure analysis or materials characterization (internship experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s or PhD in materials science, electrical engineering, physics, chemical engineering, or other STEM discipline with a focus on microelectronics or failure analysis</li> <li>Direct experience with failure analysis tools and techniques (SEM, FIB, EDS, cross-sectioning, fault isolation, or equivalent)</li> <li>Strong understanding of semiconductor physics and common microelectronics failure mechanisms (electromigration, thermal fatigue, delamination, solder joint fatigue, electrical overstress/ESD, etc.)</li> <li>Proficiency with advanced FA tools including SEM, FIB, SAM, and EDS</li> <li>Hands-on experience in electrical characterization and fault isolation techniques such as IV curves, RF/VNA measurement, LIT, OBIRCH, EBIRCH, EBAC, nanoprobing, photon emission, or voltage contrast</li> <li>Experience applying JEDEC and AEC reliability test standards and physics-of-failure methodologies to root cause investigations</li> title: Fluids Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FLUIDS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>Starship is the largest and most capable space launch system ever developed. With the capability to deliver in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth’s orbit, it will fundamentally change access to space, and is the technology that will be used to establish a self-sustaining city on Mars. We will ultimately need thousands of Starships to accomplish that feat.</p> <p>The production fluids team develops (1) machinery used for flight-like validation of all vehicles prior to flight, and (2) all gas generation farms to produce and distribute manufacturing and test gasses throughout the production site! We are looking for enthusiastic and creative individuals to pave the future of Starship production testing &amp; automation. As a Fluids Engineer, you will be responsible for developing systems from the ground-up using multidisciplinary skills. Specifically, this involves taking a problem, breaking it down to its core fundamentals, and designing / building / deploying a solution in the form a production-grade automated fluids system. We are looking for exceptional and aspirational engineers ready to take on this challenge.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, and deploy automated / manual fluids systems to support high-rate production vehicle performance validation testing</li> <li>Design, build, and deploy simple data acquisition and control systems for control and monitoring</li> <li>Own full integration, validation, and handoff to production of each test system at each deployed production cell</li> <li>Perform detailed fluids analysis to characterize and troubleshoot expected design performance</li> <li>Work closely with our in-house build shop to develop and own the scaling of the manufacturing line for your system</li> <li>Support critical vehicle test campaigns &amp; operations, provide troubleshooting and technical support</li> <li>Develop build, maintenance, and upgrade plans for new and existing equipment to maximize up-time</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, mechanical engineering, or other technical discipline</li> <li>Hands-on project experience with mechanical/electrical systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of manufacturing design experience</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience in the field of aerospace/mechanical/ process engineering</li> <li>2+ years of experience with GD&amp;T concepts</li> <li>2+ years of experience with industrial waste/wastewater/chemical processing</li> <li>2+ years of experience with oil and gas operations or processing</li> <li>Ability to work effectively in a team environment</li> <li>Experience with mechanical design, including basic structures calculations and design considerations</li> <li>Experience with Siemens NX and Teamcenter CAD</li> <li>Experience with fluid system design, build and test</li> <li>Electrical schematic design experience</li> <li>Hands-on experience building and commissioning high quality electrical control panels</li> <li>Experience in fast-paced iterative design and manufacturing environments</li> <li>Experience solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; title: Fueling Facilities Technician (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FUELING FACILITIES TECHNICIAN (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Fueling Facilities Technician is a highly skilled and respected professional responsible for the maintenance, troubleshooting, and operational efficiency of fueling systems supporting Starship fleet operations. This role supports the Starship fleet maintenance team across a variety of fleet assets, including vehicles, heavy equipment, ground support equipment, generators, and related fuel storage and transfer systems. This role requires advanced technical expertise, leadership, and coordination across multiple teams to ensure mission-critical operations are executed flawlessly. The technician is a proactive leader who drives safety, mentors team members, and implements innovative solutions to enhance team performance and system reliability. SpaceX doesn’t shut down production for maintenance, and instead, we find ways to predict failures and perform the maintenance without interrupting production. This role will require direct work with the engineers and technicians who design and build unique machines and perform risk analysis together to map out the maintenance strategy and find the best condition monitoring systems to monitor the performance.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair fueling systems, pumps, dispensers, filtration, and transfer equipment across a variety of fleet assets, ensuring team proficiency in these areas</li> <li>Implementing process improvements and physical upgrades to improve reliability of fueling operations</li> <li>Execute fueling, defueling, and emergency procedures for fleet vehicles, ground support equipment, and related systems</li> <li>Create basic and complex work orders from scratch for fueling assemblies and support equipment</li> <li>Provide preventative and corrective maintenance on fuel storage, transfer, filtration, and dispensing systems</li> <li>Develop complex rework work order dispositions, including custom hardware installs without design references and functional/leak checks post-rework</li> <li>Drive fuel trucks, forklifts, and other company equipment</li> <li>Design and create specialized tooling to complete projects or tasks</li> <li>Trains and mentors the operations team to ensure fleet operators are capable of self-diagnosing, troubleshooting, and performing common fueling and repair tasks</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of experience with fueling operations, fuel system service, or fleet maintenance</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Able to adapt to constantly changing work assignments and fast-paced work environment</li> <li>Excellent concentration and attention to detail with outstanding work efficiency and accuracy</li> <li>Work in compliance with the applicable SpaceX and industry standards and regulations</li> <li>Understanding of hazardous materials handling, fuel quality control, and spill prevention best practices</li> <li>Read and interpret engineering work instructions/drawings and verify that fueling, transfer, and loading/unloading processes are carried out successfully and in accordance with the fueling plan</li> <li>Proven track record in high-pressure, mission-critical environments</li> <li>5+ years of experience as a maintenance technician or field service engineer</li> <li>Experience with CAD and/or mechanical design</li> <li>Experience operating a forklift, fuel truck, and other related fleet equipment</li> <li>Ability to read and interpret electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic schematics and drawings</li> <li>Ability to write detailed repair reports (advanced MS Office skills)</li> <li>Ability to use power tools and hand tools as well as heavy equipment</li> <li>Ability to maintain a safe and clean working environment while adhering to company policies, quality policies, and industry standards</li> <li>Detail-oriented, organized, and able to demonstrate a high sense of urgency</li> <li>Analytic thinker who gets to the root of problems and comes up with permanent solutions to remedy issues</li> <li>Experience in aerospace maintenance, fleet fueling, cryogenic or hazardous commodity transfer, or vehicle assembly operations</li> <li>Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to stand for extended periods (8 hours min)</li> <li>Must be able to travel for short and extended trips as needed</li> <li>Willing to travel up to 25%</li> <li>Must be available for all shifts, overtime, and weekends as needed</li> <li>Capable of lifting up to 50 lbs. unassisted and working at heights</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Full Stack Software Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>FULL STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.</p> <p>Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop highly reliable software solutions that are used across SpaceX</li> <li>Create new applications that improve how SpaceX operates</li> <li>Build prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints</li> <li>Own all aspects of software engineering and product development</li> <li>Deep dive into your users’ problems to find and create efficient solutions</li> <li>Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree</li> <li>Experience in full stack development</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Programming experience in Python, C#.NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar object-oriented language</li> <li>1+ years of rigorous experience building single page web applications</li> <li>Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts</li> <li>Expertise in designing software systems</li> <li>Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment &amp; monitoring</li> <li>Expertise in profiling and improving application performance</li> <li>Experience with build systems (Make, Bazel/Pants/Buck, Gradle) and package management tools (pip, npm)</li> <li>Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and tools like Terraform, Ansible, Puppet for managing them</li> <li>Experience working with in-stream data processing&nbsp;using Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, or similar technologies</li> <li>Production experience with Docker and Kubernetes</li> <li>Front-end experience in Angular, React, or similar JavaScript framework</li> <li>Database experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>This role requires you to be onsite. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>GNC ENGINEER - EMBEDDED CONTROLS, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.</p> <p>The Starmind team is developing key technologies to power this satellite – massive solar power generation systems, active cooling, propulsion, and the highly reliable software stack that enables our vehicles to accomplish their mission safely and autonomously.</p> <p>As an Embedded Controls Engineer on the Starmind Guidance, Navigation, and Control team (GNC) team, you will apply a strong expertise in dynamics and closed loop controls to achieve robust and precise pointing on satellites, payloads, propulsion systems, and mechanisms. This is not just an analysis role – you will be responsible for vehicle design trades, simulation, flight software implementation, and ultimately deploying and operating your features in space.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, analysis, implementation of electromechanical control systems such as solar array actuators, antenna gimbals, and high bandwidth active optics.</li> <li>Design, analysis, implementation of satellite attitude control and momentum management systems.</li> <li>Design, analysis, implementation of fluid and power system controls for the Starlink hall thrusters.</li> <li>Optimal state estimation as applied to mechanical alignment and attitude determination.</li> <li>Hardware performance specification and sizing, support for hardware iteration and firmware bringup, design qualification, automated production screening, and performance monitoring in the fleet.</li> <li>Development and maintenance of high fidelity simulations using C++, python, matlab, integration of those simulations into collaborative analysis tools.</li> <li>Implementation, validation, unit testing, and deployment of production software (C++) pertinent to the systems described above.</li> <li>Provide engineering and data review support for hardware development, network level performance monitoring.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in aerospace, physics or an engineering discipline.</li> <li>Software development experience in C++.</li> <li>Experience with design and analysis of closed loop control systems.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master's degree or PhD in physics or an engineering discipline.</li> <li>Very strong expertise and demonstrated project or professional experience in linear closed loop controls analysis and design, including state space and frequency domain methods.</li> <li>Experience with flexible body dynamics and reduced finite element models thereof in the context of closed loop control systems analysis.</li> <li>Expertise in state estimation, kalman filters, information filters, etc.</li> <li>Strong expertise in embedded C++, ideally in the context of electromechanical control systems firmware.</li> <li>Strong understanding of classical rigid body dynamics, orbital mechanics, modeling and simulation thereof.</li> <li>Direct experience with spacecraft operations and flight software development, testing, and deployment.</li> <li>Capable of identifying and solving complex problems in a self-directed title: Hardware Development Engineer, Gateway Failure Analysis (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>HARDWARE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, GATEWAY FAILURE ANALYSIS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation that provides fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, hundreds of gateway ground stations, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a Hardware Development Engineer on Starlink, you’ll contribute to the design, build, and test electronics for the world's largest network of ground stations, which function as an intermediary between the satellites and our end-users to ensure smooth data transfer and transmission. You will sit at the intersection of electrical, mechanical, thermal analysis, software, and antenna engineering - ultimately ensuring that our ground antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. This is an opportunity to work on cutting edge R&amp;D technology, and some of the most complex applications of electrical and mechanical engineering in the industry.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and execute novel environmental, RF, mechanical, and electrical test solutions for our ground antenna electronics and payload</li> <li>Perform detailed failure analysis of ground antenna hardware, identifying root causes of failures and implementing corrective actions</li> <li>Select commercial-off-the-shelf hardware and/or design custom PCBAs to measure signals, apply flight-like loads, and power units under test</li> <li>Hands-on support of hardware through design qualification, production ramp, and ground network rollout</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Perform electrical bench testing of failures to replicate and inform mitigation of anomalies</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected both in the field and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in hardware development, failure analysis, or reliability engineering (internships and co-ops acceptable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>Experience with both electronics and mechanical design and analysis including knowledge of RF principles</li> <li>Experience analyzing circuits and PCBAs, and developing functional test plans</li> <li>Experience with test equipment and measurement techniques to verify and validate product requirements (oscilloscope, multimeter, electronic load, spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, vector signal generator, source measurement unit, etc.)</li> <li>Experience in environmental testing such as HALT/HASS, thermal, humidity, shock &amp; vibration</li> <li>Strong understanding of computers and programming languages (Python, C/C++)</li> <li>Thorough understanding of electronics reliability, manufacturing, and failure mechanisms</li> <li>Knowledge of quality tools such as Lean principles, Six Sigma, and root cause analysis methods</li> <li>Thorough understanding of metrology, sources of measurement error, and uncertainty analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> <li>Occasional travel to ground network sites to support root cause investigations</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. Starlink also designs, builds, and delivers high-volume consumer hardware that allows users to connect to these satellites within minutes of unboxing, as well as our advanced gateways that we deploy regionally throughout the world. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game-changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</p> <p>As an Hardware Engineer on the Starlink team, you will have complete ownership over the development of millions of customer-facing products and devices that we ship directly to end users (Starlink dishes/user terminals, Wi-Fi routers, etc.). Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. You will be responsible for the design, implementation, and verification of the entire electrical system for these products. You could also be responsible for the design and performance of next-generation gateways - ultimately ensuring that our ground station antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. You will interact regularly with partner teams including silicon, software, mechanical, and manufacturing engineering to steer this hardware from initial concept development to full-scale production.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, develop, and test highly reliable electronics for communicating with our satellites</li> <li>Partner with software, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, and production test teams</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, component selection, analysis, schematic capture, PCB layout, prototyping, hardware bring-up, debugging, documentation, manufacturing, and test of complex electrical designs</li> <li>Get hands-on and support hardware through production, satellite integration, and flight</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Drive continual improvements to our designs by building physical and digital tools to analyze data collected on orbit and in the lab</li> <li>Challenge assumptions and work to find simple solutions to complex problems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience designing circuits, electronic products, or hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or similar engineering degree</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience rapidly designing and delivering highly reliable products</li> <li>2+ years of electronic product experience designing hardware from concept through production; title: Hardware Test Automation Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>HARDWARE TEST AUTOMATION ENGINEER, SATELLITES (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation with over 9,500 in-orbit and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Hardware Test Automation Engineer you will design, build, and automate test systems to support the development and qualification of satellite payloads, propulsion systems, mechanisms, and more. This role encompasses design, analysis, and manufacturing disciplines, with the ability to spearhead large-scope projects from early design through implementation. Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here – engineers on this team are curious, collaborative, love to learn new things, and work effectively in a dynamic environment to deliver high-impact technology on a massive scale.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop, document, and implement cross-functional automation solutions to improve test capability, coverage, and safety.</li> <li>Design and implement test and ground support equipment (GSE) to include flight hardware fixtures, automated test equipment, facilities infrastructure, vacuum systems, etc.</li> <li>Design user interfaces that make complex machines easy to use and troubleshoot.</li> <li>Create electrical, pneumatic, and fluid schematics.</li> <li>Provide innovative solutions to unique requirements and challenges faced by the team, which can range from specialized equipment to difficult installation locations.</li> <li>Perform electrical installation of valves, limit switches, potentiometers, transducers, etc.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years of experience automating test systems.</li> <li>1+ years of experience with instrumentation, data acquisition (DAQ) system design, or electronics test engineering.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE</strong></p> <ul> <li>1+ years of programming experience using Python, MATLAB, or C/C++.</li> <li>Experience with one or more of the following electrical test equipment: oscilloscopes, digital multimeters (DMM), DAQs, power supply, electronic load, spectrum analyzer, source measurement unit.</li> <li>Experience with programmable logic controllers (PLC).</li> <li>Experience in one or more of the following: electronics test rack design and build, DAQ setup and field measurements, build of electronic systems or test systems for local assembly or industrial applications.</li> <li>Extensive knowledge of various digital and analog interfaces including but not limited to: USB, VISA, TCP/IP, CAN bus, SPI, I2C, Modbus, analog-to-digital conversion.</li> <li>Experience troubleshooting interactions between software and hardware.</li> <li>Experience with the design, build, and activation of fluids, thermal, vacuum, structural or electromechanical systems.</li> <li>Understanding of metrology, sources of measurement error, and uncertainty analysis.</li> <li>Able to collaborate with a wide range of people and effectively work in a team.</li> <li>Sound verbal and written communication skills.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willing to work weekends and extended hours as needed.</li> </ul><div These systems consist of varying data acquisition and control hardware, wiring and interface harnesses, and a wide variety of instrumentation. The goal of this team is to meet a variety of test requirements to achieve safe, economical, and reliable access to space.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Maintain, calibrate,
