title: Instrumentation & Controls Technician, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INSTRUMENTATION &amp; CONTROLS TECHNICIAN, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, we are building the next generation of space infrastructure to enable large-scale AI data centers in orbit. These orbital AI platforms require massive amounts of reliable, high-efficiency solar power, and we are standing up one of the largest solar cell manufacturing facilities in the world. The Instrumentation &amp; Controls Technician will provide hands-on support for the integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and maintenance of automation and controls systems on our advanced solar cell production lines.</p> <p>This role focuses on safe, structured execution of repairs and recoveries that maximize uptime, wiring and building industrial control panels, supporting PLC/HMI/SCADA systems, and ensuring reliable operation of electromechanical, robotic, sensor, motion, and process-critical equipment while collaborating closely with Specialists and Engineers.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support integration and commissioning of vendor/OEM equipment into centralized SCADA software (Ignition) and production line controls</li> <li>Perform safe controls and electrical work within LOTO, arc-flash, guarding, interlock, robot/AGV, bypass-control, and restart-verification requirements; identify hazards, verify zero energy, validate safety devices after repair, and escalate unsafe conditions or unauthorized changes</li> <li>Maximize uptime of automation assets through hands-on troubleshooting, basic repairs, and corrective actions on electromechanical, robotic, pneumatic, and control systems</li> <li>Wire, commission, validate, build, and maintain industrial control panels and field devices to NFPA 79 &amp; UL 508A standards; replace like-for-like components (power supplies, relays, fuses, terminal blocks, sensors, etc.), restore wiring condition, and create accurate redlines</li> <li>Navigate and diagnose PLCs, HMIs, alarms, permissives, sequences, I/O status, recipes, and logic behavior; clear approved alarms, perform basic recovery, capture evidence (screenshots, codes, states), and support minor authorized parameter/recipe adjustments with documentation</li> <li>Set up, diagnose, replace, and validate sensors, instrumentation, vision, barcode/RFID, encoders, IO-Link devices, and industrial networks; verify signals, alignment, scaling, and network health</li> <li>Support controls for VFDs, servo systems, motion axes, robots, conveyors, AGV/AMR interfaces, and controlled movement; perform documented resets, homing, recovery, and safe dry-cycle checks</li> <li>Provide controls support for process-critical solar cell equipment (e.g., deposition, chemical processing, printing, firing, testing, material transfer) and facilities/utility interfaces; protect product quality, recipe state, contamination control, and process stability during recovery</li> <li>Perform structured fault finding, root-cause support, and rapid corrective actions to minimize downtime on solar cell manufacturing equipment</li> <li>Collaborate with engineers, Instrumentation &amp; Controls Specialists, production, and maintenance teams to deliver safe, reliable solutions and continuous improvement</li> <li>Maintain accurate documentation, work tickets, and records; support 5S principles, inventory control, and a clean, organized workspace</li> <li>Ensure all work complies with safety protocols, cleanroom standards (as applicable), lock-out/tag-out, and regulatory requirements in a high-volume manufacturing environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of experience in a manufacturing and production environment with mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, or hydraulic systems; OR bachelor's degree in an engineering, math, or science discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong working knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E (Standard for Electrical Safety), NFPA 79, and UL 508A codes</li> <li>Demonstrated hands-on skill in fault finding, structured troubleshooting, electrical panel work, multimeter use, schematic reading, and problem resolution</li> <li>Ability to read, interpret, and redline electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic schematics and drawings</li> <li>PLC and HMI experience or familiarization with Beckhoff TwinCAT, Siemens TIA Portal, and/or Allen-Bradley RSLogix/Studio 5000; ability to navigate alarms, I/O status, sequences, and basic diagnostics</li> <li>Experience with electrical control panel design, building, and wiring; sensors and instrumentation (photoeyes, proximity, pressure, vacuum, temperature, flow, encoders, vision, barcode/RFID, IO-Link)</li> <li>Experience with SCADA systems (Ignition preferred), sensors, actuators, servo drives, interlocks, production support devices, VFDs, robots, conveyors, AGVs/AMRs, and industrial networks</li> <li>Familiarity with process-critical controls, recipes, facilities/utility interfaces, hazardous gas/chemicals, cleanroom protocols, and product-protection practices</li> <li>Excellent skills in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); detail-oriented with strong organizational, documentation, and communication skills</li> <li>Creative problem-solver with a high sense of urgency, ability to work independently or as part of a team, and flexibility in a fast-paced, high-stress production setting</li> <li>Experience with 5S, lean principles, CMMS/work ticket systems, and continuous improvement for uptime and reliability</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work overtime and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Must be able to walk and stand for long periods of time</li> <li>Must be comfortable working in a production environment with extensive use of hazardous chemicals such as acids, alkalis, and solvents</li> <li>Must be able to wear appropriate PPE for lab and electro-chemical manufacturing environment</li> <li>Must be comfortable with climbing up and down ladders, grasping, standing, lifting, bending, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, carrying, crawling, and maneuvering in tight spaces</li> <li>Must be willing to train on 1st shift from 6:00 AM – 4:30 PM for initial 30 days</li> <li>Must be willing to work one or more of the following schedules:</li> <ul> <li>A-Shift: 5:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Sunday - Tuesday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>B-Shift: 5:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Thursday - Saturday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>C-Shift: 5:00 PM - 5:00 AM (Sunday - Tuesday and every other Wednesday)</li> <li>D-Shift: 5:00 PM - 5:00 AM (Thursday - Saturday and every other Wednesday)</li> </ul> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Intelligence Analyst
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>INTELLIGENCE ANALYST</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world’s most advanced technologies, including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we attract foreign and domestic adversaries intent on impeding our progress and stealing our technology. The work we do will safeguard mankind as we become an interplanetary species.</p> <p>You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the security of personnel, global assets, and operations at SpaceX. You will use various collection methods and platforms to explore data, identify critical information, build queries, and assess risk to produce actional insights that drive informed business decisions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Conduct in-depth research, evaluation, analysis, integration, and interpretation of information sourced from various open sources.</li> <li>Produce high-quality intelligence products on a daily, weekly, and monthly cadence, including data visualization, briefings, and analytic reports.</li> <li>Perform enhanced due diligence on companies and people within established tradecraft standards.</li> <li>Utilize data aggregators and OSINT tools to conduct open-source research, and leverage social media platforms, deep web, dark web, and breach data to identify hidden connections.</li> <li>Identify emerging risks to the company, our technology, and people and quickly synthesize information to share with relevant stakeholders.</li> <li>Communicate findings effectively and accurately to team members, leadership, and relevant stakeholders.</li> <li>Facilitate information sharing by fostering relationships and partnering with internal stakeholders as well as external local and federal law enforcement.</li> <li>Conduct intelligence analysis, threat assessments, and investigations on persons, companies, and organizations of interest.</li> <li>Develop risk mitigation strategies to address identified and work with internal teams to implement them.</li> <li>Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case file and intelligence reports.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in intelligence analysis, enhanced due diligence (EDD), third party risk management (TPRM), supply chain risk management (SCRM), and/or investigations; OR 4+ years of professional experience in the aforementioned areas in lieu of a degree.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of all-source intelligence experience in the military, intelligence community, federal law enforcement, or in the private sector at a high-tech company and/or US Government contractor.</li> <li>Familiarity with trade compliance regulations and restrictions, including export controls (ITAR, EAR, etc.) and import controls.</li> <li>Experience supporting trade compliance and/or supply chain teams and implementing TPRM and Denied Party Screening programs.</li> <li>Experience with open-source intelligence gathering tools/techniques for application/web-based social media platforms including web scraping, data parsing, and metadata extraction.</li> <li>Experience performing business process automation, constructing data pipelines, building dashboards, and developing robust queries and AI prompts.</li> <li>Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate with security and engineering teams on technical topics. This includes maintaining conceptual understandings of foundational topics related to data structures, databases, APIs, network infrastructure, and access controls.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze large data sets and draw actionable insights.</li> <li>Knowledge of analytic tradecraft standards, source validation, and disinformation detection.</li> <li>Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise research reports and briefings for a wide variety of internal and external audiences.</li> <li>Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment in a fast-paced, high-tech environment.</li> <li>Highly organized with a strong attention to detail.</li> <li>Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.</li> <li>High degree of emotional intelligence and maturity.</li> <li>Strong critical thinking skills and a solutions-oriented mindset.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations.</li> <li>Must be willing to travel ad hoc, although only minimal travel is expected at this time.</li> <li>Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: IT Network Infrastructure Engineer, Launch
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>IT NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE ENGINEER, LAUNCH</strong></p> <p>As a Network Infrastructure Engineer at SpaceX, you will work in a complex environment designing and supporting a variety of IT systems critical for Starship launch pads. This position will require you to design, install, and maintain the physical cabling, network hardware, on-premises compute, electrical enclosures, and data center environments that together make up our mission critical control networks. You will work directly with the launch automations &amp; controls teams to provide reliable and robust connectivity to their critical control systems. The fiber and copper data network cabling that you will design must survive extreme launch environments to carry operational voice, video, vehicle/payload commanding, ground support equipment telemetry, and the rest of the data needed to launch Starship in high-cadence, airport-like operations to enable life beyond Earth.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Be an extreme owner of network infrastructure including product selection, procurement, configuration, install, and troubleshooting</li> <li>Monitor network&nbsp;health, troubleshooting, and determining root cause of system issues as they arise</li> <li>Perform job walks with customers,&nbsp;vendors,&nbsp;and contractors to gather requirements and create project implementation plans&nbsp;</li> <li>Closely&nbsp;collaborate&nbsp;with stakeholders and engineers across programs to create highly operable, scalable, and&nbsp;maintainable&nbsp;products&nbsp;</li> <li>Continuously create and innovate to build solutions for unique layer1 challenges&nbsp;</li> <li>Participate in the day-to-day operation of IT systems, ensuring seamless functionality and reliability during critical launch windows</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, or other STEM discipline and 5+ years of experience designing, implementing, testing, and maintaining system-level communication architectures, OR 7+ years of experience designing, implementing, testing, and maintaining system-level communication architectures in lieu of a degree</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Ability to prioritize multiple concurrent competing projects effectively and incorporate significant design changes quickly</li> <li>Project management skills including schedule development, writing scopes of work, reading construction drawings, and creating specification documents</li> <li>Experience supervising crews of technicians/contractors to execute implementation of your designs</li> <li>Experience with configuration and operation of TCP/IP based communication equipment</li> <li>Knowledge of industry standards (BICSI, NEC, TIA/EIA), fiber optic cabling types (MM, SM) for interior and exterior usage, copper ethernet cabling types (CAT5, CAT6, CAT6A)</li> <li>Understanding of code requirements and fire protection specifications for cable pathways such as tray and conduit, especially in hazardous rated locations</li> <li>Motivation to oversee projects from early design through build and closeout</li> <li>Keen attention to detail and dedication to thorough documentation</li> <li>Proficient with CAD and/or electrical schematics software</li> <li>Confidence to present designs and clearly articulate project goals for review by internal and external stakeholders</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Ability to work in tight quarters and at height</li> <li>Must be willing to work long hours and weekends when necessary to support launches and critical path project timelines. Flexibility is required</li> <li>Availability for occasional travel to other launch sites</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: IT Network Infrastructure Specialist
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>IT NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE SPECIALIST</strong></p> <p>Our IT Network Infrastructure Specialists design layer 1 network infrastructure for supporting critical launch, landing and production facilities. The IT Network Infrastructure team installs and supports the infrastructure used for all types of telecommunications in support of our launch vehicles, spacecraft and production areas, including the layer 1 fiber and copper data network cabling infrastructure, operational voice (both wired and wireless systems), mission video, ground-side vehicle and payload interface RF systems, ground stations, telemetry and optical tracking systems, marine communications, readiness testing, and other systems involved in real-time communications and operations for Falcon, Dragon, Starship and other missions.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Plan, design and implement local and wide-area network solutions between multiple platforms and protocols</li> <li>Conduct fiber optic detailed network design for middle mile and last mile fiber-based networks</li> <li>Conduct project planning, cost analysis and vendor comparisons</li> <li>Assist in job walks and in determining needs for new installations and redesigns</li> <li>Work in conjunction with professional services and outsourcing functions as needed</li> <li>Collaborate with all staff members and stakeholders in the development and use of proper procedures in support of all layer 1 infrastructure </li> <li>Ensure all components and materials are clean and serviceable</li> <li>Obtain and maintain licenses, operator permits, or certifications as required</li> <li>Monitor and maintain a reasonable inventory of replacement hardware, general use materials, and tools</li> <li>Acquire proper inventory parts and equipment needed for repair or replacement of defective components</li> <li>Process, track and efficiently execute work orders and support tickets</li> <li>Assist in vendor scheduling, installation, and subcontracting activities on large and complex facility system infrastructure</li> <li>Maintain documentation of job status, job change revisions, material flow and other project and maintenance records</li> <li>Perform a variety of related duties in support of network operation</li> <li>Develop novel ways to streamline processes and increase the reliability of network functionality</li> <li>Support infrastructure in a multitude of environments with our land and sea based assets&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of experience in OSP and/or ISP fiber detailed design</li> <li>Experience with wired and wireless voice intercom communication systems&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering, technical, or mechanical field</li> <li>Basic knowledge of TCP/IP networking protocols</li> <li>3+ years of experience in basic construction techniques and the use of power tools, hand tools, and calibrated tooling</li> <li>Experience in the space exploration industry, aviation, military or other high-reliability operating environment</li> <li>Basic experience in project management</li> <li>Ability to read and understand basic wiring schematics and construction blueprints</li> <li>Communication skills for relaying data (verbally and in-writing) between other employees and customers</li> <li>Ability to work effectively in a team environment</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Availability for overtime hours and weekends, as the schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility is required</li> <li>Must have valid driver's license.</li> <li>Availability for occasional travel, as required</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background check for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg</li> <li>Must be willing to travel (approximately 20%) to other launch sites as necessary&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: IT Network Infrastructure Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>IT NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>SpaceX technicians work in a complex environment supporting a variety of critical production, launch, and landing activities. The IT network infrastructure team installs and supports the cable infrastructure used for all types of telecommunications in support of our production facilities, launch infrastructure and spacecraft support systems, including the layer 1 fiber and copper data network cabling, operational voice (both wired and wireless systems), video, ground-side vehicle and payload interface RF systems, ground stations, telemetry and optical tracking systems, marine communications, readiness testing, and other systems involved in real-time communications and operations for Falcon, Dragon, Starship and other missions.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Install, terminate, test, troubleshoot, and document test results for fiber, network, audio, video, and RF cabling</li> <li>Install, test, and troubleshoot audio, video, and RF equipment</li> <li>Install cable pathway systems (cable trays, cable racks, J-hooks or D-rings)</li> <li>Install, terminate, test, label, and document horizontal, backbone and other cables</li> <li>Build out telecommunication and equipment rooms</li> <li>Install connectors, connector pins, terminals, and lugs</li> <li>Perform continuity checks, locate and correct wiring errors using measuring instruments</li> <li>Investigate, diagnose, correct, and document instrumentation or system malfunctions</li> <li>Perform complex technical assignments involving communications systems, instrumentation and data acquisition/processing systems</li> <li>Collaborate with team members to troubleshoot failures and issues derived from test data</li> <li>Read and interpret planning documents, schematics, wiring diagrams, specifications, drawings, manuals, blueprints, and engineering sketches</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of experience installing, testing, troubleshooting, and repairing: fiber optics, copper cabling (RF, Ethernet), network and telephony installation, and audio/video systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-teams="true">3+ years of raceway installation (conduit, cable tray installation, PVC installation)</span></li> <li>Ability to install, terminate and test low voltage cables and fiber optical cables to include twisted pair, coaxial, stranded and solid conductor low voltage cables, single mode and multi-mode fiber optical cables</li> <li>Strong knowledge of industry standards (BICSI, NEC, TIA/EIA); different types of fiber (MM, SM) for interior and exterior usage; Cat5E, Cat6 and Cat6A data cabling; and cable pathways such as conduit, fire penetrations and cable trays</li> <li>Knowledge of the telecom network best practices and concepts including network security, network architecture design, technical standards and deliverables, troubleshooting tools (e.g., line analyzers, breakout boxes, and network traces), software and hardware installation and configuration, network hardware, and protocols (e.g., TCP/IP, DLC, and ASYNC)</li> <li>Working knowledge of audio, video, and wireless systems and corresponding physical means of delivery (i.e. analog, digital, AoIP, VoIP)</li> <li>Operational knowledge of oscilloscopes and multi-meters, soldering wires and connectors, various crimping tools, wire stripping techniques, Ohm’s law, continuity testing, pinning out a military type connector, routing and tie wrapping cables, drilling and tapping holes, and building junction boxes&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with DC power supplies, DC-DC converters, heat shrink tubing, cable harnessing, lacing, and proper strain relief concepts</li> <li>Experience with IP and HD-SDI video cameras and infrastructure</li> <li>Comprehension of modern networking architecture and what is necessary for physical layer inter-connectivity</li> <li>Experience operating articulating boom lifts, fork lifts, scissor lifts, and other work site machinery</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg</li> <li>Must have valid driver's license</li> <li>Ability to distinguish between different colors and possess manual dexterity to complete fine motor tasks</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights and/or tight spaces</li> <li>Physical effort including standing, lifting and carrying moderately heavy materials or equipment up to 25 lbs&nbsp;</li> <li>Regularly exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work occasionally performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Available to work overtime hours, nights and weekends when required by mission milestones</li> <li>Ability to travel (~10-25%) as required to other SpaceX locations</li> <li>Typical 50 hour work weeks with overtime as required; schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility is required</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p></p> <p><strong>IT STORAGE ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is seeking an experienced storage engineer with deep expertise in enterprise storage platforms. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in performance-critical settings and is eager to build storage infrastructure supporting mission-critical workloads like simulation, telemetry, and test data processing.</p> <p>The ideal candidate will possess knowledge of both Pure and NetApp storage systems running iSCSI with hands-on keyboard as well as on hardware in an on-premises environment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, implement, and maintain storage infrastructure across multiple tiers: high-performance, capacity, archive, backup/recovery, and disaster recovery.</li> <li>Architect and operate high-throughput, low-latency storage and support exabyte scale file systems (e.g., VAST,) for simulation, telemetry, and high-concurrency workloads.</li> <li>Administer storage systems including NetApp, Pure FlashArray/FlashBlade, Vast, and HPE Alletra.</li> <li>Monitor and troubleshoot storage performance across the full stack: hardware, transport (RDMA), and protocol layers.</li> <li>Troubleshoot complex issues that require an understanding of the interaction of various protocols and operating systems.</li> <li>Manage storage access, data permissions, and access controls across different protocols and operating systems.</li> <li>Develop automation and tooling for monitoring, capacity utilization and planning, configuration management, and alerting.</li> <li>Define and enforce standards for storage deployment, performance tuning, and operational management.</li> <li>Collaborate with compute, networking, and application teams to align storage strategies with system architecture and workload requirements.</li> <li>Participate in scheduled maintenance, on-call rotation, and occasional physical installation of hardware.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or other STEM discipline and 3+ years of professional IT storage engineering experience; OR 5+ years of IT storage engineering experience in lieu of a degree.</li> <li>Experience with enterprise storage platforms: NetApp, Pure Storage, Vast, HPE Alletra.</li> <li>Strong understanding of storage protocols: NFS, CIFS/SMB, iSCSI, and NVMe over TCP.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with client and server hardware/software, monitoring tools, enterprise networking, and virtualization.</li> <li>Mid-level experience with DFS administration.</li> <li>High level of network knowledge.</li> <li>Experience automating infrastructure with Python, PowerShell, or Ansible.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills; title: Launch Operations Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LAUNCH OPERATIONS ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, our commitment to reliability begins with design but is realized through exhaustive testing and a high future launch cadence at our Starbase, TX facility. In order to thoroughly vet hardware and ensure vehicle quality, the launch operations team pushes our hardware to its limits in as close to flight-like conditions as possible, and then sends it to orbit! Launch Operations Engineers are ultimately responsible for the entire operational process. They develop test requirements, develop launch plans, integrate the on-pad flight/test articles, perform on-console operation of the entire launch system, conduct tests, analyze data to confirm performance and inform the vehicle and ground design/production process, and are the primary flight controllers for launch events.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as on-console flight controllers during launch events&nbsp;</li> <li>Test integrated rocket hardware to determine suitability for flight&nbsp;</li> <li>Provide on-console engineering support for technicians during daily test/launch stand operations&nbsp;</li> <li>Write and review control logic/automation for test &amp; launch systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform real-time and post-op data review to evaluate the performance of launch/test article and stand systems (software, fluid, structural, thermal, electrical). This includes documenting operational results and recommending areas for upgrades and improvement&nbsp;</li> <li>Find innovative ways to create, review, and optimize test &amp; launch processes/procedures to increase launch system capability and rate&nbsp;</li> <li>Identify and characterize system pitfalls and potential hazards; then work to resolve these by collaborating with design, production, and ground system engineers on improvements for flight hardware and processes&nbsp;</li> <li>Serve as the final authority to ensure all operations are conducted in a safe manner&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform other related duties, as assigned, for the purpose of ensuring an efficient and effective work environment&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, aerospace engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on build or design experience (internship, club, and competition team experience qualifies)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of hands-on experience with complex and/or low-margin mechanical, structural, fluid, and electronic systems</li> <li>Ability to thrive in ambiguous requirements and aggressive timelines</li> <li>High levels of personal autonomy and self-driven motivation&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team environment, accomplishing tasks with limited resources at a rapid pace</li> <li>Demonstrated history of working efficiently with hazardous systems (high pressure, high voltage, cryogenic, toxic, flammable, hypergolic, pyrophoric)&nbsp;</li> <li>High level of familiarity with complex system control and instrumentation&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with analytical data review tools and numerical methods to solve real-world problems (Python, R, MATLAB, NI LabVIEW)&nbsp;</li> <li>Demonstrated experience in effective root cause and failure analysis&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience writing and optimizing high-risk technical procedures and work instructions&nbsp;</li> <li>Ability to read, understand, and apply technical drawings, data reports, mechanical schematics, electrical schematics, and design specifications&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Flight hardware is Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD DEVELOPMENT TEST ENGINEER (STARLINK)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a Lead Development Test Engineer to oversee a team responsible for development and qualification test of satellite hardware in Bastrop. This individual owns design, activation, safety, and reliability of thermal, fluids, chamber, structural, and vibration test capability (HASS, HALT, TVAC, static/dynamic/vibe). The role spans design, analysis, and manufacturing. You will take large-scope projects from early trades through implementation, define processes, drive requirements, and activate systems that meet the bar.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead a team of engineers enabling rapid hardware development through test — thermal, fluids, environmental chambers, structural, vibration, and dynamic test</li> <li>Oversee and own development-focused thermal chambers (HASS / HALT) and, as capability stands up, TVAC — hardware, fixturing, profiles, instrumentation, controls/dashboards, safety</li> <li>Oversee structural, vibration, pressure, and related mechanical test: test article and stand configuration, boundary conditions, schematics, CONOPS</li> <li>Act as technical decision maker and advisor to the team</li> <li>Coach and develop direct reports; jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD ELECTRICAL TEST ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers, and the software that brings it all together.</p> <p>As a Lead Electrical Test Engineer you are the technical owner of high-volume PCB electrical test at the Starlink factory in Bastrop: in-circuit test, flying probe, programs, multi-unit fixtures and racks, test PCBAs, coverage, and first-article. You spend a substantial share of time on the testers and technically lead test engineers, technicians, and specialists. You report to the Electrical Test Engineering Manager, who owns the organization, staffing, and the yield and throughput numbers.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own electrical test production program quality: in-circuit (Teradyne or equivalent) and flying-probe programs, fixtures, correlation, change control, and first-article for new products and panel revisions, including yield, false-fail / false-pass, and throughput.</li> <li>Design and own test fixtures and racks for multi-unit production test: mechanical structure, unit presentation, and electrical interface, designed for production rate and durability.</li> <li>Design and own test PCBAs: schematic, layout, bring-up, and fabrication/assembly of boards used in the test process.</li> <li>Debug yield, false-fail, and false-pass on the production floor; drive technical root cause with CAM and process engineering.</li> <li>Develop and maintain Design For Test (DFT) guidelines and work with design and CAM teams to implement them on new panels.</li> <li>Develop test strategies, perform test coverage analyses, and conduct formal test strategy reviews with peer teams.</li> <li>Write or maintain automation software to interact with testers, instrumentation, and production documentation systems.</li> <li>Technically lead test engineers, technicians, and specialists on programs, fixtures/racks, test PCBAs, and debug.</li> <li>Spend a substantial share of time on individual technical work (programs, fixtures/racks, test PCBAs, equipment).</li> <li>Travel to other SpaceX factories to transfer working production programs and fixtures as needed.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline.</li> <li>3+ years of experience in high-volume electrical or manufacturing test (ICT, flying probe, functional, or equivalent production board test).</li> <li>2+ years of expereince mentoring engineers on a test process.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE</strong></p> <ul> <li>High-volume PCB or PCBA production test in a factory (yield, escapes, units per hour).</li> <li>Hands-on fixture and multi-unit rack design (mechanical and electrical) used in production.</li> <li>Designed and released test PCBAs (schematic and layout) and owned fabrication and assembly.</li> <li>Hands-on in-circuit test (ICT / Teradyne or equivalent) and/or flying probe: programs, fixtures, and debug.</li> <li>Experience analyzing circuits, developing functional or in-circuit test plans, and performing test coverage analysis.</li> <li>Experience with test equipment and measurement techniques (oscilloscope, multimeter, electronic load, source measurement unit, etc.).</li> <li>Understanding of electrical schematics and electronics manufacturing to analyze and improve test coverage.</li> <li>Understanding of metrology, sources of measurement error, and uncertainty analysis.</li> <li>Programming experience (Python, C/C++) for tester automation.</li> <li>Experience interacting with repositories using Git.</li> <li>Experience closing a yield, coverage, or throughput gap with data on a production test process.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD ENGINEER, DEVELOPMENT OPERATIONS (STARLINK) - BASTROP</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system — thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together.</p> <p>Development Operations in Bastrop is the shop that turns engineering intent into hardware: fixtures, tooling, CNC, weld, modular automation cells, and the mechanical catalog that factory and test programs pull from. We are looking for a Lead Engineer to own that engineering stack — design, DFM, and the engineers who run it — so programs hit schedule without a hero on every job.</p> <p>This role encompasses design, analysis, and manufacturing. You will spearhead large-scope projects from early design trades through fab and handoff. You will define processes, drive requirements, and set the design bar (GD&amp;T, NX, fixtures that the mill can actually cut). You partner with Development Supervisors who own technician people ops.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the Development Operations engineering team (Build Engineers and design/DFM ICs): hire, coach, set goals, and raise the bar on quality, throughput, and schedule</li> <li>Own design for manufacturability from concept through fab: original CAD, GD&amp;T, design reviews, and design changes that reduce cost, complexity, and cycle time</li> <li>Own fixtures, tooling, workholding, and mechanical catalog items (cells, conveyors, buffers, stands) from raw material through handoff to the customer program</li> <li>Act as technical decision maker for the shop engineering stack — what we make, how we make it, and when we push a design back to the RE</li> <li>Partner with Development Supervisors on intake, queue, and expedite</li> <li>Partner with CNC programmers, machinists, welders, ACE specialists, and inventory</li> <li>Drive NCR, root cause, and corrective action on non-conforming product (tooling, cells, fixtures, piece parts)</li> <li>Create and maintain build documentation: procedures, MBOMs, integration instructions, and planning that technicians and vendors can execute</li> <li>Interface with supply chain and vendors so piece parts and sub-assemblies hit rate</li> <li>Present look-ahead with a recommendation (options, capacity, risk)</li> <li>Support Development Test with fixtures and fab</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ year leading a product development, manufacturing engineering, or project team</li> <li>3+ years of hands-on design, analysis, build, and/or manufacturing of mechanical or electromechanical hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of experience with CAD (NX, SolidWorks, or equivalent)</li> <li>Demonstrated full-cycle ownership of a hardware project from concept through fab and handoff</li> <li>Design for manufacturability (DFM/DFA) with design teams — including pushing back on over-constrained CAD</li> incomplete requirements</li> <li>Strong desire to mentor engineers</li> <li>High-mix development shop</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hands-on: time on the floor title: Lead Full Stack Engineer, Starship Manufacturing (Application Software)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD FULL STACK ENGINEER, STARSHIP MANUFACTURING (APPLICATION SOFTWARE)</strong></p> <p>The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service.</p> <p>Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.</p> <p>As a Lead Software Engineer on the Application Software team, you will have the opportunity to lead a team of highly skilled engineers both from a technical and personnel development perspective.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Directly manage a team of software engineers</li> <li>Own all aspects, including prioritization, implementation, and delivery, of a system roadmap</li> <li>Provide strong technical leadership with a focus on continuous improvement</li> <li>Manage and track multiple priorities while maintaining a focus towards common project goals</li> <li>Develop highly reliable and available software systems</li> <li>Maintain highest standards of excellence, never settle for the status quo</li> <li>Collaborate with other leaders in the department, and across the company, to ensure success for SpaceX</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline and 3+ years of software development experience; OR 6+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree</li> <li>1+ years of experience with object-oriented programming</li> <li>1+ years of experience with leading software teams or projects</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Programming experience in Python, C#, .NET, Go, Java, or similar object-oriented language</li> <li>Front-end experience in Angular, React, or similar JavaScript framework</li> <li>Experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies</li> <li>4+ years of experience building single page web applications</li> <li>Expertise in designing software systems</li> <li>Expertise in testing and infrastructure</li> <li>Expertise in profiling and improving application performance</li> <li>Domain expertise in manufacturing systems</li> <li>Strong desire to mentor and grow employees</li> <li>Able to collaborate across group and department lines with a wide range of engineers and managers, including networking and working in a team development environment</li> <li>Excellent communication and teamwork skills</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>Must be willing to travel when needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD HARDWARE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to serve populations with little or no connectivity. We design, build, launch, and operate the world’s largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;335559739&quot;:160}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">We are developing cutting-edge, highly reliable, and high-volume electronics for communicating with our constellation of satellites and are looking for outstanding engineers to join our team.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;335559739&quot;:160}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">The Starlink Product Development Team is responsible for the development of customer-facing products which are manufactured in the range of many millions per year, including phased array satellite dishes, high speed WiFi routers, and power supplies.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;335559739&quot;:160}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">As a Lead Hardware Engineer on the Starlink team, you will lead a team of 3–5 engineers, and own the full ecosystem and roadmap of our consumer electronics from start to finish. production test to take this hardware from initial concept through full-scale production.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;335559739&quot;:160}">&nbsp;</span></p> jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. You will own the successful delivery of large capital projects for internal customer groups across the company, drive technical decisions, mentor team members, and ensure projects meet performance, schedule, and quality objectives. Travel may be required, and based on business needs, opportunities to support other SpaceX facilities may arise in the future.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide technical and commissioning for large capital projects</li> <li>Direct the development and issuance of engineering drawings, design documentation, and technical reports for aerospace, industrial, and commercial infrastructure projects</li> <li>Lead the preparation, negotiation, and management of construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines, from initial award through final close-out</li> <li>Drive the real-time resolution of complex design and construction conflicts in the field, ensuring minimal impact to schedule and cost</li> <li>Lead coordination efforts with electrical utility providers on design and engineering activities to ensure reliable and resilient power delivery to critical site infrastructure</li> <li>Serve as the primary technical interface with engineers, contractors, fabricators, and key project stakeholders, fostering alignment and driving successful project outcomes</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ years of professional experience with the design or build of MEP building systems</li> <li>1+ years of leadership experience leading teams, projects, or people</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Primary experience with electrical and power distribution systems (&lt;600Vac)</li> <li>Knowledge of HVAC operation and design principles including refrigeration, chillers, boilers, and air-handling equipment</li> <li>Experience with jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD OPERATIONS ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>The Lead Operations Engineer supports SpaceX's business operations team by providing company level support for the environmental health and safety department systems and tools. They lead the operations engineers that support the various systems and resources that assist the EHS team and organization.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and implement dashboards and tools as needed for the environmental health and safety department.</li> <li>Analyze data related to environmental monitoring, incident reports, and safety performance to identify opportunities for data visualization.</li> <li>Collaborate with teams across all sites to solicit feedback on developed systems.</li> <li>Provide training sessions and educational materials to employees on awareness of proper usage of safety applications and visualization platforms.</li> <li>Collaborate with application software teams and/or contractors to create application improvements and manage software development projects to completion.</li> <li>Produce specific metric reports upon request.</li> <li>Identify operational challenges within the organization, lead problem formulation, determine root cause, and implement creative and effective solutions.</li> <li>Communicate effectively with different levels of the organization, including everything from layout reviews with engineers to presentations with leadership.</li> <li>Lead the operations engineers who run these systems. Set their priorities and review their work.</li> <li>Staff the team with the hiring manager, including requisitions, interviews, and leveling for operations engineers.</li> <li>Clear blockers and ensure redundancy across the team for consistent department and organization support.</li> <li>Manage projects and relationships with software team partners.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s Degree.</li> <li>5+ years of experience in data analytics, environmental health and safety project management, and/or environmental health and safety coordination.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Attention to detail and commitment to quality.</li> <li><span data-teams="true">Proficiency with MS office, SQL databases, Excel and PowerPoint and Power BI.</span></li> <li>Ability to multi-task, to manage shifting priorities, and to follow through on projects with minimal supervision.</li> <li>Demonstrate innovative and futuristic thinking to drive continuous improvement.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to travel regularly to U.S. SpaceX sites.</li> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends for incidents, audits, and system cutovers.</li> <li>Must be able to walk manufacturing and industrial areas using required controls.</li> <li>Must be able to obtain and maintain any required site or government access.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Lead Physical Security Hardware Specialist
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>LEAD PHYSICAL SECURITY HARDWARE SPECIALIST&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Help SpaceX protect life and property anywhere company assets are deployed by leading the Security Systems and Technology Organization. This role is responsible for the global physical security technology stack and hardware organization supporting all SpaceX sites and personnel worldwide; encompassing strategy, systems and hardware integration, architecture, implementation, and lifecycle operations of access control systems (ACS), closed-circuit television (CCTV)/video management systems (VMS), intrusion detection systems (IDS), and related platforms. The Security Systems and Technology Senior Manager will build, mentor, and direct a high-performing global team of specialists while driving enterprise-wide projects, organizational change, system reliability, and continuous improvement through cutting-edge technology.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the Security Systems and Technology Organization, providing strategic direction and organizational leadership for the entire hardware and systems function</li> <li>Lead, mentor, train, and develop the global Security Hardware Specialist organization, including performance management, career progression, and knowledge transfer</li> <li>Develop and communicate the overall security systems and technology strategy, roadmap, and change management plans, aligning with SpaceX business objectives</li> <li>Drive end-to-end systems and hardware integration of access control, video management, intrusion detection, analytics, and related platforms with IT infrastructure, network security, facilities, HR systems, and other enterprise tools to deliver unified, scalable, and resilient security capabilities company-wide</li> <li>Serve as Principal Administrator and License Manager for enterprise platforms (Genetec Security Center, Lenel, Avigilon, and equivalents); provision and integrate new servers/systems; coordinate closely with IT, INFOSEC, and Purchasing</li> <li>Demonstrate and apply strong knowledge of Genetec platforms for unified access control, video surveillance, analytics, intrusion management, and related functions; evaluate and implement advanced capabilities</li> <li>Set and enforce enterprise standards for equipment selection, configuration, installation, training, certifications, and best practices; evaluate measures of effectiveness for new equipment types and technologies</li> <li>Ensure on-schedule completion of complex, multi-site projects with minimal supervision; standardize equipment, pricing, processes, and best practices</li> <li>Lead vendor/contractor management for design, installations, large-scale facility security infrastructure, and special projects</li> <li>Collaborate as senior representative on SCIF development, data centers, MDFs, and other high-priority security technology initiatives; maintain TS/SCI eligibility</li> <li>Oversee preventive maintenance programs, system health monitoring, troubleshooting protocols, inventory of hardware/tools/materials, and documentation of job status, changes, and project records</li> <li>Drive process improvements, creative applications of existing and new systems to solve emerging or systemic problems, and continuous reliability enhancements</li> <li>Maintain SOPs, Confluence pages, and JIRA tracking for enterprise projects</li> <li>Own budget planning, resource allocation, headcount, and performance metrics for the global Security Systems and Technology Organization; report program effectiveness and strategic progress to senior leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certification</li> <li>5+ years of experience managing enterprise-level physical security systems such as CCTV, access control, VMS, intrusion detection systems, fire and alarm systems), or alert systems</li> <li>1+ years of direct leadership responsibility across global sites</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s&nbsp;degree in a relevant field (engineering, security management, information systems, or related) preferred</li> <li>Strong expertise and certifications in Genetec Security Center, Lenel Access Control, and/or Avigilon systems; prior experience as principal system administrator or license manager for large-scale global deployments</li> <li>Proven track record managing complex multi-site security technology projects, vendor portfolios, enterprise standardization, organizational change, and large-scale technology transformations at global scale</li> <li>Experience with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR)</li> <li>Experience managing a portfolio of programs and projects, including owning enterprise programs in addition to site leadership responsibilities</li> <li>Experience with JIRA (or similar tools) to track work, issues, and project status</li> <li>10+ years of progressive experience in physical security technology, systems engineering, or hardware in space exploration, aviation, military, or other high-reliability operating environments</li> <li>Experience with SCIF design/support (ICD-705 / NISPOM), TS/SCI environments, and special programs</li> <li>Established skills in strategic and critical thinking, decision-making, communications, and relationship-building</li> <li>Highly organized, detail oriented, and possess a proven ability to thrive under pressure and to execute on a number of projects simultaneously</li> <li>Successful experience working in a fast-paced, dynamic, results-oriented team environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work all shifts, extended hours, and/or weekends as needed</li> <li>Willingness to travel as needed (up to 35% or more) to support global sites and projects</li> <li>Must be able to obtain a TS/SCI clearance</li> <li>An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing</li> <li>Position is subject to random drug and alcohol testing</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>
