raise issues early with proposed solutions rather than problems alone</li> <li>Support qualification of precursors, consumables, and film stacks, and production troubleshooting on the manufacturing floor; follow through until work is complete and understood</li> <li>Champion a culture of safety and quality in all vacuum, plasma, chemical/gas handling, lab, and production support activities</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a STEM discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience with thin films, PECVD or vacuum-deposited coatings, or semiconductor/PV materials</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="none"> Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, physics, or a STEM discipline</span></li> <li>Hands-on experience with PECVD-deposited films in semiconductor or solar cell manufacturing</li> <li>Experience working closely with process engineering on deposition, film qualification, or production materials issues</li> <li>Familiarity with thin-film and solar-cell metrology such as spectroscopic ellipsometry, reflectance, FTIR, minority-carrier lifetime (QSSPC/PL), SEM-EDS, XPS, four-point probe, and optical inspection</li> <li>Working knowledge of film growth, precursor chemistry, plasma/vacuum processing, and how film properties couple to solar-cell passivation and optics</li> <li>Experience supporting structured root cause analysis (e.g., DOE, 5-why, fishbone) and converting findings into material or process recommendations</li> <li>Experience working in a high-volume manufacturing or fab environment and partnering with process, quality, and production teams</li> <li>Comfortable with data analysis (Python, JMP, MATLAB, or equivalent) to correlate process, metrology, and electrical results</li> <li>Strong first-principles problem-solving and a demonstrated ability to dig deep on ambiguous materials and device-performance challenges</li> <li>Passion for building, learning quickly, and owning outcomes end-to-end; You will work with construction project managers, facility engineers, designers, vendors, and internal partners/customers to support these goals. You will have the opportunity to drive positive change and own projects from start to finish with the goal of making the SpaceX campus a world-class facility. This position is based in College Station, TX.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead a project team of engineers, consultants, and contractors throughout the engineering, construction projects simultaneously</li> <li>Accountable for accurate budgeting and cost forecasting</li> <li>Oversee project schedule accuracy and milestone reporting to engineers, contractors, jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>Our Starbase team is working on the toughest and most audacious project on our planet: making humanity multiplanetary. If you are a high performing engineer, want to immerse yourself in never-before-solved challenges, and are excited to put in the effort to make this goal a reality, we want to hear from you.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Own the design and development of next generation launch vehicles, launch pad and production lines</li> <li>Transform system requirements into hardware concepts and trade implementation and architecture options</li> <li>Perform hand calculations and FEA to develop, assess, and optimize designs</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on manufacturing processes and development testing in a fast-paced environment&nbsp;</li> <li>Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure hardware integrates with all Starship systems and supports necessary mission operations</li> <li>Participate in design reviews internally and with suppliers and customers</li> <li>Partner with engineering and production teams to generate ideas, designs, and improvements for current and next-generation vehicles&nbsp;</li> <li>Own large business outcomes</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline or physics</li> <li>1+ years of mechanical or fluids design, analysis, or build experience (internship and school projects experience qualify)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Master's or PhD in an engineering or physics discipline</li> <li>Strong ability to use data and analysis to make fast data-driven decisions</li> <li>Ability to perform trade studies and make clear recommendations using first principles and engineering fundamentals even with partial information. title: Mechanical Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing&nbsp;solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.&nbsp;Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance mechanical systems including large deployable solar, large radiators, and in space fluid distribution. We will build these satellites at a scale that far exceeds even Starlink. &nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking talented Mechanical Engineers to own the full lifecycle of the hardware that make Starmind possible.</p> <p>We will be developing</p> <ul> <li>Large, fluid-based deployable radiator</li> <li>Biggest deployable solar arrays flown on SpaceX satellites</li> <li>Packaging at high volume for compute trays</li> <li>Satellite mechanisms + other high power satellite payloads</li> <li>Optical and networking payloads</li> </ul> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Own hardware from conceptual design through high volume production and on-orbit operation for the Starmind constellation&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop design criteria, collaborate on requirements, and drive system-level optimization&nbsp;</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on designs and analysis to inform high level systems trades and steer overall product direction&nbsp;</li> <li>Design for extreme high volume - drive holistic DFM to create elegant designs with a focus on piece part and process count reductions, error proofing at every step of fabrication and integration, and consistent performance and production metrics</li> <li>Establish an efficient product lifecycle starting in the supply chain all the way through final integration that balances cost, complexity, and quality; work closely with partner teams to design and realize an efficient in-house production line</li> <li>Perform environmental and performance testing on hardware to validate analysis and demonstrate compliance to design criteria</li> <li>Own product delivery timeline through conception, design, assembly, and launch</li> <li>Demonstrate extreme ownership of product outcomes at every stage of development and production&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with CAD and FEA software packages&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience (including internships) with mechanical/electromechanical design, analysis, testing, and/or manufacturing</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline</li> <li>3+ years of professional experience in mechanical design and analysis</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on project experience with complex mechanical systems, preferably as a team lead</li> <li>Proficient in 3D CAD (NX preferred)</li> <li>Solid understanding and application of title: Mechanical Engineer, Cabin Structures (Crew Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, CABIN STRUCTURES (CREW STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>After 50 years, humankind will once again return to the surface of the moon using SpaceX’s new vehicle, Crew Starship (also known as HLS or the Human Landing System) – this time for good. Starship will usher in the next era of crewed spaceflight and exploration, ultimately allowing us to establish permanent communities on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. As a Mechanical Engineer on the Crew Starship team, you will design and build spacecraft systems that are critical to the success and safety of future astronauts. Disciplines within this team include primary and secondary structures, mechanisms, and crew-interfacing hardware. Your design solutions will be driven by all future Crew Starship missions (Lunar, Mars, etc.). This role requires full hardware ownership, from initial design requirements and concepts all the way through design, analysis, prototype, qualification, and integration.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the design and development of next generation structures, mechanisms, or interior systems for Crew Starship vehicles</li> <li>Perform hand calculations and FEA to develop, assess, and optimize designs</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on manufacturing processes and development testing in a fast-paced environment</li> <li>Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure hardware integrates with Starship systems and supports necessary mission operations</li> <li>Lead design reviews internally and externally with suppliers and customers (e.g., NASA)</li> <li>Negotiate complex trade studies to optimize for cost, schedule, safety, and performance, among other considerations</li> <li>Be responsible for project delivery timeline from early design through production, launch, and recovery</li> <li>Exemplify technical excellence and be accountable for your work</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS </strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience with mechanical design and analysis (internship experience qualifies)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of professional experience in mechanical design and analysis</li> <li>Leadership experience on an engineering or project team</li> <li>Strong ability to use title: Mechanical Engineer, Hardware Reliability (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>MECHANICAL ENGINEER, HARDWARE RELIABILITY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>The Hardware Reliability Team at Starlink is an interdisciplinary team that is committed to the reliability of the mechanical and electrical hardware required to connect our customers to our satellites.&nbsp;Your breadth of exposure will span across dozens of areas (mechanical, electrical, RF, software, test, etc.) as you collaborate with core groups at SpaceX to bring hardware from initial concept development to full-scale high-volume production.</p> <p>You will use data to understand the factors that drive process and product reliability in design and manufacturing. You will dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems to influence product design and manufacturing processes. You will be exposed to a hands-on environment that will enable you to spend time on the factory floor and in the test lab to improve the reliability of hardware and, ultimately, the user experience.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and implement reliability test strategies for new products and their subcomponents to maximize field life and minimize early life failures</li> <li>Develop, implement, and validate test and inspection processes for new and existing products and production processes, ensuring that criteria are objective and that reliability goals are consistently met</li> <li>Design and execute novel environmental, RF, mechanical, and electrical testing techniques tailored to the product and its functions</li> <li>Write test programs to exercise the functionality of the product over various conditions and environments</li> <li>Automate reliability test initiatives and reporting using proper data visualization techniques and thorough knowledge of the product and its functions</li> <li>Define the ongoing reliability testing strategy to monitor the manufacturing process and screen for long-term reliability defects caused by process and component variability</li> <li>Monitor product and process quality through production ramp-up using a suite of analysis tools, and drive improvements to areas that are under-performing&nbsp;in terms of key quality metrics</li> <li>⁠Investigate failures in production and test, identifying and mitigating the immediate and underlying root causes in order to reduce risk and improve reliability of designs and processes</li> <li>⁠Contain suspect or known non-conforming product, providing guidance to production representatives and engineers to assist in quarantining and rework activities</li> <li>Work closely with hardware, software, manufacturing, and network engineering teams to maximize reliability across all disciplines</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or other engineering discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience in test, analysis, manufacturing, or hardware development (internship and project experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with both electronics and mechanical design and analysis including knowledge of RF principles</li> <li>Programming experience in Python, C, and SQL with an emphasis on data analysis and automation</li> <li>Demonstrated capability to think As a mechanical and/or fluids engineer on the starship launch pad and test site, you will support the development of SpaceX's Starship Tower, Launch Mount, and test stands, part of a fully reusable transportation system designed to launch both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, and beyond.</p> <p>Engineers in this role are responsible for hardware development from initial system architecting through the design, analysis, manufacturing, integration, activation, and operational phases. Mechanical engineers design welded structures, large-scale mechanisms, electromechanical &amp; fluid power actuation systems, and fluid systems, including hydraulic and cryogenic.&nbsp;These systems are involved with performing proof and static fire testing of individual Starship stages<em>, </em>stacking the vehicle on the launch pad, loading propellant before launch, releasing fluid and structural connections at T-0, catching both stages when they return to the launch site, and configuring the vehicles to a safe state post-catch so they can be rapidly reflown. The Starship program is focused on rapid iteration and improvement, which enables engineers to continuously innovate and advance technology throughout the life of the program. The overarching goal of the launch mount team is to get to a ZERO refurbishment state where the pad can launch one vehicle and immediately be ready to launch again.</p> dynamic, thermal, and fluids analysis as necessary to determine requirements and to optimize the design of these systems &nbsp;</li> <li>Work closely with software and operation engineers to develop the concept of operations for launch mount systems with the goal of developing robust, fault tolerant systems and software that perform every time in the varying extreme conditions of a launch This position is responsible for the development and implementation of all equipment, facilities, tooling, and manufacturing process technologies necessary to scale production to high volumes. You will design and implement advanced manufacturing processes and automation, owning your projects from conception and factory design through machine installation, commissioning, factory ramp, and process optimization. You will design and run large, hands-on process Design of Experiments (DOE), optimize complex mechanical and chemical process equipment, and interact regularly with senior leadership during critical design phases. By the end of this year, the Starlink factory in Bastrop will be the largest PCB manufacturing facility, by volume, in North America.</p> <p>Your work will form the backbone for millions of next generation consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. The breadth of exposure as an NDE Inspector is immense, as the organization is responsible for a large diversity of inspection types across Starship. You will have the ability to engage with the process to provide continuous improvement to execute the mission to make humanity interplanetary.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform internal and external inspections to determine if a weldment/structure meets the acceptance criteria of a specific code, standard, or document</li> <li>Interpret codes and specifications in accordance with the drawing requirements</li> <li>Use a computer to compile and submit data of acceptance or rejection of inspections, as well as for inter-office communications</li> <li>Recommend and approve repairs as well as perform visual inspection of work in progress and completed work</li> <li>Monitor welding processes such as gas tungsten arc welding (GTAW), gas metal arc welding (GMAW), flux cored arc welding (FCAW), shielded metal arc welding (SMAW), and plasma arc welding (PAW) to ensure they are performed in accordance with qualified procedures</li> <li>Verify and document welder qualifications</li> <li>Verify the compliance of base metals with the applicable specifications</li> <li>Appraise welding joint designs and joint preparations for compliance with drawing</li> jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE - '26/'27 (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As arguably SpaceX's most complex software engineering challenge, Starlink offers a variety of areas within software engineering that you can focus. As a Software Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges underpinning every aspect of the program’s growth. The teams and areas you could have an impact on could include, but are not limited to:</p> <ul> <li>Next generation networking technologies to direct data through an ever-changing network of satellites, ground stations, planes and users.</li> <li>Firmware, embedded and controls software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.</li> <li>Infrastructure and tools to enable rapid development and reliable deployment of our code to dynamic production environments.</li> <li>Measurement system software and hardware, supporting our in-house RF Silicon designs.</li> <li>Physic based software engineering to design and simulate the orbital life cycle of the Starlink constellation.&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop software running on custom hardware that is deployed to millions of devices around the world</li> <li>Create infrastructure and tools for rapid and reliable deployment of our code to our customers no matter where they are</li> <li>Write software for Starlink’s custom phased array and modem silicon</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support. We expect our engineers to close the feedback loop between software design and real-world performance. In this role, your software will have a meaningful and measurable impact on the world.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop highly reliable, real-time software.</li> title: Operations Analyst, Reliability (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>OPERATIONS ANALYST, RELIABILITY (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, the Build and Flight Reliability team ensures hardware—from engines to fully integrated vehicles—is built to the highest standards and performs flawlessly on missions to make humanity multiplanetary. This team bridges manufacturing excellence with mission-critical reliability, developing data-driven tools and processes to identify, mitigate, and prevent risks from factory floor to flight. As a Reliability Analyst, you'll develop and maintain data-driven tooling and infrastructure to guide decisions, with a focus on identifying AI opportunities, defining and leading AI-driven solutions for predictive analytics, automation, and risk mitigation. You'll drive sustainable improvements to reduce build failures and boost vehicle performance, partnering with software engineering for AI workflow deployment into agents or enterprise systems.</p> <p>In this role, you'll collaborate across teams to turn production and test data into insights, own build-to-flight metrics, and drive improvements in a fast-paced environment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify opportunities in reliability processes (e.g., predictive modeling, anomaly detection); define problems, develop prompts/workflows using LLMs or generative AI, evaluate outputs, monitor performance, provide go-live support, and create operational protocols—partnering with software engineering to define implementation direction while maintaining ownership of outcomes.</li> <li>Design, implement, and maintain dashboards (e.g., Grafana, PowerBI, Tableau, SQL reports) for monitoring build metrics (defect rates, tolerances, nonconformances) and flight indicators.</li> <li>Maintain and optimize dashboards and tools for ongoing accuracy and usability, including troubleshooting issues, updating data feeds, and ensuring seamless integration with user workflows across production, quality, and reliability teams.</li> <li>Improve data infrastructure (pipelines, ETL, schemas) for scalability, integrity, and real-time use, with ownership of data integrity to support reliable AI tools and initiatives.</li> <li>Develop/track KPIs for build health and flight risk, including yields, pass rates, traceability, and predictive models to inform decisions and actions.</li> <li>Analyze datasets (SQL, Python) to find root causes of anomalies, correlate build/flight data, and recommend solutions; use AI for pattern recognition and forecasting.</li> <li>Collaborate with production, design, reliability, and software teams to define data requirements for emerging use cases, such as integrating build data with flight test results, and develop automation scripts to mitigate risks, streamline reporting, and enhance efficiencies.</li> <li>Create ad-hoc queries, reports, and simulations for workflows, nonconformances, constraints, and gaps.</li> <li>Standardize data capture for manufacturing processes (e.g., welding, assembly, NDE, and checkouts), ensuring comprehensive traceability and feedback loops that capture lessons learned from builds and flights to prevent repeat issues.</li> <li>Train users/leaders on tools, data interpretation, AI workflows, and best practices; share knowledge to build expertise in analytics and AI.</li> <li>Actively contribute creative thinking and leadership to solving complex problems under tight deadlines, with a focus on "reliability by any means necessary" to align production scaling with mission success.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree.</li> <li>1+ years in building and operating metric based dashboards.</li> <li>1+ years of experience building data structures and query optimizations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment.</li> <li>Experience working in in a factory or production environment.</li> <li>3+ years of experience with SQL, Python, C++, Tableau, or PowerBI.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Paint & Coatings Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PAINT &amp; COATINGS TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>As a member of the construction projects and facilities team, the paint &amp; coatings technician mixes, strips, paints, and details advanced paint systems, prepares metallic substrates via abrasion and etchants, applies sealants/adhesives, maintains spraying equipment, and uses precision tools like calipers while supporting safety, quality, and delivery improvements. You will have the opportunity to drive positive changes in a fast-paced, low-drag environment. This technician owns tasks and projects from start to finish, with the goal of making the SpaceX campus a world-class test facility that can support the mission of enabling life beyond Earth.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Manage and coordinate ticket system requests for paint projects across the site to ensure timely and quality execution of work</li> <li>Prepare, prime, sand, seal, patch, and paint steel surfaces, buildings, and fixtures utilizing all types of painting materials such as varnish, lacquer, shellac, enamel, latex, epoxy, waterproofing, and heat-resistant finishes</li> <li>Tape, float, paint, and repair wall finishes and apply texture</li> <li>Operate, clean, and maintain all painting equipment, including brushes, rollers, sprayers, electrostatic sprayers, and pumps</li> <li>Safely store and label all materials on a daily basis</li> <li>Erect scaffolding, rigging, and ladders as necessary in a manner consistent with safety codes</li> <li>Operate and use required tools and equipment skillfully and safely</li> <li>Apply finishes to a wide variety of surfaces</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>1+ years of experience as a painter in a residential, commercial, industrial, or manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience painting projects indoors and outdoors</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in commercial and industrial painting practices and processes, including the properties and application of paints, varnishes, lacquers, enamels, epoxies, paint removers, and related materials</li> <li>Familiarity with applicable code requirements, methods and practices for maintaining tools, machinery, and equipment</li> <li>5+ years of experience as a painter in a residential, commercial, industrial, or manufacturing environment</li> <li>Experience painting internal and external surfaces</li> <li>Ability to safely operate aerial platforms, lifts, man lifts, and heavy equipment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Role may require extended hours, weekend work and shift schedules, that vary depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Physical dexterity and the ability to lift heavy objects are required in this position (up to 25lbs unassisted)</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting the upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings, and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Ability to comfortably wear breathing air respirators on a frequent basis, occasionally for extended durations, as required by the position</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. title: PCB Designer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PCB DESIGNER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a PCB Designer at SpaceX, you’ll be responsible for creating the layout for all our in-house board designs. You’re not just connecting the dots. Here you’ll partner closely with Hardware Development Engineers as they develop their schematics, providing your expertise and recommendations at each design review, and iterating your designs to come up with the best possible solutions. You’ll contribute to a variety of design mixes from radio phased arrays to solar power converters and more.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Determine layer stackup, perform component package selection, component placement, routing feasibility studies, and signal routing of digital, analog, RF, and power conversion of printed circuit boards (PCB)</li> <li>Library creation and maintenance</li> <li>Create and release documentation for fabrication of PCBs</li> <li>Collaborate with internal teams and PCB vendors to continually improve design rules, constraints and design for test and manufacture guidelines</li> <li>Utilize PCB design tools, maintain and evaluate new tools, and train team members to use tools&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s&nbsp;degree in electrical engineering and 1+ years of professional experience with PCB layout OR 3+ years of professional experience with PCB layout in lieu of a degree (internships and club/project work applies)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+&nbsp;years of experience with PCB layout and routing in one or all of the following areas: modern passive and active electronics components, surface-mount, RF components, ball-grid array and similar fine pitch, or high pin density components&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of experience with ECAD libraries and library configuration management</li> <li>Demonstrated understanding of design for manufacturability, assembly, and test</li> <li>Experience with Mentor Xpedition and/or Altium Designer (Mentor Xpedition preferred)</li> <li>Experience with layout of mixed analog and digital designs, high speed buses, FPGA, DRAM and CPU designs, power supplies, DC-DC converters, transmission lines, impedance-controlled traces and power traces</li> <li>Experience with MIL-STD, commercial and IPC standards and design</li> <li>Experience monitoring industry-wide As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a PCB Designer at SpaceX, you’ll be responsible for creating the layout for all our in-house board designs. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PCB TECHNICIAN (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a PCB Technician, you will be working on the many processes within printed circuit board manufacturing in the Starlink factory. This is a versatile and highly skilled, hands-on manufacturing job that includes operating production equipment, performing quality inspections, performing chemical analysis and additions, and handling chemical materials to meet the goals for output and quality. The ideal candidate is comfortable working in an electro-chemical manufacturing environment and is motivated by Starlink’s mission to provide high speed, low-latency connectivity across the globe.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Execute startup and shutdown procedures for production equipment</li> <li>Monitor process conditions, equipment, and control systems for title: PECVD Process Engineer, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">PECVD PROCESS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK) </span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to those that need it most. We design, build, and launch the world's largest and most advanced satellite constellation that is capable of delivering high-speed internet to even the most remote locations.&nbsp;</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a solar cell process engineer on Starlink, you will spearhead state of the art production processes for an internal solar cell production line, providing high efficiency and high-quality solar cells for both our latest generation Starlink satellites and for Starship missions to the Moon and Mars. You will work through the life cycle of setting up a greenfield solar cell production plant, including equipment procurement, plant design/layout, equipment commissioning and ramp-up, recipe and process development, and working to develop a world-class production team and environment.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a PECVD Process Engineer, you will own the development, optimization, and scaling of Plasma-Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition (PECVD) processes critical for depositing the intrinsic and doped hydrogenated amorphous and nanocrystalline silicon layers that passivate the wafer surface and form the carrier-selective contacts of high-efficiency SHJ cells. You will develop and iterate on the manufacturing processes and recipes to achieve a state-of-the-art silicon cell efficiency, low defect rate and cost, and high reliability cell for space-based applications. Your work will form the backbone of the Starlink network (photons of sunlight in is directly proportional to photons of data out to customers!) and help provide internet to tens of millions of customers all around the world.&nbsp;</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">RESPONSIBILITIES:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Design, qualify, and optimize PECVD processes for SHJ intrinsic passivation layers and p-type/n-type doped layers, ensuring film thickness uniformity, passivation quality (minority carrier lifetime, implied Voc), doping efficiency, and contact resistivity at GW-scale volumes</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Lead process development for new toolsets and materials, including gas chemistry, plasma power and frequency, pressure, temperature, and electrode gap optimization to support state of the art efficiency cells</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Own chamber conditioning strategy, including seasoning, in-situ/remote plasma clean recipes, and clean intervals, to control particles, cross-contamination, and run-to-run drift while maximizing tool uptime</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Partner closely with the CVD Equipment Engineering team on tool qualification, chamber matching, preventive maintenance recovery, and throughput (UPH) improvements</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining new and/or improved manufacturing processes, equipment, technologies, and facilities</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Analyze production processes and machinery from a first principles, physics-based approach</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Develop experiments to diagnose and correct manufacturing problems, utilizing robust DOE and statistical methodologies. Optimize process conditions and materials to improve the optical and electrical quality of solar cells</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Perform defect characterization and analysis to determine root cause and develop action plans to improve yields</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Develop project plans, budgets, and cost/benefit analysis for implementation of new processes or machines</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Own and perform machine activation and testing with a small team of engineers and technicians</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Prepare detailed content for technical design reviews. Demonstrate extreme ownership of the production outcome of the Starlink solar factory across yield, uptime, and cost</span></li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">1+ years of experience in system design, analysis, and/or system implementation (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Master’s degree or Ph.D. in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, physics, or related technical discipline</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">5+ years of hands-on experience in PECVD process engineering, preferably in SHJ/HJT or TOPCon solar, semiconductor, or display manufacturing</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Proven track record of scaling PECVD processes to high-volume production (&gt;1GW/year equivalent)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Strong understanding of vacuum systems, plasma physics, gas-phase and surface chemistry, and thin-film growth of amorphous and nanocrystalline silicon</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Deep understanding of SHJ surface passivation and carrier-selective contacts, including epitaxial growth suppression, hydrogen content and bonding, and band alignment at the a-Si:H/c-Si interface</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Hands-on experience with thin-film and PV characterization techniques (e.g., spectroscopic ellipsometry, FTIR, Raman crystallinity, dark/photo conductivity, Sinton lifetime, PL/EL)</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience safely handling pyrophoric, toxic, and flammable process gases (e.g., silane, phosphine, diborane)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience with SPC, DoE, and lean manufacturing principles</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Ability to work in a cleanroom environment</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Hands-on experience working with complex fluid or mechanical based production systems in a professional setting</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience transitioning products from design to manufacturing and scaling to high volume as part of a cross-functional team</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience with solar cell manufacturing equipment, such as wet chemical processing equipment, PE-CVD equipment, PVD machines, metallization and final test equipment, and wafer inspection equipment. Experience in hot-wire CVD, evaporation tools, and ALD tools are a plus.&nbsp;</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience or expertise with perovskite solar cells or perovskite tandem solar cells</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience with micro-structure analysis tools (SEM, TEM, EDX, SIMS, etc.) and optical/electrical characterization tools (UV-VIS, I-V, Resistance, etc.)</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Familiarity with large-area, high-throughput PECVD platforms (in-line and cluster/batch) and automation/integration for inline production</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Proficiency in data analysis/scripting (Python, R, SQL) and plasma or device simulation tools (e.g., COMSOL, Quokka, AFORS-HET)</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Experience in cost-of-ownership modeling, capex justification, and fab ramp-ups to multi-GW scales</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Passion for sustainable energy and space technology; prior work in photovoltaics at GW-scale a plus</span></li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</span></strong><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Ability to travel frequently for work, potentially for extended periods of time during machine buyoffs and startup</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Ability to lift 25 lbs. unassisted</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span data-contrast="auto">Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PHYSICAL SECURITY SPECIALIST</strong></p> <p>Physical Security Specialists are highly experienced and adaptable security professionals who operate with significant autonomy in dynamic, high-threat environments. Specialists are expected to operate as an individual or small team, make independent decisions in the field, and deliver executive-level protection while conducting reconnaissance, counter-surveillance, and border proximity security operations. This position requires a flexible schedule driven by threat trends and company commitments rather than fixed shifts.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Conduct executive protection operations and provide close protection for senior leadership as required</li> <li>Perform reconnaissance and counter-surveillance in support of executive movements and threat mitigation</li> <li>Lead small teams during operations while also demonstrating the ability to work independently and make sound decisions with limited oversight</li> <li>Support the planning and execution of security for title: Piping Technician (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>PIPING TECHNICIAN (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven technicians to drive manufacturing output and yield. You will have ownership of one or more process areas and will have the opportunity to directly impact Starlink’s products. You will have frequent interaction with engineering teams and leadership and will participate in developing and validating new equipment, processes, and technologies. The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, security, and user experience of the products that you will manufacture.&nbsp;</p> <p>As a Piping Technician at&nbsp;Starlink, you will take ownership of state-of-the-art piping systems that support our&nbsp;Starlink User Terminal Production Facility—supporting our PCB operations (largest printed circuit fab in North America!) and our Chip Packaging Plant (featuring a&nbsp;state-of-the-art&nbsp;panel level packaging process). You will install, maintain, and repair&nbsp;all piping systems&nbsp;to ensure reliable water quality and system uptime for our partner teams in a fast-paced, innovative manufacturing environment.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Install, assemble, modify, and maintain PVC piping systems, including solvent welding, threading, and mechanical joining for UPW and wastewater treatment processes</li> <li>Read and interpret P&amp;IDs, blueprints, isometric drawings, and technical specifications to route and install piping systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Install, align, and maintain pumps, valves, sensors, tanks, and other process equipment connected to piping systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform routine maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs on piping infrastructure to support system availability greater than 99.9%</li> <li>Conduct pressure testing, leak checks, and system commissioning on new and existing piping runs&nbsp;</li> <li>Collaborate with water treatment technicians, manufacturing, EHS, and engineering teams to optimize piping layouts, reduce leaks, and support continuous improvement initiatives&nbsp;</li> <li>Ensure adherence to OSHA, EPA, and SpaceX safety protocols, including lockout/tagout (LOTO), hot work permitting, and proper chemical handling around piping systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Execute startup and shutdown procedures for piping and associated equipment&nbsp;</li> <li>Identify equipment and process deviations and perform corrective actions&nbsp;</li> <li>Maintain accurate documentation of piping modifications, as-built drawings, and spare parts inventory&nbsp;</li> <li>Safely handle and transport piping materials, fittings, and chemicals&nbsp;</li> <li>Ensure 5S standards are upheld by maintaining a clean and organized work area&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform other related duties, as assigned, for the purpose of ensuring an efficient and effective work environment&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate&nbsp;</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience as a plumber or pipefitter, or an associate’s degree in a relevant technical field</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Experience installing and maintaining PVC, CPVC, or other plastic piping systems in industrial or manufacturing environments&nbsp;</li> <li>Stainless steel welding experience (TIG and/or MIG)&nbsp;</li> <li>Welding certifications (AWS or equivalent)&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience working in water treatment, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, or electronics manufacturing facilities&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong ability to read and interpret P&amp;IDs, isometric drawings, and schematic diagrams&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with mechanical equipment isolation, disassembly, and repair&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with lockout/tagout, job hazard analysis, and hot work permitting&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience handling corrosive or hazardous chemicals around piping systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Proficiency with basic hand and power tools, as well as pipe threading and fusion equipment&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience using production and inventory management software such as MES/ERP&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills to work closely with other technicians and cross-functional teams&nbsp;</li> <li>Ability to identify and maintain priorities while working independently in a high-paced, challenging work environment with minimal oversight&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;<strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Must be able to&nbsp;lift up&nbsp;to of&nbsp;25 lbs. unassisted&nbsp;</li> <li>Must be able to walk and stand for long periods of title: Power Electronics Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER ELECTRONICS ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>Our Power Electronics team designs and develops the power conversion and control systems at the heart of Starmind satellites and orbital data centers — enabling the reliable, high-efficiency power delivery required for massive on-orbit AI compute. As a member of the team, your designs will run the gamut from low voltage to kV range, and powers from 1W to many kW (applications include high-density compute power delivery, battery systems, motors/actuators, propulsion, laser optical links, and other vehicle systems critical to orbital AI platforms).</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide engineering expertise in design, analysis, and testing of DC-DC power converters for harsh environments</li> <li>Work on electrical power system and sub-system level design trades and develop requirements</li> <li>Define and perform electrical power system verification testing and analysis</li> <li>Work with multidisciplinary teams of design, test, and production engineers to create new power electronics hardware</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline</li> <li>1+ years of professional experience in power converter development (internships/co-ops can apply)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in electrical engineering or related field</li> <li>Strong grasp of analog control and discrete logic design</li> <li>Experience in modeling, simulation, and testing of power electronics</li> <li>Working experience in voltage and current mode control and compensation design</li> <li>Experience with AC-DC converters and power factor correction</li> <li>Strong grasp of DC-DC topologies, with ability to select optimal architectures and components</li> <li>Understanding of design for fault tolerance and reliability</li> <li>Familiar with failure mode effects and criticality analysis</li> <li>Familiarity with design of wire wound and planar inductors and transformers</li> <li>Familiarity with power supply testing and packaging for harsh environments</li> <li>Experience with in-lab impedance measurement and loop-gain measurement</li> <li>Familiarity with spacecraft electrical power systems and knowledge of radiation effects</li> <li>Familiarity with lithium-ion battery handling, safety, and usage</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <p>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR We design, build, launch, and operate the world's largest constellation of satellites, enabling us to operate a global internet network unbounded by traditional ground infrastructure limitations. The root of SpaceX’s success so far lies in our mission to keep all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision-making, and speedy deliverables. With millions of daily users worldwide already online, Starlink is truly a game changer and levels the playing field for those who were previously unconnected.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a Power Electronics Engineer on Starlink in Bastrop, you could be responsible for the design and performance of next-generation gateways power electronics - ultimately ensuring that our ground station antenna hardware can withstand the harshest environmental conditions while maintaining reliable communication with millions of users on a global scale. These are challenging high power multi kW systems needing high performance and reliability. Alternatively, you could spearhead the design and development of the power supply for millions of consumer-facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. Our customers currently include teachers in the most remote parts of the Amazon, researchers in Antarctica, digital nomads who travel via RV, emergency responders, commercial airlines, cruise lines, and residential users who live in more rural or developing areas. jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER GENERATION ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>Join the Power Systems Engineering team at SpaceX to pioneer the design, build, operation, and maintenance of advanced power generation, transmission, and distribution systems for Starship's launch, production, propellant generation, and the city of Starbase, TX. As a power systems engineer, you'll work with a team to scale high-capacity electrical infrastructure for the world's most powerful rocket, ensuring seamless energy flow for groundbreaking missions. The position is based at Starbase, TX, with potential travel to other SpaceX facilities.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design, build, operate, and maintain the various microgrids that comprise Starbase, TX.</li> <li>Collaborate with cross-functional teams; lead projects; and drive rapid, continuous improvements at Starbase launch sites.</li> <li>Be responsible for infrastructure upgrades to dynamically scale systems for Starship's production rate targets.</li> <li>Create and maintain sitewide power budgets, monitoring, and metering for mission-critical assets to optimize visibility and efficiency.</li> <li>Develop and execute asset strategies for high-power launch and grid infrastructure.</li> <li>Develop standardized designs for launch, propellant generation, and power delivery facilities.</li> <li>Performs detailed design on all aspects of electrical power systems: one-lines, three-lines, control/relaying schematics, wiring diagrams, SCADA, conduit/cable sizing/routing, grounding design, general arrangement, etc.</li> <li>Develops and implements protective relay settings and schemes for high voltage equipment.&nbsp;</li> <li>Maintain organized design and asset documentation for all Starbase launch and power facilities.</li> <li>Ensure compliance with NFPA 70, 70B, 70E, NESC, and IEEE standards, prioritizing safety and engineering excellence.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.</li> <li>1+ years of experience in power systems design, analysis, and build, with a focus on high-power, high-voltage systems.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years of professional experience in a similar role.</li> <li>Professional Engineering license or intention to actively seeking PE license.&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with power systems analysis software and tools: ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, PowerWorld, Matlab, PSCAD, PSEE, Simulink, etc.</li> <li>Experience performing basic load flow, short-circuit, arc-flash, coordination, and transient stability studies.</li> <li>Familiarity with industrial power systems up to 345 kV, including switchgear, transformers, BESS, VFDs, motors, distribution systems, UPS/emergency backups, power generation, relaying, metering, protective devices, and networking.</li> <li>Familiarity with industrial communications protocols and networking: Modbus, IEEE C37.115, IEEE C37.111, DNP3, etc.</li> <li>Experience with CAD software: Revit, AutoCAD, NX, etc.</li> <li>Demonstrated initiative, creative problem-solving, and strong analytical/engineering fundamentals.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills.</li> <li>Proven ability to lead teams, work independently, and thrive in dynamic, high-stress environments with tight deadlines.</li> <li>Strong organizational skills to prioritize, schedule, and implement solutions with minimal operational impact.</li> <li>Ability to quickly troubleshoot issues and support technicians hands-on.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.</li> <li>Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support launch operations.</li> <li>Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.</li> <li>Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.</li> <li>Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. title: Power Plant Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER PLANT ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is building and operating combined-cycle gas turbine power plants that must come online, stay online, and perform. This role owns the design and build of the full power plant: gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, and everything else that keeps the plant running at rated output, day after day. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support the full lifecycle of gas turbine power generation assets — installation, commissioning, startup, operations, and long-term maintenance</li> <li>Lead or support commissioning activities including combustion tuning, control system checkout, protective relay testing, and performance/reliability run verification</li> <li>Own root-cause analysis and corrective action for turbine trips, forced outages, and performance degradation; drive fixes that prevent recurrence</li> <li>Develop and refine operating procedures, startup/shutdown sequences, and abnormal operating condition playbooks</li> <li>Interface directly with OEMs (GE, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan) on warranty issues, LTSA scope, outage planning, and technical issues</li> <li>Plan and execute major/minor inspections, hot gas path outages, and combustion inspections in line with OEM maintenance intervals</li> <li>Analyze turbine performance data (heat rate, capacity factor, degradation curves) to identify efficiency losses and recommend corrective action</li> <li>Coordinate with balance-of-plant teams (HRSG, steam turbine, cooling systems, water treatment) to ensure integrated performance</li> <li>Build and maintain relationships with EPC contractors during construction handoff to ensure a clean transition from construction to commercial operation</li> <li>Develop spare parts strategy, critical spares inventory, and maintenance budgets</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related&nbsp;engineering discipline</li> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience with utility-scale gas turbines in commissioning, operations, or maintenance roles</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Working knowledge of combined-cycle plant systems: gas turbines, HRSGs, steam turbines, generators, and balance-of-plant equipment</li> <li>Experience reading and interpreting P&amp;IDs, single-line diagrams, and turbine control logic</li> <li>Direct commissioning experience with GE 7/9HA, Siemens Energy SGT6/8-8000H, Mitsubishi M501/701JAC, or Doosan H-class turbines</li> <li>Experience with DCS/turbine control platforms (Mark VIe, SPPA-T3000, or equivalent)</li> <li>Familiarity with LTSA structures, OEM contract negotiation, and outage scope development</li> <li>Background in root-cause failure analysis (RCA/5-Why/Fishbone) for rotating equipment</li> <li>Experience with performance monitoring tools and heat balance modeling</li> <li>Exposure to grid interconnection requirements, PPA performance obligations, or capacity market rules</li> <li>Experience integrating power generation with co-located industrial or data center loads</li> <li>A bias toward action: comfortable making a call in the field without waiting for a committee</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work under pressure during startup, outages, or unplanned events, with a sense of urgency and ownership over outcomes</li> <li>Experience using SOLIDWORKS, Siemens NX, or similar CAD software</li> <li>Knowledge of engineering standards and best practices such as ASME B31.3, ASME BPV Code Section VIII, and AFSPCMAN 91-710</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as business needs require</li> <li>Flexibility to travel to other SpaceX sites</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand</li> <li>Typically exposed to work in outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Stand: Up to 3 hours per day</li> <li>Sit: Up to 6 hours per day</li> <li>Push/Pull: Up to 50lbs. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Power Plant Operator (Starbase)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>POWER PLANT OPERATOR</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is seeking a Power Plant Operator for its Starbase, TX facility. This is a hands-on role supporting day-to-day operations, maintenance, and troubleshooting at a power generation facility. You will inspect running equipment, respond to issues as they come up, restore systems, and keep generation and balance-of-plant online. You will work across mechanical, electrical, and controls equipment — pumps, piping, chillers, cooling towers, HVAC, generators, motors, water systems, UPS, switchgear, and plant control systems — following procedures and engineering direction in a fast-paced environment.</p> <p>This position entails ownership of equipment performance and reliability by monitoring process parameters and maintaining components, with a keen eye for leading indicators of instability or malfunction, and a drive to correct those issues in advance of undesirable events. Ideally, the operator has experience working with industrial processes that utilize engines, motors, fluid piping, electrical equipment, and instrumented controls.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide operational and maintenance support for plant mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and process systems, including pumps, piping, chillers, cooling towers, HVAC, generators, motors, water systems, UPS, switchgear, and related balance-of-plant equipment</li> <li>Perform daily inspections of critical systems, identify issues early, and self-report problems before they affect generation</li> <li>Identify equipment and process deviations and perform corrective actions</li> <li>Troubleshoot and repair operational issues found during normal plant operation, start-up, outages, or commissioning</li> <li>Assist with maintenance and troubleshooting of plant control systems, including PLC, HMI, SCADA, and related industrial controls for generation, cooling, power distribution, and safety</li> <li>Support HMI/interface monitoring and help maintain automated controls for fire protection and emergency shutdown</li> <li>Read and interpret P&amp;IDs, schematics, data sheets/manuals, drawings, and equipment documentation</li> <li>Work with engineers and technicians to create operating procedures</li> <li>Write, follow, and execute MOPs, SOPs, and EOPs, and learn and run standard operating procedures on the machinery</li> <li>Support lockout/tagout, hot work, confined space, and site safety and environmental requirements</li> <li>Coordinate and support scheduled system shutdowns, outages, and utility events as directed</li> <li>Support commissioning by witnessing equipment start-up, assisting with functional testing, and monitoring construction and turnover progress</li> <li>Coordinate with operations, maintenance, and engineering to restore equipment and keep the plant running</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of hands-on experience as a technician or operator working with industrial mechanical, electrical, and/or control systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate’s degree in a technical field (e.g., Power Plant Technology, Controls, Mechatronics, Automation) or equivalent experience</li> <li>Experience operating or maintaining equipment in a power plant, process plant, or similar industrial facility</li> <li>Experience writing and executing MOPs, SOPs, and EOPs</li> <li>Basic understanding of process parameters and engineering units for temperature, pressure, flow, and power</li> <li>Ability to read and understand P&amp;ID and schematic wiring diagrams</li> <li>Experience troubleshooting industrial equipment, including use of PLC/HMI/SCADA platforms (e.g., Ignition, Siemens, Rockwell, SEL)</li> <li>Experience with generators, UPS, switchgear, HVAC, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, or plant water systems</li> <li>Familiar with 120V, 480V, and 4160V electrical switchgear and components</li> <li>Familiar with lock out tag out, job hazard analysis, and hot work permitting</li> <li>Strong documentation, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently in a team environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be able to lift at least 25 lbs (unassisted)</li> <li>Willing and able to work outside with hand tools, which includes the ability to stand, walk, climb, and work with objects overhead</li> <li>Must be able to climb ladders and work in confined spaces</li> <li>Ability to work in all environments (heat, cold, rain) while wearing appropriate PPE</li> <li>Ability to remain focused in hazardous environments while following site safety procedures</li> <li>Flexible schedule, which could include days or nights and also weekends</li> <li>Must be available to work overtime, weekends, and rotating shifts as needed based on plant operational needs; flexibility required</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful,
