title: Sr. Manager, Power Plant (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SENIOR MANAGER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is building and operating combined-cycle gas turbine power plants that must come online, stay online, and perform. This role owns the design and build of the full power plant: gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, and everything else that keeps the plant running at rated output, day after day. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build, lead, and develop a multi-disciplinary power plant team spanning gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, controls, and commissioning</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of gas turbine power generation assets — installation, commissioning, startup, operations, and long-term maintenance — and be accountable for plant availability, reliability, and performance</li> <li>Set technical direction and execution plans for commissioning, including combustion tuning, control system checkout, protective relay testing, and performance/reliability run verification</li> <li>Own root-cause analysis and corrective action for turbine trips, forced outages, and performance degradation; drive fixes that prevent recurrence and hold the team to a no-repeat standard</li> <li>Establish and continuously improve operating procedures, startup/shutdown sequences, and abnormal operating condition playbooks</li> <li>Serve as the primary technical and commercial interface with OEMs (GE, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan) on warranty issues, LTSA scope, outage planning, and technical issues</li> <li>Plan, staff, and execute major/minor inspections, hot gas path outages, and combustion inspections in line with OEM maintenance intervals; own outage cost, duration, and quality of return-to-service</li> <li>Drive turbine performance analysis (heat rate, capacity factor, degradation curves) to identify efficiency losses and convert findings into funded corrective action</li> <li>Coordinate across balance-of-plant teams (HRSG, steam turbine, cooling systems, water treatment) to deliver integrated plant performance, not siloed subsystem success</li> <li>Own the construction-to-operations handoff with EPC contractors; ensure a clean transition from construction to commercial operation</li> <li>Develop and own spare parts strategy, critical spares inventory, and maintenance budgets; manage spend against reliability and availability targets</li> <li>Hire, coach, and retain engineers and technicians; set performance standards and grow the next generation of plant leadership</li> <li>Represent the power plant organization to internal stakeholders (operations, grid interconnection, commercial, construction) and make timely field decisions under pressure</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 14+ years of experience working utility-scale gas turbines in commissioning, operations, maintenance, or plant engineering roles</li> <li>2+ years of project management experience leading operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Working knowledge of combined-cycle plant systems: gas turbines, HRSGs, steam turbines, generators, and balance-of-plant equipment</li> <li>Experience reading and interpreting P&amp;IDs, single-line diagrams, and turbine control logic</li> <li>Direct commissioning or operations leadership experience with GE 7/9HA, Siemens Energy SGT6/8-8000H, Mitsubishi M501/701JAC, or Doosan H-class turbines</li> <li>Experience with DCS/turbine control platforms (Mark VIe, SPPA-T3000, or equivalent)</li> <li>Familiarity with LTSA structures, OEM contract negotiation, and outage scope development</li> <li>Background in root-cause failure analysis (RCA/5-Why/Fishbone) for rotating equipment</li> <li>Experience with performance monitoring tools and heat balance modeling</li> <li>Exposure to grid interconnection requirements, PPA performance obligations, or capacity market rules</li> <li>Experience integrating power generation with co-located industrial or data center loads</li> <li>Proven ownership of plant or fleet reliability metrics (availability, forced outage rate, heat rate) and of the budgets that fund them</li> <li>Experience standing up a new plant, commissioning organization, or operations team from construction through commercial operation</li> <li>A bias toward action: comfortable making a call in the field without waiting for a committee</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work under pressure during startup, outages, or unplanned events, with a sense of urgency and ownership over outcomes</li> <li>Experience using SOLIDWORKS, Siemens NX, or similar CAD software</li> <li>Knowledge of engineering standards and best practices such as ASME B31.3, ASME BPV Code Section VIII, and AFSPCMAN 91-710</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. title: Sr. Manager, Product Growth Strategy (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MANAGER, PRODUCT GROWTH STRATEGY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink is scaling consumer broadband worldwide. As Sr. Manager, Product Growth Strategy, you will lead the Starlink product growth team that takes service programs and offering changes to market, and you will be accountable for their growth impact.</p> <p>The team owns how we deploy programs such as plan and offer mechanics, referral programs, and market-specific value proposition work. You plan and product selection experiences and service programs work for markets, in partnership with global go-to-market teams. You organize how we ship changes to the product offering, new features, and new functionality across the service suite: launch coordination, impact planning, and prioritization.</p> <p>Direction comes from Consumer Growth leadership, the broader growth team, and go-to-market. This is not an order-taking seat. The team is expected to bring ideas, justify them, vet them, test them, and take them to market. The work is high impact and closely reviewed. You need to be strong enough to stand behind the choices the team makes, read back in-market performance, and iterate or stop.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the product growth team: set the bar, assign ownership, and hold the team to launch quality, timeline, and growth impact</li> <li>Own how service programs and offering changes go to market (multi-family, community access, cash referral, market-specific value propositions, and similar programs), including what is in the offer, where it launches, and what GTM needs in each market</li> <li>Organize deployment of product offering changes, new features, and new functionality across the service suite: roadmap, sequencing, launch coordination, and readiness with product, engineering, marketing, and in-market GTM</li> <li>Partner with global go-to-market teams so online experiences and service programs actually work in market (positioning, eligibility, in-store activation, onboarding, ops handoff, and local constraints)</li> <li>Drive impact planning and prioritization: size the growth case, sequence work against Consumer Growth goals, and kill or re-scope what will not move the number</li> <li>Be accountable for program and offering growth impact: get work executed, read back performance after launch, and use that feedback to iterate, scale, or stop</li> <li>Bring a point of view. Source ideas, justify them with data and GTM input, vet feasibility, run tests, and take winners to market. Do not wait to be assigned a list</li> <li>Represent product growth in Consumer Growth and GTM forums: defend the plan, surface tradeoffs early, and keep US and in-market teams aligned through launch</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree</li> <li>8+ years of experience in product, growth, go-to-market, consumer programs, or a related role in a technical or consumer business</li> <li>3+ years of direct people leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>10+ years in product growth, consumer subscription, telecommunications, broadband, or marketplace businesses</li> <li>5+ years leading a team that shipped programs or product changes into market</li> <li>Demonstrated ownership of launch coordination across product, engineering, marketing, and in-country GTM</li> <li>Experience taking service plans, promotions, or packaging changes live, then reading impact and iterating or killing</li> <li>Experience making digital purchase and onboarding experiences work across multiple countries or languages</li> <li>Comfort with market-specific value proposition work (including high-context markets such as Japan)</li> <li>Strong analytical chops: sizing, prioritization, experiment design, and post-launch readouts (Excel required; SQL or BI tools preferred)</li> <li>Experience in a fast-paced, high-scrutiny environment where you are expected to have a point of view and stand behind it</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel as needed to support global go-to-market teams</li> <li>Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Materials Engineer, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MATERIALS ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Materials Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work sits at the intersection of process, packaging, mechanical, and thermal engineering. The Payload team is responsible for the design of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Rapidly develop high-reliability microelectronics packages, cooling systems, and radiator hardware for satellites.</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of materials specification, validation, and process development— including device modeling, characterization of performance metrics, and materials failure analysis.</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, materials selection, prototyping, manufacturing, failure analysis.</li> <li>Build supply chains for build-up layers, plating chemicals, coatings, thermal interface materials, and other materials for compute and satellite manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for materials.</li> <li>Address materials and process challenges in advanced packaging while spearheading the development of next-generation TIM materials to improve packaging performance.</li> <li>Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Design thermal test vehicles and test setups to evaluate material/electronic properties. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted improvements via material or process changes.</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, electrical, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind</li> <li>Manage compliance risks related to materials and processes, ensuring safety and environmental compliance with industry standards.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain—to integrate materials innovations into product roadmaps and ensure accountability for operations and reliability.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline</li> <li>5+ years of experience in microelectronics device research or manufacturing&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Advanced degree in materials science or similar field</li> <li>Experience in hardware, robotics, automation, or manufacturing environments</li> title: Sr. Materials Engineer, Corrosion Control and Fluid Compatibility (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MATERIALS ENGINEER, CORROSION CONTROL AND FLUID COMPATIBILITY (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future, developing key in-house technologies from satellites’ flight computers and power systems to custom compute electronics, memory, and networking for on-orbit data centers. As a Senior Materials Engineer, you will serve as the technical owner for corrosion control, chemical resistance, liquid coolants and long-term material compatibility - defining and maintaining specifications for base fluids, additives, and wetted materials (including contaminant limits and compatibility criteria), while building and driving a comprehensive testing program evaluating coolant quality, contamination, and materials reliability.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own design criteria, selection, and reliability evaluations of materials used in liquid cooling systems</li> <li>Define and perform laboratory testing evaluating relevant corrosion mechanisms and long-duration chemical compatibility</li> <li>Define material and fluid performance requirements, specifications, validation approaches, and approval criteria</li> <li>Evaluate and down-select supplier technologies and formulations against performance, quality, cost, timing, and compliance objectives</li> <li>Drive material characterization and root cause analysis for failure resolution</li> <li>Define and execute experimental design and reliability campaigns for materials used in thermal management systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in materials science, chemical engineering, corrosion engineering, or a STEM field</li> <li>5+ years of experience in chemical and fluids processing or thermal management systems</li> <li>Hands-on experience with materials selection, testing, manufacturing processes, fluid compatibility and corrosion evaluations</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, chemical engineering, corrosion engineering, or a STEM field</li> <li>Strong understanding of chemical compatibility, corrosion mechanisms, coolant formulation, contaminant analysis, and the effects of vacuum, radiation, thermal cycling, and microgravity on fluids and materials</li> <li>Broad knowledge of thermal control systems, coolants (e.g., dielectric, ammonia, or specialized formulations), radiators, and/or two-phase systems</li> <li>Experience with spacecraft thermal control systems, satellite/ ISS/ CubeSat fluids, space-qualified coolants (e.g., dielectric, ammonia, or specialized formulations), radiators, or two-phase systems in vacuum/microgravity</li> <li>Experience coordinating material trials with process engineering, equipment suppliers, and material vendors</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to lead structured root cause analysis (e.g., DOE, 5-why, fishbone, fault-tree) and convert findings into durable material or process recommendations</li> <li>Experience working in a high-volume manufacturing or assembly environment and partnering with process, quality, production, and supply-chain teams</li> <li>Track record of owning complex, ambiguous materials problems end-to-end, setting priorities with limited supervision, and delivering results on tight timelines</li> <li>Experience mentoring engineers, technicians, interns, or new hires to a high-performing level</li> <li>Comfortable with data analysis (Python, JMP, MATLAB, or equivalent) to correlate process, metrology, and reliability results</li> <li>Strong first-principles problem solving and a demonstrated ability to dig deep on ambiguous materials and reliability challenges</li> <li>Passion for building, learning quickly, and owning outcomes end-to-end; thrives in a fast-paced, scrappy environment with tight timelines</li> <li>Effective written and interpersonal communication skills; able to convey complex technical ideas, influence decisions, and drive alignment across teams</li> <li>Self-motivated with strong organizational skills and a bias toward action</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willingness to travel to other SpaceX sites and/or vendors title: Sr. Materials Engineer, Electronic Materials
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. MATERIALS ENGINEER, ELECTRONIC MATERIALS</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world's most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world's largest satellite constellation, providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system - thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We've only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink's potential global impact. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we are looking for the best-in-class engineers to join the team.<br>&nbsp;<br>We are seeking a Sr. Materials Engineer to join our Bastrop, TX team, where we are advancing materials technologies to support the deployment of Starlink, the world's most advanced broadband internet system. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in semiconductor device physics and device fabrication, along with hands-on industry experience in at least one of the following domains—solar cell development, panel-level packaging, or printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing—to drive material and process innovations across all three areas. This position requires a technical expert who delivers thoughtful leadership, collaborates with stakeholders to execute strategies aligned with Starlink's business objectives, budget, and priorities, while orchestrating end-to-end equipment and process development. You will push material and device performance limits to enable high-efficiency, reliable systems for space and terrestrial applications.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the development and optimization of CVD recipes and device fabrication processes to boost solar cell efficiency.</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of equipment specification, validation, and process development— including device modeling, characterization of performance metrics, and materials failure analysis.</li> <li>Build supply chains for wafers, gases, chemicals, and equipment for solar cell manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for materials (e.g. silicon wafers, conductive pastes).</li> <li>Address material and process challenges in panel-level packaging while spearheading the development of next-generation dielectric materials to improve packaging performance and scalability.</li> <li>Specify and implement in-process metrology tools for quality control. Design wafer-level test structures to evaluate material/electronic properties. Integrate simulation tools with experimental data to guide and drive targeted improvements via material or process changes.</li> <li>Drive end-to-end material and process R&amp;D programs, from concept through product implementation, to drive cost down, efficiency improvements, and reliability in electronic systems.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain—to integrate materials innovations into product roadmaps and ensure accountability for operations and reliability.</li> <li>Manage compliance risks related to materials and processes, ensuring safety and environmental compliance with industry standards.</li> <li>Mentor and develop engineers, providing technical guidance and project oversight.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in materials science, electrical engineering, or an engineering degree.</li> <li>5+ years of experience in microelectronics device research or manufacturing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, electrical engineering, or a related field.</li> <li>Strong background in semiconductor device physics with extensive hands-on CVD, PVD and related device fabrication experience; preferred background in photovoltaics.</li> <li>Expertise in electrical device testing methods (IV, CV, Hall effect, TLM) and optical device characterization (ellipsometry, UV-VIS-IR spectroscopy, PL, EL, QSSPC).</li> <li>Proficiency in microscopy and analytical techniques (SEM/EDS, Raman, XRD, AFM, XPS, SIMS, FTIR, DMA, DSC).</li> <li>Proven cross-functional leadership skills, with experience aligning diverse teams to achieve shared technology goals.</li> <li>Strong communication skills for presenting to stakeholders as well as guiding and mentoring junior engineers.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work extended hours and weekends as needed.</li> <li>Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% time.</li> <li>Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.</li> <li>Comfort occasionally working in tight or confined spaces.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

MATERIALS ENGINEER, THIN FILMS</strong></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">Starlink is building the world's largest satellite constellation to deliver fast, reliable internet to people who need it most—and powering that constellation starts on the factory floor. We are insourcing solar cell manufacturing end-to-end, from crystal growth and ingot production through wafering and cell fabrication, to drive performance, cost, and scale at every step. High-efficiency, high-reliability cells made in-house are the backbone of the Starlink network: more photons in means more data out to customers around the world.</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">As a Sr. Materials Engineer for thin films, you will partner with solar cell process engineering on PECVD-deposited films that set the optical and electrical performance of insourced cells. You will build deep understanding of film chemistry, microstructure, interfaces, and failure modes, then work with process, production, and quality teams to turn that insight into higher efficiency, yield, reliability, and cost. You will operate as a technical expert for the team: setting priorities from program needs, solving poorly defined materials problems autonomously, and raising the bar for how we specify, evaluate, and improve thin-film materials. If you are passionate about solving hard problems, anchor your engineering judgment with first principles thinking, and are relentless about acting with urgency, this role is for you.</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none"><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></span></p> <ul> <li><span data-contrast="none"> Partner with solar cell process engineering on PECVD thin films (e.g., passivation, anti-reflection, and related dielectric or semiconductor layers), developing materials requirements, film-property targets, and the physical understanding of how deposited films perform in the reliability; translate that understanding into clear recommendations that improve cell performance and manufacturability</li> <li>Operate as the technical expert for thin-film materials: independently reliability recovery, supplier materials) and come to leadership with solved problems and already-implemented solutions</li> <li>Partner with process engineering on DOEs and process trials: define materials-relevant responses, interpret how plasma, chemistry, and hardware changes affect film properties and cell results, and recommend durable improvements</li> <li>Define film material requirements, specifications, and acceptance criteria; qualify precursors, consumables, and film stacks so materials used in production are understood, controlled, and scalable</li> <li>Lead structured root cause analysis for materials-limited performance, yield, and reliability issues (film defects, interface failure, contamination, stoichiometry, stress, delamination); correlate process history with metrology (ellipsometry, lifetime, FTIR, SEM, I-V, and related methods) and drive corrective actions to first principles</li> <li>Influence cross-functional decisions with process, equipment, quality, production, and characterization teams; challenge assumptions that do not serve cell performance or manufacturability; create materials methods, specifications, and tools that thin-film materials, PECVD-relevant materials science, and first-principles problem solving; generate and share high-quality engineering content, specifications, and best practices</li> <li>Champion a culture of safety and quality in all vacuum, plasma, pyrophoric/toxic gas, chemical handling, lab, and production support activities</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> with thin films, PECVD or other vacuum-deposited coatings, or electronic materials in a manufacturing or R&amp;D environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> PECVD-deposited films in semiconductor or solar cell manufacturing</li> <li>Experience working closely with process engineering on PECVD or other vacuum deposition processes in a manufacturing or development environment</li> <li>Proficiency with thin-film and solar-cell metrology such as spectroscopic ellipsometry, reflectance, FTIR, minority-carrier lifetime (QSSPC/PL), SEM-EDS, XPS, four-point probe, film stress, and optical inspection</li> <li>Deep understanding of film growth mechanisms, precursor chemistry (e.g., SiH4, NH3, N2O, TMB, PH3), plasma/vacuum processing, and how jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. PACKAGING ENGINEER – THERMAL MATERIALS, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Sr. Packaging Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work sits at the intersection of process, packaging, materials, and thermal engineering. The Payload team is responsible for the design of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the full lifecycle of advanced packaging through board assembly process development— including requirements capture, materials selection, prototyping, process optimization, manufacturing, and failure analysis.</li> <li>Drive system trades, requirements capture, materials selection, prototyping, manufacturing, failure analysis.</li> <li>Spearhead the development integrated thermal solutions including next generation TIMs to improve package performance.</li> <li>Own the full lifecycle of equipment specification, qualification, and ramp.</li> <li>Build supply chains for die, packages, components, consumable chemicals, and equipment for satellite compute manufacturing. Define incoming acceptance criteria for components and materials.</li> <li>Work closely with engineers from adjacent disciplines (mechanical, thermal, materials, electrical, software, test engineering, supply chain, silicon design, etc.) to deliver tightly integrated, high-performance hardware</li> <li>Challenge assumptions, question requirements, learn from your mistakes, and approach problems with an open mind</li> <li>Collaborate closely with leadership and stakeholders across all departments—including design, reliability, production, and supply chain to deliver best in class PARTNERSHIP MANAGER (STARLINK BUSINESS AVIATION)</strong></p> <p class="WordSection1">The Starlink Aviation Partnerships team is hiring a local, results-driven Sr. Partnerships Manager to support Starlink’s adoption in business aviation worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. As we continue to upgrade and expand the constellation, we’re looking for best-in-class engineers to join the team.</p> <p>As a Sr. PCB Designer at SpaceX, you’ll be responsible for creating the layout for all our in-house board designs. You’re not just connecting the dots. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference.</p> <p>Our Power Electronics team designs and develops the power conversion and control systems at the heart of Starmind satellites and orbital data centers — enabling the reliable, high-efficiency power delivery required for massive on-orbit AI compute. title: Sr. Power Plant Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. POWER PLANT ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is building and operating combined-cycle gas turbine power plants that must come online, stay online, and perform. This role owns the design and build of the full power plant: gas turbines, mechanical and electrical balance of plant, and everything else that keeps the plant running at rated output, day after day. This is not a desk job. You will be constructing the power plant, owning commissioning in the control room during startup, and in the field troubleshooting.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Support the full lifecycle of gas turbine power generation assets — installation, commissioning, startup, operations, and long-term maintenance</li> <li>Lead or support commissioning activities including jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. PROCESS CONTROLS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p><span data-teams="true">The Solar Cell team is revolutionizing power generation for space applications through advanced solar cell manufacturing. title: Sr. Product Security Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. PRODUCT SECURITY ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Security Software Engineer you will influence the security of software across our product lines. We are looking for people with a track record of shipping reliable software and who have a broad understanding of the security design of today’s Internet, including the cryptographic primitives involved. You see the big picture, prioritize accordingly, and are comfortable with working at different levels of abstraction. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:</p> <ul> <li>Software engineering</li> <li>Applied cryptography</li> <li>Network security</li> <li>Operating system security</li> <li>Secure/Authenticated boot</li> <li>Incident response and adversary detection</li> <li>Vulnerability research</li> </ul> <p>Being flexible, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams are paramount to success. If you are passionate about building quality products, love the challenges of outsmarting adversaries, and want to make an impact on an inter-planetary scale, then you will fit right in.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and build security infrastructure for Starlink, including cryptographic services and other security-critical services</li> <li>Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites</li> <li>Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this</li> <li>Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams</li> <li>Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements</li> <li>Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science or another STEM discipline and 5+ years of professional experience in security software development; OR 7+ years of professional experience in security software development in lieu of a degree</li> <li>Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing security solutions for operating systems, distributed systems, or other enterprise/large-scale infrastructure</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems</li> <li>Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of network protocols; including the TCP/IP stack as well as UDP based protocols</li> <li>Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems</li> <li>Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams</li> <li>Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and in a team</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly</li> <li>Advanced degree in a technical or engineering discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Propulsion Engineer (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. PROPULSION ENGINEER (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>The Sr. Propulsion Engineer role is responsible for developing the fluid systems to enable high-performance and highly manufacturable interplanetary vehicles. This role will be responsible for designing, analyzing, and building a wide range of fluid systems across the Starship and Super Heavy vehicles.</p> <p>The role includes sizing vehicle fluid systems, engaging in detailed mechanical design, performing structural analysis, and driving the manufacturing and build flow of parts and systems. Systems will include high-pressure gas storage and control, cryogenic fluid management, attitude control systems, and thermal control systems. The Sr. Propulsion Engineer will also develop the concept of operations for their systems, from acceptance testing to in-flight operations.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform fluids system sizing analysis to determine basic system requirements</li> <li>Transform system requirements into hardware concepts and trade implementation and architecture options</li> <li>Design a range of pressurized and unpressurized structures and parts to enable system capability, creating original CAD models and prints</li> <li>Perform structural analysis of parts and components to ensure survivability</li> <li>Execute design for manufacturability changes to enhance production efficiency</li> <li>Drive the first builds of flight hardware and work with a manufacturing team to establish a production line</li> <li>Coordinate and execute development, qualification, and acceptance testing of flight hardware</li> <li>Participate in design reviews </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's or advanced degree in aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, or professional experience in the field of aerospace/mechanical engineering</li> <li>4+ years of experience with GD&amp;T concepts</li> <li>Experience with fluid dynamics, finite element, or related or associate degree and 6+ years of experience; or 7+ years of professional experience as a recruiter in lieu of a degree</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of high-volume recruiting experience, ideally in the manufacturing sector</li> <li>Experience with in-house recruiting</li> <li>Experience recruiting for skilled trades (technicians, electricians, facilities, etc.)</li> <li>Strong tenure with demonstrated success in recruiting roles</li> <li>Full life cycle recruiting experience, from sourcing to closing</li> <li>Comfort with reviewing, evaluating and reporting on recruiting data</li> <li>Ability to distinguish between the top 50% and the top 5% of talent within their respective fields</li> <li>Demonstrated expertise in non-standard recruiting methods: cold calling candidates and companies, organizing and executing ad hoc networking events, identifying industry experts and finding unique methods to engage with them, creating unique targeted sourcing campaigns, etc.</li> <li>Comfortable interfacing directly with hiring managers including director and VP level technical leaders</li> <li>Ability to build strong relationships with both hiring managers and candidates</li> <li>Ability to accurately present but not oversell candidates to client groups; title: Sr. Responsible Engineer - Turbomachinery (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. RESPONSIBLE ENGINEER - TURBOMACHINERY (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>This role as a responsible engineer (RE) focuses on the development of turbomachinery for Starship's fluid systems, with the goal of creating high-performance and highly manufacturable interplanetary vehicles. The position involves designing, analyzing, and building advanced turbopumps that manage pressurization for Starship throughout all phases of travel to the Moon and Mars, including in-space propellant transfer. This is a unique opportunity to expand the frontiers of turbomachinery knowledge and manage cryogenic fluids in space.</p> <p>Key responsibilities include sizing turbomachinery components, performing detailed mechanical design, conducting structural and fluid analysis, and overseeing the manufacturing and assembly of parts and systems. The RE will be the primary owner of turbomachinery hardware, tasked with developing the concept of operations for each unit, from acceptance testing through in-flight performance.</p> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>&nbsp;Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of turbomachinery and manufacturing engineers, driving the rapid development and execution of designs for Starship's propulsion system turbomachinery</li> <li>Design,&nbsp;build&nbsp;and&nbsp;test&nbsp;turbopumps for Starship, the most advanced orbital vehicle propulsion system ever designed</li> <li>Develop and train teammates to support empowered product ownership utilizing risk-conscious decision-making skills under pressure</li> <li>Own turbomachinery product families – every engineer at SpaceX assumes profound responsibility for their hardware</li> <li>Interface with our world-class production team to ensure that your team’s designs are successfully translated into the fleet of rockets that is revolutionizing access to space</li> <li>Maintain a positive and constructive attitude in the face of technical and non-technical challenges</li> <li>Work collaboratively with commercial and governmental customers to ensure 100% mission success</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering title: Sr. Screen Printing Equipment Engineer, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">SR. SCREEN PRINTING EQUIPMENT ENGINEER, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK)</span></strong></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Starlink&nbsp;believes in providing fast, reliable internet to those that need it most. We design, build, and launch the world's largest and most advanced satellite constellation that&nbsp;is capable of delivering&nbsp;high-speed internet to even the most remote locations.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559739&quot;:200,&quot;335559740&quot;:276}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">As a Sr. Screen Printing Equipment Engineer, you will own the screen printing and related metallization equipment used to manufacture silicon heterojunction solar cells at massive scale. You will work closely with our existing Metallization/Screen Printing Process Engineering team to ensure world-class equipment performance, reliability, and uptime. While the process team focuses on paste properties, contact formation, and cell efficiency, you will be the hardware owner responsible for tool availability, stability, and scaling to support our ambitious goals.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559739&quot;:200,&quot;335559740&quot;:276}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Your work will form the backbone of the&nbsp;Starlink&nbsp;network (photons of sunlight in is directly proportional to photons of data out to customers!) and help provide internet to tens of millions of customers all around the world. You will spearhead state of the art production equipment for an internal solar cell production line, providing high efficiency and high-quality solar cells for both our latest generation&nbsp;Starlink&nbsp;satellites and for Starship missions to the Moon and Mars.</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559739&quot;:200,&quot;335559740&quot;:276}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">RESPONSIBILITIES:</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;201341983&quot;:0,&quot;335559739&quot;:200,&quot;335559740&quot;:276}">&nbsp;</span></p> <ul> <li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="16" data-list-defn-props="{&quot;335552541&quot;:1,&quot;335559685&quot;:720,&quot;335559991&quot;:360,&quot;469769226&quot;:&quot;Symbol&quot;,&quot;469769242&quot;:[8226],&quot;469777803&quot;:&quot;left&quot;,&quot;469777804&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;469777815&quot;:&quot;multilevel&quot;}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="auto">Work with facilities and process engineering teams to install, qualify, maintain, and continuously improve high-throughput screen printing equipment for heterojunction silicon solar cell&nbsp;manufacturing</span></li> <li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="16" data-list-defn-props="{&quot;335552541&quot;:1,&quot;335559685&quot;:720,&quot;335559991&quot;:360,&quot;469769226&quot;:&quot;Symbol&quot;,&quot;469769242&quot;:[8226],&quot;469777803&quot;:&quot;left&quot;,&quot;469777804&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;469777815&quot;:&quot;multilevel&quot;}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1">Drive equipment reliability and uptime to support very large volume production with minimal downtime. title: Sr. Security Engineer (Infrastructure)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. SECURITY ENGINEER (INFRASTRUCTURE)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is looking for a Sr. Security Engineer (Infrastructure) to join Information Security to help protect and drive the SpaceX mission.&nbsp;Information drives our business. We must protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems and processes across the enterprise, and defend against loss of control or confidence in our systems.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design on-premises Kubernetes platforms that security services run on, and the compute, storage, and networking they depend on.</li> <li>Lead cluster lifecycle work, including upgrades, capacity, failure domains, and safe change.</li> <li>Build the automation other engineers use to provision, configure, and operate the platform.</li> <li>Set standards for how security services are deployed, hardened, and run on Kubernetes.</li> <li>Harden clusters and workloads, including RBAC, policy, secrets, and secure configuration.</li> <li>Respond to the hardest production incidents and drive them to a durable fix.</li> <li>Define the signals, alerts, and operational practices that keep the platform supportable.</li> <li>Document what you run, keep it working, and advise other teams on it.</li> <li>Find systemic gaps with security and IT, then ship platform and deployment changes that reduce risk.</li> <li>Deliver solutions that are scalable, repeatable, maintainable, and secure.</li> <li>Coordinate with information security, IT, software, and other partners.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science or another STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience operating production infrastructure and high school diploma or equivalency certificate in lieu of a degree.</li> <li>5+ years of experience operating on-premises Kubernetes in a production environment.</li> <li>5+ years of experience with Linux system administration and with Python, Go, or another language used to automate infrastructure.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Production Kubernetes at scale, including control plane, networking, storage, RBAC, and upgrades.</li> <li>Designing on-premises compute, storage, and network architectures for container platforms.</li> <li>Cluster and node hardening, admission control, and secure workload configuration.</li> <li>Infrastructure as code and configuration management.</li> <li>Python or Go for platform tooling and automation.</li> <li>Linux internals and troubleshooting.</li> <li>Observability, alerting, and operational readiness for production platforms.</li> <li>CI/CD or GitOps-style delivery onto Kubernetes.</li> <li>Capacity planning, failure domains, and recovery for on-premises platforms.</li> <li>TCP/IP at the level needed to build and debug cluster networking.</li> <li>Root-cause debugging under time pressure.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed.</li> <li>This role requires you to be onsite. Hybrid or remote work will not be considered.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Sr. Security Software Engineer (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. SECURITY SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As a Security Software Engineer you will influence the security of software across our product lines. We are looking for people with a track record of shipping reliable software and who have a broad understanding of the security design of today’s Internet, including the cryptographic primitives involved. You see the big picture, prioritize accordingly, and are comfortable with working at different levels of abstraction. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:</p> <ul> <li>Software engineering</li> <li>Applied cryptography</li> <li>Network security</li> <li>Operating system security</li> <li>Secure/Authenticated boot</li> <li>Incident response and adversary detection</li> <li>Vulnerability research</li> </ul> <p>Being flexible, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams are paramount to success. If you are passionate about building quality products, love the challenges of outsmarting adversaries, and want to make an impact on an inter-planetary scale, then you will fit right in.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and build security infrastructure for Starlink, including cryptographic services and other security-critical services</li> <li>Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites</li> <li>Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this</li> <li>Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams</li> <li>Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements</li> <li>Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science or another STEM discipline and 5+ years of professional experience in security software development; OR 7+ years of professional experience in security software development in lieu of a degree</li> <li>Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing security solutions for operating systems, distributed systems, or other enterprise/large-scale infrastructure</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems</li> <li>Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of network protocols; including the TCP/IP stack as well as UDP based protocols</li> <li>Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems</li> <li>Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams</li> <li>Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and in a team</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly</li> <li>Advanced degree in a technical or engineering discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Sr. Software Engineer, Flight Software (Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER, FLIGHT SOFTWARE (STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>As an engineer on the Starship software team, you will design, develop and test software that is used to control SpaceX flight systems for the Starship and Super Heavy vehicles. You will engage with other SpaceX software and hardware engineers to code highly reliable software that allows Starship to become an orbital vehicle. You will be responsible for the complete life cycle of the software you create, from development to testing to operation during a mission.</p> <p>Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop highly reliable autonomous software systems and simulations to validate them</li> <li>Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints</li> <li>Own all aspects of software development, including design, testing, and mission integration</li> <li>Provide strong technical leadership, focus on continuous improvement</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline and 4+ years of professional experience in software development; jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Starlink is building the hardware to make a global communications network real: user terminals, gateways, satellites, and datacenter products, at a rate and a cost aerospace has not shipped before.</p> <p>This is one role because the work is one job. You own a technology, a supplier, and a manufacturing process from selection through high-volume production, and you are accountable for how that hardware performs after it ships. The scope runs across silicon, advanced packaging, printed circuit boards, mechanical parts, and assembly. Some weeks you are choosing the process and the factory. Some weeks you are the reliability engineer or the quality engineer standing up a new design, a new line, or a new process. You do not hand the outcome to someone else.</p> <p>You will do this with a manufacturing team that has already taken flight hardware and consumer hardware from first article to rate. The problems are on the floor, at the supplier, and in the field.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own hardware from selection to scale for Starlink consumer, gateway, satellite, or datacenter products. Technology choice, supplier choice, process choice, equipment, yield, cost, schedule, and field performance sit with you.</li> <li>Select suppliers who can build at the quality and rate the program needs, and develop them until the process is capable. Change the supplier when the technical path is not there.</li> <li>Choose the manufacturing process and the equipment. Define the process window, the control plan, and the evidence of capability before rate, not after the line is already late.</li> <li>Bring up new designs, new factories, and new processes. Be on the floor, debug the tool, and close the yield and rate gap yourself.</li> <li>Do the reliability and quality work the hardware needs: failure analysis, test and screen strategy, process FMEA, corrective action, and a field-to-factory loop that changes the product.</li> <li>Carry the technical decision with design, test, supply chain, and the supplier. Make the call and live with the field result.</li> <li>Scale what is proven. Stop what will not scale.&nbsp;</li> <li>Own escapes into customer deployments, gateway sites, orbit, and datacenter operation.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline.</li> <li>8+ years of hands-on experience in supplier development, manufacturing or process engineering, equipment engineering, quality engineering, or reliability engineering for hardware.</li> <li>Experience with driving a supplier, design, or process from initial conception to production.</li> <li>Experience owning the outcomes related to final yield, quality, and performance.</li> <li>Experience in at least one of the following: <ul> <li>Semiconductor or packaging&nbsp;</li> <li>PCB fabrication or assembly</li> <li>Mechanical fabrication</li> <li>Electromechanical assembly</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: </strong></p> <ul> <li>10+ years, including ownership of a commodity or process from selection through a high-volume ramp.</li> <li>Consumer electronics, networking, satellite, or datacenter hardware, with production measured in thousands to millions of units.</li> <li>New factory or new process bring-up: equipment selection and installation, process development, capability, and rate.</li> <li>Technology and supplier selection on a new design, including process trade studies, make-or-buy, and second source.</li> <li>Reliability: life test, HALT/HASS or equivalent, physics of failure, and corrective action tied to field returns.</li> <li>Using FMEA, control plans, SPC, DOE, MSA, and structured root cause as engineering tools.</li> <li>International supplier travel, and sound judgment when you are the person representing SpaceX in the factory.</li> </ul> jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain with world-class precision measurement capabilities for high-tolerance mechanical components.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. The role also includes ownership to deliver on time, monitor field performance, react to issues, and feed lessons learned back to engineering teams for iterative improvement.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking a Metrology Engineer with strong technical and leadership skills to drive supplier development, metrology strategy, and AI-enabled measurement systems for mechanical parts in high-volume production.&nbsp;The Supplier Development Engineer, Mechanical Metrology will be responsible for executing end-to-end supplier strategies focused on precision mechanical components and their associated metrology processes. This position will have significant technical and leadership influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end supplier development for mechanical metrology and high-precision mechanical components within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, spanning strategic supplier selection, new product introduction (NPI), qualification, production ramp, and reactive quality support&nbsp;</li> <li>Engage early with suppliers on selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to properly set up high-volume manufacturing programs by ensuring material and process corners are fully characterized and completed&nbsp;</li> <li>Provide technical guidance on mechanical metrology methods, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&amp;T) implementation, datum scheme development and best practices, PC-DMIS programming, surface texture and surface technology standards, and tight-tolerance mechanical parts&nbsp;</li> <li>Indirectly manage internal metrology lab activities and technicians by setting technical direction, prioritizing work, and ensuring consistent execution of measurement standards and best practices&nbsp;</li> <li>Implement artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning solutions for metrology, including automated vision inspection, predictive clear engineering inferences, trend analysis, and actionable recommendations derived from metrology results&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s manufacturing, or supplier development (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)&nbsp;</span></li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-teams="true">10+ years of experience in mechanical metrology, precision manufacturing, or supplier development</span></li> <li>Strong technical background in Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&amp;T), dimensional metrology, measurement system analysis, and high-volume production environments&nbsp;</li> <li>Demonstrated leadership skills with experience indirectly managing labs, technicians, or cross-functional technical teams&nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience implementing artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for metrology applications&nbsp;</li> datum scheme development, GD&amp;T best practices, measurement fixture design, and fixture qualification processes&nbsp;</li> <li>Deep knowledge of mechanical metrology tools and methods including CMMs, optical scanners, surface profilometers, laser trackers, and automated inspection systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), Advanced Product Quality mechanical components&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong understanding of manufacturing capability and metrology capability assessments, including process window validation, uncertainty analysis, and process capability indices (Cp/Cpk)&nbsp;</li> <li>Proven ability to translate raw metrology data into meaningful engineering insights and inferences that drive design and process decisions&nbsp;</li> title: Sr. Terrestrial Services Sales Manager (Starlink Aviation)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. TERRESTRIAL SERVICES SALES MANAGER (STARLINK AVIATION)</strong></p> <p>The Starlink Aviation team is hiring a local, results-driven Senior Sales Manager to drive adoption of Starlink’s high-speed terrestrial connectivity across airport and ground operations worldwide. Starlink presents a major opportunity to transform how airlines and airports operate on the ground by delivering reliable, multi-gigabit connectivity to lounges, gates, hangars, maintenance bays, fleet vehicles, and other critical facilities. This hunter-focused role requires strong personal drive to engage new and existing airline and business aviation customers, uncover new terrestrial opportunities, build key relationships, maximize internal and external outcomes, and consistently sign high-value deals that deliver immediate impact.</p> <p>We are partnering with airlines, aircraft operators, airports, and aviation service providers to deliver connectivity that matches or exceeds terrestrial standards for ground operations and passenger-facing facilities. We’re seeking tenacious, commercially sharp sales professionals who excel at hunting and closing deals to help reshape the realities of airport infrastructure. title: Sr. Thermal Engineer - Fluids Analysis, AI Satellites (Starmind)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SR. THERMAL ENGINEER (FLUIDS ANALYSIS), AI SATELLITES (STARMIND)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Scaling AI in space is a thermal problem as much as a power and processing problem. With a dense compute payload dissipating hundreds of kilowatts, the thermal system must efficiently transfer heat to large radiators that reject it to space, under solar load, eclipse, and multi-mode AI duty cycles.</p> <p>You will join the StarmindThermal team, which owns the satellite cooling stack end-to-end. Rejecting hundreds of kilowatts of accelerator waste heat to space is limited by high-flux loads transferring heat to massive deployable radiators. No capable cooling architecture has been flown at this scale. As a Senior Thermal Engineer focused on fluids analysis, you own conjugate heat transfer and thermal-fluid analysis of cold plates, heat exchangers, and radiator channels and manifolds, and the system 0-D/1-D thermal-fluid network that sets flow split, ΔP budget, loop ΔT, and pump operating point. You co-evolve geometry and flow path with mechanical and fluid-systems owners under tight feedback from manufacturing and test. You sit where the local physics is hardest and the design decisions stick: predictions that close margins, ground in test, and drive rate-production hardware.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own conjugate heat-transfer (CHT) and thermal-fluid analysis of high-performance cold plates, heat exchangers, and radiator channels for STARMIND satellites</li> <li>Own the system 0-D/1-D thermal-fluid network that sizes and balances the cooling loop: flow split, ΔP budget, loop ΔT, pump operating point</li> <li>Drive cooling-loop architecture trades with hardware and vehicle-level thermal teammates</li> <li>Co-evolve geometry, materials and processes with hardware owners to find mass producible, efficient thermal solutions</li> <li>Predict component and system performance under wide range of flow and thermal conditions</li> <li>Own pre-test prediction, test design, and model-test correlation for fluid component and integrated thermal tests</li> <li>Automate analysis workflows for re-running trades as designs and boundary conditions change</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or a related engineering discipline</li> <li>5+ years of professional experience in fluids, CFD, or thermal analysis</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or a related engineering discipline</li> <li>Steady/transient conjugate heat-transfer CFD of liquid-cooled or high-heat-flux hardware (STAR-CCM+, ANSYS Fluent/CFX, or equivalent)</li> <li>Hand-calc checks and engineering judgment on mesh, turbulence modeling, and model fidelity</li> <li>Hands on hardware testing inclusive of instrumentation selection and model correlation</li> <li>Relevant manufacturing techniques, and judiciously pushing their constraints</li> <li>Watertight CFD geometry (Siemens NX or equivalent)</li> <li>Package/board-level tools as secondary (Icepak, Flotherm)</li> <li>0-D/1-D thermal-fluid network modeling to size and balance cooling loops (flow split, ΔP budget, loop ΔT, pump operating point)</li> <li>Scripting analysis workflows and post-processing (Python preferred)</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours or weekends as needed for mission critical deadlines</li> <li>Some travel may occasionally be required</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
