title: Supplier Development Engineer (Materials Engineering)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><span data-teams="true"><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER (MATERIALS ENGINEERING)</strong></span></p> <p>SpaceX demands a new type of supply chain. We require our suppliers to provide premium quality with rapidly evolving designs at increasingly ambitious volumes. We are actively looking for candidates who possess comprehensive knowledge of manufacturing and quality tools and have unrelenting motivation to enable suppliers for success. This position will support our Starship program and requires a combination of proven leadership and technical capabilities.</p> <p>This is a highly technical position that requires practical experience in manufacturing engineering and new product development through to stabilized production for an array of fabrication processes (components and assemblies) used in rockets and rocket engines.&nbsp;The ideal candidate will have a broad and thorough understanding of propulsion/fluid system component fabrication including extrusions, draw forming, welded and seamless tubing, cutting, and assembly, along with associated processes. This candidate should have the desire and capability to take on new challenges in unfamiliar areas to help enable our mission to Mars.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the technical point of contact for assigned parts and assemblies of the rocket, solving emergent challenges at suppliers, and mitigating risk to the manifest by addressing high-impact manufacturing and quality challenges</li> <li>Own the new product introduction of new assemblies on the rocket, including determining the ideal manufacturing method, identifying suppliers, and developing a reliable process for ramping to rate. This individual is expected to be the extreme owner for the process at suppliers for new parts, drawing changes, or when re-sourcing existing parts to a new supplier</li> <li>Conduct design for manufacturing (DFM) reviews to ensure parts are manufacturable at early stages, preferably prior to sourcing</li> <li>Work with procurement to find exceptional suppliers and vet them appropriately for quality and ability to meet our aggressive takt times</li> <li>Create and develop specifications as needed to flow down quality and manufacturing requirements to the supply base</li> <li>Scope out new forming, cutting, and inspection technologies and suppliers that may be employed to improve rate/quality/efficiency</li> <li>Review issues on assigned parts and solve to the root cause, implementing changes at the supplier, at SpaceX or both, as appropriate, drive further actions to closure, and re-source to new suppliers where appropriate</li> <li>Create and disposition issue tickets where needed, working with engineering counterparts to implement, but not limited to, required re-work, repair or use as-is disposition</li> <li>Become thoroughly familiar with your assigned parts and the processes that make up the overall assembly and become the primary point of contact for supply chain related defects on your parts</li> <li>Demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, attention to detail, self-direction and courage to push the technical envelope which is conventionally held in the industry.</li> <li>Lead containment activities on assigned parts, working with cross-functional counterparts to agree on scope, path forward and ultimate resolution</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li>1+ years of experience with manufacturing and/or inspection of mechanical products in a production environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in engineering or business</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of propulsion/fluid systems and the respective component manufacturing processes including: raw materials, draw forming, extrusions, seamless and welded tubing, pipe manufacturing, bending, welding, proof/pressure testing, and other forming &amp; assembly processes.</li> <li>Fundamental understanding of sheet metal forming, cutting, and assembly processes, particularly in stretch forming (longitudinal and transverse), stamping (progressing and transfer), spin forming, roll forming, roll bending, press brake forming, hydroforming and tube forming/bending of primarily, but not limited to, stainless and carbon steels.</li> <li>Experience with machining and ancillary operations such as milling, turning, and tube cutting of materials</li> <li>Experience with engineering drawings, modeling, GD&amp;T, etc.</li> <li>General familiarity with welding (TIG, MIG and orbital tube welding) of stainless and carbon steels is a plus</li> <li>Knowledge of supplier quality processes (production part approval process, advanced product quality planning, first article inspection reports, etc.)</li> <li>Knowledge of statistical techniques and methods, e.g., design of experiments, Lean, Six Sigma, etc.</li> <li>Experience with quality systems (ISO 9000/TS/AS9100/NADCAP) and MRP/ERP systems</li> <li>Disciplined approach to problem solving - 8D</li> <li>Proficient in MS Office and Excel applications and report writing</li> <li>Experience with sharing information and influencing others across organizational lines, internally and externally</li> <li>Experience with PPAP and related elements (PFD, PFMEA, control plan, process capability, etc.)</li> <li>Experience leading containments of discrepant product</li> <li>Experience in manufacturing with different grades of stainless steel</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to work extended hours, some nights and/or weekends when needed</li> <li>Ability to travel: up to 40-50% work week travel</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

title: Supplier Development Engineer, Assembly Processes (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, ASSEMBLY PROCESSES (STARLINK)&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain with world-class precision assembly processes at contract manufacturers.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. title: Supplier Development Engineer, Mechanical Metrology (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, MECHANICAL METROLOGY (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain with world-class precision measurement capabilities for high-tolerance mechanical components.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. The role also includes ownership to deliver on time, monitor field performance, react to issues, and feed lessons learned back to engineering teams for iterative improvement.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are seeking a Metrology Engineer with strong technical and leadership skills to drive supplier development, metrology strategy, and AI-enabled measurement systems for mechanical parts in high-volume production.&nbsp;The Supplier Development Engineer, Mechanical Metrology will be responsible for executing end-to-end supplier strategies focused on precision mechanical components and their associated metrology processes. This position will have significant technical and leadership influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end supplier development for mechanical metrology and high-precision mechanical components within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, spanning strategic supplier selection, new product introduction (NPI), qualification, production ramp, and reactive quality support&nbsp;</li> <li>Engage early with suppliers on selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to properly set up high-volume manufacturing programs by ensuring material and process corners are fully characterized and completed&nbsp;</li> <li>Provide technical guidance on mechanical metrology methods, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&amp;T) implementation, datum scheme development and best practices, PC-DMIS programming, surface texture and surface technology standards, and measurement system analysis (MSA) while driving adoption of AI-powered metrology solutions&nbsp;</li> <li>Design, develop, and qualify precision measurement fixtures, including fixture concept design, datum scheme optimization, repeatability studies, and qualification to ensure measurement system stability and accuracy&nbsp;</li> <li>Assess supplier manufacturing and metrology capabilities, including capacity, process windows, gage repeatability and reproducibility (GR&amp;R) performance, uncertainty budgets, datum scheme robustness, and scalability for high-volume production of tight-tolerance mechanical parts&nbsp;</li> <li>Indirectly manage internal metrology lab activities and technicians by setting technical direction, prioritizing work, and ensuring consistent execution of measurement standards and best practices&nbsp;</li> <li>Implement artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning solutions for metrology, including automated vision inspection, predictive analytics on measurement trends, anomaly detection, and intelligent data interpretation systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Lead Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), First Article Inspections (FAI), gage repeatability and reproducibility (GR&amp;R) studies, and production rate ramps to enable full-rate, high-volume manufacturing&nbsp;</li> <li>Develop and execute robust qualification plans including dimensional validation, surface finish and texture analysis, coordinate measuring machine (CMM) and optical measurement correlation, and environmental stability testing&nbsp;</li> <li>Drive supplier performance improvement through Lean methodologies, supplier scorecards, process audits, and systematic problem solving to deliver measurable gains in quality, cost, and delivery&nbsp;</li> <li>Perform reactive quality engineering support, including rapid containment, root cause analysis, and corrective actions for measurement escapes, dimensional non-conformances, and field issues&nbsp;</li> <li>Own on-time delivery of qualification and production ramp activities while continuously monitoring field performance, reacting quickly to issues, and feeding lessons learned from field data back to design and process engineering teams for iterative improvement&nbsp;</li> <li>Ensure internal customers are highly satisfied by delivering not only precise measurement data but clear engineering inferences, trend analysis, and actionable recommendations derived from metrology results&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, metrology, industrial engineering, or a other engineering discipline&nbsp;</li> <li><span data-teams="true">1+ years of experience in mechanical metrology, precision manufacturing, or supplier development (internship and extracurricular experience is applicable)&nbsp;</span></li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-teams="true">3+ years of experience in mechanical metrology, precision manufacturing, or supplier development</span></li> <li>Strong technical background in Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&amp;T), dimensional metrology, measurement system analysis, and high-volume production environments&nbsp;</li> <li>Demonstrated leadership skills with experience indirectly managing labs, technicians, or cross-functional technical teams&nbsp;</li> <li>Hands-on experience implementing artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for metrology applications&nbsp;</li> <li>Proficiency in PC-DMIS programming for coordinate measuring machines (CMM) and strong familiarity with Hexagon CMM and Optical Measurement Machine (OMM) hardware&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong expertise in datum scheme development, GD&amp;T best practices, measurement fixture design, and fixture qualification processes&nbsp;</li> <li>Deep knowledge of mechanical metrology tools and methods including CMMs, optical scanners, surface profilometers, laser trackers, and automated inspection systems&nbsp;</li> <li>Experience with Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA), Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA), Measurement System Analysis (MSA), and Gage R&amp;R specifically for precision mechanical components&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong understanding of manufacturing capability and metrology capability assessments, including process window validation, uncertainty analysis, and process capability indices (Cp/Cpk)&nbsp;</li> <li>Proven ability to translate raw metrology data into meaningful engineering insights and inferences that drive design and process decisions&nbsp;</li> <li>Familiarity with relevant standards including ASME Y14.5 (GD&amp;T), ISO 4287 / ISO 4288 (surface texture), ASME B46.1 (surface technology), ISO 17025, AS9100, and IPC standards&nbsp;</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills using structured root cause analysis methods and statistical tools such as Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), and Six Sigma&nbsp;</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex technical topics and data inferences into clear one-pagers, dashboards, and executive presentations&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL title: Supplier Development Engineer, PCB (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, PCB (STARLINK) </strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain for printed circuit boards (PCBs) that form the foundation of our User Terminals. We are seeking a technically strong engineer to drive supplier selection, development, qualification, and scaling specifically for the PCB portfolio in high-volume production.</p> <p>The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in PCB manufacturing processes, materials, quality systems, and reliability, combined with practical experience developing suppliers for high-volume electronics. This role demands a strong balance of hands-on technical capability, understanding of manufacturing capability, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to mature suppliers rapidly to support Starlink’s aggressive growth targets.</p> <p>The Supplier Development Engineer will be responsible for executing supplier strategies focused on bare PCBs, multilayer boards, high-frequency/RF PCBs, including and not limited to raw materials used in PCB fabrications. This position will have significant technical influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams. Success requires solid engineering judgment, strong communication skills, and the ability to turn suppliers into reliable, high-volume production partners.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own supplier development activities for the PCB portfolio within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, with primary focus on managing incoming PCB supply chain quality and reliability.</li> <li>Build and maintain a resilient, high-quality, and scalable supply base capable of supporting high-volume production ramp and sustained growth of the Starlink User Terminal business.</li> <li>Assess supplier manufacturing capabilities, including production capacity, process stability, equipment suitability, process windows, material control, and overall technical readiness for high-volume PCB fabrication (lamination, drilling, plating, etching, solder mask, surface finishes, impedance control, and automated optical/electrical testing).</li> <li>Lead Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), First Article Inspections (FAI), production rate ramps, and reliability campaigns to enable high-volume manufacturing.</li> <li>Develop and execute robust qualification plans tailored to PCBs, including dimensional and electrical verification, RF performance testing, thermal/mechanical reliability demonstration, and compliance to applicable standards.</li> <li>Create and standardize qualification protocols across the PCB supply base, including equipment buy-off checklists, Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), Site Acceptance Tests (SAT), and consistent reliability demonstration methods.</li> <li>Drive supplier performance improvement through Lean methodologies, supplier scorecards, process audits, and systematic problem solving to deliver measurable gains in quality, cost, and on-time delivery.</li> <li>Perform root cause analysis and lead corrective actions for quality issues, with focus on common PCB defect modes and failure mechanisms such as delamination, plating voids or thin plating, open/short circuits, warpage, copper thickness variation, solder mask defects, impedance drift, CAF (conductive anodic filament), pad cratering, and material-related reliability issues.</li> <li>Partner closely with Design Engineering, Reliability Engineering, RF/Electrical teams, and Production to ensure supplier processes and manufacturing capability align with Starlink’s high-volume product requirements and performance goals.</li> <li>Support continuous improvement of supplier quality systems and manufacturing processes to meet escalating volume, cost, and reliability targets for both standard and high-frequency/RF PCBs used in indoor and outdoor-rated products.</li> <li>Qualify new suppliers and manage ongoing performance of the incoming PCB supply base.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Material Science, RF Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.</li> <li>3+ years of experience in PCB engineering, quality engineering, reliability engineering, or supplier development.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong technical background in manufacturing processes, materials, quality systems, and high-volume electronics production.</li> <li>Hands-on knowledge of high-volume PCB manufacturing processes including multilayer lamination, mechanical/laser drilling, electroless and electrolytic plating, etching, solder mask application, surface finishes (ENIG, HASL, OSP, etc.), impedance control, and automated inspection/testing, with demonstrated understanding of manufacturing capability assessment.</li> <li>Experience with PPAP, APQP, PFMEA, DFMEA, and First Article Inspection specifically for PCBs and electronic interconnects.</li> <li>Deep familiarity with relevant IPC standards (e.g., IPC-A-600, IPC-6012, IPC-6013, IPC-4101, IPC-4552, IPC-TM-650) as well as related quality and reliability standards.</li> <li>Strong understanding of PCB reliability, common defect modes, failure analysis techniques, and material science aspects of laminates, copper foils, and finishes.</li> <li>Practical experience qualifying rigid, flex, rigid-flex, and high-frequency/RF PCBs for high-volume production, including controlled impedance, high-speed digital, and RF performance requirements.</li> <li>Strong understanding of manufacturing capability evaluations, including capacity analysis, Cp/Cpk process capability studies, process window validation, and scalability for high-volume PCB production.</li> <li>Strong problem-solving skills using 8D, 5-Why, fishbone analysis, and statistical methods (JMP, Design of Experiments, Six Sigma).</li> <li>Knowledge of reliability engineering practices such as accelerated life testing, thermal cycling, humidity exposure, thermal shock, CAF testing, and PCB-specific failure mechanism analysis.</li> <li>Ability to read and interpret 2D drawings, Gerber/ODB++ files, stack-up designs, material specifications, and performance requirements.</li> <li>Experience with Lean manufacturing concepts, supplier scorecard systems, and high-volume process capability (Cp/Cpk).</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex technical topics into clear one-pagers and presentations.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and suppliers in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to travel up to 25% of the time, both domestically and internationally.</li> <li>Position may require extended working hours and occasional weekends to support production ramps and critical issue resolution.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, PHOTOVOLTAICS (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>Starlink User Terminal business is experiencing exponential growth across consumer, retail, enterprise, and mobility applications. This rapid expansion requires a highly resilient and scalable supply chain for solar cells, wafers, ingots, and polysilicon to support high-volume photovoltaic module production.&nbsp;The role entails early engagement in supplier selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to set programs up for success in high-volume manufacturing by ensuring material and process corners are fully completed. The role also includes ownership to deliver on time, monitor field performance, react to issues, and feed lessons learned back to engineering teams for iterative improvement.</p> <p>We are seeking a technically strong Supplier Development Engineer to drive end-to-end supplier development and manufacturing bring-up across the photovoltaic supply chain — with strong focus on solar cell fabrication as well as upstream polysilicon, ingot, and wafer supply — to enable high-volume module output. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in solar cell manufacturing processes and the ability to provide technical guidance on high-efficiency cell technologies. The Supplier Development Engineer, Photovoltaics will be responsible for executing supplier strategies focused on polysilicon, ingots, wafers, and solar cell manufacturing. This position will have significant technical influence across Starlink engineering, quality, and supply chain teams, with extreme end-to-end ownership from early engagement through production scaling and field performance.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own end-to-end supplier development and manufacturing bring-up for the photovoltaic supply chain within the Starlink User Terminal Bill of Materials, spanning polysilicon, ingots, wafers, solar cells, and module integration</li> <li>Engage early with suppliers on selection, equipment selection, and process engineering to properly set up high-volume manufacturing programs by ensuring material and process corners are fully characterized and completed</li> <li>Lead the bring-up of solar cell manufacturing lines while also supporting upstream wafer, ingot, and polysilicon supply chain development to enable high-volume module output</li> <li>Assess supplier manufacturing capabilities with strong emphasis on solar cell fabrication processes including texturing, diffusion, passivation, anti-reflective coating, metallization, and cell testing, along with upstream silicon material processes</li> <li>Lead new product introduction (NPI) activities, production part approval process (PPAP), first article inspections (FAI), production rate ramps, and qualification campaigns to enable full-rate, high-volume manufacturing</li> <li>Develop and execute robust qualification plans covering polysilicon purity, ingot quality, wafer specifications, solar cell efficiency, reliability, and overall module performance</li> <li>Implement artificial intelligence (AI) solutions for process control, defect detection, yield optimization, and predictive analytics in solar cell manufacturing</li> <li>Create and standardize qualification protocols across the supply base, including equipment buy-off checklists, factory acceptance tests (FAT), site acceptance tests (SAT), and consistent reliability title: Supplier Development Engineer, SMT (Starlink)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SUPPLIER DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER, SMT (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is developing a low latency, broadband internet system to meet the needs of consumers across the globe. Enabled by a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites, Starlink will provide fast, reliable internet to populations with little or no connectivity, including those in rural communities and places where existing services are too expensive or unreliable. We are looking for talented, creative, and driven engineers to develop, drive, and maintain suppliers, from initial concept development to full scale production.<strong><br></strong><br>As a Supplier Development Engineer focused on Surface Mount Technology (SMT) for Starlink, you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and scalability of PCBA (Printed Circuit Board Assembly) manufacturing at our global suppliers. You will lead New Product Introduction (NPI) efforts, drive process improvements, and manage the ramp-up of SMT production lines to meet SpaceX's high-volume demands. This position requires deep technical expertise in SMT processes, hands-on experience with PCBA manufacturing, and the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and suppliers worldwide. Based in Bastrop, Texas, you will report to the Supplier Development Engineering team lead and contribute to the rapid iteration and production scaling of Starlink hardware.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead supplier qualification, development, and ongoing performance management for SMT and PCBA manufacturing processes to ensure compliance with SpaceX quality standards and production timelines.</li> <li>Drive NPI activities for new SMT lines, including process validation, equipment selection, and yield optimization at supplier facilities around the world.</li> <li>Identify and resolve manufacturing defects, process inefficiencies, and quality issues in SMT assembly, such as solder paste application, component placement, reflow soldering, and automated optical inspection (AOI).</li> <li>Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions for production failures, utilizing tools like PFMEA, DOE, and SPC to improve process capability and reduce defects per million opportunities (DPMO).</li> <li>Collaborate with SpaceX design, manufacturing, and quality teams to incorporate DFM/DFA feedback into supplier processes</li> <li>Travel to supplier sites (up to 50%) to audit facilities, oversee ramp-ups, and provide on-site technical support for high-volume SMT production.</li> <li>Develop and maintain supplier scorecards, KPIs, and continuous improvement plans focused on cost reduction, yield enhancement, and supply chain resilience.</li> <li>Support the transition from prototype to mass production, including capacity planning, equipment upgrades, and automation integration for SMT lines.</li> <li>Ensure adherence to industry standards (e.g., IPC-A-610, J-STD-001) and SpaceX-specific requirements for mission-critical electronics.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related technical field.</li> <li>2+ years of experience in PCBA manufacturing, with a focus on SMT processes (e.g., screen printing, pick-and-place, reflow, wave soldering, and inspection).</li> <li>Hands-on experience with SMT equipment from manufacturers such as Fuji, Panasonic, DEK, or similar, including programming, maintenance, and troubleshooting.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in SMT engineering, including leadership roles in supplier development or process engineering for complex consumer electronics systems.</li> <li>Expertise in advanced SMT technologies, such as fine-pitch components, BGA/CSP assembly, selective soldering, and high-mix/low-volume to high-volume transitions.</li> <li>Experience with statistical process control (SPC), Six Sigma certification, or Lean manufacturing principles applied to SMT environments.</li> <li>Knowledge of environmental testing and reliability standards for consumer electronics (e.g., vibration, thermal cycling).</li> <li>Prior experience in the consumer electronics industry, particularly with high volume hardware assembly.</li> <li>Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple suppliers and projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.</li> <li>Proven track record in NPI and production ramp-up for high-volume electronics manufacturing, preferably in consumer electronics.</li> <li>Strong understanding of PCBA failure modes, defect analysis, and quality control methodologies (e.g., 8D, Fishbone, Pareto).</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Position is based in Bastrop, TX and requires being onsite - remote work not considered</li> <li>Must be willing to work long hours and weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines</li> <li>Ability to travel: Up to 50% work week travel may be required</li> <li>Valid driver's license</li> </ul><div Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>SURVEILLANCE OPERATOR</strong></p> <p>The Surveillance Operator is responsible for the real-time surveillance of camera systems, rapid response to security alerts, and dispatching of personnel. This role serves as a critical first line of defense in maintaining situational awareness and ensuring timely response to incidents across the facility.</p> <p><strong>&nbsp;RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Active Camera Monitoring: Continuously monitor multiple live camera feeds to detect suspicious activity, safety hazards, or security breaches in real time</li> <li>Alarm Alert Clearing: Receive, assess, verify, and clear security alarms according to established protocols while maintaining accurate records of all events</li> <li>Dispatching: Coordinate and dispatch security officers, maintenance teams, emergency services, or other responders as needed using radio, phone or dispatch systems</li> <li>Incident Command: Assume incident command for security events until relieved by higher authority; provide clear direction, gather critical information and coordinate response efforts</li> <li>Document all incidents, alarms, dispatches and actions taken in the incident management system with accuracy and attention to detail</li> <li>Maintain constant communication with field teams, supervisors and other departments</li> <li>Identify and report system malfunctions, camera outages, or technical issues to the appropriate support team</li> <li>Follow all standard operating procedures, post orders and emergency response protocols</li> <li>Maintain confidentiality and professionalism at all times while handling sensitive security information</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certification</li> <li>2+ years of experience in security monitoring, CCTV operations, or dispatching</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Excellent visual attention to detail and ability to monitor multiple screens simultaneously for extended periods</li> <li>Strong decision-making and critical thinking skills under pressure</li> <li>Excellent jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. So, while you are not expected to go it alone, you are expected to show initiative, take responsibility, and see tasks through to completion.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proactively source passive candidates via X, LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search, GitHub, niche technical forums, and other channels</li> <li>Build and maintain strong talent pipelines for hard-to-fill engineering roles</li> <li>Leverage AI-powered sourcing and research tools to increase pipeline speed and quality while maintaining a personal touch</li> <li>Partner with recruiters and hiring managers to understand role requirements and refine sourcing strategy</li> <li>Conduct initial candidate outreach and phone screens to assess interest and qualifications</li> <li>Track sourcing metrics and pipeline health and share relevant data points with recruiters and hiring teams</li> <li>Represent SpaceX’s mission and culture compellingly to prospective candidates</li> <li>Stay current on market trends, competitor talent pools, and compensation benchmarks</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree and 1+ years of recruiting experience; Our school consists of four studios: Spark (Grades K-2), Discovery (Grades 3-5), Adventure (Grades 6-8), and Launch Pad (Grades 9-12). This is not a traditional school model. title: Telecommunications Engineer
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TELECOMMUNICATIONS ENGINEER</strong></p> <p>As a Telecommunication Engineer at SpaceX, you will work in a complex environment designing and supporting a variety of critical infrastructure. The IT network infrastructure team designs, installs and supports the cable infrastructure used for all types of telecommunications in support of our production facilities, launch infrastructure and spacecraft support systems. This includes the layer 1 fiber and copper data network cabling, operational voice (both wired and wireless systems), video, ground-side vehicle/payload interface RF systems, ground stations, telemetry and optical tracking systems, marine communications, readiness testing, and other systems involved in real-time communications and operations for Falcon, Dragon, Starship, All Recovery Vessels and other missions. Additionally, you will be tasked with designing and overseeing the installation of new cabling infrastructure and processes, with the goal of creating world-class connectivity that can support the mission of enabling life beyond Earth.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide engineering support for the design, operation, improvement, and troubleshooting of all fiberoptic and copper supported network infrastructure for multiple IP based systems</li> <li>Coordinate downtime activities between maintenance, construction, and production teams to minimize disruptions</li> <li>Drive telecommunication projects using design change requests, power monitoring data, and advanced detection methods</li> <li>Troubleshoot electrical system problems, conduct breaker coordination, arc flash studies, and track electrical load and capacity</li> <li>Coordinate material procurement for large scale projects</li> <li>Write, negotiate, and manage construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines through contract close-out</li> <li>Collaborate within interdisciplinary teams to design, optimize, and maintain systems</li> <li>Provide telecom engineering support to field technicians to troubleshoot existing equipment</li> <li>Oversee equipment installation, operation, and maintenance to meet specified parameters</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>BICSI RCDD (Registered Communications Distribution Designer) certification; OR bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline</li> <li>2+ years of experience in industrial electrical engineering and medium or high voltage power systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of professional experience with the design or build of commercial or industrial telecommunication systems as LAN/WAN/WIFI/LTE and ISP/OSP structured cabling systems</li> <li>Primary experience with structured cabling for high density commercial applications</li> <li>Working knowledge of low voltage AC and DC applications required for powering IT and telecom equipment through multiple power sources</li> <li>Experience with critical power infrastructure including UPS systems, backup generators, and automatic transfer switches</li> <li>Experience creating and implementing process/design solutions with minimal impact to business operations</li> <li>Able to quickly assess an issue and assist technicians with troubleshooting and repair instructions</li> <li>Ability to work in a high-concentration, high-stress environment, under possible extended work hours and tight deadlines</li> <li>Acute attention to detail, ability to see interactions with other systems to avoid problems</li> <li>AutoCAD/Revit – beginner to intermediate skill level</li> <li>Familiarity with National Electric Code, National Fire Protection Association, and International Building Code</li> <li>Understand and ability to design to national cabling standards (ANSI/TIA/BICSI)</li> <li>Ability to multi-task, prioritize and work in an extremely fast-paced environment</li> <li>Strong understanding of construction project management principles, including scheduling, budgeting, and contractor management</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Physical ability to perform hands-on work in various environments, including heat, cold, rain, and tight quarters</li> <li>Must possess or be eligible for Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC)</li> <li>Must be able to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg</li> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> <li>Ability to travel as needed</li> <li>Valid driver's license</li> <li>Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or title: Test Engineer (Dragon)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TEST ENGINEER (DRAGON)</strong></p> <p>The Development Test team is responsible for testing that supports every major program at SpaceX: Starship, Dragon, Falcon, and Starlink. In this role, your primary responsibility will be ensuring engines and components used on Dragon spacecraft have been tested and qualified to function in flight conditions. Our engineers specialize in the design and execution of unique tests for engines, components, and spacecraft on an accelerated schedule. This role offers a constant variety of diverse engineering challenges in a fast-paced, hands-on team environment.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop and execute tests at the engine and component level to evaluate hardware performance and survivability during the mission.</li> <li>Repeated ownership of a test campaign, including test plan creation, new system activation, test operations, data review, and some test stand equipment design/fabrication.</li> <li>Provide daily direction and instruction to technicians to fabricate and integrate test articles and stand equipment.</li> <li>Develop and maintain test procedures, sequences, scripts, configuration files, and software.</li> <li>Operate and troubleshoot data acquisition and control systems, wiring, and instrumentation. DAQ systems are primarily National Instruments-based.</li> <li>Operate and troubleshoot fluid and mechanical systems that include low-to-high-pressure gaseous working fluids and rocket propellants (including hypergols &amp; cryogenics) as well as structural components and supporting infrastructure.</li> <li>Operate mechanical systems; these include test stand support structures, heat exchangers, vacuum pumps, tooling, and fluid components such as valves, reliefs, burst disks, tubing, etc.</li> <li>Automate repetitive test operations to increase efficiency and safety. Develop innovative processes to increase testing capability and rates, while maintaining high rigor of safety.</li> <li>Identify and characterize system pitfalls and potential hazards, then work to resolve such anomalies by collaborating with design engineers on improvements for test stands and flight hardware.</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, or other engineering field</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on experience with mechanical systems, structural systems, propulsion systems, fluid systems, flight hardware, or test operations</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>2+ years of hands-on experience with mechanical systems, structural systems, propulsion systems, fluid systems, flight hardware, or test operations</li> <li>Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team environment, accomplishing tasks with limited resources at a rapid pace</li> <li>Knowledge of hazardous systems (cryogenic, flammable, hypergolic, pyrophoric) and high-pressure system design and handling</li> <li>Strong multitasking abilities with a high degree of ownership in project management, consistently driving projects from planning through to successful completion</li> <li>Demonstrated leadership in high-pressure situations, with the ability to provide clear and decisive guidance to fellow teammates during high-risk operations</li> <li>Familiarity with instrumentation and control components (pressure transducers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors (RTDs), strain gauges, accelerometers, flow meters, load cells, relays, solenoids, pneumatic valves)</li> <li>Experience using 3D modeling software (Siemens NX, Inventor, CATIA, etc.)</li> <li>Experience with at least one coding language (Python, Matlab, C, C++, Java, Visual Basic)</li> <li>Experience reviewing data from anomalies and identifying root causes</li> <li>Experience writing and maintaining test procedures and hardware work instructions</li> <li>Creative ability to imagine and design from scratch, while retaining low-cost, reliability, efficiency, and maintainability</li> <li>Ability to read, understand, and apply technical manuals, data reports, mechanical schematics, electrical schematics and design specifications</li> <li>Ability to communicate clearly, confidently, and effectively in both individual and group settings – candidates should enjoy working on a team and be able to work efficiently with others, including stressful situations such as rapid pace operations and times of limited resources</li> </ul> <p><strong>&nbsp;</strong><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Flight hardware is typically built in tight quarters and physical dexterity is required</li> <li>Physical effort including sitting or standing for extended periods of time, lifting and carrying weight such as materials or equipment up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Work performed in an environment with exposure to fumes, odors, and noise</li> <li>Ability to comfortably wear breathing air respirators on a frequent basis, occasionally for extended durations, as required by the position</li> <li>Occasionally exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments (heat, cold, rain)</li> <li>Must be available to work extended hours, weekends, and shifts, which vary depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations title: Test Engineer (Falcon Test)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TEST ENGINEER (FALCON TEST)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX, our commitment to reliability begins with design but is realized through exhaustive testing at the Rocket Development Facility in McGregor, TX. To eliminate anomalies and ensure maximum product quality, the test team pushes our hardware to its limits in as close to flight-like conditions as possible. Test engineers are ultimately responsible for the entire test process. title: Test Stand Maintenance Technician
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>TEST STAND MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN</strong></p> <p>Maintenance technicians at the Rocket Development and Test Facility work in a fast-paced testing environment, where the extraordinary becomes the everyday. This role helps with the build, activation, modification, and improvement of fluid and mechanical systems that test the most powerful high-volume rocket engines in the world. With a focus on repairs and reliability, maintenance technicians are expected to use every tool they have to keep the rocket development and production test stands working well. This work includes performing corrective, preventive, and predictive maintenance on test systems, troubleshooting mechanical and electrical hardware, and giving operations and design feedback to drive improvements across our entire test site.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Modify and maintain test stands and ground support equipment that support testing of fully integrated flight vehicles, individual rocket engines, and various rocket components</li> <li>Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair hardware associated with rocket test stand systems, typically part of fluid, structural, and mechanical subsystems</li> <li>Maintain structural/mechanical systems and related components such as rollers, bearings, rams, and similar items</li> <li>Maintain fluid systems and related components such as process piping, pumps, valves, filters, and similar items</li> <li>Collaborate with design and operations engineers to maintain systems in peak operating condition, provide feedback on designs and operations, and promote continual improvement of ground support equipment</li> <li>Develop novel methods to streamline and increase the reliability of internal processes across the entire test site</li> <li>Follow all regulations and appropriate SpaceX procedures, including quality policies, safety policies, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), National Electrical Code (NEC), and other standards</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>3+ years of experience working with hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, cryogenic, high-pressure gas, or data systems</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience working as a maintenance technician, service technician, field service engineer, or mechanic</li> <li>Strong experience with schematics and diagrams for fluid routing, instrumentation, and electrical components</li> <li>Experience working in a fast-paced production environment in fields such as power generation, oil and gas, aerospace, automotive, or electronics</li> <li>Knowledge of vacuum systems, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, process piping inspections and operations, tubing and pipe fittings, rotating machinery (pumps, air compressors), and a wide variety of mechanical fasteners</li> <li>Knowledge of high-pressure gas, hydraulic, cryogenic, flammable, hypergolic, and pyrophoric systems</li> <li>Experience with heavy equipment or industrial operations and maintenance</li> <li>Experience in equipment maintenance and calibration, instrumentation troubleshooting, process controls, and data and control systems</li> <li>Operational knowledge of process instrumentation (pressure transducers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors (RTDs), load cells, flow meters, and similar items)</li> <li>Operational knowledge of basic electrical theory and electrical troubleshooting (multimeter fault finding, soldering and connecting, operation of various crimping tools, and similar items)</li> <li>Experience with computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) or enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems such as Maximo, SAP, Oracle, and others</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to rapidly change roles and responsibilities while keeping a high sense of urgency in a fast-paced, challenging work environment</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and as part of a team, take individual initiative, and communicate effectively with peers, leadership, and customers</li> <li>Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting the upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings, and climbing hand-over-hand</li> <li>Ability to work at elevated heights (up to 300 feet) with proper personal protective equipment (PPE)</li> <li>Ability to lift heavy objects (up to 25 pounds) without help</li> <li>Ability to respond to emergencies to support priority projects, missions, and launches</li> <li>Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed with flexibility</li> <li>Ability to work in extreme outdoor environments when needed, including heat, cold, wind, rain, and similar conditions</li> <li>Ability to travel to other SpaceX locations as needed (up to 25 percent of the time)</li> <li>Ability to work in tight quarters that require physical dexterity</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> title: Thermal Control and Life Support Hardware Engineer (Crew Starship)
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>THERMAL CONTROL AND LIFE SUPPORT HARDWARE ENGINEER (CREW STARSHIP)</strong></p> <p>After 50 years, humankind will once again return to surface of the moon using SpaceX’s Crew Starship (also known as HLS or the Human Landing System) – this time for good. Leveraging the lessons learned from our flight proven Dragon spacecraft and Falcon rocket, Starship will usher in the next era of crewed spaceflight and exploration, ultimately allowing us to establish permanent communities on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.</p> <p>As a Thermal Control and Life Support Engineer, you will have the opportunity to utilize your knowledge, experience, and creativity to develop novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology. This team develops the necessary hardware to maintain environmental and thermal control as well as support life onboard the Starship spacecraft. The role requires attentiveness across disciplines, as it involves design, analysis, testing, and manufacturing of components that are critical to the safety of future astronauts and passengers.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the conceptualization, design, and build of creative life support and thermal control systems for all Crew Starship missions, including Mars missions, across disciplines such as fans and air distribution, air sanitation, water collection and reclamation, waste management, fire suppression, and active thermal control</li> <li>Rapidly iterate on manufacturing processes and development testing in a fast-paced environment</li> <li>Be responsible for project delivery timeline from early design through production, launch, and sustained operations.</li> <li>Lead design reviews internally and externally with suppliers and customers</li> <li>Work with interdisciplinary customers to ensure the component will integrate with the necessary avionics, software, mission operations, etcetera</li> <li>Ensure designs are manufacturable and reliable</li> <li>Exemplify technical excellence and be accountable for your own work</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in an engineering or science discipline</li> <li>1+ years of experience working with fluid systems, mechanical systems, environmental control systems, or components (internship and project team experience is applicable)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ability to perform trade studies using first principles and engineering fundamentals to make clear recommendations even with partial information</li> <li>Experience with rotating machinery</li> <li>Experienced in NX</li> <li>Solid understanding and application of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&amp;T) and tolerance stack-up analysis</li> <li>Experience with structural analysis methods (hand calcs, ABAQUS, ANSYS) in order to optimize hardware to strength requirements as well as to evaluate for life and fracture</li> <li>Knowledge of metallic and fluid system manufacturing techniques, processes, equipment, and other processes such as machining, welding, brazing, tube bending, etc.</li> <li>Experience with selection of materials considering engineering properties, manufacturing, and fluid compatibility</li> <li>Able to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, and managers</li> <li>Highly self-motivated with strong organizational and written/oral communication skills – able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment with the&nbsp;ongoing drive for continuous improvement in all aspects of work</li> <li>Master’s degree in engineering discipline</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work long hours and weekends as needed to support critical milestones</li> <li>Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>

flying astronauts back to the United States.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Preprocess and manufacture ceramic fibers, filaments, and powders required for the fabrication of next-tier products (candidate must be comfortable working with these types of ceramic materials)</li> <li>Fabricate ceramic refractory billets, ceramic tiles, thermal gap fillers, coatings, and other components required for a robust thermal protection system</li> <li>Basic fabrication, surface preparation for processing, bonding, and oven curing</li> <li>Document processes precisely to be able to jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Scaling AI in space is a thermal problem as much as a power and processing problem. With a dense compute payload dissipating hundreds of kilowatts, the thermal system must efficiently transfer heat to large radiators that reject it to space, under solar load, eclipse, and multi-mode AI duty cycles.</p> <p>You will join the Starmind Thermal team, which owns the satellite cooling stack end-to-end. Rejecting hundreds of kilowatts of accelerator waste heat to space is limited by high-flux loads transferring heat to massive deployable radiators. No capable cooling architecture has been flown at this scale. As a Senior Thermal Engineer focused on fluids analysis, you own conjugate heat transfer and thermal-fluid analysis of cold plates, heat exchangers, and radiator channels and manifolds, and the system 0-D/1-D thermal-fluid network that sets flow split, ΔP budget, loop ΔT, and pump operating point. You co-evolve geometry and flow path with mechanical and fluid-systems owners under tight feedback from manufacturing and test. You sit where the local physics is hardest and the design decisions stick: predictions that close margins, ground in test, and drive rate-production hardware.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own conjugate heat-transfer (CHT) and thermal-fluid analysis of high-performance cold plates, heat exchangers, and radiator channels for STARMIND drivers, pole car operators, and escorts)</li> <li>Review all transportation documentation (permits, route surveys, height checklists, pre-trip and post-trip inspections) prior to departure and develop contingency plans to mitigate risk</li> <li>Travel with assigned flight hardware at all times during long-haul transports</li> <li>Serve as the primary point of contact for all in-transit decisions, including route adjustments, repairs, additional escorts, or driver changes</li> <li>Provide technical input on Department of Transportation (DOT) and Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) requirements to the Logistics and Manufacturing teams for the continuous improvement of transport hardware, procedures, and processes</li> <li>Utilize heavy equipment (forklifts, spotters, overhead cranes) to safely load, unload, and stage flight hardware and ground support equipment</li> <li>Coordinate with the master production schedule (MPS) to ensure required resources, personnel, and transport equipment are available and aligned with program needs</li> <li>Oversee the completion and quality of all daily pre-trip and post-trip inspections, security briefings, permit reviews, and procedural documentation</li> <li>Develop and maintain work instructions, transport procedures, and best practices in collaboration with logistics leadership</li> <li>Track and report key performance metrics, including on-time delivery, safety incidents, and transport efficiency</li> <li>Identify and implement improvements to transportation systems, processes, and hardware to increase safety, reliability, and efficiency</li> <li>Identify various lifting hardware (shackles, slings, chain hoists, wire ropes, D-rings, web straps)</li> <li>Assist with planning and performing lift procedures</li> <li>Assist with crane operations and rigging under supervision</li> <li>Assist in maintaining transport equipment and materials needed for operational success</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>1+ years of experience working with load transport and inventory processes</li> <li>1+ years of hands-on experience with preparing loads, rigging, and packaging</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>1+ years of hands-on experience with overhead cranes and general lifting procedures</li> <li>Knowledge and experience in transport equipment (tractor and trailer) design and maintenance</li> <li>Experience with scheduling and production work instructions to manufacture hardware</li> <li>Advanced skills with Microsoft Office Suite</li> <li>Experience working with and troubleshooting high-pressure systems</li> <li>Experience working in a challenging and fast-paced environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be available to work all shifts, overtime, and weekends as needed based on operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Must be available to travel up to 40% of the time</li> <li>Valid driver’s license</li> <li>Must be bridge (overhead) crane certified within the first 180 days</li> <li>Ability to successfully pass U.S. Air Force background checks required for access to Cape Canaveral, Florida, and Vandenberg, California</li> <li>Must be able to lift 25 pounds unassisted and perform physical activities such as stooping, bending, crawling, and maneuvering in tight or confined spaces</li> <li>Ability to safely work in confined spaces and operate heavy equipment and machinery</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or from the U.S. Department of State. As a tube bender on the SpaceX sheet metal technician team, you will be responsible for the successful fabrication of precision tube assemblies that support projects that make up the Starship vehicle.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Coordinate activity with technicians and support functions through all tube bending operations, including tube prep, flaring, CNC lean/continuous improvement tools</li> <li>Ability to set up and operate tube fabrication equipment</li> <li>Ability to interpret blueprints and articulate work instructions</li> <li>Knowledge of tube cleaning requirements for aerospace</li> <li>Knowledge of orbital tube welding (OTW)</li> <li>Experience with manual tubing benders</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> title: Utility Operator Specialist - Level 4/5
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>UTILITY OPERATOR SPECIALIST - LEVEL 4/5</strong></p> <p>SpaceX is seeking utility operators for its Starbase, TX facility. Ideally, the operator has experience working with industrial processes that utilize engines, motors, fluid piping, electrical equipment, and instrumented controls. This position entails ownership of equipment performance and reliability by monitoring process parameters and maintaining components, with a keen eye for leading indicators of instability or malfunction, and a drive to correct those issues in advance of undesirable events.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify equipment and process deviations and perform corrective actions</li> <li>Troubleshoot, maintain, and calibrate a variety of process equipment including centrifugal and reciprocating compressors, gas analyzers, control systems, instrument electrical systems and process control valves</li> <li>Work with engineers, technicians, and fabricators to implement fluid and mechanical designs in the field</li> <li>Work with engineers and technicians to create operating procedures</li> <li>Coordinate across multiple disciplines to ensure that required resources are available to complete builds</li> <li>Use knowledge of systems and existing documentation like schematics and parts lists to create and maintain a mature and efficient hardware inventory system – including procurement of critical spares&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> <li>Learn and run standard operating procedures on the machinery</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Associate degree in mechanical or electrical engineering technology and 4+ years of experience working with automated processes in one of the following areas; OR a high school diploma or equivalency certificate and 6+ years of experience in one of the following areas: <ul> <li>Control room operations</li> <li>Plant operations</li> <li>Mechanic/millwright support</li> <li>Instrumentation/electrical operations</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li><span data-teams="true">Holds a Class B or higher Water Operator and/or Wastewater Operator license through TCEQ or equivalent</span></li> <li>Basic understanding of process parameters and engineering units for temperature, pressure, flow, and power</li> <li>Ability to read and understand P&amp;ID and schematic wiring diagrams</li> <li>Familiar with mechanical equipment and systems requiring the isolation of the malfunction, disassembly of industrial machinery and repair/replacement of bearings, gears, structural components</li> <li>Familiar with lock out tag out, job hazard analysis, hot work permitting</li> <li>Familiar with 120V, 480V, and 4160V electrical switchgear and components</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Willing and able to work outside with hand tools, which includes the ability to stand, walk, climb, and work with objects overhead</li> <li>Required to climb ladders to elevated platforms and operate man-lifts at elevations in excess of 100 feet</li> <li>Must be willing to work all shifts, overtime and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Welder - 2nd Shift
jd_text: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of&nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>WELDER – 2ND SHIFT</strong></p> <p>Welders in McGregor, TX, will work to build structural and/or fluid systems to support various testing campaigns in Central Texas. The welders work with an elite team of other fabricators to rapidly build the large assemblies that will support vehicle and component testing at our test site.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Perform at least two of the following processes, depending upon the needs of the business: Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW), Shielded Metal Arc Welding/stick welding (SMAW), Gas Tungsten Arc Welding/TIG welding (GTAW), and Gas Metal Arc Welding/MIG welding (GMAW)</li> <li>Fit up and weld structures or pipe spools made of mild carbon steel, low alloy, stainless, aluminum, or exotics, depending upon the needs of the business</li> <li>Communicate with management/supervisors, engineering staff, and planners to achieve build efficiency</li> <li>Perform fabrication math to derive dimensions, angles, pup lengths, part locations, etc., from drawings (understand take-offs for pipe fittings)</li> <li>Analyze engineering drawings and specifications to plan fitting and welding operations where procedural information is unavailable</li> <li>Make a continuous effort to improve operations, decrease turnaround times, streamline work processes, and work cooperatively and jointly</li> <li>Check drawings and instructions after each Work Order operation to ensure they are complete</li> <li>Handle and dispose of hazardous materials in an approved manner</li> <li>Set up safety equipment and work platforms at elevation</li> <li>Perform other related duties, as assigned, for the purpose of ensuring an efficient and effective work environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>High school diploma or equivalency certificate</li> <li>2+ years of experience (experience from a college welding program qualifies) in two of the following processes: Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW), Shielded Metal Arc Welding/stick welding (SMAW), Gas Tungsten Arc Welding/TIG welding (GTAW), or Gas Metal Arc Welding/MIG welding (GMAW)</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in one of the following processes: FCAW, SMAW, GTAW, or GMAW</li> <li>Knowledge of standard tools, materials, and work practices of the welding trade</li> <li>Knowledge of occupational hazards and effective safety precautions of the trade</li> <li>Experience using overhead cranes and forklifts</li> <li>Ability to rapidly change focus in a high-paced, challenging work environment</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Anticipated hours for this position are 1:30 PM – 12:30 AM</li> <li>Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required</li> <li>Ability to stand for extended periods (8 hours minimum) and lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted</li> <li>Ability to stand, kneel, crouch, climb, twist the upper body, and work in cramped positions</li> <li>Ability to work at heights up to 100 feet and in confined spaces</li> <li>Ability to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain</li> <li>Work performed in an environment exposed to fumes, odors, sparks, and noise</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href="https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987">here</a>. &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to&nbsp;<a href="mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com">EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>.&nbsp;</em></p></div>
